info.title: Check Networks API
info.description:
The Check Networks API lets you run your services from your own systems:
qualify and order NBN and Opticomm data services, manage phone numbers,
SIP trunks and SMS, raise support tickets, receive webhooks, and read your
account and billing.

This is the reference: every endpoint and webhook, with the scope it
needs, its parameters, its responses and request samples. How the API
works, the guides and the client libraries are on the
[developer site](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/):

- [Quick start](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/start/quick-start/):
  a key, a token and a first call against the sandbox.
- [Conventions](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/concepts/conventions/):
  names, money, lists, time zones and the error body.
- [Errors](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/concepts/errors/),
  [retrying writes safely](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/concepts/idempotency/),
  [rate limits](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/concepts/limits/) and
  [versions and deprecation](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/concepts/versioning/).
- [Webhooks](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/webhooks/webhooks/) and
  every [event type](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/webhooks/event-types/).
- [Client libraries](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/sdks/client-libraries/)
  for PHP, Python and JavaScript, and the
  [changelog](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/reference/changelog/).

Endpoints marked **Coming Soon** are published early so you can build
against them. Until they go live they answer `501 - Not Implemented`.

For help with the API, email support@checknetworks.com.au and quote the
`CN-Message-Id` header of the response.

tags.description: Find this reference and check the API is up. No token needed.

tags.name: Account

Your account's details, balance, invoices, credit notes and payments.

**Webhooks:** invoices and payments send [Account & Billing events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Account).

**Webhooks:** status changes and technician appointments send [Orders & Appointments events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Orders).

Your data services on any network, in one shape, with their live status and their usage.

tags.name: Data RADIUS

Your RADIUS users, their sessions and their realm.

**Webhooks:** a realm request being approved or rejected sends [RADIUS Realms events](#tag/Webhook-Events-RADIUS).

tags.name: Data Bundles

Order data services, numbers and a voice trunk together, in sequence,

tags.name: Colocation

Your colocation services, ordering rack space, and remote-hands and

tags.name: VPN

Your VPN access groups and users, as the portal's VPN pages: what each

tags.name: Users
tags.description: The staff users on your wholesale account: their roles, two-factor, notice choices and open invitations. An API key acts as an Admin here, so it can neither change nor remove an Owner, nor make anyone an Owner.

tags.name: Support Tickets
tags.description:
Raise and follow support tickets with Check Networks.

**Webhooks:** new tickets, replies, status changes and ratings send [Support Tickets events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Tickets).

tags.name: Network Outages

Check Networks outages affecting your services, from our outage register.

**Webhooks:** outages opening, changing and closing send [Network Outages events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Outages).

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Register the URLs that receive events, test them, and see and replay their deliveries.

The events are listed in this group by area. Read [How Delivery Works](#tag/Webhook-Delivery) first.

tags.name: Webhook Delivery
tags.description:
Each event is sent as a `POST` with a JSON body to every endpoint subscribed to it. Reply with any `2xx` status to acknowledge it, including for an event type you do not handle.

### What a delivery carries

The body has `eventId`, `eventType`, `occurredAt`, `sequence` and `data`, plus `apiVersion` (`2`), `livemode` (`false` from the sandbox), `test` (`true` for a delivery you asked for with `POST /webhooks/{webhookId}/test`), `accountId` (your `clientNumber`) and `resourceUrl`, where to read the current state of what the event is about. Events can arrive late or out of order, so re-read `resourceUrl` before acting on one.

The headers carry `X-CN-Event-Id` (the `eventId`) and `X-CN-Delivery-Attempt` (`1` for the first try, counting up on each retry; a redelivery or replay is a new delivery and starts again at `1`).

Within a version, events only gain fields and new event types are only added. Ignore a field or type you do not know, and answer `2xx` to it.

### Checking a delivery came from us

Every delivery carries an `X-CN-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<signature>` header. Check it: it is the only proof a delivery came from us. The secret itself is never sent, so nothing that logs your request headers can forge a delivery.

The signature is an HMAC-SHA256, in hex, of `<t>.<raw body>`, keyed with your endpoint secret. Work it out over the exact bytes you received, compare it in constant time, and reject a delivery whose `t` is more than 5 minutes old.

For a while after you rotate the secret, the header carries a second `v1` signed with the old one. Accept the delivery if any `v1` matches.

### Retries

What happens next depends on the status your endpoint answers:

- A `5xx`, a timeout or a connection failure is tried again: 6 attempts in all over about 8.6 hours, waiting 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 6 hours between them. After the last one it is marked `dead`.
- A `429` is tried again when your `Retry-After` header says, or on the same ladder if you send none.
- A `408` is treated like a timeout and tried again on the ladder.
- Any other `4xx` is **not retried**: it is marked `dead` at once, since the endpoint would answer the same way in six hours.
- A `3xx` is **not followed and not retried**: it is marked `dead` at once. Register the final URL instead.

Every `dead` delivery counts toward the auto-disable below, whichever way it got there, with one exception: for 30 days after an event type is added, a `4xx` to it does not count, so an endpoint that does not know the new type yet is not turned off for it. The endpoint's `lastError` still shows the rejection.

After 20 dead deliveries in a row, the endpoint is turned off (`disabledReason: auto`), your technical contact is emailed, and your other endpoints that take it get a `webhook.endpointDisabled` event. Events are still recorded while it is off. Turn it back on with `PATCH /webhooks/{webhookId}`, then replay the dead deliveries to catch up.

### Duplicates and order

An event can arrive more than once, and out of order. Use `eventId` to ignore repeats, and `occurredAt` to put them in order: a redelivered or replayed event keeps both. `sequence` counts up for each endpoint as each delivery is queued, and a redelivery or a replay is a new delivery with a new `sequence`, so do not order by it. Better still, treat an event as a hint and re-read `resourceUrl`.

### Answering

We wait 10 seconds for an answer, 5 of them to connect, and each endpoint has at most two deliveries in flight at once. Answer `2xx` quickly and do the work afterwards.

tags.name: Webhook Events End Users

tags.name: Webhook Events SMS

tags.name: Webhook Events Fax

tags.name: Numbers
tags.description:
Your phone numbers: their labels, inbound routing and emergency address.

An Australian number (geographic, mobile, 1300, 1800 or 13) needs an emergency address before it can be routed or used as an outbound caller ID. Link one with `emergencyAddressId`.

To get a number: find the area for a customer's address (`GET /numbers/areas`), see what is available and its price (`GET /numbers/available`), hold one if you like (`POST /numbers/holds`), order it (`POST /numbers`) and read the order until it is set up (`GET /numbers/orders/{id}`). `POST /numbers/lookup` says who holds and who serves a number before you port it.

tags.name: Emergency Addresses
tags.description: The addresses emergency services are given for your numbers: in Australia, the number's IPND listing. Create one, then link numbers to it with `PATCH /numbers/{number}`.

tags.name: SIP Trunks
tags.description:
Create and manage SIP trunks, their IP allow-lists and registrations.

**Webhooks:** a trunk going live, suspended, resumed or disconnected sends [Services events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Services), and a trunk going down or coming back sends [Voice events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Voice).

tags.name: Fax Plans
tags.description:
Fax is an ordered service. A number sends and receives faxes only while
it is on a fax plan, and faxes go to Australian landlines, mobiles and
13, 1300 and 1800 numbers only. Order a plan, put numbers on it, and
authorise the email addresses that may send as them. A number on a plan
has no separate monthly number charge.

tags.name: Fax
tags.description:
Send a fax, read your fax history, and set your fax domain and cover
page. History is metadata only, never the documents.

**Webhooks:** faxes received, sent or failed send [Fax events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Fax).

tags.name: Voice
tags.description:
Call records (with filters, a summary and one call), the scheduled call
record exports, live calls and hanging one up (never an emergency call).

**Webhooks:** completed calls send [Voice events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Voice).

tags.name: SMS
tags.description: Send SMS and read your message history.

tags.name: Number Ports
tags.description: Bring numbers to us from another carrier, and follow numbers leaving you. Request a port-in, confirm a mobile port's verification code, withdraw a port before its cutover is booked, and read every port with who it is waiting on and what has happened so far, as the portal's Number Ports pages do. A port is named by its `reference`; another account's answers 404. Each step also arrives as `order.statusChanged`.

tags.name: IP Transit Blackholes
tags.description:
**Not available yet.** IP transit is not offered by API yet: these
endpoints answer `404` and their `transit:*` scopes cannot be granted
until it is.

Drop the traffic to one address of an IP transit service, to stop an
attack on it reaching you. The traffic is dropped at our border.

**Webhooks:** a blackhole placed, released or expired sends [IP Transit events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Transit).

tags.name: End-User Price Book
tags.description:
What you charge your end users for each product: your default markup,
a price per product, a voice product's default call plan, and the
products you sell that are not priced yet. Only for an account that
bills its end users: every route answers 404 otherwise.

Prices are ex-GST, as in the portal. GST is added on the end user's
invoice under your own tax settings.

tags.name: End-User Call Plans
tags.description:
Your own call plans for your end users: build one, edit its draft
destinations, and publish a version.

tags.name: End-User Service Billing
tags.description:
How one service you have given an end user bills: a call plan pinned to
it, its own price and setup fee in place of your price book, or not
billed at all.

tags.name: End-User Charges
tags.description:
Your own recurring and one-off charges on an end user's bill, such as a
support fee or a site visit.

tags.name: End-User Usage
tags.description:
Usage you rated yourself (managed-service hours, seats, a third-party
feed), billed on your end users' invoices.

tags.name: End-User Spend
tags.description: An end user's spend this month against its monthly limit.

tags.name: End-User Billing Settings
tags.description:
The settings on every invoice to your end users, the payment reminder
schedule, the wording of the notices they receive, and whether your
payment gateways are working.

tags.name: End User Billing
tags.description:
The invoices, credit notes and payments on your end users' accounts:
approve, release and resend invoices, credit them, record payments,
pause reminders, issue a final invoice, and read an end user's ledger.
Only for an account that bills its end users: every route answers 404
otherwise.

tags.name: End User Cases
tags.description:
Your end users' billing disputes and financial hardship cases: review,
credit and close a dispute, and assess and close a hardship case, as
the portal does.

tags.name: Xero
tags.description:
Your own Xero organisation, which your end-user invoices, credit notes
and payments are sent to. Connecting and disconnecting stay in the
portal, as they need a browser sign-in to Xero.

tags.name: End Users
tags.description:
Your end users: your own customers, who use your services. Create and
change them, give them services, suspend, archive and restore them, and
manage their notes, representatives and logins to the end-user portal,
as the End Users pages of the portal do.

An end user is named by its number (`endUser`), never an internal id.
An end user of another account answers 404, as an unknown number does.

While a family violence safety record withholds an end user's contact
details, every end-user call masks them, as the portal does.

tags.name: Residential Lines
tags.description:
Home phone lines: one SIP line each on our residential domain, billed as
a PAYG or Ultimate plan. Order one, move it between plans, and set its
call forwarding, Do Not Disturb, anonymous call reject, call waiting and
voicemail, as the portal's Residential Lines pages do.

A line is named by its SIP username, the `trunk` that call records and
numbers carry with `trunkType: residentialLine`. A SIP trunk's username
answers 404 here, and a line's answers 404 under `/trunks`.

**Webhooks:** a new voicemail sends [Voice events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Voice).

tags.name: Caller ID Authorisations
tags.description:
Ask for the right to present a number your account does not hold as a
trunk's caller ID, with proof that you may use it. We review each
request; until one is approved, setting that number as a trunk's
`defaultCallerId` answers `422` with the code
`caller_id_authorisation_required`.

**Webhooks:** each decision sends `callerId.statusChanged` ([Voice events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Voice)).

tags.name: Call Recordings
tags.description:
The recordings of calls on trunks with call recording on: list them and
fetch one with a download link that lasts 5 minutes. Recordings are call
content, so they need their own scope, `recordings:read`, never
`voice:read`; every fetch is audited. Recordings are deleted by our
staff only.

**Webhooks:** a stored recording sends `voice.recording.ready` ([Voice events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Voice)).

tags.name: Delegated Steps
tags.description:
Hand one step of an order to a person with no login: the mobile
number's holder who must confirm a port, or someone at the site who
must pick an install time. Name them and their email; they get a
one-use link to a page on your end-user portal, in your branding.
They pass a code sent to that email, then see only that step and do
it once. Resend the link (a new link; the old one stops working) or
cancel it. A link works for 7 days.

The page opens on your end-user portal, so an account without one
answers `403` with the code `no_end_user_portal_access`.

**Webhooks:** a step done sends `delegation.used` ([Delegated Steps events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Delegated-Steps)).

post.description:
Exchanges your API Client credentials for an access token. This is the
first call any integration makes, and the only one that does not carry a
bearer token.

Tokens are valid for **one hour**. Request a new one when it expires.
The client-credentials flow has no refresh token.

### Scopes

Ask for the scopes the token needs, space-separated. A token requested
**without** a `scope` carries none, and every endpoint refuses it with
`403`. Request only the scopes each job needs, especially for anything
running unattended.

We drop scopes outside your Client's allowance silently rather than
reject them. **The `scope` field in the response is the source of truth
for what your token can do.** Check it first when an endpoint answers
`403`. That error names the scope it wanted.

### IP allowlist

A Client with an IP allowlist gets tokens only from an address on it. A
request from anywhere else answers `403` with code `ip_not_allowed`.
We answer before we check the secret, so the answer says nothing about
whether the secret was right.

### Rotation and end dates

While a rotation's overlap runs, we accept both the old and the new
secret here. Start a rotation with `POST /account/api-keys/self/rotate`
or Roll Secret in the portal. A token the old secret mints ends when the
overlap does, even if that is under an hour away.

A key may have an end date. Past it, the right secret answers `401` with
code `key_expired`. A wrong secret answers as any wrong secret does.
Tokens the key minted before then stop at the end date too.

### Rate limit

The limit is **30 requests per minute for each `client_id` from one
address**. Systems behind one NAT or cloud address each keep their own
limit. A second limit is 120 per minute from one address, whatever the
`client_id`. A token lasts an hour, so a client that reuses its token
never comes near either.

### OAuth apps

A registered OAuth app uses this endpoint for the authorization code
grant and to refresh. For the authorization code grant, send
`grant_type=authorization_code` with the `code` from the consent screen,
the same `redirect_uri` and the PKCE `code_verifier`. To refresh, send
`grant_type=refresh_token`. Both send the app's `client_id` and
`client_secret`. The response then carries a `refresh_token` as well.

Each refresh replaces the refresh token and the access token, so use the
new ones. A refresh token lasts 30 days from the refresh that issued it.
An app that refreshes at least every 30 days stays connected. One left
idle longer must be connected again.

Sending a replaced refresh token again is treated as a stolen copy. We
refuse it, disconnect the app from the account with all its tokens, and
email the account's Owners. We also refuse a refresh after the account
revoked the app, or after we disabled it.

An app's client cannot use `client_credentials`. See
[OAuth apps](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/guides/oauth-apps/).

grant_type.description: `client_credentials` for an API key. An OAuth app sends `authorization_code` to exchange a code, and `refresh_token` to refresh.

code.description: The code from the consent screen (`authorization_code` only). Lasts ten minutes and works once.

redirect_uri.description: The redirect URI the code was issued for (`authorization_code` only).

code_verifier.description: The PKCE verifier whose S256 hash the authorise step was sent (`authorization_code` only).

refresh_token.description: The app's latest refresh token (`refresh_token` only).

client_id.description: Your API Client's id, from the Wholesale Portal. Required, here or as the user of an `Authorization: Basic` header (RFC 6749 2.3.1) with `client_secret` as its password.

client_secret.description: Your API Client's secret. Shown once when the client is created; if it is lost, rotate it in the portal. A production secret starts `cn_live_` and a sandbox one `cn_test_`. Required, here or in an `Authorization: Basic` header.

scope.description: Space-separated; ask for the scopes the token needs. A token requested without a scope carries none, and every endpoint refuses it with `403`.

access_token.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every other endpoint.

refresh_token.description: OAuth apps only. Send it with `grant_type=refresh_token` for the next access token. It is replaced on every use and lasts 30 days from that use.

scope.description: Space-separated, and authoritative — the scopes this token actually carries, which may be narrower than requested.

400.description: The request is malformed or the grant is unsupported. Uses the OAuth2 error shape (RFC 6749), not this API's standard error envelope.

401.description: The client id or secret is wrong: the OAuth2 error shape (RFC 6749), not this API's standard error envelope. The right secret of a key past its end date answers in this API's standard error envelope instead, with code `key_expired`.

403.description: The request came from an address outside the Client's IP allowlist (`ip_not_allowed`). No token is issued. This API's standard error envelope.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** none; any valid token

Make this call first with a new token, and again when a call is refused.
It answers `200` when the token and your API Client are good.

The answer shows which key and account answered, the scopes the token
carries, and the address we saw you call from. It also shows whether the
key's IP allowlist is on, which environment answered and when the token
expires.

A token from a revoked client, or one issued before its secret was
rotated, is refused here as on every other endpoint, with `403`.

keyId.description: Your API Client's id, the `client_id` you requested the token with.

name.description: Your API Client's name, as set in the Wholesale Portal.

scopes.description: The scopes this token carries. A scope you requested but your Client is not allowed is not listed.

accountId.description: The account the key belongs to, its `clientNumber` on `GET /account`.

ip.description: The address we saw this call come from, as your IP allowlist is checked against.

ipAllowlistActive.description: Whether the key has an IP allowlist. When it does, only addresses on it may call or request tokens.

environment.description: Which environment answered. A production secret starts `cn_live_` and a sandbox one `cn_test_`.

tokenExpiresAt.description: When this token expires. Request a new one before then.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** none; any valid token

Finds Australian addresses in our copy of G-NAF, best match first. It
does not call a carrier, so it is quick enough for type-ahead.

Send some of the address in `q`, the structured parameters, or both. The
unit, level and road parameters are matched with `q`. `localityName`,
`stateTerritoryCode` and `postcode` must match exactly. You need `q` or
at least one of the unit, level or road parameters.

Each match carries its G-NAF id. Use it for the carrier step. For NBN,
call `GET /nbn/address/search?gnaf=`. For Opticomm, use the match's
`opticommOpcId`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text, such as `12 smith st parramatta`.

parameters.name: roadTypeCode

>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Returns your account details, so you can check that we hold the right ones for you.

The credit position and `billingEmail` in `billingDetails` are billing data. The credit position is
`amountOwed`, `creditLimit`, `creditUsed`, `availableCredit`, `creditUsedPercent` and the deprecated `credit`
or `balance`. We return them only when your token also holds **billing:read**. Without it, `billingDetails`
carries only `accountType` and `currency`. The fields mean the same as on
[Get Account Balance](#tag/Account/operation/get_account_balance).

clientNumber.description: Your client number with Check Networks.

postcode.description: The postcode. Null when we hold no such line.

country.description: The country. Null when we hold no such line.

billingAddress.description: The address printed on our invoices to you, in the same shape as `address`. Every line is null when none is on file. Change it with [Update Billing Details](#tag/Account/operation/patch_account_billing_details). Returned only when your token also holds **billing:read**.

billingContact.description: Your billing contact, where invoices and billing notices go. Each field is null when not on file. Returned only when your token also holds **billing:read**.

features.description: What your account may order and use. You can tell from this whether a call would be refused. We accept an order only when its product is `true` in `orderable`, `orderChecksOutstanding` is empty and `ordersHeld` is false. Otherwise every order answers 403.

fax.description: Fax to email and email to fax are offered.

invoiceDisputes.description: Invoice disputes are offered, on our invoices and on your end users' bills.

callerScopes.description: The scopes of the token making this call, and the scopes its API key may ask for. A call that needs a scope outside `token` answers 403 with code `missing_scope`. If the scope is in `key` but not `token`, request a new token that asks for it.

>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Returns the figures on your portal dashboard in one call. They are how many
trunks, numbers and data services you have, how many orders, tickets and
outages are open, and what needs you. The numbers are the dashboard's own.

`needsAttention` lists only the groups with something in them. Each entry's
`link` opens the list filtered to exactly the rows it counted. It is null
where there is no API list for that group yet.

`endUser` is an end user's number. It narrows every figure to that end
user's services, orders and tickets. Outages affect the whole network, so
`openOutages` is your account's either way. The port groups belong to your
account, so they are left out.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: An end user's number. An unknown number answers 422.

200.description: Your account's headline figures and what needs you.

trunks.description: Your SIP trunks. Residential lines are not counted.

byNetworkAndState.description: Your data services counted by network and state, largest first.

openOrders.description: Every kind of order still in progress.

openOutages.description: Outages affecting your services that are not yet resolved.

link.description: The list filtered to this group, e.g. `/data/orders?needsAttention=orderAwaitingAction`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Returns every notice we sent you and your end users, newest first, with
what happened to each. That covers invoices, statements, payment notices,
overdue and suspension warnings, outage notices and others. Use it to
answer "I never got that notice". It shows whether the notice went, to
which address, and whether it bounced.

Page as with every list, by `page` or by cursor. To use the cursor, pass
the `nextCursor` of one page as `cursor` for the next. A notice sent while
you walk by cursor never shifts a row into or out of a page. `nextCursor`
is null on the last page.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Sent at or after this date or time.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Sent at or before this date or time. A date alone covers the whole day.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only notices of this kind, such as `overdue_notice`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only notices sent to this end user (its number). An unknown number answers 422.

total.description: Notices matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass it back as `cursor` for the next page. It is `null` on the last page, or on a page that was not full.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Returns one notice we sent you or one of your end users, by its `id`.

>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Shows where your account stands with us. You see what you owe, your credit
limit, how much of it is used and how much is left. Your system can use it
to warn you before your services are held.

200.description:
Your current account balance.

`amountOwed` means the same on every account. It is positive when you
owe us and negative when you hold credit with us. It is your **billed**
position: invoices raised, less payments and credits applied, with GST.

`creditUsed`, `availableCredit` and `creditUsedPercent` are your credit
line as credit control reads it and the portal dashboard shows it. They
are without GST. Credit used is what you owe plus usage not yet
invoiced. We hold your services when `availableCredit` reaches zero.

`unbilledUsage` is metered usage that has **not** been invoiced yet,
with GST. It is the calls and messages since your last invoice. It is
not in `amountOwed`. On a postpaid account, `amountOwed` plus
`unbilledUsage` is roughly what you would owe if invoiced now. On a
prepaid account, your credit left after that usage is `unbilledUsage`
taken from the credit you hold (`-amountOwed`). Read `availableCredit`
for the figure that holds your services.

`unbilledUsage` is null when the figure is not available. Treat null as
**unknown**, never as zero.

balance.description: The amount owed on a postpaid account, and the credit left on a prepaid one. Its meaning changes with the account type. Deprecated, so read `amountOwed` and `accountType`.

currency.description: The currency of every amount here.

unbilledUsage.description: Metered usage not yet invoiced, with GST, as a decimal string in dollars. Always present. Null when the figure is unavailable. Not in `amountOwed`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns a paginated list of invoices for your account, ordered newest first.
`q` searches the invoice number.

### Bulk export

For a bulk pull, set `format=csv` or `format=ndjson`. You get the **entire**
matching result set as one download instead of paged JSON. The `status`,
`number` and date filters still apply. `page` and `perPage` are ignored.
`csv` returns `text/csv`, with a header row and one row per invoice.
`ndjson` returns `application/x-ndjson`, with one JSON object per line,
each identical to a `results[]` item. An unrecognised `format` returns
`422`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Bulk export format. Omit for paged JSON; `csv` or `ndjson` streams the full matching result set as a download.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by the status an invoice shows. You can send several, comma-separated, as in `status=unpaid,overdue`. Case does not matter. Any other value is `422`. `unpaid` is issued and not yet overdue. `overdue` is issued and due before today on the invoice's own calendar. No invoice is both.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Invoices whose number contains this text, as the portal's invoice search matches it. Not case-sensitive.

parameters.name: issuedFrom
parameters.description: Invoices issued on or after this date, as YYYY-MM-DD. The day is the one the invoice shows, in the time zone it was cut in (its `timezone`). Send `CN-Time-Zone` to read the date in your own zone instead. You can leave either end open. A date that is not real, or a start after the end, answers `422`.

parameters.name: issuedTo
parameters.description: Invoices issued on or before this date, the whole day included.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing invoices.

total.description: Total number of invoices matching the query.

perPage.description: The number of invoices per page.

schema.description: Sent only when `format=csv`. The full matching result set as CSV, with a header row and one row per invoice. The columns are the same as a `results[]` item.
Sent only when `format=ndjson`. The full matching result set as newline-delimited JSON, with one object per line. Each is identical to a `results[]` item.

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: The invoice's `id`, as `GET /account/invoices` gives it.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns the full details of one invoice. It shows what is paid, what is
owed and what a dispute holds. It shows any card or direct debit charge
still processing. It lists every line, with the service, end user and
period it bills and the rows behind it.

`amountDue` is what is still owed now. While `amountInFlight` is more than
zero, a charge is already under way. Do not pay the same invoice again in
the portal.

### One invoice as CSV

Set `format=csv` for the invoice's lines as `text/csv`, one row per line.
Each row has the invoice number and dates. The money is in
`unitPriceExGst`, `unitPriceGst`, `unitPriceIncGst`, `totalExGst`,
`totalGst` and `totalIncGst`. The lines' `totalIncGst` add up to the
invoice's. No cell begins with a character a spreadsheet reads as a
formula. Any other `format` returns `422`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Omit it for JSON. `csv` returns the lines as a spreadsheet.

200.description: The invoice and its line items.

tax.description: The GST on this invoice's new charges. Deprecated, so read `totalGst`.

amountInFlight.description: The card and direct debit charges on this invoice still processing, with GST. They are not in your balance yet. `0.00` once each settles or fails.

charges.description: Every card and direct debit charge on this invoice, newest first.

invoiceGroups.description: The invoice's group sections as issued, in name order with Other last. Each has its PO, cost centre and subtotal. Empty when no line carries a group, label, PO or cost centre.

schema.description: Sent only when `format=csv`. A header row, then one row per line. When the invoice has group sections, the lines come group by group. Each group is followed by a row whose `rowType` is `groupSubtotal`, with the group's subtotal in the total columns. Every other row's `rowType` is `line`.

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: The invoice's `id`, as `GET /account/invoices` gives it.

>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns a paginated list of the payments received on your account, newest
first. Each payment lists the invoices it settled and how much of each. Use
it with [List Invoices](#tag/Account/operation/list_invoices) and
[List Credit Notes](#tag/Account/operation/list_credit_notes) to reconcile
what you paid against what you were invoiced.

A payment your bank later dishonours stays in the list with
`status: reversed`, so you can see the money's return too. Its `invoices`
are the ones it settled before the reversal.

To walk every payment while new ones arrive, follow `nextCursor`. Pass it
back as `cursor` until it is `null`. `q` searches the payment reference.

### Bulk export

For a bulk pull, set `format=csv` or `format=ndjson`. You get the **entire**
result set as one download instead of paged JSON, and `page` and `perPage`
are ignored. `csv` returns `text/csv`, with a header row and one row per
payment. `invoices` is a JSON array in its cell. `ndjson` returns
`application/x-ndjson`, with one JSON object per line, each identical to a
`results[]` item. An unrecognised `format` returns `422`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Returns a paginated list of the users on your wholesale account.

The list holds your staff logins, not your clients' logins.

It is ordered by name. `q` searches name and email.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A page of the users on your wholesale account.

total.description: How many users your account has.

perPage.description: The number of users per page.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:create

Invites a new user to your wholesale account, as the Users page in the
portal does.

This is for adding staff, not your clients' users.

We send the person the normal invitation email. No login exists until
they accept it. They choose their own password then, and a `password` in
the request is refused with `422`. The invitation lasts 72 hours. Inviting
the same address again replaces the open invitation.

An `Idempotency-Key` is required. A retry then returns the first answer,
and does not send a second email that cancels the link in the first.
Without the key the request answers `400`. A client written before
2.0.0-pre.3, when the key was optional here, must now send it.

`role` is `admin`, `billing` or `readonly`. An API key may assign only what
an Administrator may, so it can never make an Owner. We email the account's
Owners when a user is invited, naming the API key that made the request.
Only an Owner can grant a key the `account:create` scope.

firstName.description: The first name of the person to invite.

lastName.description: The last name of the person to invite.

email.description: The email address to invite. It must not already be in use by another login.

role.description: What the user may do. `admin` manages the account, its services, users and API keys. `billing` sees invoices and payments. `readonly` reads only.

202.description: The invitation is sent. The user exists once the invitation is accepted, and then appears in `GET /account/users` with its own `id`.

result.description: The pending invitation. It has no user id yet. The login exists once the invitation is accepted, and then has its own `id` in `GET /account/users`.

inviteId.description: The invitation's id, as `/account/invites/{inviteId}` takes it to resend or revoke it.

status.description: Always `pending`. The invitation has not been accepted.

expiresAt.description: When the invitation lapses unaccepted, in UTC.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The user's id. Get it from Get All Users.

Returns one user on your wholesale account.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Changes the name or role of a user on your wholesale account.

Send the new name or role. A request that changes nothing is rejected.

A key acts as an Admin. It may give a user the Admin, Billing or Read
Only role. It may never give Owner or Partner, and it cannot change an
Owner. Any change to an Owner (name, email or role) is `403` with
`error.code` `owner_protected`. A role the key may not give is `422`, as
in the portal. Names and role change together or not at all.

You cannot change a login's email address through the API. Its own user
changes it in the portal. A request that sends `email` is refused with
`422`, or with `403 owner_protected` for an Owner.

This is for your staff users, not your clients' users.

firstName.description: The first name of the user to be modified.

lastName.description: The last name of the user to be modified.

id.description: The id of the user you changed.
