lastName.description: The user's last name before the change.

email.description: The user's email address before the change.

role.description: The user's role before the change.

newDetails.description: The details as they are now.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:delete

Deletes a user on your wholesale account.

**Important:** This deletes the user at once, with no confirmation. We may be unable to recover the user afterwards. We strongly recommend restricting access to this endpoint.

This is for your staff users, not your clients' users.

A key acts as an Admin, which may never remove an Owner. That request is
refused with `403` and `error.code` `owner_protected`. The portal's
other refusals are a `422` naming why. The removal is audited as the
portal's is, naming the API key.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The user's id. Get it from Get All Users.

204.description: The user is deleted. The response has no body.

get.summary: Check whether a premises' path has room for more services
get.description:
Asks whether the path that would serve your orders has room. Use it before you place many orders in one area. The path is the one an order at this premises would use. That is our NNI to the carrier at the premises' POI. For a Layer 2 handoff it also includes your own interconnect. The answer is `hasCapacity` only. We return no headroom, utilisation or contracted figure.

The check is advice. If it answers false, we still accept and build an order you place. A path over capacity is slower at busy times. We don't refuse the order.

parameters.name: locId
parameters.description: The premises the orders are for. Send an NBN Location ID (LOC…) or an Opticomm Property ID (OPC…).

parameters.name: services
parameters.description: How many more services you plan to order on this path.

parameters.name: downMbps
parameters.description: The download speed of each service, in Mbps. Send 100 for a 100/40 plan.

parameters.name: deliveryMode
parameters.description: `l3` is a service that ends on our network. `l2` is a Layer 2 handoff to your interconnect, and it checks that interconnect too.

hasCapacity.description: True when the path has room for the services you asked about. False when ordering them would take it past what it is sized for.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Lists the active Layer 2 link destinations available to your account.
These are the outer VLANs (S-Tags) on your customer interconnects, where
we can hand off a Layer 2 service to you.

Each destination's carrier comes from its Point of Interconnect. A
single-tag interconnect carries all your services on one outer VLAN
across every POI and carrier. It shows under the reserved POI code
`0NAT` and serves both NBN and Opticomm.

parameters.name: carrier
parameters.description: Only destinations serving this carrier. Single-tag (`0NAT`) destinations serve both carriers, so they always appear.

results.description: The active Layer 2 link destinations available to you.

get.description:
Lists your orders on every network, newest first. Each is a summary row
with enough to act on. Its `href` (GET /data/orders/{orderId}) returns the
whole order.

An open order is always listed, however long ago it last changed. A
parked or waiting order stays until it ends. Without `status` or
`updatedSince`, completed and failed orders are listed for the **last 30
days**. Send `status=completed`, `status=failed` or an `updatedSince` to
reach older ones. The list is paged like every list.

Narrow the list with `status` (`open` is every order not finished),
`type`, `network`, `locationId`, `orderReference`, `endUser`, `tag` and
`updatedSince`. A value outside its set or its form is `422`. It never
gives you a wider list instead. `q` searches the order id, PND, your
order reference and the location id.

Send `expand=service` to get each order's service in full in the same
call.

An order appears here once it is placed with the carrier, or once it is
waiting for your appointment or port. A waiting order is listed under
its PND.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only orders of these types. Send one or several, comma-separated. Case does not matter, so you can send the `type` an order shows (`Connect`) as it is. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only orders in these statuses. Send one or several, comma-separated. Case does not matter, so you can send the `status` an order shows (`InProgress`) as it is. `open` is every order not finished, the same as `inProgress`. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: network
parameters.description: Only orders on these networks. Send one or several, comma-separated. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Only orders for this premises. Send an NBN location id (`LOC` and 12 digits) or an Opticomm one (`OPC` and 12 digits), in any case. Any other form is `422`.

parameters.name: orderReference
parameters.description: Only the orders placed with this reference of yours. The whole reference must match. Case does not matter.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: `service` inlines each order's service in full. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

parameters.name: needsAttention
parameters.description: Only the orders in this needs-attention group, as `GET /account/summary` counts them. Add `endUser` (an end user's number) to narrow the group to that end user.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the orders for this end user, by its public number. A number that is not one of your end users is `422`, not an empty list. Used with `needsAttention`, it narrows the group to that end user.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Places a Connect order on any data network and technology. You need no
separate endpoint for each. The location picks the order. We place an
NBN Location ID as an NFAS (Fibre), NWAS (Fixed Wireless), NHAS (HFC) or
NCAS (FTTB, FTTN, FTTC) order, by its access technology. We place an
Opticomm Property ID as an Opticomm order. You can't order Satellite or
Enterprise Ethernet here.

Take the plan and the resource from the Service Qualification
(GET /data/sq/{locId}). The order takes what the portal's order page
takes. That is the end user it is for, its add-ons, the restoration SLA,
a static IPv4 address and IPv6, a new or additional install, and a
transfer. NTD delivery and the other options of each network are on the
network's own order endpoints under /nbn and /opticomm.

We check the order against the Service Qualification before we send it.
A mistake comes back as a 422 with the reason, and no order is placed. A
201 means we accepted the order. Follow it with GET
/data/orders/{orderId}.

An order can need something only you can give. We accept it and hold it
on our side, and send nothing to the carrier. It needs a technician
appointment (`order.appointmentRequired`). Or, where every port on the
NTD is in use, it needs a new NTD or a port to take over
(`order.ntdFull`). Its `actionRequired` says what it needs, and its ID is
a PND. Answer it with PATCH /data/orders/{orderId}. An order still
waiting after 7 days is cancelled.

Send `bundleId` to add the order to a bundle as a draft instead (see
`POST /bundles`). We check the order the same way. Nothing is sent until
you submit the bundle. The answer is the bundle item, with the bundle at
`Location`. A retry with the same `orderReference` returns that item
again.

200.description: An order with this `orderReference` was already placed, and this is that order. With `bundleId`, it is already in the bundle, and this is the item.

201.description: The order was placed with the carrier, or accepted to wait for your appointment or port (see `actionRequired`). With `bundleId`, it joined the bundle, and this is the item.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Lists your Delayed Orders. These are orders scheduled for a future
submission time, on either network. We hold them, so nothing is sent to
any carrier until a Delayed Order submits. An order the carrier asked us
to try again is not listed. It is in progress, and we resend it
ourselves.

The list is paged like every list. `q` searches the pending reference, your order
reference and the location id.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

queryDateTime.description: When this query was received, in UTC

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Places a Connect order and holds it until `submitTimestamp`. Nothing is
sent to the carrier until then. You can create only Opticomm orders
here today. Opticomm is the one network whose delayed lane is ours. For
nbn, the delayed orders are the carrier's own, at /nbn/orders/delayed.
Use the Opticomm Service Qualification API first to find the options you
can select.

The order takes the end user and the add-ons as `POST /data/orders`
does. If you leave out `addons`, the plan's default add-ons are
attached. A list attaches exactly that list. An empty list attaches
none. Add-ons start billing when the carrier accepts the order, once we
send it.

Before submission you can reschedule a Delayed Order, submit it
immediately, or cancel it at no cost.

submitTimestamp.description:
When to submit this order to the carrier. It must be at least 15 minutes and no more than 30 days in the future.
Send an ISO 8601 date-time with its UTC offset, for example `2026-12-01T09:00:00+11:00` or `2026-11-30T22:00:00Z`. A time without an offset is refused with a 422 naming the field.

parameters.name: delayedOrderRef
parameters.description: The Check Networks Delayed Order Reference #

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Returns the full detail of a Delayed Order. That is the Connect order
fields it was created with and its scheduled submission time.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:delete

Cancels a Delayed Order before it submits. We never sent it to the
carrier, so cancelling is free. You get a 409 if our scheduler has just
submitted the order, because it can no longer be cancelled.

204.description: The order is cancelled. The response has no body.

parameters.name: delayedOrderRef
parameters.description: The Check Networks Delayed Order Reference #

patch.summary: Change the Submission Time for a Delayed Order
patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Changes when a Delayed Order is submitted to its carrier. We keep
holding the order, and send nothing, until the new time.

submitTimestamp.description:
The new time to submit to the carrier. It must be at least 15 minutes and no more than 30 days in the future.
Send an ISO 8601 date-time with its UTC offset, for example `2026-12-01T09:00:00+11:00` or `2026-11-30T22:00:00Z`. A time without an offset is refused with a 422 naming the field.

parameters.name: delayedOrderRef
parameters.description: The Check Networks Delayed Order Reference #

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Submits a Delayed Order to its carrier now, instead of waiting for
its scheduled submission time.

result.description: The submission outcome. The order now has its carrier order id. It also appears with that carrier's orders, for Opticomm at /opticomm/productOrders.

id.description: The carrier order id assigned.

409.description: The order has already been submitted and can no longer be submitted manually.

get.description:
Returns one order, in the same shape on every network. Use the ID from
the order list.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The order ID, as returned by the order list.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: `service` inlines the order's service in full. Any other value is `422`.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Gives an order that is waiting for you what it needs. You see this on the
order as `actionRequired`, and in the `order.appointmentRequired` or
`order.ntdFull` webhook. We then place the order with the carrier, and it
keeps its ID.

- **Appointment required:** send `appointmentId`, an appointment you
  reserved from the order's timeslots.
- **NTD full:** send `appointmentId` for a technician to install another
  NTD, or `resourceId` for the port to take over. With `resourceId`, also
  send `serviceId` (the AVC on NBN) and `customerAuthorityDate`.

We check the order again as when it was placed. A mistake comes back as
a 422 with the reason, and the order keeps waiting.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The order ID (the PND in `order.appointmentRequired` or `order.ntdFull`).

200.description: The order was placed with the carrier.

get.description:
Returns the technician timeslots for an order waiting for an appointment.
We read them live from the order's network, for the appointment type the
order needs. The read starts at the order's `preferredAppointmentDate`,
or today. On Opticomm it looks two weeks ahead.

Reserve a slot on the network's appointment endpoint (/nbn/appointments
or /opticomm/appointments). Then attach it with PATCH
/data/orders/{orderId}. `timeslots` is that network's own timeslot
document, as its appointment search returns it.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The order ID (the PND in `order.appointmentRequired` or `order.ntdFull`).

demandType.description: The appointment type the order needs.

get.description:
Lists every provisioning request you have made, newest first, on any
network.

A request appears as soon as it is configured, before the carrier has
accepted it. Watch it here as it goes from Pending to Complete. When it
is done, pick up the tags or login you need to configure your own side.

`q` searches the provisioning request reference, the carrier order id and
your reference.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

total.description: Every provisioning request you have made, across all pages.

get.description:
Returns one provisioning request. Look it up by its own reference or by
the order id it belongs to.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The provisioning request reference (PRQ…) or the order id.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

The simplified provisioning step for an IPoE (DHCP) Layer 3 service.
Call it after you place the order. Send only the IP preferences. We
take everything else from the order.

**A service is not built until you ask.** Completing at the carrier does
not provision anything by itself. If you call no provisioning step for
an order, the service never goes live.

We accept this call until the service is built. After that, a change
needs a Modify Order.

orderNumber.description: The Order to provision (your PND reference or the carrier order number).

staticIp.description: Hold the service's IPv4 address stable. This also allows custom reverse DNS.

ipv6.description: Provision IPv6, which is a /64 on-link prefix and a delegated prefix. The delegated prefix size depends on the plan. It is /56 by default, or /48 where your plan or service is configured for it. Send false for an IPv4-only service.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

The simplified provisioning step for a Layer 2 pass-through service.
Call it after you place the order.

Billing does not start when we build the service. It starts once the
path to your interconnect is applied. It starts on the day the service
is first seen live, or 10 business days after the path is applied,
whichever comes first.

The optional `handoff` names one of your Layer 2 link destinations, as
listed by `GET /data/layer2/destinations`. If you leave it out, we hand
the service off on your default destination for the order's POI.

**A service is not built until you ask.** Completing at the carrier does
not provision anything by itself. If you call no provisioning step for
an order, the service never goes live.

We accept this call until the service is built. After that, a change
needs a Modify Order.

orderNumber.description: The Order to provision (your PND reference or the carrier order number).

handoff.description: The interconnect to hand this service off on, from GET /data/layer2/destinations. Leave it out to use your default destination for the order's POI. We choose the outer VLAN (S-Tag) on it from that POI.

cTag.description:
The inner VLAN (C-Tag) to use for this service, if you want
to pick it. It only has to be unused on the handoff it lands
on.

If you leave it out, we allocate the next free one and return
it to you.

Either way, we allocate the tags as soon as you ask, not when
the carrier finishes. You can configure your own side
immediately, and no other order can take the tag meanwhile.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

The simplified provisioning step for a PPPoE Layer 3 service. Call it
after you place the order. Send only the IP preferences. We take
everything else from the order.

PPPoE logins live in your account's realm, so they can't collide with
another provider's. The username is always `<name>@<your realm>`. We set
up your realm, and you can't provision PPPoE until it is in place.

Choose a login by sending `username` and `password`. Or leave both out,
and we create one with the service. It uses the carrier's service ID as
the name and a generated password. Either way, the username appears on
the Radius User Status endpoint. The password is on the dedicated RADIUS
Password endpoint.

You can set a chosen login only once the carrier has accepted the order
and the service exists, because the login belongs to the service.

**A service is not built until you ask.** Completing at the carrier does
not provision anything by itself. If you call no provisioning step for
an order, the service never goes live.

We accept this call until the service is built. After that, a change
needs a Modify Order.

orderNumber.description: The Order to provision (your PND reference or the carrier order number).

staticIp.description: Hold the service's IPv4 address stable. This also allows custom reverse DNS.

ipv6.description: Provision IPv6, which is a /64 on-link prefix and a delegated prefix. The delegated prefix size depends on the plan. It is /56 by default, or /48 where your plan or service is configured for it. Send false for an IPv4-only service.

username.description:
The name part of the PPPoE login. We append your realm, so
don't include "@".

Use letters, numbers, full stops, underscores and hyphens. It
must not already be in use.

password.description: The PPPoE password. We generate one if you don't send it. Use 8 to 64 printable ASCII characters, with no single quote (') or backslash (\). The same rule applies to a later change with PATCH /data/radius/{ref}/password.

get.description:
Lists every data service you hold, on NBN and Opticomm, in one shape. The
most recently requested comes first, as the portal's Services list opens.
Narrow the list with `network`, `status`, `endUser`, `technology`,
`customerReference`, `plan`, `locationId` or `tag`. They work as the
portal's filters of the same names do. A value outside its set or its
form is `422`. It never gives you a wider list instead. `q` searches what
the portal's search does. That is the product and service references,
the RADIUS username, the carrier order, the address, your customer
reference, and the end user's reference and name.

Send `expand=endUser` to get each service's end user in full, as
`endUserDetail`, in the same call.

A connect still in flight is an order (GET /data/orders), not a service.
It appears here once it is live.

A service with no request date comes after every service that has one.
An example is a service taken over from another provider. This holds in
the default order and in any `sort`. So does any service with no value
in the field a `sort` names, such as `activatedAt` before it is live.

parameters.name: network
parameters.description: Only services on these networks. Send one or several, comma-separated. Case does not matter. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only services in these statuses. Send one or several, comma-separated. Case does not matter, so you can send the `status` a service shows (`Live`) as it is. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: `endUser` adds each service's end user in full, as `endUserDetail`. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

parameters.name: technology
parameters.description: Only services on these access technologies. Send one or several, comma-separated, as the `technology` a service shows. Case does not matter. Any other value is `422`. A technology none of your services has gives an empty list.

parameters.name: customerReference
parameters.description: Only the services with this customer reference. The whole reference must match. Case does not matter.

parameters.name: plan
parameters.description: Only the services on this plan, by its SKU (the `plan.sku` a service shows). Case does not matter.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Only the services at this premises. Send an NBN location id (`LOC` and 12 digits) or an Opticomm one (`OPC` and 12 digits). Any other form is `422`.

parameters.name: needsAttention
parameters.description: Only the services in this needs-attention group, as `GET /account/summary` counts them. Add `endUser` (an end user's number) to narrow the group to that end user.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description:
Only the services of this end user, by its public number (the
`endUser` each service returns). A number that is not one
of your end users is a 422, not an empty list. Used with
`needsAttention`, it narrows the group to that end user.

total.description: Every service that matches, across all pages.

get.description:
Returns one of your data services, with its speed and whether it is
connected right now.

Address it by its product reference (`id`, an NBN PRI or an Opticomm
product) or its service reference (`serviceId`, such as an AVC).

We read the live status from our RADIUS. Some networks can only tell us by running
a test. Then `session.status` is `OnRequest`. Ask
GET /data/radius/{ref}/online with the service's `radiusUser`.

`contract` is the term end and what disconnecting today would charge. It
is null when there is no term.

If a carrier reference was reused, the live service answers first. A
suspended one comes next, then the newest.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: `endUser` adds the service's end user in full, as `endUserDetail`. Any other value is `422`.

patch.description:
Sets your own `externalRef` and `metadata` on the service. You can then
find it by your customer or job id without keeping a map of ours. Send
either or both. We keep one you leave out, and null clears it.
Everything else on a data service is the carrier's, and changes through
an order.

An `externalRef` that another of your data services holds is `422`. Find
the service again with `GET /data/services?externalRef=`.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

200.description: The service as it now is.

get.description:
Returns one month of a service's data usage, in total and by day. These
are the figures your portal's usage card shows. We report usage and
never charge for it.

`period` is a month, `YYYY-MM`, in the last 13 months. It defaults to
the current month, counted up to now (`complete` is false).

Months and days follow your bill's calendar, not UTC. That is your
account's time zone, the zone your invoices are cut in. You set it in
the Wholesale Portal's Company Settings, and it is Brisbane until you
set another. A sample at 2 am on the 1st there counts in the new month
and on that day. Send `CN-Time-Zone` to have the months and days on your
own zone instead. `from` and `to` carry the zone's offset.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: The month, `YYYY-MM`. Defaults to the current month.

get.summary: List a Service's Outages, Planned Work and Degradations
get.description:
Tells you whether anything is wrong at this service right now. It
returns three lists in one answer, as your portal's service page shows
them, on either network.

- `outages`: the entries on our outage register that cover the service's
  address, in the shape `GET /outages` gives. Each carries what you need
  to report it. That is `cause`, `premisesAffected`, `serviceCounts` and
  `updates`. `serviceCounts` is the count of services hit by each
  affected type, and is null for a type we have no count of. `updates`
  is each update we posted on it, with its time, newest last.
- `plannedWork`: the maintenance windows you were sent notice of whose
  area takes in the service's address. A window that names no area
  covers every service it was noticed for.
- `degradations`: the Potential Service Degradations at the service's
  point of interconnect. The service is slower at peak, not down.

You get open ones only by default. `include=resolved` adds those
resolved in the last 30 days. A service with nothing on it answers three
empty lists. Every time is UTC.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: `resolved` adds what was resolved in the last 30 days. Any other value is `422`.

updates.description: Each update we posted on the outage, with its time, oldest first, so the newest is last. The list starts with the update that was current when we published the outage, and includes every one since. The newest is the outage's `additionalInfo`.

text.example: A technician is on site replacing the faulty card.

serviceCounts.description: The count of services the outage hit, by each of its `affectedServiceTypes`. It is null for a type we have no count of.

post.summary: Run a Line Test on a Service
post.description:
Runs one of the tests that `GET /data/services/{ref}/diagnostics/types`
lists for the service, on either network. Send that test's `inputs`. An
input you leave out takes its `default`. An input the test does not take
is `422`, and so is a missing required one. The service must be live.

It answers `202` with the test's id. The result comes from the carrier
later, and you read it on `GET /data/diagnostics/{id}`. While the same
test is still running on the service, a second one is `409`, and
`error.runningTestId` names the one running. We ask nothing of the
carrier. When the carrier's test system is down, you get `503` with
`Retry-After`.

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

202.description: The test was asked for.

409.description: The same test is already running on the service.

runningTestId.description: The id of the test still running.

get.description:
Lists the service's line tests on either network, newest first and
paged. Session History is not listed here. Use
`GET /data/services/{ref}/sessions` for it.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only tests in these statuses, comma-separated. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only these tests, by code, comma-separated, in any case. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: result
parameters.description: Only tests with these results, comma-separated. Any other value is `422`.

get.summary: List the Line Tests a Service Allows
get.description:
Lists the line tests the carrier allows for this service now, on either
network, as your portal's Run Test offers them. Each test says when to
use it (`description`). It says when to raise a fault ticket rather than
test again (`escalateIf`). It also lists the inputs it takes. We read the
carrier live when you ask.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

escalateIf.description: When to raise a fault ticket instead of running the test again.

name.description: The key to send it under in `inputs`.

default.description: Used when you leave the input out.

options.description: For an `enum` input, the values it takes.

get.description:
Returns one of your line tests, on either network. It shows the inputs
the test was run with and the carrier's reason if it rejected or
cancelled the test. Once the carrier has detailed results, it shows
those too.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The test's id.

reason.description: Why the carrier rejected or cancelled it.

details.description: The carrier's detailed results, once it has them. Their fields depend on the test.

get.description:
Prices what disconnecting the service would charge if it ceased on
`ceaseOn`. It uses the same early termination quotes the cease bills, so
you can tell your customer before you place the disconnect. There is one
line per open subscription, which is the plan and each add-on. A line
past its term charges nothing.

`ceaseOn` is a Sydney calendar day from today to 90 days ahead. That is
the window a disconnect accepts. It defaults to today. Reading the quote
books nothing and changes nothing.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

parameters.name: ceaseOn
parameters.description: The day the service would cease, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Any other value, or a day outside the window, is `422`.

id.description: The service's product reference.

chargeExGst.description: The whole early termination charge, in dollars ex GST.

chargeWaived.description: True when we waived the early termination charge, so the charge is `0.00` though the service is still in its term.

chargeable.description: Whether ceasing on `ceaseOn` charges anything for this line.

chargeWaived.description: True when we waived this line's charge, so it is `0.00` though still in term.

get.description:
Lists the service's connection sessions, newest first, as the portal's
service page shows them. Each shows when it started and ended, how long
it ran, its address, the bytes each way, the router's MAC and why it
ended. Use it when your customer says the internet keeps dropping.

- A service on our own network: our RADIUS accounting (`source`
  `checknetworks`).
- An Opticomm Layer 3 service: the sessions in the last Session History
  test Opticomm answered (`source` `opticomm`). `retrievedAt` says when.
  Reading never starts a test at Opticomm. POST
  /data/services/{ref}/sessions/refresh asks for a new one.
- A service whose sessions another carrier holds has no history here.
  That is `422`. Its current
  session is on GET /data/radius/{ref}/session.

`from` and `to` keep the sessions that ran in that window. That is
sessions started by `to` that are still open or ended at or after
`from`. One request covers at most 90 days. `to` defaults to now, and
`from` defaults to 90 days before `to`. A longer window is `422` naming
`from`. To read an older or longer period, go 90 days at a time.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: An ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone is the start of that day (UTC). It is at most 90 days before `to`, and defaults to 90 days before `to`. A value that is not ISO 8601, or is further back, is `422`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: An ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone includes that day. It defaults to now. A value before `from` is `422`.

retrievedAt.description: For `opticomm`, when Opticomm answered the test these sessions are from. It is null when none has been answered yet. It is null for `checknetworks`, which is current.

endedAt.description: Null while the session is open.

mac.description: The router's MAC address, as the network reported it.

terminateCause.description: Why the session ended, as RADIUS reports it (`Lost-Carrier`, `User-Request`…). Null while open.

post.description:
Asks Opticomm for the service's sessions now, by starting a Session
History test there. It works for an Opticomm Layer 3 service only. Our
own network's sessions are always current. This is a request to the
carrier, so it needs `data:update`.

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

`202` says we asked for the test. Once Opticomm answers, the sessions
are on GET /data/services/{ref}/sessions. That is usually within a
minute or two, and the `data.radius.sessionRetrieved` webhook says when.
`409` says a test is already on its way. `error.testId` names it, and
its answer will be on the read.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

202.description: The test is asked for.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before reading the sessions.

id.description: The service's product reference.

409.description: A Session History test is already on its way.

testId.description: The running test's reference. Absent when it was started elsewhere and is not yet known here.

post.description:
Asks the carrier for a new health report on the service, as the portal's
service page does. The call is the same for an NBN and an Opticomm
service. This is a request to the carrier, so it needs `data:update`.

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

`202` says we asked for the report, and gives its `id`. Once the carrier
answers, the report is on GET /data/health/{id}, and the
`serviceHealth.reportReady` webhook says when. `409` says a report is
already on its way, and `error.reportId` names it. A report still not
answered after an hour no longer blocks a new one.

The carrier's own calls still work, with the carrier's bodies. They are
POST /nbn/service_health/service/{serviceRef} and
POST /opticomm/serviceHealth.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC, OAC).

202.description: The report is asked for.

id.description: The report's id.

serviceId.description: The service's product reference.

409.description: A health report is already on its way.

reportId.description: The id of the report on its way. Absent when it was asked for elsewhere and is not yet known here.

get.description:
Lists the service's health reports, newest first, pending ones included.
The shape is the same on every network. `overall` is the result the
portal's service page shows.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC, OAC).

get.summary: Get a Service's Latest Health Report
get.description:
Returns the service's newest health report, pending or complete, in the
same shape on every network. It is `404` when no report has been asked
for.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC, OAC).

get.description:
One health report on one of your data services, by the `id` that
POST /data/services/{ref}/health answered or the
`serviceHealth.reportReady` webhook named.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The report's id.

put.description:
Sets your own tags on the service. Use them to map it to your sites, cost
centres or customers. The list you send replaces the whole list, and
`[]` clears it. Filter the services and orders lists by tag with `tag`.

We trim each tag. A tag is at most 255 characters, and case does not
matter when we match it. `Brisbane Office` and `brisbane office` are one
tag, kept as first written. A service carries at most 20. Anything else
is `422`.

Tags you send with POST /data/orders carry over to the service the order
builds.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

id.description: The service's product reference.

tags.description: The tags the service now carries.

get.description:
Lists every tag on your data services and orders, each once. Case does
not matter when we match, and we show the spelling first written. Each
tag comes with how many services and orders carry it, by name. Use a
name with `tag` on GET /data/services or GET /data/orders.

services.description: How many of your services carry it.

orders.description: How many of your orders carry it.

get.description:
Lists your active RADIUS users, one row each with its realm, by username.
The list is paged like every list. `realm` narrows the list to one
realm. `q` searches the username and the user reference.

Some services authenticate on their access circuit instead of a login.
These have no realm, so their `realm` is `null`.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Only users in this realm, such as `example.net.au`. Case does not matter. A value that is not a realm name is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

realm.description: Everything after the `@` in the username; null for a user with no realm.

post.description:
Requests a PPPoE realm for your account. Use a domain you control.

Every PPPoE username sits in your realm. A realm is globally unique, and
it is effectively permanent once services are built on it. We review each
request instead of granting it at once. You can't provision PPPoE
services until your realm is in place.

realm.description: The realm you would like, as a domain name.

202.description:
Requested, not granted. This is `202` rather than `201` because the realm stays `Pending` until we confirm it. PPPoE ordering stays closed until then.

The `Location` header names where to poll. *Retrieve a Realm* reports the request as `Pending`, `Approved` or `Rejected` (with the reason), and `Active` once the realm is on your account. If you subscribe to the `data.realm.approved` and `data.realm.rejected` webhooks, they carry the decision, so polling is optional.

Location.description: Where to poll for the decision.

get.description:
Returns your realm and how many active users sit in it. For a realm you
have requested, it shows where that request stands.

The `Location` header of *Request a Realm* points here. Poll it until
`status` leaves `Pending`. `Active` means the realm is yours and you can
order PPPoE. `Rejected` carries the reason. A realm that is neither yours
nor requested by you is a `404`.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: The realm.

status.description: `Active` once the realm is on your account. A request you have made is `Pending` until we decide it. It is then `Approved` (and `Active` from the next read) or `Rejected`.

reason.description: Why a request was rejected; null otherwise.

users.description: Active RADIUS users in this realm (0 for a request).

get.description:
Returns one RADIUS user.

Address it by its own reference. Or use any reference you already hold
for the service, which is the order id, the product reference or the
service id. There is one user per service, so all of them give the same
record.

The record carries the RADIUS detail. That is whether the address is
static, the CGNAT public address and ports, IPv6, the last
authentication and recent dropouts. For some services we read it live on
each request. If it cannot be read, `detailAvailable` is false and the
detail fields are null.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A RADIUS user (USR…), order, product or service reference.

get.summary: Check Whether a User Is Online
get.description:
Says whether the user has a session up right now. A session that has
stopped reporting accounting counts as gone.

For some services we read the answer live on each request. If it cannot
be read, the request fails with a 502 rather than guess.

For a service on Opticomm's RADIUS, the answer comes from the latest
session check at Opticomm. `retrievedAt` says when Opticomm reported it.
Reading never asks Opticomm. To ask for a check, call
`POST /data/radius/{ref}/session-check`. While a check is on its way,
this answers `202`. Call again after `Retry-After`, or subscribe to
`data.radius.sessionRetrieved`. With no check held, it answers
`status: NotChecked`, which is neither online nor offline.

A service handed to you at layer 2 on your interconnect never logs on to
our RADIUS. It answers `status: NotOnOurRadius`, which is neither online
nor offline.

Limit: 2 a second and 30 a minute for the account, shared with
`DELETE /data/radius/{ref}/session`.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A RADIUS user (USR…), order, product or service reference.

source.description: Where the answer came from: our own RADIUS sessions, or Opticomm's session history.

retrievedAt.description: For an `opticomm` answer only: when Opticomm reported it.

get.description:
Returns the password this user authenticates with.

A password is a secret, so this call needs the `data:credentials` scope.
A `data:read` key gets `403`. Only a live service answers. A cancelled or
suspended one is `404`.

We record every read against the service. A service that authenticates
on its access circuit has no password to return.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A RADIUS user (USR…), order, product or service reference.

patch.description:
Sets a new password for this user.

We accept a change only where it takes effect. That is a live PPPoE
service that logs on to our own RADIUS, while PPPoE is offered.
Anything else is `422`, and nothing is changed. These are the cases:

- We have switched PPPoE off, so it is not offered.
- The service is not live (suspended or cancelled).
- The service logs on at the carrier, which holds its password.
- The service does not log on with a password at all (IPoE).

A reference that is not one of your services is `404`, whatever the
body holds.

The password is 8 to 64 printable ASCII characters (letters, digits,
spaces and symbols), with no `'` or `\`. The same rule applies to a
password chosen at provisioning.

The service keeps its current session. It re-authenticates with the new
password the next time it connects, so you must reconfigure the CPE to
match. We record changes against the service, as we do reads.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A RADIUS user (USR…), order, product or service reference.

password.description: The new password: 8 to 64 printable ASCII characters, with no single quote (') or backslash (\).

get.description:
Returns the user's current session. It shows when the session came up,
how long it has been up, the address it holds and the traffic it has
passed.

`result` is null where nothing is connected.

For some services we read the session live on each request. If it cannot
be read, the request fails with a 502. So a null `result` always means
nothing is connected.

For a service on Opticomm's RADIUS, the session comes from the latest
session check at Opticomm. Its `lastSeenAt` is when Opticomm reported
it. Reading never asks Opticomm. To ask for a check, call
`POST /data/radius/{ref}/session-check`. While a check is on its way,
this answers `202`. Call again after `Retry-After`, or subscribe to
`data.radius.sessionRetrieved`. With no check held, it answers
`status: NotChecked`, never a null that would read as not connected.

A service handed to you at layer 2 on your interconnect never logs on to
our RADIUS. It answers `status: NotOnOurRadius`, never a null.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A RADIUS user (USR…), order, product or service reference.

delete.description:
Drops the user's live session. The service then connects again on its
own and picks up a new password or plan. It works for a live service on
our own network. A service on a carrier's RADIUS keeps its session
there. A suspended account can't reset a session.

Limit: 2 a second and 30 a minute for the account, shared with GET
/data/radius/{ref}/online. Past it, the answer is `429` with
`Retry-After`.

`202` says we dropped the session. `409` with `no_live_session` says
nothing is connected. `422` with `session_not_resettable` says the
session is on a network where it can't be reset. That is the legacy NAS,
a carrier's RADIUS, or a service handed to you at layer 2, which has no
session here. A plain `422` says the service is not live.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A RADIUS user (USR…), order, product or service reference.

202.description: The session was dropped.

post.summary: Check a User's Session at Opticomm
post.description:
Asks Opticomm for the user's session now, by starting a Session History
test there. It works only for a live service on Opticomm's RADIUS. For
other services, GET /data/radius/{ref}/online and /session are read
live. This is a request to the carrier, so it needs `data:update`, and a
suspended account can't make it.

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

`202` says the check is on its way. If a check is already on its way, we
reuse it and don't ask twice. Once Opticomm gives the answer, it is on
GET /data/radius/{ref}/online and /session. That is usually within a
minute or two, and the `data.radius.sessionRetrieved` webhook says when.
If Opticomm refused the last check under five minutes ago, or does not
answer, this fails with a 502.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A RADIUS user (USR…), order, product or service reference.

get.summary: List Every Service's Usage for a Month
get.description:
Returns one month of data usage for every data service on your account,
one row per service, paged. It gives you what you need to bill or warn
your end users in one call, not one call per service. Each row's totals
are the ones `GET /data/services/{ref}/usage` gives for the same month.
We report usage and never charge for it.

`period` is a month, `YYYY-MM`, in the last 13 months. It defaults to
the current month, counted up to now (`complete` is false). Months
follow your bill's calendar, as on the per-service read. A service
disconnected before the month began has no row.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: The month, `YYYY-MM`. Defaults to the current month.

parameters.name: network
parameters.description: Only services on these networks. Send one or several, comma-separated. Case does not matter. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the services of this end user, by its public number. A number that is not one of your end users is a 422, not an empty list.

total.description: Every service that matches, across all pages.

to.description: The month's end, or now for the current month.

parameters.name: locId
parameters.description: The premises to qualify. Send an NBN Location ID (LOC…) or an Opticomm Property ID (OPC…). Use the address search endpoints to find these.

get.summary: Qualify a premises on whichever network serves it
get.description:
Returns one carrier-neutral qualification document. An NBN Location ID runs the NBN single-site qualification plus an Enterprise Ethernet check. An Opticomm Property ID runs the Opticomm qualification. Where the premises also has an NBN footprint, it runs the Enterprise Ethernet check against that footprint too. The carrier-shape endpoints under /nbn/service_qualification and /opticomm/service_qualification stay available for the fuller per-carrier documents.

The Service Transfer parameters apply to NBN locations only. Sending either with an Opticomm Property ID is rejected with a 422 naming the field.

parameters.name: serviceRef
parameters.description: NBN only. The existing Service ID for a Service Transfer, which is the entire AVC # or its last 5 digits. It needs `customerAuthorityDate`. The matching resource shows in `serviceIdMatch` on the `resources` entries. Validation issues show in `siteRestrictionError`.

parameters.name: customerAuthorityDate
parameters.description: The date Customer Authority was obtained for the premises, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. We read a date-time as its date. It must be less than 45 days old. It is mandatory with `serviceRef`.

parameters.name: potsInterconnect
parameters.description: NBN only. An existing Full National Number (FNN) or ULL ID to check against.

parameters.name: latitude
parameters.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the address.

parameters.name: longitude
parameters.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the address.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most locations to return. Leave it empty to get all available results.

schema.description: Locations matching the supplied coordinates.

get.summary: Request nbn™ Location IDs (LOC #) for a Latitude and Longitude
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Finds the addresses at a latitude and longitude. The answer is a bare array
of addresses, without a `results` wrapper, in nbn's own shape.

parameters.name: secondaryComplexName
parameters.description:
Name associated with a building or area within a complex site.
This data element may represent the name given to an entire building within an address site that has its own separate address.

parameters.name: unitTypeCode
parameters.description:
Sub dwelling unit type code.
Within a complex, an abbreviation used to distinguish the type of an address found within a building / sub-complex or marina.

parameters.name: unitNumber
parameters.description:
Sub-dwelling unit number.
Within a complex, a number used to distinguish an address found within a building / sub-complex or marina.
The data element may include a leading alphabetic prefix. The data element may include a trailing alphabetic suffix.

parameters.name: levelNumber
parameters.description:
Within a complex, the number of the floor or level of a multi-storey building/ sub-complex.
The data element may include a leading alphabetic prefix. The data element may include a trailing alphabetic suffix.

parameters.name: complexRoadNumber1
parameters.description: Within a complex, identifies the number of the address in the road or thoroughfare and for a ranged address is the start number.

parameters.name: complexRoadNumber2
parameters.description: Within a complex, identifies the last number for a ranged address in the road or thoroughfare.

parameters.name: complexRoadName
parameters.description:
Within a complex, the name of the road /thoroughfare of the address. Within a Road name it is possible to find what appears to be a Road type (eg. The Boulevard).
It is also possible to have a null Road type.

parameters.name: complexRoadTypeCode
parameters.description: Within a complex, an abbreviation used to distinguish the type of road / thoroughfare of the address.

parameters.name: complexRoadSuffixCode
parameters.description: Within a complex, an abbreviation representing the suffix of the road/ thoroughfare of the address.

parameters.name: addressSiteName
parameters.description:
Synonyms: Building property name, Primary Complex name

The official place name or culturally accepted common usage name for an address site, including the name of a building, homestead, building complex, agricultural property, park or unbounded address site. This data element represents the name given to an entire building or address site

parameters.name: lotNumber
parameters.description:
The Lot number is a reference number allocated to a property for subdivision administration purposes prior to road numbering.

Usage: Where an official Road number has not been assigned, this field may be used for postal purposes as well as the physical identification of an address site.

parameters.name: planNumber
parameters.description: The deposited plan number allocated to a property for subdivision administration purposes prior to road numbering in addition to the Lot number.

parameters.name: roadNumber1
parameters.description:
Identifies the number of the address in the road or thoroughfare and for a ranged address is the start number.
The data element may include an alphabetic prefix. The data element may include an alphabetic suffix.

parameters.name: roadNumber2
parameters.description:
Identifies the last number for a ranged address in the road or thoroughfare.
The data element may include an alphabetic prefix. The data element may include an alphabetic suffix.
This data element is used for ranged street numbers otherwise it is left blank.

parameters.name: roadName
parameters.description:
The name of the road/thoroughfare applicable to the address site or complex.
Only the road name should be stored in this data element.

parameters.name: roadTypeCode
parameters.description: The abbreviation code used to distinguish the type of road/thoroughfare applicable to the address site/complex.

parameters.name: roadSuffixCode
parameters.description: The abbreviation code used to represent the suffix of road/thoroughfare applicable to the address site/complex.

parameters.name: localityName
parameters.description: The name of the locality/suburb of the address.

parameters.name: postcode
parameters.description:
The Australian numeric descriptor for a postal delivery area, aligned with locality, suburb or place

*Mandatory if stateTerritoryCode not provided

parameters.name: stateTerritoryCode
parameters.description:
The State or Territory code of the address.

*Mandatory if postcode not provided

parameters.name: gnaf
parameters.description: Geocoded National Address File (GNAF) ID

parameters.name: latitude
parameters.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the address.

parameters.name: longitude
parameters.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the address.

parameters.name: fullText
parameters.description: A whole address as one string. We try to parse it.

parameters.name: adjustFullText
parameters.description:
[beta] (Optional) Has us adjust the `fullText` value before we query nbn™, to get better search results.
The adjustments change over time. They may include:
 - Removing the Country
 - Inserting the missing State when PostCode is included
 - Reordering State and Postcode. e.g., "2000 NSW" >> "NSW 2000"
 - Changing Road Types to their codes. e.g. "Street" >> "ST"
 - Adding sub-premise prefix. e.g. "2 12 Some St" >> "UNIT 2 12 Some St"
 - Stripping excess spaces. e.g. "12 - 24 Some St" >> "12-24 Some St"

parameters.name: requeryFullText
parameters.description:
[beta] (Optional) Asks us to query nbn™ a second time when an address search finds nothing. We do this only when the first query returns no results.
For a full text query, we try to split the `fullText` value into its parts and run an Advanced Search.
For an advanced query, we try to build a full text string from the address components and run a full text search.

parameters.name: rankResults
parameters.description:
[beta] (Optional) Adds a rank to each result.
The rank is a number between 0 and 100. It shows how well the result matches your search. A higher rank is a better match.

parameters.name: fuzzy
parameters.description: Turns on fuzzy searching, for more results that are less accurate.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most results to return, from 1 to 500. We bring a value outside that range into it. It defaults to 50.

schema.description: Locations matching the search criteria.

rank.description: How well this result matches your search, as a number between 0 and 100. A higher rank is a better match. It is present only when the `rankResults` parameter is true.

get.summary: Request the nbn™ Location ID (LOC #) for an address
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Finds the nbn Location ID (LOC #) for an address. It also returns the
official address details. The answer is a bare array of addresses, without
a `results` wrapper, in nbn's own shape.

Send at least one of these:

- A `gnaf` ID.
- A `fullText` address string.
- `latitude` and `longitude` coordinates.
- Physical address fields, with `postcode` or `stateTerritoryCode`.

A parameter combination we do not support returns `400 Bad Request` with
the reason.

get.summary: Get the address details for a nbn™ Location ID (LOC #)
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Returns the address body in nbn's own shape, without a `result` wrapper.

To try calls without reaching the carrier, use the
[sandbox](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/start/sandbox/) with one of
your account's [test addresses](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/start/sandbox/#addresses).

get.summary: List the known services that you have active at this location
get.description:

Lists your account's own NBN services provisioned at this location, keyed
by the NBN LOC id. Services at this location managed by other providers are
not listed. A location where you hold no service returns an empty list.

get.summary: Retrieve the details of an Appointment from nbn

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Asks nbn™ to run a diagnostic test against an Access Virtual Circuit
(AVC). Get the results from the /diagnostics/{testRef} endpoint. You do
not need to poll. A webhook subscribed to `diagnostic.completed` gets the
result when the test finishes.

Every request here reaches nbn™. Some tests drop the end user's service
while they run, such as a Port Reset or an NTD Reset. To try this call
without reaching the carrier, use the
[sandbox](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/start/sandbox/).

Access Virtual Circuit (AVC) ID Reference.
For Example: "AVC000000000000"

test.description: The test to run against this AVC service.

trafficClass.description:
For the "Network Performance Test" only. That test requires it.
The traffic class to run the test on:
  - "TC-1" - Traffic Class #1
  - "TC-2" - Traffic Class #2

resyncType.description:
For the "Line Quality Diagnostic" test only. That test requires it.
  - "No Resync" - the test runs without resynchronisation.
  - "Normal" - the test runs with resynchronisation in Normal Initialisation mode, and collects the HLOG and QLN.
  - "Robust" - the test runs with resynchronisation in Robust Initialisation mode. It collects the HLOG and QLN, and gives a longer initialisation time with less strict parameters.

monitoringDuration.description:
(Optional) For the "Line Quality Diagnostic" test only.
The monitoring duration in minutes. If you leave it out, the test runs for the default 6 minutes.

packetSize.description:
(Optional) For the "Loopback" test only.
The packet size for the loopback test. If you leave it out, the test runs with a preset default packet size.
The minimum is 64 and the maximum is 1500.

forceTest.description:
For the "Metallic Line Test" only. It is required if the AVC is on a NFAS (Fibre) line. Do not send it if the AVC is on a NCAS (FTTB, FTTC, FTTN) line.
Whether to force a test if there is a call in progress on the target line:
  - "true" - the test runs even if there is a call in progress, and the call is dropped.
  - "false" - the test does not go ahead if there is a call in progress.

technology.description:
For the "Metallic Line Test" only.
The test parameters differ by line technology. If we know the AVC, we detect the technology. If we do not, you must send the line technology here, or we reject the test request.

forceMeasurement.description:
For the "Single End Line Test" only. That test requires it.
Forces the testing platform to give detailed measurements on the associated Copper Loop.

patch.summary: Add an Appointment to an in-flight Product Order
patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Attaches one of your reserved appointments to one of your orders already
placed with the carrier, and answers the order. To book an appointment on
a new order, name it on the Connect instead. The carrier cannot simulate
this call, so it answers 503 while our carrier testing mode is on. This
call needs an `Idempotency-Key` header.

orderId.description:
The nbn Order ID to attach the appointment to.
For Example: "ORD000000000000"

appointmentId.description:
The nbn Appointment ID to attach to this order.
For Example: "APT000000000000"

get.description:
Lists your Delayed Orders — orders scheduled for a future submission
time. Nothing is sent to the carrier until a Delayed Order submits.
An order the carrier asked us to try again is not listed: it is in
progress, and we resend it ourselves.

post.description:
Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Places an nbn Connect order and holds it until `submitTimestamp`. Nothing
is sent to the carrier until then.

The order fields are those of the Product Order for the location's access
technology (NFAS, NHAS, NCAS or NWAS). Send an NTD (`ntdId`) for fibre,
HFC and fixed wireless. Send a copper pair (`copperPairId`) for copper.
Add the options that technology takes. Find the selectable SKUs first with
the Product Qualification APIs. A Delayed Order takes no transfer, so we
do not read the transfer fields.

**An order a technician attends is placed now, not held.** An order that
needs an install appointment is scheduled by that appointment. That means
a new NTD, or a copper pair a technician attends. Reserve a slot on the
day you want with `POST /nbn/appointments/reserve`. Then send its
`appointmentId`. We check it as the Product Order checks it.

We then place the order with nbn at once, with that appointment, so the
slot is locked in. You do not need `submitTimestamp`, and we do not read it.
The 201 answers `status` `Submitted` with the carrier's `orderId` and the
`appointmentId`. The order is not held, and it is not listed among your
Delayed Orders. You can schedule it as far ahead as nbn offers
appointments.

To change its day, move the appointment with
`PATCH /nbn/appointments/appointment/{appointmentId}/reschedule`. The
reschedule route here answers 409 `placed_with_appointment`.

To cancel it, send `DELETE /nbn/orders/delayed/{delayedOrderRef}`. It
answers 202. nbn takes no withdraw call from us, so our team withdraws
the order with nbn and lets you know.

Without an `appointmentId`, such an order is refused with a 422. The
violation is `appointment_required` on `appointmentId`, and its message
says to reserve an appointment and send it.

**A Fibre Uplift** is scheduled the same way. Send these:

- `fibreUplift` `true`.
- An uplift plan: a `bandwidthProductSku` ending `-UPL`.
- The `appointmentId` of a slot reserved with `alternativeTechnology`
  `Fibre`.

Do not send `ntdId`, `unidPortId` or `copperPairId`. nbn installs a new
NTD. We place it as an NFAS order at once, where the location's
qualification says `upliftAvailable` and nbn's own uplift qualification,
read again then, still offers it. Otherwise it is a 422. Any other plan on
an uplift, or an uplift plan on any other order, is a 422 too. A 12-month
term applies.

The order records the location's own access technology. We read it from
the location's qualification when the order is held, as a Connect does. A
location with no technology that can be ordered is a 422. A qualification
that cannot be read is a 502.

We build and check the order for that technology as its Product Order is
checked, when it is held. HFC uses port 1. Copper takes the pair and its
options. We refuse an order the Product Order would refuse with the same
422 and its `violations`. That includes an NTD or pair the location does
not have, an installation workforce or delivery details the location's
Service Class does not allow, and a phone service on a pair that has none.

Whether a UNI-D port is free, and whether the location still offers the
bandwidth and SLA, are checked when we send the order, as they can change
before then.

The order takes the end user and the add-ons as `POST /data/orders` does.
If you leave `addons` out, we attach the plan's default add-ons. A list
attaches exactly that list. An empty list attaches none. Add-ons start
billing when the carrier accepts the order, once it is sent.

You can reschedule a Delayed Order, submit it immediately, or cancel it at
no cost, any time before submission.

A location that already has an open order on your account is refused with
a 409. An open order is draft, delayed, submitted or in progress. A hold
never makes a second order for the same premises. We run the check again
at the submit time. A clash then holds the order for you (see
`order.delayed`).

fibreUplift.description: (Optional) Makes the order a Fibre Uplift. That is an NFAS order onto a new NTD at a location whose qualification says `upliftAvailable`. We place it now with its `appointmentId`.

submitTimestamp.description:
When to submit this order to nbn. It must be at least 15 minutes and no more than 30 days into the future.
Send an ISO 8601 date-time with its UTC offset, for example `2026-12-01T09:00:00+11:00` or `2026-11-30T22:00:00Z`. A time without an offset is refused with a 422 naming the field.
It is required unless you send `appointmentId`. When you do, we do not read it.

Submits an order to disconnect one of your active services.

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

We accept the order at once and process it in the background. The service
is not disconnected when this call returns. The response has the order
number and its current status.

A service still in its contract term is charged early termination. To see
the charge before you disconnect, call
GET /data/services/{ref}/disconnect-quote.

get.summary: Retrieve an order using its Order ID
get.description:
Returns the current detail of one of your orders by its Order ID.

Once an order has completed, you get its final detail. While an order is
in progress, you get the latest available detail, so you can poll its
status through to completion.

An order that nbn does not hold yet is found by its PND. We answer from our
own record, with no nbn detail. The `state` is one of these:

- Acknowledged, while the order is on its way to nbn.
- PendingReview, if nbn could not accept it as we sent it. We correct and
  resubmit it.
- Rejected or Cancelled, if it ended before reaching nbn.

A known order is never a 404. Once nbn holds the order, its `id` is the
Order ID. A PND that was PendingReview keeps returning nbn's detail. Any
other PND then finds nothing. Poll by the Order ID.

post.summary: Submit an Order to NBN for a NCAS Product
post.description:
Places an order with nbn for an NCAS product. NCAS products include FTTB,
FTTC and FTTN.

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Run the Service Qualification API first. It lists the copper pairs at the
premises with the Service Class of each, and that decides what the order
needs.

A successful submission answers "Acknowledged". Check the order's status
on the Order Details.

If nbn cannot accept the order as we sent it, the answer is still a
success. The `state` is "PendingReview" and the order's PND is its `id`.
The fault is ours, and we correct and resubmit the order. Poll the PND on
the Order Details. A genuine refusal from nbn, such as informed consent not
evidenced or no NTD capacity, is a 422 instead.

To hear when the order is "Accepted", "Complete" or "Rejected", register a
callback URL with the Callbacks API.

## Validation

An order runs over a copper pair, not an NTD. `copperPairId` names the
pair: an existing CPI, or "NEW" for a new line. The order is then one of
three things.

- A connection on that pair.
- A Service Transfer: add `transferType`, `serviceRef` and
  `customerAuthorityDate`.
- A Connect Outstanding: as a transfer, but without `serviceRef`, as the
  previous occupant's AVC is unknown.

We check the order against the Service Qualification for the Location
before we send it to nbn. A mistake comes straight back as a 422 with the
reason, and no order is created at nbn. The reasons are:

 - `location_not_serviceable` the Location cannot take a service
 - `wrong_access_technology` the Location is not FTTB, FTTC or FTTN — use the order endpoint for its access technology
 - `copper_pair_id_required` supply a copper pair (CPI #) or "NEW"
 - `unknown_copper_pair` no such copper pair at this Location
 - `copper_pair_not_available` that pair carries a service — transfer it, or choose another pair
 - `new_pair_not_allowed` the premises has a spare pair, so a new line cannot be ordered
 - `appointment_required` this order needs an appointment — see the `appointmentId` field for the Demand Type it takes
 - `appointment_not_allowed` no appointment is required for this order
 - `appointment_wrong_demand_type` the appointment is not the Demand Type this order needs
 - `transfer_type_invalid` / `transfer_type_unsupported` see the `transferType` field for the accepted values
 - `service_ref_required` / `service_ref_not_allowed` only a Service Transfer names the AVC being taken over
 - `avc_mismatch` nbn does not report that AVC on that copper pair — check both
 - `authority_date_required` / `authority_date_invalid` / `authority_date_in_future` / `authority_date_expired` the Customer Authority must be dated within the last 45 calendar days
 - `pots_interconnect_required` a Service Class 12 Active line must name the phone service being transitioned
 - `pots_interconnect_not_allowed` the line does not transition a phone service
 - `central_splitter_not_allowed` a central splitter can only be installed on a Service Class 12 line
 - `installation_workforce_not_allowed` no installation is being performed
 - `installation_workforce_invalid` see the `installationWorkforce` field for the accepted values
 - `bandwidth_sku_required` / `bandwidth_sku_not_eligible` / `sla_sku_not_eligible` use the Product Qualification APIs for the selectable options
 - `order_reference_required` / `order_reference_invalid` up to 35 characters of letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens and periods
 - `informed_consent_required` confirm the End User has given Informed Consent
 - `vlan_mode_invalid` / `uni_vlan_id_required` / `uni_vlan_id_invalid` / `uni_vlan_id_not_allowed` `uniVlanId` applies only when `vlanMode` is "Tagged"

post.summary: Submit an Order to NBN for a NFAS Product
post.description:
Places an order with nbn for an NFAS product. NFAS products include Fibre
and FTTP.

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Run the Service Qualification API first. The Service Class, the NTDs at
the premises and the UNI-D port status decide which fields the order
needs.

A successful submission answers "Acknowledged". Check the order's status
on the Order Details.

If nbn cannot accept the order as we sent it, the answer is still a
success. The `state` is "PendingReview" and the order's PND is its `id`.
The fault is ours, and we correct and resubmit the order. Poll the PND on
the Order Details. A genuine refusal from nbn, such as informed consent not
evidenced or no NTD capacity, is a 422 instead.

To hear when the order is "Accepted", "Complete" or "Rejected", register a
callback URL with the Callbacks API.

## Validation

An order is one of four things.

- A new install: `ntdId` "NEW" with a "Standard Install" `appointmentId`.
- A spare port on an installed NTD: send `ntdId`, and optionally
  `unidPortId`.
- A Service Transfer: add `transferType`, `serviceRef` and
  `customerAuthorityDate`.
- A Connect Outstanding: as a transfer, but without `serviceRef`, as the
  previous occupant's AVC is unknown.

A transfer that moves to a different UNI-D Port without downtime adds
`overlapPeriod` "4" and `fromPortId`.

We check the order against the Service Qualification for the Location
before we send it to nbn. A mistake comes straight back as a 422 with the
reason, and no order is created at nbn. The reasons are:

 - `location_not_serviceable` the Location cannot take a service
 - `wrong_access_technology` the Location is not FTTP — use the order endpoint for its access technology
 - `ntd_id_required` supply an NTD ID or "NEW"
 - `ntd_must_be_new` Service Class 1 or 2 has no NTD installed yet, so `ntdId` must be "NEW"
 - `unknown_ntd` no such NTD at this Location
 - `appointment_required` a new NTD needs a "Standard Install" appointment
 - `appointment_not_allowed` an installed NTD needs no technician
 - `unknown_port` no such UNI-D Port on that NTD
 - `port_not_free` the Port carries a service — transfer it, or choose a free Port
 - `port_not_in_use` a transfer needs the Port the existing service is on
 - `no_free_port` the NTD is full — order an additional NTD with `ntdId` "NEW"
 - `transfer_type_invalid` / `transfer_type_unsupported` see the `transferType` field for the accepted values
 - `unid_port_required_for_transfer` a transfer must name the Port
 - `service_ref_required` / `service_ref_not_allowed` only a Service Transfer names the AVC being taken over
 - `avc_mismatch` nbn does not report that AVC on that Port — check both
 - `authority_date_required` / `authority_date_invalid` / `authority_date_in_future` / `authority_date_expired` the Customer Authority must be dated within the last 45 calendar days
 - `overlap_requires_service_transfer` / `overlap_period_invalid` / `overlap_period_required` the overlap applies only to a Service Transfer
 - `from_port_required` / `from_port_same_as_target` / `unknown_from_port` / `from_port_not_in_use` an overlap moves the service between two different Ports
 - `bandwidth_sku_required` / `bandwidth_sku_not_eligible` / `sla_sku_not_eligible` use the Product Qualification APIs for the selectable options
 - `order_reference_required` / `order_reference_invalid` up to 35 characters of letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens and periods
 - `informed_consent_required` confirm the End User has given Informed Consent
 - `vlan_mode_invalid` / `uni_vlan_id_required` / `uni_vlan_id_invalid` / `uni_vlan_id_not_allowed` `uniVlanId` applies only when `vlanMode` is "Tagged"

post.description:
Places an order with nbn for an NHAS product. NHAS products include HFC.

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Run the Service Qualification API first. The Service Class and the NTD at
the premises decide which fields the order needs.

callback URL with the Callbacks API.

## Validation

An order is one of four things.

- A new install: `ntdId` "NEW" with a "Standard Install" `appointmentId`.
- A self-install where nbn delivers the NTD: Service Class 23 with
  `installationWorkforce` "NBN Co Install End User", and the delivery
  fields.
- A Service Transfer: add `transferType`, `serviceRef` and
  `customerAuthorityDate`.
- A Connect Outstanding: as a transfer, but without `serviceRef`, as the
  previous occupant's AVC is unknown.

We check the order against the Service Qualification for the Location
before we send it to nbn. A mistake comes straight back as a 422 with the
reason, and no order is created at nbn. The reasons are:

 - `location_not_serviceable` the Location cannot take a service
 - `wrong_access_technology` the Location is not HFC — use the order endpoint for its access technology
 - `ntd_id_required` supply an NTD ID or "NEW"
 - `ntd_must_be_new` the Location has no NTD installed yet, so `ntdId` must be "NEW"
 - `unknown_ntd` no such NTD at this Location
 - `appointment_required` a new NTD needs a "Standard Install" appointment
 - `appointment_not_allowed` an installed NTD needs no technician
 - `transfer_type_invalid` / `transfer_type_unsupported` see the `transferType` field for the accepted values
 - `service_ref_required` / `service_ref_not_allowed` only a Service Transfer names the AVC being taken over
 - `avc_mismatch` nbn does not report that AVC at this Location — check the AVC
 - `authority_date_required` / `authority_date_invalid` / `authority_date_in_future` / `authority_date_expired` the Customer Authority must be dated within the last 45 calendar days
 - `installation_workforce_not_allowed` the NTD is already installed, so there is nothing to install
 - `installation_workforce_invalid` see the `installationWorkforce` field for the accepted values
 - `delivery_details_not_allowed` nbn only delivers an NTD for a Service Class 23 self-install
 - `delivery_details_required` a self-install must say where the NTD goes and who receives it
 - `delivery_address_not_allowed` `deliverToLocation` sends the NTD to the premises, so no address is given
 - `delivery_address_required` `deliverToLocation` is false, so the full delivery address is required
 - `bandwidth_sku_required` / `bandwidth_sku_not_eligible` / `sla_sku_not_eligible` use the Product Qualification APIs for the selectable options
 - `order_reference_required` / `order_reference_invalid` up to 35 characters of letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens and periods
 - `informed_consent_required` confirm the End User has given Informed Consent
 - `vlan_mode_invalid` / `uni_vlan_id_required` / `uni_vlan_id_invalid` / `uni_vlan_id_not_allowed` `uniVlanId` applies only when `vlanMode` is "Tagged"
