parameters.name: productInstanceRef
parameters.description:
The NBN Product Instance Reference of the active product to modify.
For Example: "PRI000000000000"

patch.summary: Submit a Modify Order to change an active NBN Product
patch.description: **🚧 Coming Soon — not yet available.**

productSku.description:
(Optional) The SKU of the Bandwidth Product to change to. We
ignore it if empty.
For Example: "NBN-BW-TC4-100_20-FTN"

serviceRestorationSla.description:
(Optional) The SKU of the Service Restoration SLA to change to. We ignore it if empty.
A Premium or Enhanced SLA costs extra.
You cannot set an Enhanced SLA for a (NWAS) Fixed Wireless service, or for a residential-grade bandwidth.
For Example: "NBN-SLA-TC4-STD"

stabilityProfile.description:
(Optional, NCAS (FTTN/FTTB) only) The stability profile to use. We ignore it if empty.
For Example: "Stable"

vlanId.description:
(Optional) Changes the VLAN ID the CPE must supply to the UNI
Port. It applies to Tagged services only. We ignore it if
empty.
For Example: "100"

wiringIsolation.description:
(Optional, NCAS (FTTC) only) Requests Wiring Isolation.
You cannot modify any other attribute in this order. You must send a Standard Install `appointmentRef`.

appointmentRef.description:
(Optional) The nbn Appointment Ref # of an appointment this modification needs.
You must send it for the following:
 -  FTTC where `wiringIsolation` is true
 -  FTTP for Hyperfast NTD replacement via NBN Co Install
 -  HFC for Hyperfast NTD replacement via NBN Co Install
 -  FW for FW HST NTD replacement via NBN Co Install

endUserRef.description:
(Optional, NFAS/NCAS only) Changes the End User for this service.
For example, "EUP000000000001"

customerRequiredDate.description:
(Optional) Changes the Customer Required Date for this order.
Date format: "YYYY-MM-DD"
It applies to NTD replacement orders with delivery details only.

removeBatteryBackup.description:
(Optional, NFAS only) Send "true" to disable the Battery Backup for this Product Instance. We ignore "false".
You need Informed Consent from the End User first.

installationWorkforce.description:
(Conditional, NHAS only) The Installation Workforce for the network shortfall and missing devices.
Do not send it for HFC SC24 orders against an existing NTD.
If a device needs installing, we prefer "NBN Co Install".

ntdMacAddress.description:
(Conditional, NHAS only) The MAC Address of the existing NTD.
Send it if `installationWorkforce` is "RSP Install" or "RSP Install End User". Do not send it if `installationWorkforce` is "NBN Co Install" or "NBN Co Install End User".

ntdSerialNumber.description:
(Conditional, NHAS only) The Serial Number of the existing NTD.
Send it if `installationWorkforce` is "RSP Install" or "RSP Install End User". Do not send it if `installationWorkforce` is "NBN Co Install" or "NBN Co Install End User".

ntdType.description:
(Optional, NFAS Residential Hyperfast Uplift only) The type of new Hyperfast NTD to upgrade to.
 - "1_PORT" - default option
 - "4_PORT" - additional upgrade fee may apply

portId.description:
(Optional, NFAS only) Moves the service to a different UNI
Port on the NTD. It does not apply to a V3 (1_PORT) NTD.
The new Port cannot be zero (0), "Used" or reserved.

speedAndDuplex.description: (Optional, older NFAS only) It does not apply to services with V13, V14 or newer Product Templates.

afterHours.description: For EEAS (Enterprise Ethernet) products only. Asks for this Modify Order to be processed after standard business hours.

Query the nbn™ Rollout Status Report for planned or ready Fibre Uplift
locations, filtered by locality, postcode or location reference.

>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Returns the Change of Access Technology (COAT) status for a location. That
is the current access technology, the planned technology flip and related
planning data. The body is nbn's resource planning record,
without a `result` wrapper.

parameters.name: location_ref
parameters.description: The Address LOC # for the order. Send `location_ref` or `locId`. One is required.

parameters.name: service_type
parameters.description:
The Service Type to find Product SKUs for, as the
/product_qualification/service_types API endpoint names it. You can send
`serviceType` instead. If you send both, we read `service_type`, and the
response's `serviceType` echoes it.

parameters.name: serviceType
parameters.description: The same as `service_type`.

parameters.name: cpi_ref
parameters.description:
(Conditional) The Copper Pair Identifier (CPI #) for the order. You can send `cpiRef` instead.
Each Copper Line can support different speeds, because line quality differs. Send the CPI # when you order NCAS (FTTN/FTTB/FTTC) technology against an existing Copper Line.
Do not send it for "Enterprise Ethernet" or `techUplift`.

parameters.name: techUplift
parameters.description:
(Optional) Filters the results for technology uplift Product SKUs.
Send "true" to get Tech Uplift SKUs only. Send "false" to get normal bandwidth SKUs only. Leave it out to get both.
Send "true" only when the Location (LOC #) is:
 - NCAS (FTTN/B/C) and eligible for a Fibre Uplift
 - NWAS (Fixed Wireless) and eligible for a High-Speed Uplift

parameters.name: termLength
parameters.description: (Optional) Returns only Product SKUs with this minimum Term Length.

get.description:
Returns the eligible Bandwidth Product SKUs for a Location and Service Type, in the Qualify Bandwidths document and without a `result` wrapper.

Call the Service Qualification > Single Site and Enterprise Ethernet endpoints with the `loc_id` first. That keeps the results accurate.

get.summary: Feasibility of a Product Connect Order
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Asks nbn to evaluate a 'Connect' order without reserving or committing any services or resources. Other order types are not supported. These are 'Amend', 'Modify', 'Disconnect' and 'Service Transfer'.
Send the order you intend to place as query parameters. Use the Connect order's fields for the location's technology, without `orderReference` and `ntdId`. No order is created.

These Primary Access Technologies are supported:
 - Fibre
 - FTTB
 - FTTN
 - FTTC
 - Wireless
 - Satellite

These technologies are not supported. We refuse them with a 422:
 - HFC
 - Enterprise Ethernet

parameters.name: locId
parameters.description: NBN Location ID of the Premises the order will be for

parameters.name: bandwidthProductSku
parameters.description:
The Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) of the bandwidth product you would order from Check Networks.
Find the SKUs available at the location with the /product_qualification/bandwidths API endpoint.

parameters.name: restorationSlaSku
parameters.description: (Optional) SKU identifier for the Service Restoration SLA.

parameters.name: unidPortId
parameters.description: (Optional) The UNI-D port the service would use on an existing NTD. Leave it out and nbn chooses.

parameters.name: copperPairId
parameters.description: (Optional, FTTB/FTTN/FTTC) The copper pair (CPI #) the service would run over. Its Service Class sets the jumpering and exchange pair options for you.

parameters.name: potsInterconnect
parameters.description: (Optional, FTTB/FTTN/FTTC) The Full National Number (FNN) or Unconditioned Local Loop (ULL) of the phone service being transitioned.

parameters.name: installOptionCentralSplitter
parameters.description: (Optional, FTTB/FTTN/FTTC) Installation Options, Central Splitter

parameters.name: appointmentId
parameters.description:
(Optional) One of your NBN Appointment IDs to evaluate with the order.
For Example: "APT000000000000"

parameters.name: priorityAssist
parameters.description:
(Optional) Whether Priority Assistance is required: `true`/`false` or `1`/`0`. Send "true" only where the end user is eligible for a Downstream Priority Assistance Service under NBN Co's Wholesale Broadband Agreement.
We accept "true" only for a customer on our Priority Assistance register. That is the end user named in `endUser`. If you name none, it is the account or your own end user. Otherwise we refuse the check with a 422 on `priorityAssist` before we ask the carrier.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description:
(Optional) The number of the end user the order would be for, as `POST /data/orders` takes it. This is ours, not the carrier's.
With `priorityAssist` "true", that end user's registration is the one that counts. An end user that is not this account's is refused with a 422 on `priorityAssist`.
If you leave it out, the account's own registration counts, or the one on your own end user (made when you register yourself). Another end user's counts only when you name them.

contract keep working.

To see orders in progress, use `GET /data/orders`. That covers quoting,
ordered, provisioning, or waiting for you. It covers NBN and Opticomm
alike, and gives each order's status and what it needs next.

>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

To change the nbn™ values, use a Modify Order instead.

You can edit these fields:
 - `customerReference` - Your Reference for this record
 - `endUser` - The End User this record is delivered to

Check Networks holds these details. Updating them does not change the
carrier's records. A request that sends `customer` is refused. Use
`endUser` instead.

customerReference.description: Changes the Customer Reference for this Product Instance. Send null to clear it.

endUser.description: Changes the End User this Product Instance is linked to. Send the End User Number of one of your End User records, as the portal shows it. Send null to unlink the End User.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Lists the active Layer 2 link destinations available to your account for
nbn™ services. These are the outer VLANs (S-Tags) on your customer
interconnects, where we can hand a Layer 2 service off to you. Use an
`interconnectRef` from this list as the `destination` when you provision a
Layer 2 order.

A single-tag interconnect carries all your services on one outer VLAN
across every POI and carrier. It appears under the reserved POI code
`0NAT`, and it is listed here as well as under Opticomm.

This is the carrier-scoped view of `GET /data/layer2/destinations`, which
returns the same destinations across every carrier at once. For new
integrations, we suggest that one.

results.description: The active Layer 2 link destinations available to you.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create

Provisions a Connect Order as a service on the Check Networks network. That
covers its authentication identity, addressing, VLAN tags and edge
configuration.

This is a separate step from ordering the tail. The Connect Order APIs
(NFAS, NWAS, NHAS, NCAS) order the access service from nbn™. This call
builds the service on our side and links it to that order.

**A service is not built until you ask.** Completing at the carrier does
not provision anything by itself. If you never call this for an order, the
service never goes live. You can call it at any point after the order is
placed. Ask before the carrier has finished, and we build the service as
soon as it delivers. Ask afterwards, and we build it immediately.

The same endpoint serves both delivery modes. Send `destination` for a
Layer 2 handoff. Send the Layer 3 fields (`fixedIp`, `ipv6Method`,
`protocol`) for a Layer 3 service. Do not mix the two.

You can change your settings by calling this again, until the service is
built. After that, a change needs a Modify Order.

If the carrier later rejects or cancels the order, we cancel the
provisioning request with it.

orderRef.description:
The Reference ID of the Connect Order to provision.
If the order is marked "Rejected", we reject its provisioning requests too.

fixedIp.description:
(Optional) Assigns a Fixed IPv4 address to a Layer 3 Service.
Fees and charges may apply. See your Agreement.
Leave it empty and we assign a Dynamic address instead.
Do not send this field for a Layer 2 Order.

ipv6Method.description:
(Optional) Enables IPv6 for a Layer 3 service.
If you leave it out, IPv6 is enabled.
Notes:
 - There is no charge for enabling IPv6 for a service.
 - You can set it whether you send `fixedIp` or not.
 - The End User's CPE may need configuring to enable IPv6.
 - You can safely assign IPv6 to services without IPv6 support.
 - We assign IPv6 addresses and prefixes at processing.
 - Do not send this field for a Layer 2 Order.

Options:
 - 'Disabled' - Do not enable IPv6 for this service.
 - 'DHCPv6' - Enable IPv6 via DHCPv6 with Prefix Delegation.

protocol.description:
(Optional) The protocol used to connect and authenticate the Layer 3 service within RADIUS.
We prefer the default, "IPoE". If you use "PPPoE", send the exact username and password configured on the end-user's device.
PPPoE needs a realm on your account. Contact support if you do not have one.
Do not send this field for a Layer 2 Order.

username.description:
(Optional) For `protocol` = "PPPoE" only.
The PPPoE username the user authenticates with. Leave out the
realm, as we append yours.
If you leave it out, we generate a username with the service.
Do not send this field for a Layer 2 Order.

password.description:
(Optional) For `protocol` = "PPPoE" only.
The PPPoE password the user authenticates with.
If you leave it out, we generate a password with the service.
Do not send this field for a Layer 2 Order.

destination.description:
(Conditional) Required for Layer 2 Orders.
The Peer NNI to use as the "Destination" of the Layer 2 link for this Service. We hand its traffic over to you there.
Find the allowed values with the Provisioning Layer 2 Destinations API (`GET /nbn/provisioning/layer2/destinations`).
Do not send this field for a Layer 3 Order.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: A 15-character order reference (`PND…` draft, `ORD…` NBN order, `OPO…` Opticomm order) or a carrier provisioning-request id (`PRV…`). Both give the same provisioning status. Anything else returns 404.

get.summary: Get Provisioning Status (Order or Provisioning Request)
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Returns the provisioning status for one of your orders or provisioning
requests. Send either an order reference (`PND…`/`ORD…`/`OPO…`) or a
carrier provisioning-request id (`PRV…`). Both give the same status.

Once the service is provisioned, the `provisioning` block carries the
carrier's connection detail: protocol, IP, speed plan and Layer 2 handoff
tags. It is empty for an order still in progress.

get.summary: List your in-date EE FBC Quotes
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Lists the Enterprise Ethernet Fibre Build Contribution quotes attributed to
your account that are still in date. These are the quotes you requested,
and any our staff attributed to you. A build cost belongs to the location.
So a quote someone else requested for the same location is listed only once
it is attributed to you.

Expired quotes are not listed. Request a new one with `POST /nbn/quotes`.
An account with no in-date quote gets an empty list.

You can search, filter and sort the list as the portal's NBN Quotes page
does. The same choice gives the same quotes in the same order. The order is
soonest to expire first, unless you ask for another. The quote id breaks
every tie, so the order is stable between pages. The list is paged by
`page` and `perPage`, like every list of your own records.

The search, filters, sort and paging are ours, not the carrier's. The
carrier has no list of quotes. This list is our own register of your
quotes, not a relay.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Returns quotes whose premises address, location id, quote id or your reference contains this text. Case is ignored. It can be up to 100 characters.

parameters.name: poi
parameters.description: Returns quotes at this nbn POI, as `poiName` shows it (`2ALB - Albury`). Case is ignored.

parameters.name: buildCategory
parameters.description: Returns quotes with this fibre build category, as `fibreBuildCategory` shows it (`A`). Case is ignored.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: What to sort by: `premises` is the premises address, or the location id where we hold no address. `poi` is the POI. `category` is the fibre build category. `cost` is the Fibre Build Contribution. `expiry` is the last day the quote is valid.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Ascending or descending.

total.description: Quotes matching the search and filters.

results.description: One page of your in-date quotes.

post.summary: Create an Enterprise Ethernet (EE) Fibre Build Contribution (FBC) Quote
post.description:
A successful request answers "Acknowledged". Repeat the request for a location with an in-date quote, or one the carrier is still working, and you get that quote back. We do not ask the carrier again.
The carrier works the quote over hours or days. We send the `quote.completed`, `quote.actionRequired` or `quote.closed` webhook when the quote is priced, held waiting on you ("Action Required"), or ends unpriced. We also email your users who have EE quote updates on. Read the quote any time with `GET /nbn/quotes/{quoteId}`.

To try this call without reaching the carrier, use the [sandbox](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/start/sandbox/) with one of your account's [test addresses](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/start/sandbox/#addresses).

The 400 response can carry these nbn error codes:
|Type|Code|Message|
|---|---|---|
|ValidationException|001000|The following mandatory field is not provided: %fieldName%|
|ValidationException|001003|Incorrect enumeration of %enumeration% provided for field %fieldName%|
|ValidationException|001012|The value for %fieldName% : %fieldValue% is in an invalid format|
|ValidationException|001015|The value of %fieldName% %value% is invalid|
|InvalidAddressException|005036|The requested location is currently not serviceable|
|InvalidAddressException|012000|The NBN Location ID provided in the request : %NBN Location ID% does not result in a valid NBN Location Address match|

201.description: The quote request has been acknowledged.

The EE FBC Quote ID.
For Example: "EEQ-0000000000"

Returns one quote attributed to your account, in any status. It may be still being worked, held waiting on you (`subStatus` Pending), priced, or ended. A quote not attributed to your account answers 404, as a missing one does.

We answer from what the carrier last told us. Its callbacks and an hourly re-read keep that current, so this call never waits on the carrier.

>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Searches the Opticomm property dataset with the carrier's npis-address
parameters. The answer is a bare array of the carrier's own
`geographicAddress` documents. We serve it from our copy of the carrier
feed, which we import daily. There is no call to the carrier, so you
have no rate to worry about.

Send at least one search parameter. The carrier offers an unbounded
dataset read called `bulkDownload`, and this API does not expose it.
For the truth on serviceability (service class and offered products),
use the live single-site qualification read. The dataset's values can
lag the carrier by up to a day.

Returns one Opticomm property by its OPC #, as the carrier's own
`geographicAddress` document. An unknown id and a malformed id both
answer 404.

>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Lists your Opticomm appointments as the carrier's own `Appointment`
documents. The answer is a bare array, newest first. We serve it from the
documents we hold, so there is no call to the carrier. Filter by
property (`place`), your reference (`externalId`), `status` (the
carrier's vocabulary, such as RESERVED), or a slot-start window
(`startDateTime` and `endDateTime`).

parameters.name: place
parameters.description: The Opticomm Property ID (OPC #) to filter to.

parameters.name: externalId
parameters.description: Your reference for the appointment.

parameters.description: Only slots starting at or after this instant.

parameters.name: endDateTime
parameters.description: Only slots starting before this instant.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Reserves a technician slot. The body is the carrier's own `Appointment`
create shape. The carrier answers the appointment RESERVED with a sunset
timer. Attach it to a Connect order before the timer lapses to book it.
The call answers `200` with the created document in a single-element
array, as the carrier does.

`externalId` is your reference, and we hold it on our side. We set
`accessSeekerContact` ourselves, so a request that sends it is refused.
`Service Restoration` and `Single Truck Roll` need you to hold a service
at the property.

An account may hold at most **5 open install reservations**. An open
install reservation is a `Standard Install` or `Additional Install` that
is RESERVED, not yet attached to an order, with its timer not lapsed.
The next one answers `409`. Waiting does not free a place, so attach one
to a Connect order or cancel it first. Like every carrier write, it
needs an `Idempotency-Key`.

priorityAssist.description: We send this to the carrier as its priority assist flag. "Yes" is accepted only for a customer on our Priority Assistance register. That is the end user named in `endUser`, or the account or your own end user when none is named. Otherwise we refuse the reservation with a 422 on `priorityAssist` before we ask the carrier.

endUser.description: The number of the end user the appointment is for, as `POST /data/orders` takes it. This field is ours, not the carrier's. With `priorityAssist` "Yes", that end user's registration is the one that counts. An end user that is not this account's is refused with a 422 on `priorityAssist`. If you leave it out, the account's own registration counts, or the one on your own end user (made when you register yourself). Another end user's registration counts only when you name that end user.

validFor.description: The slot as `GET /opticomm/timeSlots` returned it. It is a date-time with or without an offset, and we pass it to Opticomm as you give it.

400.description: The request was malformed, sent a field we set ourselves, or the carrier rejected it outright. In that last case we pass on the carrier's own error object.

409.description: The account already holds 5 open install reservations. Release one first, by attaching it to a Connect order or cancelling it. Retrying unchanged gets the same answer.

parameters.name: appointmentId
parameters.description: The carrier appointment id (OAT #).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Returns one appointment as the carrier's own `Appointment` document. We
serve it from the document we hold. An unknown reference and another
account's reference both answer 404.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Changes an appointment. You can reschedule it with a new
`appointmentSlot` from `/opticomm/timeSlots`, replace `endUserContact`,
update `siteAccess`, or rename your own `externalId`. We hold
`externalId` on our side, and our own key for the carrier never
changes. Send at least one field. We set `accessSeekerContact`
ourselves, so a request that sends it is refused. The call answers `200`
with the updated document in a single-element array, as the carrier
does.

400.description: The request was malformed, sent a field we set ourselves, or the carrier rejected it outright. In that last case we pass on the carrier's own error object.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:delete

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Cancels the appointment. The call answers `200` with the CANCELLED
document in a single-element array, as the carrier does.

400.description: The carrier rejected the cancellation. We pass on the carrier's own error object.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Finds the available technician slots at a property within a window. We
read them live from the carrier, and never cache them, because
availability changes quickly. The answer is in the carrier's own
`SearchTimeSlot` shape. Send `propertyId`, or send `appointmentId` to
search around an existing appointment. We then use its property.
`Service Restoration` and `Single Truck Roll` searches need you to hold
a service at the property.

parameters.name: propertyId
parameters.description: The Opticomm Property ID (OPC #). Required unless you send appointmentId.

parameters.name: appointmentId
parameters.description: Search around this existing appointment (reschedule).

parameters.name: startDateTime
parameters.description: A date-time, with or without an offset. An example is `2026-09-08T00:00:00`, which is how Opticomm writes the slots it returns. We pass it to Opticomm as you give it.

parameters.name: endDateTime
parameters.description: Must be after `startDateTime`, in the same form.

parameters.name: appointmentSLA
parameters.description: Standard is the only SLA the carrier offers over the API.

parameters.name: priorityAssist
parameters.description: "Yes" asks the carrier for priority timeslots, as the appointment booking sends it. We accept it only for a customer on our Priority Assistance register. That is the end user named in `endUser`, or the account or your own end user when none is named. Otherwise we refuse the search with a 422 on `priorityAssist`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The number of the end user the appointment would be for, as `POST /data/orders` takes it. This field is ours, not the carrier's. With `priorityAssist` "Yes", that end user's registration is the one that counts. An end user that is not this account's is refused with a 422 on `priorityAssist`. If you leave it out, the account's own registration counts, or the one on your own end user (made when you register yourself). Another end user's registration counts only when you name that end user.

400.description: The request was malformed, or the carrier rejected the search parameters. In that last case we pass on the carrier's own error object.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Requests a diagnostic test. This is the only operation on the carrier's
npis-diagnostics surface, and it has its own body shape. Name the
service (`serviceRef.id`, the OAC #) and the test template
(`testSpecificationRef.id`, from the service's
`/opticomm/diagnostics/service/{serviceRef}/test_types` catalogue). The
call answers the carrier-style acknowledgement. The carrier has no
result read. Progress and results arrive by callback onto
`/opticomm/diagnostics/{testRef}`. A webhook subscribed to
`diagnostic.completed` is told once the test finishes, with its result.

If the service's delivery layer can't run a test, we refuse it at once
instead of failing later by callback. An example is a RADIUS-side test
on a service where we provide the Layer 3. `externalId` is your
reference, and we hold it on our side.

parameters.name: serviceRef
parameters.description: The service's access-circuit id (OAC #).

parameters.description: Only orders created on or before this date.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create (a Modify also requires data:update, a Disconnect data:delete)

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Submits an order of type Connect, Modify or Disconnect. One endpoint
takes all three, with the carrier's own semantics. Use the Service
Qualification read first. It confirms serviceability, whether an
installation appointment is required, and which Bandwidth Products (and
NTD ports) you can select. A live qualification also runs at submission
and refuses an order the carrier would reject.

A Disconnect of a service still in its contract term is charged early
termination. To see the charge before you place it, GET
/data/services/{ref}/disconnect-quote.

The call returns `200` with the carrier's accepted `ProductOrder`, as
the carrier does. If the carrier rejects the order, we pass on the
carrier's own error object at the carrier's status code.

400.description: The request was malformed, sent a field we set ourselves, or the carrier rejected it outright. In that last case we pass on the carrier's own error object.

422.description: The order can't be placed. Either the carrier rejected it, and we pass on their error object, or the service can't take this order type.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The Opticomm Order ID (OPO #).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Returns one product order by its Opticomm Order ID, as the carrier's own
`ProductOrder` document. We keep it current from the carrier's order
lifecycle notifications.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Amends an in-flight order, with the carrier's own PATCH semantics. You
can attach a reserved `appointment`, add a `note`, answer a carrier
action with a `reasonCode` (resume-info or action-completed), or move
the `plannedCompletionDate`. `externalId` renames your own reference on
our side only. The reference the carrier holds is our own and never
changes.

schema.description: At least one amendment key is required.

200.description: Successful operation. The body is the amended order.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:delete

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Cancels an in-flight order. The call returns `200` with the cancelled
`ProductOrder`, as the carrier does. Once the order has passed the point
of no return, it is `422`. To cease an ACTIVE service, submit a
Disconnect order instead.

200.description: Successful operation. The body is the cancelled order.

422.description: The order can no longer be cancelled.

parameters.name: ocrId
parameters.description: The change request reference (OCR #).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Returns the detail of a planned outage. We read it live from the
carrier and return the carrier's `ChangeRequest` document as it is. We
return it only when the outage affects one of your services, and its
`oacIds` name only your own. An outage touching none of your services
answers 404, the same as an unknown reference.

parameters.name: ottId
parameters.description: The trouble ticket reference (OTT #).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Returns the detail of an unplanned outage. We read it live from the
carrier and return the carrier's `TroubleTicket` document as it is.
`?extended=true` answers the fuller record, as the carrier does. That is
the condition, reason, estimated restoration and comments. We return it
only when the outage affects one of your services. Its `oacIds` name
only your own, and we leave out comment authors.

parameters.name: extended
parameters.description: Return the extended record.

parameters.name: oacId
parameters.description: One of your services' access-circuit ids (OAC #).

get.summary: Return Outage Position for a Service
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Returns the outage position for one of your services. We read it live
from the carrier, because the carrier sends no callback feed for
positions. The answer is the carrier's `NoOutage`, `CurrentOutage` or
`FutureOutage` body as it is. The id arrays name planned (OCR) and
unplanned (OTT) outages, which you can read at their own endpoints. An
OAC you do not hold answers 404.

>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Lists your Opticomm services as the carrier's own `Product` documents.
The answer is a bare array, like the carrier's npis-product-inventory
surface. Filter by property (`place`, the OPC #), your reference
(`name`) or product class (`category`, matched against the document's
`@type`).

We don't support `legacyName`, because we hold no legacy names. We
refuse it instead of silently ignoring it.

parameters.name: place
parameters.description: The Opticomm Property ID (OPC #) to filter to.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Your reference for the service.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: The product class, such as FTTP.

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: The Product Instance (OPI #).

get.summary: Add or Remove Layer 3 Service Static IP
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Toggles the static-IP add-on on a Layer 3 service at the carrier. This
is the carrier's own GET, which changes state, and we pass it on. It
answers `200` with no body, as the carrier does. Once the carrier
confirms, the applied policy shows on the service document at
`/opticomm/product/{productId}`.

It changes the service, so it is a write. A suspended account is
refused with `403` `account_suspended`, as on any other write.

400.description: The carrier rejected the action outright, for example because the service holds no Layer 3 profile. We pass on the carrier's own error object with the carrier's status code. Or our own check refused the request, such as for a missing `Idempotency-Key`. That comes in the standard `Error` envelope.

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: The Product Instance (OPI #).

post.summary: Change the ID of a Service
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Renames your reference for the service. The change applies on our side
only. The name the carrier holds is our own reference and never
changes. The call returns the updated document, as the carrier's
operation does.

externalId.description: Your new reference for the service.

200.description: Successful operation. The body is the updated document.

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: The Product Instance (OPI #).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Returns one service by its Product Instance (OPI #), as the carrier's
own `Product` document. We keep it current from the carrier's inventory
notifications and policy actions.

>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Lists the active Layer 2 link destinations available to your account for
Opticomm services. These are the outer VLANs (S-Tags) on your customer
interconnects, where we can hand off a Layer 2 service to you. Use an
`interconnectRef` from here as the `destination` when you provision a
Layer 2 order.

A single-tag interconnect carries all your services on one outer VLAN
across every POI and carrier. It shows under the reserved POI code
`0NAT`, and appears here as well as under nbn™.

This is the carrier-scoped view of `GET /data/layer2/destinations`, which
returns the same destinations across every carrier at once. For new
integrations, use that one.

results.description: The active Layer 2 link destinations available to you.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create

Provisions a Connect Order as a service on our network. That sets up its
authentication identity, addressing, VLAN tags and edge configuration.

This is a separate step from ordering the tail. The Product Order API
(`POST /opticomm/productOrders`, orderType Connect) orders the access
service from Opticomm. This call builds the service on our side and
links it to that order.

**A service is not built until you ask.** Completing at the carrier does
not provision anything by itself. If you never call this for an order,
the service never goes live. You can call it at any point after you
place the order. If you ask before the carrier has finished, we build
the service as soon as it delivers. If you ask afterwards, we build it
immediately.

The same endpoint serves both delivery modes. Send `destination` for a
Layer 2 handoff, or the Layer 3 fields (`fixedIp`, `ipv6Method`,
`protocol`) for a Layer 3 service. Don't mix the two.

You can change your settings by calling this again, up until the
service is built. After that, a change needs a Modify Order.

If the carrier later rejects or cancels the order, we cancel the
provisioning request with it.

orderRef.description:
The Check Networks Reference ID of the Opticomm Connect Order to provision.
We reject any provisioning request for an order marked "Rejected".

fixedIp.description:
Assigns a Fixed IPv4 address to a Layer 3 Service. Fees and
charges may apply, so see your Agreement for details.
Leave it empty and we assign a Dynamic address instead.
Don't send this field for a Layer 2 Order.

ipv6Method.description:
Enables IPv6 for a Layer 3 service. If you leave it out, IPv6
is enabled.

 - There is no charge for enabling IPv6 for a service.
 - You can use it whether you send `fixedIp` or not.
 - The End User's CPE may need configuring to enable IPv6.
 - You can safely assign IPv6 to services without IPv6 support.
 - We assign IPv6 addresses and prefixes at processing.
 - Don't send this field for a Layer 2 Order.

OPTIONS:
 - 'Disabled' - Do not enable IPv6 for this service.
 - 'DHCPv6' - Enable IPv6 via DHCPv6 with Prefix Delegation.

protocol.description:
The protocol used to connect and authenticate the Layer 3 service within RADIUS.
The default "IPoE" is preferred. If you use "PPPoE", send the exact username and password configured on the end user's device.
PPPoE needs a realm on your account. Contact support if you don't have one.
Don't send this field for a Layer 2 Order.

username.description:
For `protocol` = "PPPoE" only. The PPPoE username the user
will authenticate with, without a realm. We append your realm
for you. Leave it out and we generate a username with the
service. Don't send this field for a Layer 2 Order.

password.description:
For `protocol` = "PPPoE" only. The PPPoE password the user
will authenticate with. Leave it out and we generate a
password with the service. Don't send this field for a Layer
2 Order.

destination.description:
Required for Layer 2 Orders.
The Peer NNI to use as the "Destination" of the Layer 2 link for this Service. We hand its traffic over to you there.
Use the Layer 2 Destinations API (`GET /opticomm/provisioning/layer2/destinations`) for allowed values.
Don't send this field for a Layer 3 Order.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Asks the carrier to produce a fresh health report for a service. This
is the only operation on the carrier's npis-service-health surface, and
it has its own body (`oacId` and the fixed `specificationType`). It
answers `202` with the carrier-style acknowledgement. The carrier has no
report read. The RAG report arrives by callback onto
`/opticomm/service_health/{hrId}` and the service's reads. A webhook
subscribed to `serviceHealth.reportReady` is told once the report has
landed.

`externalId` is your reference, and we hold it on our side.

202.description: Accepted. The report is being produced.

parameters.name: serviceRef
parameters.description: The service's access-circuit id (OAC #).

get.summary: List Health Requests for a Service
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Lists the service's health requests, newest first. This is an extension
we add. The carrier has no read, and sends reports only by callback.
Each entry wraps the carrier's own report from the latest callback.

The body is a bare array, as the carrier's reads are. So the page comes
in headers: `X-Total-Count`, `X-Page` and `X-Per-Page`.

X-Total-Count.description: Health requests for the service, across all pages.

X-Per-Page.description: The number of entries per page.

parameters.name: serviceRef
parameters.description: The service's access-circuit id (OAC #).

get.summary: Return the Latest Health Request for a Service
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Returns the service's most recent health request, wrapping the carrier's
own report from the latest callback. It is 404 when no health checks
have been run for the service.

parameters.name: hrId
parameters.description: The health report reference (OHR #).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Returns one health request and report. This is an extension we add,
wrapping the carrier's own report from the latest callback. An unknown
reference and another account's reference both answer 404.

parameters.name: opcId
parameters.description: The Opticomm Property ID (OPC #) to qualify.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Qualifies an Opticomm property for service. The answer is the carrier's
own `SiteQualification` document. It has the serviceability status and
class, access technology, NTD and port inventory, and applicable
charges. With `productAvailability=true`, it also has the bandwidth
products offered at the premises.

We serve it from our qualification cache, which is fresh until 01:00
Sydney the next day. A request with `customerAuthorityDate` is a
transfer qualification, and the carrier's answer depends on it. We
always answer it live. We never serve it from the cache or write it
over the cache.

parameters.name: customerAuthorityDate
parameters.description: The date Customer Authority was obtained from the end user. Send it when you qualify for a Service Transfer. It must be less than 45 days old.

parameters.name: productAvailability
parameters.description: Shows the products available at this property. If you leave it out, it behaves as false, as the carrier's does.

400.description: The request was malformed, or the carrier rejected the qualification parameters. In that last case we pass on the carrier's own error object.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns a paginated list of all DID (Direct Inward Dialing) phone numbers assigned to your account,
in number order. The filters below narrow the list and combine. They match the same numbers as the
portal's Numbers page. Filter by `endUser` for the numbers one end user holds.

For the whole list, set `format=csv` or `format=ndjson`. The response streams **every** match and
ignores `page` and `perPage`. `csv` returns `text/csv`. It has a header row, then one row per number
with the columns of a `results[]` item, and `routing` and `ipnd` as JSON. `ndjson` returns
`application/x-ndjson`, with one `results[]` item per line.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of a number or of its description. A national number matches too. For example, `07` finds numbers stored as `617`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The number type.

parameters.name: szu
parameters.description: The standard zone unit (SZU) of the number's block, by name.

parameters.name: trunk
parameters.description: Only the numbers on this trunk, by its `sipUsername`. A trunk that is not yours is a 422.

parameters.name: routeType
parameters.description: Only the numbers whose first route is of this type.

parameters.name: assigned
parameters.description: `false` for the numbers on no trunk. `true` for those on one.

parameters.name: hasEmergencyAddress
parameters.description: `false` for the numbers with no emergency address linked. `true` for those with one.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Leave it out for paged JSON. `csv` or `ndjson` streams every match.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the numbers this end user holds, by its public number. That is the numbers tagged to it, and untagged ones on its trunks. A number that is not one of your end users is a 422, not an empty list. With `needsAttention`, it narrows the group to that end user.

parameters.name: needsAttention
parameters.description: Only the numbers in this needs-attention group, exactly as `GET /account/summary` counted them. With it, `endUser` narrows the group to that end user.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing an array of phone numbers.

total.description: Total number of phone numbers matching the query.

perPage.description: The number of records returned per page.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`. Every matching number as CSV: a header row, then one row per number with the columns of a `results[]` item.
Present only when `format=ndjson`. Every matching number as newline-delimited JSON, one `results[]` item per line.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Orders a number, or a block of 10 or 100, as the portal's Order Numbers
page does. Send the type. For a geographic number, send the area too. That
is the `szu`, from `GET /numbers/areas`. Then say where the number goes.
Send a trunk and the emergency address it is listed at. Or send
`spare: true` to keep it on no service, routed to Disconnected until you
route it.

To pick the number:

- A `holdId` from `POST /numbers/holds` orders the number you held.
- An `offerId` from `GET /numbers/available` orders a number offered
  where we hold none. It is ordered for you now.
- With neither, you get the next number we hold, or the first complete
  block.

If an order takes an offered number and then cannot be placed, the `422`
carries `error.holdId` and `error.heldUntil`. This happens, for example,
when the trunk's account is on credit hold. Fix the cause and order again
with that `holdId`. That order takes the same number.

With `bundle`, the order is recorded as a `draft` in that bundle. Nothing
is allocated until the bundle is released. A bundle that has been
submitted takes nothing more. A bundle's numbers are always ones we hold,
on a trunk.

We set the order up in the background. The call answers `202` with the
order and a `Location` to read it from. Poll it until it is `completed` or
`failed`. The `Idempotency-Key` is required, so a retry never orders
twice.

type.description: The number type. It is an Australian geographic, mobile, 1300 or 1800 number, or a New Zealand geographic or 0800 number. 13 and premium numbers are by request through your account manager.

szu.description: The numbering area, required for `fixed` and `nz_geographic`.

blockSize.description: Consecutive numbers to order. Blocks are for geographic types only.

holdId.description: A hold from `POST /numbers/holds`, for a single number, or the `error.holdId` of an order that took an offered number but could not be placed, for the same area and block size. A hold that has run out answers `422` with the code `hold_expired`.

offerId.description: An `offer` from `GET /numbers/available` for the same area and block size. Not with `holdId`, and not in a bundle.

spare.description: Keep the numbers on no service, routed to Disconnected. Leave `trunk`, `emergencyAddressId` and `routeType` out. Not in a bundle.

trunk.description: The `sipUsername` of the trunk the numbers go on. Required unless `spare`. In a `bundle`, you can send the `id` of a trunk drafted in the same bundle. The numbers go on that trunk once it is set up, and they always start after it.

emergencyAddressId.description: The emergency address the numbers are listed at. Required unless `spare`.

routeType.description: Where calls go. `trunk` sends them to the trunk. `redirect` forwards them to a number. `sip_address` sends them to a SIP address. You set time of day, geographic routes and failovers on the number once it is live. A Res Line always has a number that rings it, so its first number must be `trunk`. Sending `redirect` or `sip_address` is a `422` on a line with no number ringing it and none on order to ring it.

routeTarget.description: The forward number, or a `sip:`/`sips:` URI that is not a private address. A forward to 000, 112 or 106, in any form, is a `422`, "Calls can’t be diverted to an emergency number (000, 112 or 106)."

bundle.description: The bundle to add the order to.

externalRef.description: Your own reference for the number. We set it once the number is allocated. A reference names one number, so a block (a `blockSize` above 1) is a 422 with one. Give a block metadata only. A reference that another number holds is a 422 before anything is ordered. So is one that another open order holds for its number.

metadata.description: Your own metadata, set on each number the order allocates.

202.description: The order is recorded. Read it at `Location` to see it set up.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The E.164 phone number (e.g. `61299999999`).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the full details for a single DID phone number on your account.

200.description: A JSON object containing the phone number details.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Updates the label, inbound routing or emergency address of a DID phone number on your account.

Send any combination of the fields below. Fields you leave out are unchanged. A request with only
`description` leaves the routing as it is. We check every field before we apply any, so a `422` means
nothing changed.

**One route.** `routeType` and `routeTarget` set a single route. What `routeTarget` holds depends on
`routeType`:

- `trunk`: the target trunk's `sipUsername`, as `GET /trunks` returns it.
- `redirect`: the destination phone number.
- `sip_address`: a SIP URI such as `sip:user@host`. Private and reserved hosts are rejected.
- `fax2email`: the destination email address. Only a number on one of your fax plans (`faxEnabled`)
  can be routed here. Any other number answers `422` on `routeType`.
- `disconnected`: no target. `disconnectResponse` says what the caller hears. It is `hangup` when
  you leave it out.

A single route replaces the number's whole chain. A number can have more than one route
(`hasAdvancedRouting`). That means a failover, time-of-day or geographic routing. For such a number,
`routeType` answers `409` and changes nothing, unless you also send `replaceRouting: true`.

**The whole chain.** `routing` sets every route at once. It holds a first route, up to three failovers,
time-of-day windows and geographic rules. We check each step by the same rules as the portal. Read
`routing` from `GET`, change it and send it back. You cannot send `routing` with `routeType`.

**Emergency address.** On a spare number the new address applies at once. On a number in use, we send it
to the IPND record shortly after the call. The response shows `emergencyAddressChange` with
`status: pending`. `emergencyAddressId` keeps the old address until the change is done. After that,
`GET /numbers/{number}` shows the new one.

**SMS delivery.** `smsDelivery` sets where a mobile number's inbound SMS are delivered. Any other number
answers `422`. The portal's rules apply:

- A field you leave out of `smsDelivery` keeps what is stored. `method: null` turns forwarding off.
  Messages are still received and stored.
- `webhook` needs a public HTTPS `destination`. A private or reserved address is refused. `email` needs
  a valid email address.
- We sign every webhook request. See the `SmsDelivery` schema.
- For `yeastar`, send the `secret` set on the PBX. It is required while none is stored.
- For `generic` and `3cx`, leave `secret` out. We generate one and return it once, as
  `smsDelivery.secret` in this answer.
- A blank `secret` keeps the stored one. Switching to `email` or off removes it.
- `secret` is write-only. A read never returns it.

**A Res Line always has a number.** A route that takes away the last number ringing a Res Line answers
`409` `res_line_needs_number` and changes nothing. `error.resLines` names each line. Send the request
again with `resLineResolutions`, which holds a choice for each line. You can give the line a new number,
move another of your numbers to it, suspend it or cancel it. We make the route and the choices together.

description.description: A label or description for this number, up to 80 characters. Null or empty clears it.

routeType.description: How incoming calls to this number should be routed, as one route.

routeTarget.description: The target for the route, interpreted per `routeType` (see above). Omit it, or send null, for `disconnected`. A `redirect` to 000, 112 or 106, in any form, is a `422`, "Calls can’t be diverted to an emergency number (000, 112 or 106)."

disconnectResponse.description: For `routeType` `disconnected`, what the caller hears. Defaults to `hangup` when omitted or null.

replaceRouting.description: Send `true` with `routeType` to replace a chain of more than one route with the single route. Without it, such a number answers `409`.

routing.description: The whole routing chain, first route first. Replaces the number's chain.

emergencyAddressId.description: List the number at another of your emergency addresses. An Australian number needs one before it can be routed, so send it with the first `routeType` on a spare number.

smsDelivery.description: Where this mobile number's inbound SMS are delivered (see above).

vendor.description: The webhook payload shape. It is `generic` when you leave it out.

destination.description: The webhook URL or email address.

secret.description: The signing secret. Required for `yeastar` while none is stored. For `generic` and `3cx`, we generate one when you leave it out.

resLineResolutions.description: One choice for each Res Line the route would leave with no number, as a `409` `res_line_needs_number` names them.

200.description: Number updated successfully. Returns the updated number details.

emergencyAddressChange.description: Present when the request changed the emergency address of a number in use: the IPND record is updated shortly after, and `emergencyAddressId` shows the new address once it is.

emergencyAddressId.description: The address the number is moving to.

409.description: You sent `routeType`, and the number has more than one route (a failover, time-of-day or geographic routing) that a single route would delete. The message names the steps. Nothing changed. Send `replaceRouting: true` to replace them, or send the whole chain as `routing`. With `code` `res_line_needs_number`, the route would leave a Res Line with no number. `error.resLines` names each line. Send the request again with `resLineResolutions`.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:delete

Cancels (releases) the phone number in the path.

The release runs shortly after the call. Until then `GET` shows the
number as `releasing`. Once it is done, `GET` answers `404` and we send
the `number.released` webhook.

**What a release does.** When it runs, the number stops working and its
billing stops. If the number is listed in the IPND, we send an IPND
disconnect record. The number
then cools off for 30 days. During that time no one can order it, you
included. After that it can be issued to anyone. **There is no undo in
the API.** To get back a number released by mistake, ask Support. Once it
has cooled off it may already be someone else's. If your end user is
moving to another provider, have them port the number out instead.

**Refusals.** Each answers `409` with `code` `conflict` and a `reason`.
The number stays yours, unchanged.

- Check Networks has suspended the number. Only Check Networks can lift
  the suspension, so contact Support.
- A trunk presents the number as its default caller ID. Change that
  trunk's default caller ID first with `PATCH /trunks/{username}`, then
  release the number.

**A Res Line always has a number.** Releasing a Res Line's last number
answers `409` with `code` `res_line_needs_number`. `error.resLines` names
the line. Send the request again with a `resLineResolutions` body that
holds a choice for it. You can give the line a new number, move another
of your numbers to it, suspend it or cancel it. We make the release and
the choice together when the release runs. A line given a choice has its
default caller ID moved off the number.

The same checks run again when the release runs. The release is dropped if
the number was suspended after the `202`, or made a trunk's default caller
ID, or the choice can no longer be made. Then `GET` no longer shows it as
`releasing`, and we send no `number.released` webhook.

resLineResolutions.description: One choice for each Res Line the release would leave with no number, as a `409` `res_line_needs_number` names them.

202.description: The cancellation is queued.

409.description: Check Networks has suspended the number, and only Check Networks can lift that. Or a trunk presents it as its default caller ID. With `code` `res_line_needs_number`, it is a Res Line's last number and you sent no choice for the line. Nothing changed.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The E.164 mobile number (e.g. `61491570110`).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** sms:read

Returns where a mobile number's inbound SMS are delivered. It is the same
as `smsDelivery` on `GET /numbers/{number}`. A number that is not a mobile
number reads `null`. We never return the secret, only whether one is set.

A key limited to one end user reads only a number that end user holds.
Any other number answers `404`, as a missing one does.

200.description: Where the number's inbound SMS are delivered.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** sms-delivery:update

Sets where a mobile number's inbound SMS are delivered. It needs only
`sms-delivery:update`, so a key that may not change the number's calls
can still set it. `smsDelivery` on `PATCH /numbers/{number}` sets the same
thing under `voice:update`. Any other number answers `422`. The portal's
rules apply:

- A field you leave out keeps what is stored. `method: null` turns
  forwarding off. Messages are still received and stored.
- `webhook` needs a public HTTPS `destination`. A private or reserved
  address is refused. `email` needs a valid email address.
- We sign every webhook request. See the `SmsDelivery` schema.
- For `yeastar`, send the `secret` set on the PBX. It is required while
  none is stored.
- For `generic` and `3cx`, leave `secret` out. We generate one and return
  it once, as `secret` in this answer.
- A blank `secret` keeps the stored one. Switching to `email` or off
  removes it.
- `secret` is write-only. A read never returns it.

A key limited to one end user sets only a number that end user holds.
Any other number answers `404`, as a missing one does, and is unchanged.

200.description: Where the number's inbound SMS are now delivered.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns a paginated list of your emergency addresses, ordered by label.
`q` searches the label, customer name, long name, street and locality.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated list of emergency addresses.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Creates an emergency address. We lodge it with the emergency register when
you link a number to it.

To fill the address from an address search, send the `gnafId` of a
`GET /addresses/search` result as `serviceAddress.gnafPid`. For a separate
directory listing, send it as `directoryAddress.gnafPid`. Send no other
address fields. We fill in the building, unit, level, street number,
street name and type, locality, state and postcode in the shape the
emergency register needs, as the portal does. A field you send beside the
PID wins.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The emergency address's `id`.

get.description: >**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Send only the fields to change. The others are kept. We check the
resulting address as a whole, as on create. If your numbers are listed at
this address, we lodge the change with the emergency register for each of
them.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:delete

You cannot delete an address while any of your numbers are listed at it.
That is when `liveNumbers` is above zero, and the call answers `409`. Move
those numbers to another address first.

204.description: The address is deleted. The response has no body.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** fax:read

Returns the account's fax plans, oldest first, paged like every list.
You get open plans by default. Pass `status=closed` for closed ones, or
`status=all` for both. `q` searches the plan's numbers and its end user's
reference.

A key for one end user gets only that end user's plans.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Which plans to return: `open`, `closed` or `all`. `open` is the default. Send `open,closed` for both. Case does not matter. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing an array of fax plans.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** fax:create

Opens a fax plan for your account, or for one of your end users. The plan
starts billing today. Put numbers on it with
`POST /fax/plans/{planId}/numbers`.

The call answers `422` when the account cannot take new orders. That is
when it is over its credit limit or overdue.

kind.description: `bundle`: one number, pages included. `service`: any number of numbers, each charged monthly, and each page sent charged.

endUser.description: The number of the end user the plan is for. Omit it for your own plan. An end user's plan takes that end user's numbers only, and its charges go on their invoice.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The fax plan's ID.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** fax:read

Returns one fax plan, with the pages it has sent this month.

A key for one end user gets only that end user's plans. Any other plan is
`404`.

pagesCharged.description: Pages sent this month that are charged per page.

pagesIncluded.description: Pages sent this month that the plan includes.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** fax:delete

Closes the plan. Every number comes off it and stops sending and receiving
faxes: its sender addresses are removed and its Fax to Email route is
cleared. The plan stops billing today. A fax already queued still sends.

Closing a plan that is already closed changes nothing and returns `204`.

204.description: The plan is closed. The response has no body.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The fax plan's ID.

post.summary: Add a Number to a Fax Plan
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** fax:create

Puts one of your active numbers on the plan. From then on it can send and
receive faxes, and it has no separate monthly number charge.

The call answers `422` in these cases:

- The number is already on a fax plan. Move it instead.
- The plan is a Fax Bundle that already has its one number.
- The plan is for an end user and the number is not on that end user's
  services.
- The plan is closed.

number.description: One of your numbers, as E.164 digits.

201.description: The number is on the plan.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The fax plan's ID.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: A number on the plan, as E.164 digits.

delete.summary: Remove a Number from a Fax Plan
delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** fax:delete

Takes the number off the plan. It stops sending and receiving faxes: its
sender addresses are removed and its Fax to Email route is cleared. A fax
already queued still sends. The plan is charged for the days it held the
number.

To change plans without losing the sender addresses and the route, use
`POST /fax/plans/{planId}/numbers/{number}/move`.

204.description: The number is off the plan. The response has no body.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The ID of the fax plan the number is on now.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: A number on the plan, as E.164 digits.

post.summary: Move a Number to Another Fax Plan
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** fax:update

Moves the number to another of your open fax plans in one step. Its sender
addresses and Fax to Email route move with it, and each plan is charged
for the days it held the number.

The call answers `422` when the target plan cannot take the number. That
is a Fax Bundle that already has its number, or an end user's plan when
the number is not on that end user's services.

toPlan.description: The ID of the plan to move the number to.

200.description: The number is on the target plan, which is returned.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The fax plan's ID.

get.summary: List a Fax Plan's Sender Addresses
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** fax:read

Returns the email addresses that may send faxes by email under this plan.
Each comes with the number it sends as. The list is paged like every
list. `q` searches the email.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing an array of sender addresses.

id.description: The sender address's id, as `DELETE /fax/plans/{planId}/senders/{senderId}` takes it.

sendsAs.description: The plan's number faxes from this address are sent as.

createdAt.description: When the address was added, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the address last changed, in UTC.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** fax:create

Authorises an email address to send faxes by email as one of the plan's
numbers. Mail from any other address is rejected.

The call answers `422` when `sendsAs` is not a number on this plan, or
the address is already authorised on your account.

sendsAs.description: A number on this plan, as E.164 digits.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The fax plan's ID.

parameters.name: senderId
parameters.description: The sender address's `id`, as the plan's sender list gives it.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** fax:delete

Removes a sender address from the plan. Faxes emailed from it are rejected
from then on.

204.description: The sender address is removed. The response has no body.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns a paginated list of all SIP trunks assigned to your account, oldest first.
`q` searches the name, handle, description and SIP username. Filter by
`endUser` for one end user's trunks and by `status`, as the portal's trunk
list does. A trunk's `connection.allowList` is on `GET /trunks/{username}`
only, not here.

For bulk pulls, set `format=csv` or `format=ndjson`. The response streams
**every** matching trunk as a single download instead of paged JSON, and
`page` and `perPage` are ignored. `csv` returns `text/csv`. It has a header
row, then one row per trunk, with arrays and objects as JSON in their
cells. `ndjson` returns `application/x-ndjson`. It has one JSON object per
line, each identical to a `results[]` item. An unrecognised `format`
returns `422`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only trunks with this `status`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Bulk export format. Leave it out for paged JSON. `csv` or `ndjson` streams the full result set as a download.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the trunks of this end user, by its public number. A number that is not one of your end users is a 422, not an empty list.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing an array of SIP trunks.

total.description: Total number of trunks matching the query.

perPage.description: The number of records returned per page.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`. Every matching trunk as CSV. It has a header row, then one row per trunk, with the same columns as a `results[]` item.
Present only when `format=ndjson`. Every matching trunk as newline-delimited JSON. It has one object per line, each identical to a `results[]` item.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Creates a new SIP trunk on your account.

We assign the SIP domain, username and password. We create the trunk on
the shared wholesale SIP domain and return the generated credentials in
the response. The password is revealed **only once**, in the `201`
response. Store it securely.

With `bundleId`, we check the trunk the same way and it joins that bundle
as a draft instead. See `POST /bundles`. We set it up when the bundle is
submitted. The answer is the bundle item, with the bundle at `Location`.
Order numbers onto it in the same bundle, with the item's `id` as
`trunk`. Once it is set up, its `href` reads it. Take its password with
`POST /trunks/{username}/credential/rotate`.

A description, recording, number formats and calling limits are set on
the trunk after it is set up. So a request in a bundle that sends them is
a 422.

`externalRef` and `metadata` are taken now and held for the trunk. A
reference another trunk holds is a 422 now. So is one another open order
holds for its trunk. If another trunk takes the reference before the
bundle sets this one up, we leave it off this trunk. The reason is in the
bundle item's `outcomeReason`.

schema.description: `sipUsername`, `sipDomain`, `cpsLimit` and `faxEnabled` are set by Check Networks; a request that sends any of them is refused.

name.description: A friendly name for this trunk.

description.description: An optional description for this trunk.

type.description: The plan to provision on. It is `payg` when you leave it out. On `ultimate`, each channel is a recurring billed assignment. On `payg`, outbound calls are metered per use.

channels.description: Maximum concurrent calls on this trunk. On `ultimate`, it is required and is also the number of channels billed. On `payg`, it is a ceiling and defaults to 5.

maxInternational.description: Maximum concurrent international calls. It applies only to a trunk that may call internationally. A limit sent without `International` in `callingPermissions` is refused with a 422.

callingPermissions.description: The calling-permission classes to enable. If you leave it out, you get `AUNational`, `AUMobile` and `AU13`. `AUEmergency` and `AUFreecall` are always on. You can send them, as a fetched trunk lists them. You cannot leave them out.

defaultCallerId.description: Default outbound caller ID. It is a number on your account with an emergency address linked, or one approved through `POST /caller-id-authorisations`. Send digits, which may include `+` and spaces. Any other number is a 422 with the code `caller_id_authorisation_required`.

forceOutboundCli.description: Present `defaultCallerId` on every outbound call, whatever caller ID the PBX sends.

recordingEnabled.description: Order call recording with the trunk, for a monthly charge per trunk. Every call is recorded, with no announcement. You are responsible for telling your callers that calls may be recorded. It needs `acknowledgeRecording: true` and an account that may place orders.

acknowledgeRecording.description: With `recordingEnabled: true`, this confirms that you accept the monthly recording charge and are responsible for telling your callers. Without it the request answers `422` `charge_acknowledgement_required`. The error carries `error.consent`, the text you are agreeing to, and `error.charge`, the monthly price. We keep the acknowledgement on the trunk's history with the API key that sent it. A credit hold or a suspended account answers `422` and nothing is ordered.

endUser.description: The end user this trunk is for, by its public number. The trunk's calls are billed to that end user. It must be one of your end users, and not archived. Any other number is a 422. Leave it out, or send null, to make the trunk your own.

allowedCountries.description: The trunk's own list of countries it may call, as ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes. If you leave it out or send null, the new trunk follows your account's list, which Get Allowed Countries returns. It follows later changes to that list too.

dailySpendCapExGst.description: The most the trunk's outbound calls may cost in a day, ex GST, as a dollar string. If you leave it out or send null, there is no cap. 000 always connects.

calledNumberFormat.description: How the dialled number arrives on calls to this trunk. It is `international` when you leave it out.

callerNumberFormat.description: How an Australian caller's number arrives on calls to this trunk. If you leave it out, it follows `calledNumberFormat`'s plus. That means a plus for `international`, and digits only for any other format.

bundleId.description: An open bundle to add the trunk to, as a draft. We set it up when the bundle is submitted. A bundle that has been submitted, or is not yours, is a 422.

201.description: SIP trunk created successfully. Includes the one-time SIP password. With `bundleId`, the trunk joined the bundle; this is the item.

sipPassword.description: The generated SIP password. To read it again later, call `GET /trunks/{username}/credential`, which needs `secrets:read`.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username. A trunk with no SIP credential has only its `id`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the full details for a single SIP trunk on your account. They
include its IP ACL entries. They also include `connection.allowList`, the
addresses to allow through your firewall. We read those from DNS, so they
come back here and not on the list.

200.description: A JSON object containing the SIP trunk details.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Updates settings on an existing SIP trunk. Fields you leave out stay unchanged.

### Changing plan or channels

On an `ultimate` trunk, `type` and `channels` affect billing, because each
channel is a recurring charge. So they follow the upgrade and downgrade
rule rather than applying as a plain edit.

* **Upgrades take effect immediately** and are billed from today. Moving
  `payg` to `ultimate` is an upgrade whatever the channel counts say. So is
  raising the channel count on an `ultimate` trunk.
* **Downgrades take effect at the start of your next billing cycle.**
  Lowering the channel count, or moving `ultimate` to `payg`, is a
  downgrade. We never cut channels in use above the new limit mid-period.

When a plan change happens, the response carries a `planChange` block. On
a scheduled downgrade, `result` still shows the plan the trunk is on
**today**. `planChange.effectiveOn` is when the new one starts.

Requesting a change supersedes any change already scheduled on the trunk.
So an upgrade also clears a pending downgrade that would otherwise reverse
it on the 1st. A scheduled change shows in the trunk's `pendingPlanChange`
on every read until it applies. `DELETE /trunks/{username}/plan-change`
cancels it.

We check every field before we apply anything, and the whole request
applies in one step. A `422` leaves recording, the plan and every other
field as they were. A caller ID you may not present is one example.

schema.description: Check Networks manages `cpsLimit` and `faxEnabled`. A request that sends either is refused.

description.description: Your free-text notes on the trunk, up to 500 characters. Null clears them.

type.description: The trunk's billing plan. Leave it out to keep the plan. Moving onto `ultimate` requires `channels`. Each channel is a recurring charge, so we never assume a count for you.

channels.description: Maximum concurrent calls on this trunk. On `ultimate`, it is the number of billed channels. Changing it is an upgrade or a downgrade, as described above. Leave it out to keep the count. On `payg`, it is a concurrency ceiling only, with no billing effect. An `ultimate` trunk needs at least 1.

maxInternational.description: Maximum concurrent international calls. Send null to remove the trunk's own limit. It applies only to a trunk that may call internationally. A limit sent while `International` is not among the calling permissions, after this request's change, is refused with a 422. Removing `International` clears the limit.

callingPermissions.description: The trunk's call barring. It is the calling-permission classes the trunk may dial, and it replaces the current list. Remove `International` to cut international calling in one call. 000 and freecall are never barred. `AUEmergency` and `AUFreecall` stay on whether you send them or not. The answer's `callingPermissionsKept` names any this list left out.

defaultState.description: The trunk's default state; null clears it.

defaultCallerId.description: Default outbound caller ID. It is a number on your account, or one approved through `POST /caller-id-authorisations`. Send digits, which may include `+` and spaces. Any other number is a 422 with the code `caller_id_authorisation_required`. The change is in the trunk's history with its before and after values.

forceOutboundCli.description: Present `defaultCallerId` on every outbound call, whatever caller ID the PBX sends. The caller ID must pass the same checks as `defaultCallerId`.

forcePrivateCli.description: Force all outbound calls to present as Private/Anonymous.

recordingEnabled.description: `true` orders call recording, for a monthly charge per trunk. `false` cancels it, and recordings already made are kept. Every call is recorded, with no announcement. You are responsible for telling your callers that calls may be recorded. Turning it on needs `acknowledgeRecording: true` and an account that may place orders.

acknowledgeRecording.description: With `recordingEnabled: true` on a trunk without recording, this confirms that you accept the monthly recording charge and are responsible for telling your callers. Without it the request answers `422` `charge_acknowledgement_required`, with `error.consent` and `error.charge`. A credit hold answers `422` and nothing is ordered. You do not need it to turn recording off.

allowedCountries.description: This trunk's own list of countries it may call, as ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes. The United Kingdom is `GB`. `null` drops the override, so the trunk follows your account's list again, which Get Allowed Countries returns. The list applies when `International` is in `callingPermissions`. Calls to Australia and New Zealand follow their own permissions. High-risk destinations stay blocked, and 000 always connects.

dailySpendCapExGst.description: The most this trunk's outbound calls may cost in a day, ex GST, as a dollar string. At the cap, its new outbound calls stop until midnight Brisbane time. Calls already up carry on. Spend counts a call when it ends. A cap at or below `spendTodayExGst` holds the trunk at once, and `"0.00"` does too. The answer then reads `spendCapHeld: true`. Raising the cap above `spendTodayExGst` resumes calls at once. `null` removes the cap. 000 always connects.

calledNumberFormat.description: How the dialled number arrives on calls to this trunk.

callerNumberFormat.description: How an Australian caller's number arrives on calls to this trunk. A number's own inbound format still overrides it.

200.description: Trunk updated successfully. Returns the updated trunk details.

callingPermissionsKept.description: Present only when `callingPermissions` left out a class that is always on. The trunk keeps it, because 000 and freecall are never barred.

planChange.description: Present only when the request changed the trunk's plan or its billed channel count. Absent for an ordinary edit.

direction.description: Which way the change moves your entitlement.

appliedImmediately.description: True for an upgrade, which is already live. False for a downgrade, which starts on `effectiveOn`.

effectiveOn.description: The date the new plan applies from. It is today for an upgrade, and the first day of your next billing cycle for a downgrade.

type.description: The plan the trunk moves to.

channels.description: The billed channel count the trunk moves to (0 on `payg`).

delete.description:
