>**Required Scope(s):** voice:delete

Permanently deletes a SIP trunk from your account.

**Warning:** This action cannot be undone. Re-route or cancel the trunk's
numbers first. Until then the request answers `422`. New calls are
refused at once, and calls already in progress are ended within a minute.

The one exception is the trunk's `defaultCallerId`. It cannot be cancelled
while the trunk is up. When it is the trunk's only number, the delete
releases it with the trunk. If we cannot release that number just then,
the answer is `503` and nothing changes. Try again shortly.

A trunk still in contract has an early termination charge. The first
request answers `422` with the code `charge_acknowledgement_required` and
the charge in `error.charge`. Send `acknowledgeEarlyTermination=true` to
accept it and delete the trunk. We bill the accepted charge shortly after,
on your next invoice. If we cannot record the charge just then, the answer
is `503` and nothing changes. The trunk is not deleted and nothing is
billed. Try again shortly.

parameters.name: acknowledgeEarlyTermination
parameters.description: Accept the early termination charge on a trunk still in contract.

204.description: The trunk is deleted. The response has no body.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the IP ACL entries for a SIP trunk, in address order, paged like
every list. `q` searches the address or host name and its description.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing an array of IP ACL entries.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Adds a new IP address, CIDR range or host name to a trunk's IP ACL. Calls
from an address on the list are accepted without registration.

A **host name**, such as `pbx.example.com`, is resolved now and again on
its DNS TTL. It allows the public addresses it resolves to. We store it
lower-cased and list it with `type: host`. It must be a full name with a
dot. A host name already on another trunk is refused.

An address must meet all of these:

- **An IPv4 host or a range no wider than `/24`**, which is 256
  addresses. Or **a single IPv6 host** (`/128`). IPv6 ranges are refused.
  We store and return a bare address as `/32` or `/128`.
- **Public.** Private, CGNAT (`100.64.0.0/10`) and reserved ranges are
  refused.
- **Not on any other trunk**, yours or another account's. A source
  address identifies the trunk a call belongs to, so ranges cannot
  overlap. If an address has moved to you, contact support.

ipAddress.description: The IPv4 address or CIDR range from `/24` to `/32`, the single IPv6 address, or the host name, to allow.

description.description: An optional label for this IP entry. Defaults to `API`.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username.

parameters.name: ipId
parameters.description: The IP ACL entry's `id`, as the trunk's IP list gives it.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:delete

Removes an IP address from a trunk's IP ACL.

204.description: The entry is removed. The response has no body.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the live SIP registration status for this trunk. We read it from
the real-time registration state.

A registration-based trunk lists its currently active contacts. Those are
the SIP devices and gateways registered against it. An IP-ACL-only trunk
authenticates by source IP rather than registering, so it has no
registrations and `registered` is `false`.

This data is live and reflects the current state of the trunk in real
time.

username.description: The trunk's SIP digest username. Null for a trunk with no SIP credential, which authenticates by IP and never registers.

registered.description: Whether the trunk currently has at least one active SIP registration.

registrations.description: The trunk's currently active SIP registrations (empty for IP-ACL trunks).

aor.description: The SIP Address of Record the registration is bound to.

sourceIp.description: The source address the REGISTER was received from.

parameters.name: serviceNumber
parameters.description: The IP transit service's number.

get.description:
**Not available yet.** IP transit is not offered by API yet. This
endpoint answers `404`, and `transit:read` cannot be granted until it is.

>**Required Scope(s):** transit:read

Returns the blackholes in force on an IP transit service, oldest first,
paged like every list. It includes any that Check Networks placed on the
service's addresses (`placedBy` is `staff`). Those count toward the
service's limit, and only Check Networks can release them.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing an array of blackholes.

post.description:
**Not available yet.** IP transit is not offered by API yet. This
endpoint answers `404`, and `transit:create` cannot be granted until it
is.

>**Required Scope(s):** transit:create

Drops all traffic to one of the service's addresses, to stop an attack on
it reaching your service. We drop the traffic at our border within a
minute or two. We do not signal it beyond our network.

The blackhole must be:
  - **One address**, IPv4 or IPv6, with no prefix length.
  - **Inside one of the service's own prefixes.** For a BGP service
    ordered with an AS-SET, that includes any route registered under the
    AS-SET in the routing registry (IRR). We ask the registry when you
    place the blackhole. We refuse any other address. We refuse every
    address if we cannot reach the registry. Try again, or signal the
    blackhole over BGP.
  - **On a live service.**
  - **Given an expiry**, of at most 24 hours. It lifts by itself then.
    Place it again if the attack is still running.

A service holds at most 10 blackholes at once. Release one, or wait for
one to expire, to place another.

expiresInHours.description: How many hours until the blackhole lifts by itself.

reason.description: An optional note on why, shown with the blackhole.

parameters.name: serviceNumber
parameters.description: The IP transit service's number.

parameters.name: blackholeId
parameters.description: The blackhole's ID.

delete.description:
**Not available yet.** IP transit is not offered by API yet. This
endpoint answers `404`, and `transit:delete` cannot be granted until it
is.

>**Required Scope(s):** transit:delete

Releases a blackhole now, before it expires. Traffic to the address
resumes within a minute or two. A blackhole that has already been
released or has expired answers `404`.

You can release a blackhole you placed (`placedBy` is `customer`). One
Check Networks placed answers `422`. Contact support to have it lifted.

204.description: The blackhole is released. The response has no body.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns a paginated list of Call Detail Records (CDRs) for your account.

Filter by date range with the `from` and `to` query parameters. Send dates in ISO 8601 format, such as `2024-01-01T00:00:00Z`. An invalid `from` or `to` returns `422`.

When you leave out `from`, the window is the **31 days** before `to`. When you leave out `to`, it is now. `period=unbilled` starts the window at the start of
this month instead. You cannot combine it with `from`. `invoice` with no
`from` has no lower bound, because the invoice bounds the calls. Every
response gives the window it used in `window`. A cursor keeps the first
page's window, so a walk does not drift as new calls arrive.

Filter further with `trunk`, `endUser`, `direction`, `disposition`,
`invoice` and `q`. `GET /voice/cdrs/summary` gives the totals for the same
filters, and `GET /voice/cdrs/{cgrid}` returns one call. An unknown trunk,
end user or invoice, or a value outside an enum, is a `422`.

A page holds at most 200 records. `q` searches the source and destination.

A re-rated call is listed once, under its `cgrid`, at its new price. It
has `rerated: true`, and the price before the most recent re-rate is in
`previousCostExGst`, `previousCostGst` and `previousCostIncGst`. The
summary counts it once.

### Walking a large window

Page numbers reach at most 10,000 records into the window, which is
`page × perPage`. A deeper page returns `422`. `total` is exact up to
10,000. Beyond that it reads 10,000 with `totalIsBounded: true`. To walk
every record, follow `nextCursor`. Pass it back as `cursor` to get the next
page, until it is `null`. A cursor page carries `perPage`, `nextCursor` and
`results` only. Each record is returned exactly once, however many there
are.

### Bulk export

For bulk pulls, set `format=csv` or `format=ndjson`. The response streams
the **entire** filtered result set as a single download instead of paged
JSON. The `from` and `to` window still applies. `page` and `perPage` are
ignored. `csv` returns `text/csv`, with a header row and one row per call.
`ndjson` returns `application/x-ndjson`, with one JSON object per line,
each identical to a `results[]` item. An unrecognised `format` returns
`422`. An export covers at most **93 days**. A longer window answers `422`
on `from`. We audit each export with the API key that made it.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Bulk export format. Leave it out for paged JSON. `csv` or `ndjson` streams the full filtered result set as a download.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Filter CDRs on or after this datetime (ISO 8601), or from the start of this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Defaults to 31 days before `to`, or before now.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page. It walks the window by keyset rather than page number, with no depth limit. `page` is ignored when you send it.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Filter CDRs on or before this datetime (ISO 8601), or to the end of this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Defaults to now.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: `unbilled` starts the window at the start of this month. Do not send it with `from`.

parameters.name: trunk
parameters.description: Only this trunk's calls, by sipUsername. A trunk that is not yours is a 422.

parameters.name: invoice
parameters.description: Only the calls billed on this invoice of ours to you, by its `id` in your invoice list. Not one of yours is a 422.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search the source and destination numbers. A national number such as 07 … matches too.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the calls on this end user's trunks, by its public number. A number that is not one of your end users is a 422, not an empty list.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to retrieve. Defaults to `1`. `page × perPage` may not exceed 10,000; use `cursor` beyond that. A value that is not a whole number of at least 1 is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, with `-` in front for descending, in place of newest call first. A sorted list has no cursor. `nextCursor` is `null`, and `sort` with `cursor` is `422`. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing call detail records.

total.description: Number of CDRs matching the query, counted no further than 10,000. Absent on a cursor page.

totalIsBounded.description: True when more than 10,000 records match, so `total` reads 10,000. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The current page number. Absent on a cursor page.

perPage.description: The number of records returned per page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page. It is `null` when this is the last page, the page was not full, or the list was sorted.

window.description: The window the records were read over. `from` is null for an invoice with no `from`.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`. The full filtered result set as CSV — a header row followed by one row per call, with the same columns as a `results[]` item.
Present only when `format=ndjson`. The full filtered result set as newline-delimited JSON — one object per line, each identical to a `results[]` item.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the current number of active call sessions on your account. Use it for real-time capacity monitoring, or to track concurrent call usage.

The count is the calls we are rating on your account right now, across every trunk. If we cannot read the count, the endpoint returns `503` rather than a misleading `0`.

200.description: A JSON object containing the current active call count.

activeCalls.description: The number of currently active call sessions across your account.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** sms:read

Returns every SMS on your account, newest first. It covers sent and
received messages, whatever sender they went out from.

Use this endpoint when you want your account's traffic rather than one
number's. It also covers senders that `GET /sms/{number}` cannot reach on
their own. To follow one message you sent, read
`GET /sms/messages/{messageId}`. That is the `Location` of the send.

Filter by `direction`, by a `from` and `to` range on when the message was
sent, by a `q` search over the numbers and the text, and by `status`. For
a large pull, `format=csv` or `format=ndjson` streams every match as one
download.

To walk every message while new ones arrive, follow `nextCursor`. Pass it
back as `cursor` until it is `null`. A cursor page carries `perPage`,
`nextCursor` and `results` only.

We audit reads of message content. An export is audited once, with its
filters and count. We never record the text.

A key limited to one end user sees only that end user's messages. Messages
of your own and of your other end users are left out.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Limit to messages sent or received. Case does not matter. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, with `-` in front for descending, in place of newest first. A sorted list has no cursor, so `nextCursor` is `null`. An unknown field is `422`.

total.description: Messages matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page. It is `null` on the last page, on a page that was not full, and on a sorted list.

id.description: Unique message ID.

statusReason.description: Present only where the status alone is ambiguous.

createdAt.description: When the message was recorded, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the message last changed, which is its status, in UTC.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`: a header row, then one row per message (see `format`).
Present only when `format=ndjson`: one JSON object per line, with the same fields as a CSV row.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** sms:send

Sends an SMS message from a sender on your account.

The `from` sender must be one of two things. It can be a DID on your account that has SMS enabled. Check the `smsEnabled` field on `GET /numbers`. Or it can be another sender approved for your account, which is a number ported for SMS or an alphanumeric Sender ID. Request approval for any other sender with `POST /sms/senders`. An unapproved sender is rejected with a `403` whose `code` is `sender_not_approved`.

A key limited to one end user sends only from that end user's own senders. That is a mobile number they hold, or a sender they asked for and we approved. Any other sender is rejected with the same `403`. The message is recorded against the end user, so it counts on their bill.

**A send is always idempotent.** A stuck retry loop in your client can bill and deliver the same message hundreds of times if the send is not de-duplicated. Send an `Idempotency-Key`, as the Idempotency guide above describes. A retry with the same key returns the original send's result instead of sending again. If your integration cannot send the header, you can leave it out. We then make a key from the request and the current minute. The same message from the same sender to the same number within that minute is sent once.

In the [sandbox](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/start/sandbox/#sms), send to its test numbers, each with a fixed outcome.

from.description: The sender. It is an E.164 number that is an SMS-enabled DID on your account, or another sender approved for your account. That is a ported number or an alphanumeric Sender ID.

to.description: The recipient number in E.164 format.

message.description: The body of the SMS message, up to 1600 characters. A longer body is rejected with `422`. A message over one segment is sent and billed as several. A segment holds 160 characters in plain GSM text. It holds 70 if the message has any character outside that set, such as an emoji or most accented letters. Once the message is long enough to be concatenated, each segment holds one fewer.

202.description:
Accepted for delivery. The message has been submitted and is awaiting a delivery receipt — it is **not** delivered yet, which is why this is `202` rather than `201`.

A `statusReason` of "Held for review before sending" means the message was additionally screened and will be sent once it clears. Either way the message is accepted: **do not retry**, because a retry creates a second message that will also be sent and billed.

The `Location` header names where to poll: the message itself, `GET /sms/messages/{messageId}`. The message reaches `delivered`, or `failed` if it is rejected or not released.

Location.description: Where to poll for this message's outcome (`/sms/messages/{messageId}`).

messageId.description: A unique identifier for the message.

statusReason.description: Present when the message needs more than "pending" to explain it — most often that it is held for review.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** sms:send

Sends one message from one sender to up to 100 numbers. Each number gets
its own message, sent and billed as `POST /sms` sends and bills it. Each
has its own `messageId` to poll at `GET /sms/messages/{messageId}`.

A number that is refused does not stop the others. Each number comes
back in `messages`, in the order you listed it. It is either `pending`
with its `messageId`, or `rejected` with the `error` that `POST /sms`
would have answered for it:

- `validation_failed` for a number that is not E.164, or a destination
  your account cannot send to.
- `carrier_unavailable` or `service_unavailable` when the SMS service
  could not take it.

A number listed twice is sent once. The second is `rejected` as already
listed. Once the cause is fixed, send the rejected numbers again under a
new `Idempotency-Key`.

The sender is the same for every number. An unapproved sender is refused
as on `POST /sms`, with a `403` whose `code` is `sender_not_approved`.
Nothing is sent.

A key limited to one end user sends only from that end user's own
senders, as on `POST /sms`. Any other sender is the same `403`. Each
message is recorded against the end user, so it counts on their bill.

The call counts once against your rate limit, however many numbers it
names.

**A send is always idempotent.** Send an `Idempotency-Key`. A retry with
the same key returns the original send's result instead of sending again.
Without one, we make a key from the request and the current minute. The
same request within that minute is sent once.

In the [sandbox](https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/start/sandbox/#sms),
send to its test numbers, each with a fixed outcome.

to.description: The numbers to send to, each in E.164 format. At most 100.

message.description: The body, sent to every number. It is up to 1600 characters. Each number is billed per segment, as for `POST /sms`.

202.description: The numbers were taken in turn. Each `pending` message is submitted and awaiting a delivery receipt, as from `POST /sms`: **do not retry** those, because a retry under a new key sends and bills them again. `202` whatever the mix of accepted and rejected: read `accepted` and `rejected`.

messages.description: One per number listed, in the order listed.

to.description: The number as you listed it.

messageId.description: The message's id, when it is `pending`.

statusReason.description: Present when the message needs more than "pending" to explain it, most often that it is held for review.

error.description: Why the number was refused, when it is `rejected`.

code.description: The code `POST /sms` would have answered with, as the `Error` schema lists them.

reason.example: to Must Be An E.164 Number

error.reason: to Must Be An E.164 Number

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The E.164 DID phone number to retrieve SMS history for (must be on your account).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** sms:read

Returns the SMS message history (inbound and outbound) for a DID phone number on your account.

Results come newest first. To walk every message while new ones arrive,
follow `nextCursor`. Pass it back as `cursor` until it is `null`. A cursor
page carries `perPage`, `nextCursor` and `results` only.

The filters and the `format` export are those of `GET /sms`, within this
number's messages.

A key limited to one end user reads only a number that end user holds,
or a sender of theirs, and only their messages on it. Any other number
answers `404`, as a missing one does.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Filter by message direction. Case does not matter. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, with `-` in front for descending, in place of newest first. A sorted list has no cursor, so `nextCursor` is `null`. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing SMS messages.

total.description: Messages matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page. It is `null` on the last page, on a page that was not full, and on a sorted list.

id.description: Unique message ID.

status.description: `delivered` and `failed` are final. `pending` means the message may still move — queued, awaiting a delivery receipt, or held for review; `statusReason` says which.

statusReason.description: Present only where the status alone is ambiguous — most usefully to tell a message held for review before sending from one merely in flight.

createdAt.description: When the message was recorded, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the message last changed (its status), in UTC.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`: a header row, then one row per message (see `format`).
Present only when `format=ndjson`: one JSON object per line, with the same fields as a CSV row.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Check Networks outages affecting services on your account, as published
on our outage register under the Telecommunications (Customer
Communications for Outages) Industry Standard 2024. It also lists the
planned maintenance windows you were sent notice of. Unplanned outages
come first, newest first, then planned windows by start time. The list is
paged like every list, with `total`, `page`, `perPage` and `results`.

An outage is included when it covers the service address of at least one
live service on your account. That includes services you have attributed
to your own end users. It is the same matching that decides who we
notify, so this endpoint never disagrees with the outage notifications
we send you.

Each unplanned outage names which of your services it hit
(`yourAffectedServices`) and the end user each belongs to. You can tell
your end users without matching addresses yourself.

We return only published register entries.

Every time is UTC, as everywhere in the API. `timezone` names the
affected area's zone, so you can show the times locally.

`q` searches the reference, title, affected suburbs and postcodes.

This is different from the carrier outage endpoints (`/nbn/outage/...`,
`/opticomm/outage/...`). They report a single carrier's view of a single
carrier reference. Use this endpoint for what is affecting your
services, and those for carrier-specific detail.

The full public register, including outages that do not affect your
services, is available without authentication at
<https://status.checknetworks.tools>.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `open` (the default) returns only outages still in progress. `resolved` returns the resolved ones still within the register's retention period. `all` returns both. Send several comma-separated. Case does not matter. Any other value answers `422`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only planned maintenance, or only unplanned outages. Both by default. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the outages that reach this end user's services, by its public number. We give notice of planned maintenance to you, not to an end user, so a list filtered by end user holds no planned windows. A number that is not one of your end users answers `422`, not an empty list.

get.description:
Lists your account's support tickets, newest first. `sort=-lastActivityAt`
gives the portal's order, most recent activity first.

To walk every ticket while new ones are raised, follow `nextCursor`. Pass
it back as `cursor` until it is `null`. A cursor page carries `perPage`,
`nextCursor` and `results` only. `q` searches the reference and subject.
`createdFrom` and `createdTo` bound the list by when tickets were raised.
`GET /tickets/summary` gives the figures over a range.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Which tickets to return, by status. Send one status or several, comma-separated. `status=open,pending` is the portal's open group. Case does not matter. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: One or several categories, comma-separated. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the tickets about this end user, by its public number. A number that is not one of your end users is a 422, not an empty list.

parameters.name: isComplaint
parameters.description: `true` lists only complaints, `false` only the tickets that are not. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, with `-` in front for descending, in place of newest first. `status` orders as the portal does: open, pending, resolved, closed. `priority` orders from low to urgent. A sorted list has no cursor, so `nextCursor` is `null`. An unknown field is `422`.

total.description: Tickets matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page. It is `null` on the last page, on a page that was not full, and on a sorted list.

post.description:
Opens a new support ticket on your account with its first message.
The response includes the ticket's `reference` (`INC-XXXXXX`), which
addresses the ticket in all other endpoints.

attachments.description: Files to attach to the opening message. Each file can be up to 10 MB. Allowed types are PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP images, PDF, plain text, CSV, ZIP, Word (.doc, .docx) and Excel (.xls, .xlsx).

parameters.name: ticketRef
parameters.description: The public ticket reference, e.g. `INC-7K3F9Q`.

get.description:
Returns the ticket with its public conversation thread, oldest message
first. Internal Check Networks notes are never included.

patch.description:
Changes your ticket's status yourself. Mark it `resolved`, or set it back
to `open` to re-open a resolved ticket. Check Networks closes tickets.
There is no customer delete.

Read `canResolve` and `canReopen` on the ticket first. If the ticket's
`resolveBlockedReason` refuses a resolve, the call answers 422 with that
reason's `code`, such as `ticket_not_open`.

Resolving a complaint records its outcome in `complaintOutcome`. The
default is `resolved`. Only Check Networks records
`closed_no_further_action`.

`comment` is posted as a public reply before the status changes, in the
same step.

schema.description: `status`, or `externalRef` and `metadata` alone to change only your own reference on the ticket.

status.description: Required unless the request sends `externalRef` or `metadata`.

complaintOutcome.description: The outcome recorded when resolving a complaint. The default is `resolved`. It is ignored for other tickets.

comment.description: A public reply posted with the status change.

parameters.name: ticketRef
parameters.description: The public ticket reference, e.g. `INC-7K3F9Q`.

post.description:
Appends a reply to the ticket's conversation thread. Replying to a
resolved or closed ticket re-opens it. To attach files, send
`multipart/form-data` with an `attachments[]` field. `body` is required
unless you send `attachments[]`. A reply can be just a file, such as a
screenshot or a log.

body.description: The reply, as Markdown. Required unless you send `attachments[]`. A reply can be files alone.

attachments.description: Files to attach to the reply. Each file can be up to 10 MB. Allowed types are common image, document and archive formats.

parameters.name: ticketRef
parameters.description: The public ticket reference, e.g. `INC-7K3F9Q`.

parameters.name: attachmentId
parameters.description: The attachment `id` from the message's `attachments` metadata.

get.description:
Streams the attachment's content. The response's `Content-Type` is the
file's stored MIME type. Images are served inline. Other files are served
as a download, with a `Content-Disposition` header. Only attachments on
the ticket's public messages are available.

parameters.name: ticketRef
parameters.description: The public ticket reference, e.g. `INC-7K3F9Q`.

post.description:
Submits a satisfaction rating for a resolved or closed ticket. A ticket
can be rated once. The call answers `409` if the ticket is still open or
has already been rated.

get.description:
Returns the figures the portal's Support Reports page shows, over the
tickets raised in a date range. They are counts by status, priority and
category, volume by month, how often the first response and the
resolution met their targets, the average response and resolution times,
and satisfaction. Without `from` and `to`, the range is the last 90 days
to today. The days are calendar days in your account's time zone, and so
are the months in `volumeByMonth`. That time zone is Australia/Brisbane
unless you set another. A safety-sensitive complaint is in none of the
figures, as it is in no ticket list. `GET /tickets/export` gives the rows
behind them.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first day of the range, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in your account's time zone. Defaults to 90 days ago.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The last day of the range, included, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in your account's time zone. Defaults to today there. Before `from` is `422`.

get.description:
Returns the rows behind `GET /tickets/summary`, as the CSV the portal's
Support Reports page downloads. You get one row per ticket raised in the
range, oldest first. The columns are `reference`, `subject`, `status`,
`priority`, `category`, `is_complaint`, `created_utc`,
`first_response_utc`, `first_response_due_utc`, `resolved_utc`,
`resolution_due_utc`, `closed_utc` and `csat_rating`. Times are ISO 8601.
A cell that would open as a spreadsheet formula starts with `'`. Without
`from` and `to`, the range is the last 90 days to today. The days are
calendar days in your account's time zone. That is Australia/Brisbane
unless you set another.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first day of the range, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in your account's time zone. Defaults to 90 days ago.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The last day of the range, included, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in your account's time zone. Defaults to today there. Before `from` is `422`.

parameters.name: ticketRef
parameters.description: The public ticket reference, e.g. `INC-7K3F9Q`.

post.summary: Mark a Ticket as a Complaint
post.description:
Marks the ticket a complaint, as the portal's ticket page does. The
complaint's deadlines start from when the ticket's first message arrived.
They show on the ticket's `complaint`. We send the acknowledgement to the
consumer. Marking a complaint again changes nothing and answers the
ticket as it stands. A network outage complaint is `409`, because our
staff handle it on its own track. A safety-sensitive complaint is `404`,
as on every ticket call. The audit log names the API key.

urgent.description: An urgent complaint, with the shorter resolution deadline.

patch.description:
Sets or clears the complaint's urgency, which moves its resolution
deadline. A ticket that is not a complaint is `409`.

delete.description:
Use this when the ticket was not a complaint after all. It removes the
complaint, its deadlines and any TIO case logged on it. The ticket itself
stays. A ticket that is not a complaint is `409`.

parameters.name: ticketRef
parameters.description: The public ticket reference, e.g. `INC-7K3F9Q`.

post.description:
Records that the complaint was acknowledged to the consumer. Use it for a
complaint acknowledged another way, such as by phone. We send the
acknowledgement again. The first acknowledgement's time stays as
`acknowledgedAt`. A ticket that is not a complaint is `409`.

parameters.name: ticketRef
parameters.description: The public ticket reference, e.g. `INC-7K3F9Q`.

post.summary: Log a TIO Case on a Complaint
post.description:
Use this when the consumer took the complaint to the Telecommunications
Industry Ombudsman. It records the TIO's case reference and starts the
deadline to respond to the TIO. The deadline shows as
`complaint.tioDueAt`, and it has fewer working days for an urgent
complaint. A ticket that is not yet a complaint is marked one first, as in
the portal. Logging the case again updates the reference and leaves the
deadline where it is. A network outage complaint is `409`.

reference.description: The TIO's case reference.

parameters.name: ticketRef
parameters.description: The public ticket reference, e.g. `INC-7K3F9Q`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** tickets:update

Asks for more attention on one of your open tickets, with your reason.

The ticket's `priority` goes up one level. `low` goes to `normal`,
`normal` to `high` and `high` to `urgent`. An `urgent` ticket stays
`urgent`. We work out its response targets again for the new priority.

We email the engineer looking after the ticket, or our support team if no
one is yet. Our staff see the ticket flagged on their list with the
reason. We also add the escalation to the thread. The ticket read shows
the latest as `escalation`. Escalating again replaces the reason there
and raises the priority again. Each escalation stays on the thread.

A resolved or closed ticket is `409`. Re-open it first.

reason.description: Why the ticket needs more attention.
reason.example: The end user's business has been offline for two days.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

The email addresses and mobiles your keys have subscribed to our outage
notices, newest first. Each is pending or active. We never list an
address that someone signed up on the public status page, or that
another account subscribed.

post.summary: Subscribe an Address to Outage Notices
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Subscribes a team mailbox or an on-call mobile to our outage notices, as
the sign-up on the public status page does. We send the person a link to
confirm, by email or by text. The subscription stays `pending` until
they follow it, and notices start only then.

Ask again for a pending address and we send a new link once 5 minutes
have passed since the last one. We send a mobile at most 3 links. After
that, subscribe it by email.

The subscription is your account's own, with its own confirmation. If an
address is also signed up on the public status page, or by another
account, it is confirmed again for your list and theirs is left as it
is. Someone on more than one list is sent each notice once.

Stop yours with `DELETE /outages/subscriptions/{id}`. That leaves the
address's other lists as they are.

The unsubscribe link in a notice is the person's own choice. It stops
every status notice to the address, on the public list, yours and every
other account's. Their subscription then leaves
`GET /outages/subscriptions`, as one you removed does.

address.description: An email address for `email`; an Australian mobile for `sms`, in any common format.

scope.description: Which outages to be told of.

202.description: Accepted. The subscription waits for the person to confirm it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The subscription's id, as `GET /outages/subscriptions` returns it.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Stops our outage notices to one of your subscriptions at once, whether
it is pending or active. A subscription your keys did not create answers
`404`, as an unknown id does.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** watch:read

Everything your account is currently watching.

We keep a removed watch as a `disabled` record rather than delete it.
The list leaves them out by default. Pass `status=disabled` for them
alone, or `status=all` for both. The list is newest first. `q` searches
the reference and its type.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The statuses to list. Send `active` (the default) or `disabled`, or both comma-separated, or `all`. Case does not matter. Any other value answers `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** watch:create

Starts watching a reference. We email every address on the watch as
updates arrive. You get **one email per event**, never a batched digest,
and never twice for the same event.

### One watch per reference

Posting a reference you already watch **replaces** that watch's addresses
rather than creating a second watch. It also re-enables the watch if you
had removed it. The call is therefore safe to repeat. It answers `201`
when it created a watch and `200` when it replaced one. To change a watch
you already hold, `PATCH /watch/{watchId}` is the direct way.

An account can have at most 250 active watches.

### Where the emails go

`emails` is optional. Omit it and we use your account's default
notification address, which is what an integration usually wants because
an API client has no address of its own. If your account has no default
notification address and you omit `emails`, we reject the request rather
than create a watch that could never deliver anything.

### Which updates you get

`eventTypes` is optional. Omit it, or send `null`, and you are told about
everything. That is the default. Send a list to narrow it down.
`GET /watch/event-types` returns the values you can use, with the labels
that appear in the emails.

Like `emails`, the list **replaces** what the watch had rather than adding
to it. Re-posting without `eventTypes` puts a watch back to every event.

### What you may watch

You can watch four kinds of thing, all through this one field. We work
out which kind from the reference and tell you in `referenceType` on the
response:

* an **order**, by the carrier's reference or ours;
* a technician **appointment**, by its carrier reference;
* a **service**, by its carrier service id or a trunk's SIP username;
* an **outage**, by its register reference.

The reference must belong to your account. Anything else answers `404`,
including a reference that exists on another account. A `404` here never
confirms whether something exists.

An outage counts as yours when it affects services you hold. We decide
that the same way `GET /outages` decides what to show you. You can watch
exactly the outages you can already read, and no others.

reference.description: What to watch: an order (the carrier's reference or ours — both work), an appointment, a service, or an outage. See "What you may watch" above.

emails.description: Where to send notifications. Omit to use your account's default notification address.

eventTypes.description: Which updates to send. Omit or null for every update. See `GET /watch/event-types` for the accepted values.

200.description: The watch already on this reference, replaced.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** watch:read

The values `eventTypes` accepts when creating a watch, with the labels that
appear in the notification emails.

Fetch this list rather than hardcoding one. It grows as we support more of
what the carriers send, and we reject a value that is not on it.

### Each event names what it applies to

Which events exist depends on the kind of thing the watch is on. Each
item carries a `referenceType`, the same value the watch reports back to
you. The items are in the shape `GET /webhooks/event-types` uses.

An order's events are the carrier's own, finer-grained lifecycle. An
appointment, a service and an outage each carry the events the
corresponding webhook carries, spelled identically. The emailed and the
pushed version of one happening never go by two different names.

You do not have to match the `referenceType` yourself. Send whatever you
want to hear about. Anything that cannot happen to that reference never
fires.

Not everything we record is offered here. We leave out telemetry and
internal bookkeeping events, because they say nothing about the progress
of what you are watching.

200.description: The subscribable event types, each with the kind of reference it applies to; within a kind, in lifecycle order.

A single watch on your account.

Changes where a watch's emails go, or which updates it sends. Only the
fields you send change. The reference and whether the watch is active
stay as they are. Each field you send **replaces** what the watch had.
Send `eventTypes: null` to go back to every update.

Stops watching. We send no further emails.

We mark the watch `disabled` rather than erase it. It still appears under
`GET /watch?status=all`, and creating a watch on the same reference again
re-enables this one.

204.description: The watch is disabled. The response has no body.

A key limited to one end user lists only the endpoints that end user's keys registered. Any other key lists only your own. `GET /end-users/{endUser}/webhooks` lists an end user's.

post.description:
Registers an HTTPS endpoint to receive event notifications. The
response includes the endpoint's `secret` **once**. Store it, because
you cannot read it afterwards. You can rotate it with `PATCH`. The secret
is the HMAC key for the `X-CN-Signature` body signature on every
delivery. We never send the secret itself, so check the signature, not a
header.

Endpoint URLs must use `https` on port 443 or 8443, carry no username
or password, and name a host that already resolves to a public address
when you register it. We refuse a private, loopback or link-local
address, or a name that does not resolve, with `422`. An account can
register at most 25 endpoints.

A URL the account already has answers `409`, and `error.existingWebhookId`
names the endpoint. Change its events with `PATCH /webhooks/{webhookId}`,
or get a new secret with `rotateSecret`. We check this before the
25-endpoint limit.

A key limited to one end user registers an endpoint for that end user.
It gets only that end user's SMS and fax events. Its `events` may list
only `sms.received`, `sms.delivered`, `sms.failed`, `fax.received`,
`fax.sent` and `fax.failed`, and any other type, or `*`, is `422`. It
cannot set `filters`. One end user can register at most 5 endpoints. They
do not count towards your account's 25, and a URL you already use is free
for them.

secret.description: The endpoint's signing secret — shown only in this response.

409.description: The account already has an endpoint at this URL.

error.reason: This URL is already registered as webhook endpoint 12. Change its events with PATCH /webhooks/12, or get a new secret with rotateSecret.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** webhooks:read

The values `events` accepts when you register or update a webhook. `*`
subscribes to every event, including ones added later.

Fetch this list rather than hardcoding one. It grows as we add events, and
we reject a value that is not on it. `ping` is not listed. You never
subscribe to it, and the test call sends it to any webhook.

Each item has the shape `GET /watch/event-types` uses, with a label to show
a reader. `referenceType` is always null here.

A key limited to one end user is shown only the SMS and fax events it may
subscribe to, and not `*`.

parameters.name: webhookId
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint's `id`.

get.description: One of your endpoints. A key limited to one end user reads only that end user's endpoints. Any other endpoint answers `404`, as a missing one does. Any other key reads only your own, and an end user's endpoint is `404`.

patch.description:
Changes the URL or subscribed events. It can also re-enable a disabled
endpoint with `isActive: true`, which resets the failure streak. And it
can rotate the secret with `rotateSecret: true`. The new secret comes
back once, in this response.

**Rotating without dropping a delivery.** The previous secret stays valid
for `rotationOverlapHours`. The default is `24` and the most is `168`,
which is 7 days. `0` ends it at once. During that window every
delivery's `X-CN-Signature` carries two signatures, the new secret's
first: `t=<timestamp>,v1=<new>,v1=<old>`. Accept a delivery if **any**
`v1` matches a secret you hold. You can then deploy the new secret
whenever suits within the window. `previousSecretExpiresAt` on the
endpoint says when the old one stops. Once your receiver checks the new
secret, send `endRotationOverlap: true` to stop the old one at once.

`filters` replaces the endpoint's filters. Empty lists remove them.

`rotateSecret: true` REQUIRES an `Idempotency-Key` header. Without one
the call answers `400`. Rotation is not naturally idempotent, and a
client that retries a request whose response it never saw must not
silently rotate a secret it never read. With the header set, a retry of
the exact same request replays the already-rotated secret instead of
minting another one. An update that does not rotate the secret runs
without the header too. Send one on every update anyway, so a client
never has to tell them apart.

A key limited to one end user changes only that end user's endpoints,
and rotates their secrets the same way. Any other endpoint is `404`. Its
`events` may list only the SMS and fax events, and any other type, or
`*`, is `422`. Sending `filters` is `422` too.

url.description: Same rules as when registering — `https` on port 443 or 8443, no credentials in the URL, and a host that already resolves to a public address.

rotationOverlapHours.description: With `rotateSecret`: how many hours the previous secret keeps signing deliveries alongside the new one.

endRotationOverlap.description: `true` once your receiver checks the new secret: the previous one stops signing deliveries now. Does nothing outside a rotation window.

secret.description: Present only when `rotateSecret` was true — shown once.

delete.description: Removes the endpoint. Pending deliveries settle without being sent. We keep the delivery history. A key limited to one end user removes only that end user's endpoints. Any other endpoint is `404`.

Queues a `ping` event delivery to the endpoint, whatever its subscribed
event list. Use it to check connectivity and authentication.

Send an `eventType` to queue a sample of that event instead, in the
event's own shape. Use it to test your handler for that event.

Either way the delivery has `test: true` and its `data` describes
nothing real. The call answers `409` if the endpoint is disabled, or

get.description:
Every delivery to every one of your endpoints, removed ones included,
most recent first. Each delivery's `webhookId` says which endpoint it
went to. Filter to one endpoint with `endpoint`. The other filters are
the same as an endpoint's own list.

It pages like that list too. Page with `page`, or follow `nextCursor` and
pass it back as `cursor` until it is `null`. A cursor page carries
`perPage`, `nextCursor` and `results` only. `q` searches the event type
and event id.

A key limited to one end user sees only the deliveries to that end
user's endpoints. Any other key sees only those to your own endpoints.

The endpoint's delivery history, most recent first. It shows what we
sent, when, what your endpoint answered, and why an attempt failed.

Use it to answer whether an event reached you, without raising a support
ticket. Filter to `dead` to see only what exhausted its retries or was
never attempted. A `dead` delivery with `attempts: 0` is an event that
occurred while the endpoint was disabled. We recorded it but did not send
it. Replay-dead delivers it after you re-enable the endpoint.

We keep the history even after the endpoint is removed.

To walk the whole history while new deliveries are made, follow
`nextCursor` and pass it back as `cursor` until it is `null`. A cursor
page carries `perPage`, `nextCursor` and `results` only. `q` searches
the event type and event id.

A key limited to one end user reads the history of that end user's
endpoints only. Any other endpoint is `404`, as a missing one is.

get.description:
One delivery. It shows what we sent, when we sent it and what your
endpoint answered. A delivery of another endpoint or another account
answers `404`. A key limited to one end user reads only deliveries to
that end user's endpoints, and any other is `404` too.

post.description:
Limit: 10 per minute for the account (webhook send), shared by test, redeliver, replay-dead and event re-send. Each end user's keys have their own 10, apart from yours.

Sends a past event to the endpoint again. A key limited to one end user
redelivers only to that end user's endpoints. Any other endpoint is `404`.

The replay carries the **same `eventId`** as the original. A handler
that de-duplicates on `eventId`, as the webhooks guide recommends, sees
the same event rather than a new one. It also carries the **original
`occurredAt`**, which is when the event happened, not when it was
replayed. It gets its own, later `sequence` number, because delivering
it again is a new event in your endpoint's delivery order.

The replay is recorded as a new delivery with its own id. The original
is left untouched, so the history stays a faithful record of what
happened.

You can replay any settled delivery, including one that was delivered
successfully. That helps when your side acknowledged an event and then
lost it. You cannot replay a delivery that is still `queued`, because its
first attempt has not resolved yet. That answers `409`.

Redelivery works even while the endpoint is disabled, which happens
after 20 consecutive failures. That is the state the dead letters you
want to recover are stuck in. Re-enabling the endpoint first would reset
the failure count, which is the evidence of what went wrong.

A delivery is replayed once. Redelivering one that was already replayed
sends the newest replay of that event again. It answers `409` while that
replay is still `queued`. It also answers `409` while the endpoint holds
100 queued deliveries.

202.description: Queued

parameters.name: webhookId
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint's `id`.

post.description:
Limit: 10 per minute for the account (webhook send), shared by test, redeliver, replay-dead and event re-send. Each end user's keys have their own 10, apart from yours.

Redelivers every `dead` delivery for this endpoint in one call. It does
for the whole backlog what
`POST /webhooks/{webhookId}/deliveries/{deliveryId}/redeliver` does for
one delivery. A key limited to one end user replays only that end
user's endpoints. Any other endpoint is `404`.

It works even while the endpoint is disabled. An endpoint that we
auto-disabled after 20 consecutive failures is the case with dead
letters worth replaying. Re-enabling it first would reset the failure
count, which is the evidence of what broke.

Each redelivery follows the same rules as the single-delivery endpoint.
It is a new delivery with the same `eventId`, the original `occurredAt`
and a fresh `sequence`. A delivery that stops being eligible between
listing and replay is skipped, and the rest still go. For example, it
may have settled, or its endpoint may have been removed.

Each delivery is replayed once. A dead delivery that was already
replayed is skipped. If that replay died too, the replay is the one we
retry. Calling this again therefore queues nothing for deliveries it
already replayed.

An endpoint holds at most 100 queued deliveries. The call replays up to
that many. It answers `409` while the endpoint is already at 100. Wait
for the queue to settle, then call again.

202.description: Queued

replayed.description: How many dead deliveries were requeued.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

Lists your end users by name. Archived end users are left out unless you
ask for them with `status`.

`q` matches part of the name, the number or the email. It never matches
the email of an end user whose contacts a family violence safety record
withholds, so the search cannot confirm that email.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only end users with this status. Left out lists active and suspended ones.

parameters.name: externalRef
parameters.description: Only the end user with exactly this reference of yours.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:create

Creates an end user. The fields and rules are those of the End User
form in the portal. We send them a welcome email in your branding, as we
do when you add one in the portal.

billingAddress.description: Left out or null, bills go to the service address.

post.summary: Find an End User by Identity Details
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

Limit: 20 per minute for the key.

Finds the one end user a caller is, from the details the caller gives
you, such as a name, an email and a mobile. It suits a front desk or
phone tool that needs to find one caller without listing everyone.

It answers only when **at least three** of the details you send match
the same end user exactly. The name counts as one. It ignores case and
spacing. It compares a phone number in one format, so 0400 000 001 and
+61 400 000 001 are the same. It compares an ABN by its digits.

Every miss answers the same `404`. That covers too few details, a wrong
detail, no end user, and more than one end user. The call cannot tell you
which detail was wrong.

- It is a POST, so the details never appear in a URL or a log.
- We audit each call with the names of the details sent, never their
  values, and whether it matched.
- The answer carries no contact details. It is the same for an end
  user whose contacts a family violence safety record withholds.
- For such an end user, their email, phone and service address never
  count as a match. A lookup that needs one of them answers the same
  `404` as for no end user. Their name and ABN alone are too few.

serviceAddress.description:
The service address, as text ("12 Example Street, Brisbane City
QLD 4000"), or `{"gnafId": "..."}` for one picked from
`GET /addresses/search`.

200.description: The one end user the details match.

contactsMasked.description: True while a family violence safety record withholds their contacts. Read the end user with care.

404.description: No single end user matches enough of the details. Every miss answers this way.

error.reason: No single end user matches those details.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

Returns one end user, archived ones included. While a family violence
safety record withholds their contacts, the contacts and addresses are
null and `contactsMasked` is true.

It also says whether you can issue the end user's final invoice now.
The fields are `finalInvoiceAllowed`, `finalInvoiceEarliestDate` and
`finalInvoiceReasons`. The check is the same as
`GET /end-users/{endUser}/invoices/final` and the portal's Final Invoice
button. The list does not carry these fields.

finalInvoiceAllowed.description: Whether the final invoice can be issued now.

finalInvoiceEarliestDate.description: The earliest it can be issued, when that is known.

finalInvoiceReasons.description: What is still open, each with a stable `code`. Empty when allowed, except for one `already_billed_through_end` when the last invoice already billed everything, so issuing makes no new invoice.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Changes any of the end user's details. A field you leave out stays as
it is. The rules are those of the End User form in the portal.

- **Addresses**: this call refuses them with 422. Change them with
  `PATCH /end-users/{endUser}/addresses`. That call also updates the
  emergency services (IPND) record of their numbers.
- **Masked contacts**: while a family violence safety record withholds
  the end user's contacts, a change to `email`, `phone`, `billingEmail`,
  `altContactName` or `altContactPhone` is refused with 422.
- **Archived** end users are not changed. The call answers 409. Restore
  them first.
- **Time zone**: we cut their bills on `timezone`, and their portal
  shows times in it. A change applies from their next billing period.
  The period already open keeps the zone it started in. Null is your
  zone.

timezone.description:
The end user's own time zone. Send one of `Australia/Brisbane`,
`Australia/Sydney`, `Australia/Melbourne`,
`Australia/Adelaide`, `Australia/Perth`,
`Australia/Darwin` or `Australia/Hobart`. Any other
answers 422. Null clears it, so they are in your zone.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Changes the end user's service address, billing address, or both. The
end user can do the same on their Profile page in the end-user portal.
This is the only call that changes an end user's addresses.

The service address is also the address we give emergency services for
the end user's numbers. This is their IPND record. When the service
address moves, `ipnd` says what happened to that record.

- `applied`: you picked the address from `GET /addresses/search` and
  sent its `gnafId`. We are updating the record.
- `referred`: you typed the address in, so we cannot carry it into the
  record. Confirm the end user's emergency address yourself.
- `unchanged`: the service address did not move. A billing-only change
  never touches the record.

While a family violence safety record withholds the end user's
contacts, we make the change but do not return the addresses. An
archived end user is not changed. The call answers 409.

schema.description: Send at least one of the three. A field you leave out stays as it is.

gnafId.description: The address's id from `GET /addresses/search`, when picked from it.

billingSameAsService.description: True to send bills to the service address.

billingAddress.description: The billing address. Null is the service address.

contactsMasked.description: True when the addresses below are withheld by a family violence safety record.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

Returns the end user's default screening of international calls to
their lines. It also says whether they get billing texts, and whether
you bill them through the platform. The end user sees the screening on
their Profile page in the end-user portal.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Sets the end user's default for international calls to their lines. Use
it, for example, after a scam-call complaint. It screens incoming calls
only. It never affects an outgoing call, and never a 000 call. A field
you leave out stays as it is. An archived end user is not changed, and
the call answers 409.

`billingSms: false` stops their billing texts when they ask you to. The
switch on their page in the portal does the same. `true` starts them
again. Their billing emails still go.

`isBilled: false` stops billing them through the platform. Use it for an
end user you bill some other way. `true` bills them again from their
next bill. That bill covers its whole period, and never an earlier one.
While you bill your end users, `true` answers 422 until every service of
theirs has a retail price, a call plan or a markup that covers it. The
error says what to set.

`allowApiKeys: true` lets API keys limited to this end user work. You
make those keys under API Keys in the portal. `false` refuses every call
they make with `403 end_user_keys_off`. The keys are not revoked, and
they work again when you send `true`.

Each change is in your Audit Log.

get.description:

Lists your own notes on the end user, pinned first, then newest. The
Notes tab on their page in the portal shows the same. The end user never
sees them.

The webhook endpoints that this end user's own keys registered, oldest
first. They get only this end user's SMS and fax events. You can read and
remove them here, and nothing else. `GET /webhooks` lists only your own

A key limited to one end user can't call this. It manages its endpoints
under `/webhooks`.

deliveries settle without being sent, and we keep the delivery history.

end user's answers 404, the same as one that doesn't exist.

get.summary: List an End User's Safety Records
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:read

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** These are family violence
safety records under the Telecommunications (Financial Hardship and
Family Violence) rules (F2025L00664). Read the End users safety help
page before you use it.

Lists the end user's records, active first, then newest. Each record has
every field the portal shows.

post.summary: Raise a Safety Record on an End User
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:update

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Raises a safety record when the end user discloses domestic or family
violence. `suppressContactDisclosure` is on by default. While it is on,
we mask their contacts on every end-user read from then on, here and in
the portal. We audit the call, naming this key.

get.summary: Get an End User's Safety Record
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:read

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Returns one record, with the time and the person of each step. A step
taken by API names no person here. The audit log names the key.

patch.summary: Change an End User's Safety Record
patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:update

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Changes the record's fields. A field you leave out stays as it is. A
closed record is not changed, and the call answers 409.

post.summary: Confirm It Is Safe to Communicate
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:update

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Records that the person confirmed it is safe for them to communicate
(s8(1)). You can record support only after this. A closed record is not
changed, and the call answers 409.

>**Required Scope(s):** safety:update

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Records that the available support was explained to the person (s8(2)).
The call answers 409 until it is confirmed safe to communicate, and on a
closed record.

post.summary: Record Whether Further Support Is Wanted
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:update

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Records whether the person wants further information and support
(s8(3)). The call answers 409 until it is confirmed safe to communicate,
and on a closed record.

post.summary: Close an End User's Safety Record
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:update

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Closes the record. We never delete it. `retentionExpiresAt` is set to
the earliest date it may be disposed of (s31). A record that is already
closed is not changed, and the call answers 409.

post.summary: Reveal a Safety Record's Safe Contacts
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:read

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Returns the safe number, safe email and safe postal address that every
read of the safety record masks. We audit every call as a reveal of the
end user's contacts. The audit names this key, the record and the
contacts shown, never their values, whether or not any is recorded. A
closed record's safe contacts are revealed too, because we keep the
record until its retention date. Ask for them only when you need them
for the call in front of you.

id.description: The record's public id.

post.summary: Reveal an End User's Masked Contacts
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:read

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Returns the contacts a family violence safety record masks on every
other end-user read. We audit every call as a reveal that names this
key, whether or not anything was masked. No call shows these contacts
without this scope.

post.summary: Send an End User a Verification Code
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Sends a six digit code to the end user's own mobile (`sms`) or email.
You use it to check that the person you are talking to controls that
contact. You never supply the address. The code goes to the contact on
file. While a family violence safety record is active on the end user,
the code goes only to the record's agreed safe contact for that channel.
If there is none, nothing is sent and the call answers 422.

The SMS goes from one of your approved SMS senders. With more than one,
name it in `smsFrom`. The email goes in your branding.

The code is advisory. A right code records `lastVerifiedAt` on the end
user, and no other call needs it. The code expires in 10 minutes. We send
at most five codes to one end user in an hour, and the call answers 429
after that. We audit each send with the reason and this key's name,
never the code.

reason.description: Why the code is being sent, for the audit log.

smsFrom.description: The approved sender to send the SMS from, when you have more than one.

202.description: The code was sent.

destination.description: Where it went, masked, such as `*******001` or `j***@example.com`.

parameters.name: verificationId
parameters.description: The `verificationId` the send returned.

post.summary: Check an End User's Verification Code
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Checks the code the person read back. A right code answers
`verified: true` and records `lastVerifiedAt`. All of these answer the
same `verified: false`. They are a wrong code, a code already used, an
expired code, a code with five wrong tries, and an unknown verification.
We audit each check with its outcome and this key's name, never the
code.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

Lists the logins to the end user's own portal, and the invites not yet
accepted. The Logins card on their page in the portal shows the same.

post.summary: Invite a Login for an End User
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update, end-users:sign-in

Emails an invite, in your brand, to set up a login to the end user's
portal. A login is a way into the portal, so you need
`end-users:sign-in` as well as `end-users:update`. A portal session
needs both too. The call answers 422 when a login or an open invite
already has that email. It answers 409 when your end-user portal is off
or has no domain yet.

parameters.name: loginId
parameters.description: The login's `id`.

patch.summary: Change an End User Login's Role
patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update, end-users:sign-in

Changes the login's role. A role can widen a way into the portal, so you
need `end-users:sign-in` as well as `end-users:update`. Their portal
keeps an Owner while it has other logins. Taking the role from their
only Owner answers 422.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Removes the login. It can no longer sign in. Removing their only Owner
while other logins remain answers 422. Removing the last login of all is
allowed.

parameters.name: loginId
parameters.description: The login's `id`.

post.summary: Send an End User Login a Password Reset
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update, end-users:sign-in

Emails the login a password reset link, in your brand. Use it when the
end user is locked out. No call ever sets a password.

When we sent a link a moment ago, `sent` is false. That link is still
live, and we send no second one.

Where the end user has a family violence safety record, the link goes to
the safe contact on it, and `outcome` is `sent_to_safe_contact`. When
the agreed contact method allows no email, we hold the link. Then
`outcome` is `held`, `sent` is false, and we alert our staff to contact
them the agreed way.

It answers 409 when your end-user portal is off or has no domain yet.

parameters.name: inviteId
parameters.description: The open invite's `id`.

delete.summary: Revoke an End User Login Invite
delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Revokes an open invite. Its link stops working.

parameters.name: inviteId
parameters.description: The open invite's `id`.

post.summary: Resend an End User Login Invite
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update, end-users:sign-in

Sends an open invite again, with a fresh link.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

Lists the people the end user has authorised to act for them. Active
ones come first, then newest. Their page in the portal shows the same. A
revoked representative is kept as history and confers no authority.
Check this list before you act on the word of someone who says they
speak for the end user.

post.summary: Appoint a Representative for an End User
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Records someone the end user has authorised to act for them. Give at
least one area in `authorities`. `full` covers every area. We audit the
call, naming this key.

parameters.name: repId
parameters.description: The representative's `id`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Ends the representative's authority at once. We keep the record as
history. Revoking one that is already revoked changes nothing. A
representative of another end user answers 404.

>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Suspends the end user, as **Suspend** on their page in the portal does.
Use it for your own non-payment or abuse cases. Their voice services and
VPN seats are cut off. Their data services keep running, because only we
suspend a data service. When we suspend one, `suspensionTakesEffect` on
`GET /data/services/{ref}` says how soon. A 000 call still goes
through. An end user who is already suspended comes back as they stand.

- An end user on the Priority Assistance register is suspended too, with
  the `reason` you give. We record the suspension and its reason
  against their registration, naming your API key.
- An archived end user cannot be suspended. The call answers 409.

reason.description: Why, shown on the end user as `suspendReason`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Lifts a suspension you placed. It restores only what the suspension cut
off. A suspension Check Networks placed answers 409 until we lift it. An
end user that is not suspended comes back as it stands.

>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Archives a former end user. Their history stays, and their sign-in to
the end-user portal is closed. You can archive only when nothing is
live or owed. A live service, an open order, or a balance either way
answers 409, with each reason in `error.blockers`. A suspension Check
Networks placed also answers 409.

409.description: The end user cannot be archived yet.

blockers.description: What stands in the way, one sentence each. Absent for a refusal that is not about blockers.

error.reason: This end user cannot be archived yet.
blockers: They have 1 live service. Cease or move them first.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Brings an archived end user back as active. An end user that is not
archived comes back as it stands.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

Lists the services the end user owns. Each one comes with the billed
assignment it carries, and the numbers they hold. The list is not
paginated.

post.summary: Give an End User a Service
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Gives the end user one of your data services, trunks or numbers. A
service another end user holds moves to this one. The service then shows
in the end user's portal, and its charges and usage go on their bills.

This is a link on our side only. Nothing changes at the carrier, such as
the nbn end user of record. A cancelled data service, a terminated trunk
and another account's service answer 422. An archived end user takes no
service, and the call answers 409. Restore them first.

reference.description: A data service's service reference, a trunk's SIP username, or a number.

200.description: The service, now the end user's.

parameters.name: assignmentId
parameters.description: The assignment's `assignmentId` (a uuid), from `GET /end-users/{endUser}/services`.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Ends the assignment today. The end user is billed for it to the end of
today, on your calendar, and not after. The service itself is not
cancelled. An assignment that already ended, today or before, keeps its
end date, so calling this again changes nothing.

It works only for an account that bills its end users. Otherwise it
answers 404. An assignment of another end user answers 404 too.

post.summary: Sign an End User In to the End-User Portal
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:sign-in

Returns a link that signs one of the end user's logins in to your
end-user portal. The link opens the page you choose. That can be their
dashboard, their bills, one bill, one service or their support tickets.
Send the end user to it from your own app. For example, send them there
to pay by card or direct debit, which only the end-user portal takes.

The link works once, for 5 minutes, on your portal's own domain.
Opening it shows a page with a **Continue to your portal** button. Only
pressing the button uses the link. A mail scanner or link preview that
fetches the link leaves it working.

The link replaces the password only. When the login has two-factor on,
the portal asks for the code first, and no page opens until the end user
gives it. `twoFactor` tells you this.

It signs in as `portalUser`, one of the end user's active logins. See
List End-User Logins. There is no default, so always name the login.

With `returnUrl`, we send the end user there once they are signed in,
instead of to `landing`. If the portal asks for a two-factor code, that
comes first. `returnUrl` must be an `https` address on your own
website's host or your end-user portal's domain. Any other answers
`422`.

The call answers `403` with the code `no_end_user_portal_access` when
the end user cannot use the portal. That happens when the portal is off
or has no domain, the end user is archived, or they have no active
login. A `portalUser`, `invoiceId` or `assignmentId` that is not theirs
answers `422`.

We record each link in the end user's activity, naming the API key and
the login.

invoiceId.description: The bill to open, by its `id` (a ULID) on the end-user invoice calls. Required for `bill`, and we take it only with `bill`.

assignmentId.description: The service to open, by its `assignmentId` (a uuid) from List an End User's Services. Required for `service`, and we take it only with `service`.

portalUser.description: The login to sign in as, by its `id` (a uuid) from List End-User Logins.

returnUrl.description: Optional. Where to send the end user once signed in, instead of `landing`. An `https` URL on your own website's host or your end-user portal's domain.

url.description: Send the end user here. It works once.

portalUser.description: The login it signs in as.

twoFactor.description: Whether the portal asks that login for its two-factor code before the page opens.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

Lists every end-user import on the account, newest first. It includes
imports sent by API and imports uploaded in the portal, partners'
included.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:create

Makes many end users at once. It works as the portal's End User import
does, with the same checks, duplicate rules and welcome email. Send the
portal's CSV file as `file` (multipart), or the same columns as JSON
`rows`, up to 2,000 rows.

The columns are `name` (required), `type`, `business_name`, `email`,
`phone`, `external_ref` and `invite`. `type` is `residential` (the
default) or `business`. `business_name` is required for a business.
`external_ref` is your own reference. `invite` set to `yes` sends a
login invite to the end-user portal at `email`. In `rows` you can also
use the API's camelCase names, `businessName` and `externalRef`.

We skip a row (`skipped`) when an end user with its email is already
there. When the row has no email, we skip it when an end user has the
same name and external reference. We also skip a row when an earlier row
in the file is the same. A row that fails a check is `failed`, with the
reason. We still make the other rows.

`validateOnly: true` runs every check and makes nothing. This is the
portal's Check File. It answers `200` with what an import would do.
`sendWelcome: false` holds back the welcome email to each new end user.

We run up to 200 rows at once and answer `201` with each row's outcome.
We run more rows on the queue and answer `202` with the import
`processing`. Read it with `GET /end-users/imports/{importId}` until it
is `finished`, or `failed` if its run stopped part-way.

An `Idempotency-Key` is required. A retry with the same key answers the
first import and never imports the rows twice.

file.description: The CSV file, as the portal takes it. Up to 10 MB.

business_name.description: Required when `type` is `business`, as this or `businessName`.

businessName.description: The same as `business_name`, in the API's own case.

external_ref.description: Your own reference for the end user.

externalRef.description: The same as `external_ref`, in the API's own case.

invite.description: Send a login invite to `email`, which is then required.

200.description: What an import of these rows would do (`validateOnly`). Nothing was made.
