wouldSkip.description: Rows an import would pass over or fail.

201.description: The import, finished, with each row's outcome.

202.description: The import, processing on the queue.

parameters.name: importId
parameters.description: The import's id.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

Returns one import. You get its status, its counts and each row's
outcome. For each row you also get the end user made from it, and the
reason it was skipped or failed. The portal's import page shows the same.
An import of another account answers `404`.

post.summary: Create End Users from Xero Contacts
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:update, end-users:create

Creates an end user from each contact you name in your Xero organisation
(see Search Xero Contacts), as the portal's Create End Users from Xero
does. Each end user is linked to its contact. Each is a business, named
after the contact, with its email. It also gets its tax number when that
is a valid ABN. Each gets the welcome email, as any new end user does.
From then on, its invoices, credit notes and payments go to the contact.

We pass over a contact that is already linked to one of your end users,
archived in Xero, or not found, and list it in `skipped`. Sending the
same list again makes no second end user.

You can send up to 50 contacts a call. The call answers `409` while the
account has no working Xero connection.

We read the contacts from Xero one at a time, in the order sent. If Xero
fails part way, the end users already made stand, and each has had its
welcome email. The answer is still `201`. It lists them in `created`,
the failure in `error`, and the contact it failed on and every one after
it in `notTried`. Send the list again to finish, and we pass over the
ones already made. If Xero fails before any end user is made, the answer
is the error alone, as for any other Xero call.

201.description: The end users made, the contacts passed over, and any contacts not tried because Xero failed part way.

contactId.description: The Xero contact it was made from, and is linked to.

endUser.description: The new end user's number.

skipped.description: Contacts already linked, archived or not found.

notTried.description: When Xero failed part way, the contact it failed on and every one after it; empty otherwise.

error.description: Why Xero stopped part way; `null` when every contact was tried.

message.example: Xero could not answer just now: Service Unavailable

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** none; each type needs its own read scope

Finds the number, trunk, data service, order, end user, port, emergency
address, ticket or invoice for a phone number, email, name or
reference, in one call. It is the portal's header search, with the same
matches. You get up to 5 hits of each type, in the order of types below.

| Type | Matches | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `number` | the number in any format, or its alias | voice:read |
| `trunk` | its handle, alias or SIP username | voice:read |
| `dataService` | its service id, address, username or your reference | data:read |
| `order` | its PND, the carrier's ORD, or your reference | data:read |
| `endUser` | name, number, email or phone | end-users:read |
| `port` | its reference, the carrier's, or a number in it | voice:read |
| `emergencyAddress` | its label, customer name or street | voice:read |
| `ticket` | its reference or subject | tickets:read |
| `invoice` | its number (issued, paid or void) | billing:read |

Without `types`, we search every type the key holds the scope for and
leave out the rest. A type named in `types` without its scope answers
`403`, as does a key that holds none of these scopes.

A family violence safety record can withhold an end user's contact
details. You find that end user by name or number only, never by email
or phone, and a hit never shows a contact.

`href` is the API call that reads the hit. It is null where there is
none, which is the case for a port, a residential line, and an order not
yet placed with the carrier.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What to look for. At least 2 characters.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: The types to search, comma separated. Every type the key may read when left out.

200.description: The hits, grouped by type in the order above.

id.description:
How the API names it: the number, the trunk's SIP username,
the service id, the order id, the end user's number, the
port's reference, the emergency address id, the ticket
reference or the invoice id.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: The outage's or maintenance window's reference, as `GET /outages` returns it.

get.summary: Get an Outage affecting your Services
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

One outage or planned maintenance window that touches your account, in
the same shape as each item of `GET /outages`. It can be open, or
resolved within the register's retention period. One that does not touch
your account answers `404`, as an unknown reference does. The public
status site shows every outage on the register.

post.summary: Assign Services to an End User
post.description:
Links up to 100 of your data services to one end user in one call. Send
`endUser: null` to unlink them all. This is the portal's bulk **Assign
to End User** on the Data Services list. It follows the same rule and
makes the same audit entry for each service changed. The link is local.
It shows the service in the end user's portal and puts its charges and
usage on their bill. Nothing changes at the carrier.

Each service is answered on its own, in the order you sent them.

- `assigned`: now linked as asked (to the end user, or to none).
- `unchanged`: it already was.
- `notFound`: no service of yours has that reference. Another account's
  service is `notFound` too.

One unknown reference does not stop the rest. An end user that is not
yours, or is archived, refuses the whole call with a 422 and changes
nothing.

The `Idempotency-Key` is required, as on the other bulk writes. A retry
with the same key answers as the first call did.

endUser.description: The end user to link the services to, by its public number. Send null to unlink them. The field is required, so we never read an omitted field as "unlink".

services.description: The services, each by its product reference (an NBN PRI or an Opticomm product) or its service reference (an AVC), as `GET /data/services` returns them.

endUser.description: The end user the services were linked to; null when they were unlinked.

service.description: The reference as you sent it.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Returns where automated mail goes, and whether your residential end users
are sent data usage notices. Company Settings shows the same in the
portal.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Changes the notification address, the usage notices, or both. Only the
fields you send change. A sender must be one of `availableSenders`.

smsSender.description: If you leave it out, we keep the current sender.

200.description: The settings as they now stand.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Returns the end-user portal's name, colour, support details, ticket
switch, email logo position and logos. These are the same details
Portal Branding shows in the portal.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Send the branding fields you want to change. Only the fields you send
change, and the portal's rules apply to the result. The display name is
required, so set it with your first change. We refuse a brand colour
that has less than 4.5:1 contrast against white, and the error gives
its ratio. Set logos with `PUT /end-user-portal/logos/{variant}`. Each
change is in your audit log under this key's name.

200.description: The branding as it now stands.

parameters.name: variant
parameters.description: `light` is the main logo. It also appears on your end users' invoices. `dark` is the dark-mode logo.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Returns the stored logo image. It answers 404 when none is set.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Replace a logo. Send the image as the multipart field `logo`. The light
logo is PNG or JPEG, because it is also your invoice logo. The dark logo
is PNG, JPEG or WebP. We never accept SVG. We read the format from the
file's content, not its name. The size limit is the portal's, which is
1 MB unless we have told you otherwise.

200.description: The branding, with the new logo.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Remove a logo. Removing one that is not set does nothing. A variant
other than `light` or `dark` answers `404`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Returns the custom domain you claimed for your end-user portal, the DNS
records to publish and each record's last check. It answers 404 when you
have not claimed a domain.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Claim a hostname for your end-user portal. A new claim replaces any
earlier one. Publish the records in the response, then call
`POST /end-user-portal/domain/verify`. A hostname already in use on the
platform, or our own edge hostname, answers 422. An unverified claim
holds the hostname for seven days.

domain.description: A hostname, with no scheme or path.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Release the domain and any claim on it. The end-user portal stops
answering on it. Open end-user invites are revoked, because their links
use the domain. It answers 404 when you have not claimed a domain.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Limit: 5 per minute for the account (domain verify), as each call makes DNS lookups.

Checks the claimed domain's DNS records now. When both pass, the domain
is verified and the end-user portal answers on it. Otherwise the
response says which record is missing. It answers 404 when no claim is
waiting to be verified.

200.description: The claim after the check, passed or not.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Your own family violence statement, its support channels, its approval
and whether it is ready to publish, as the portal's Retail Settings
shows it. Approve and publish it in the portal, at `portalUrl`. Answers
`404` while the end-user portal is off on your account.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Saves the statement's text. A field you leave out keeps its value. Send
null or an empty string to clear one.

Approval belongs to the wording that was approved. Changing any of the
six wording fields revokes it and takes the statement off your portal
until it is approved and published again. `approvalRevoked` says when
that happened. `interimNotice` and `supportAvailableFrom` do not touch
approval.

200.description: The statement as it now stands.

approvalRevoked.description: This change revoked an approval and unpublished the statement.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Adds a way for an affected person to reach you, last in order. A web form
never counts as reaching a person, so `connectsToIndividual` is stored
false for one. Answers `404` while the end-user portal is off on your
account.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The channel's `id` (a uuid), as `GET /compliance/dfv-statement` lists it.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Removes a support channel. Answers `404` when your statement has no such
channel, or while the end-user portal is off on your account.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Your own complaints process, its contact details, its approval and
whether it is ready to publish, as the portal's Retail Settings shows
it. Approve and publish it in the portal, at `portalUrl`. Answers `404`
while the end-user portal is off on your account.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Saves the process. A field you leave out keeps its value. Send null or an
empty string to clear one.

Approval belongs to the summaries that were approved. Changing either
summary revokes it and takes the process off your portal until it is
approved and published again. `approvalRevoked` says when that happened.
The contact details do not touch approval.

`contactUrl` must be an `http` or `https` address, because we publish it
as a link.

200.description: The process as it now stands.

approvalRevoked.description: This change revoked an approval and unpublished the process.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns the card and direct debit charges we started on your account,
newest first. Your system can see a payment under way before it reaches
your balance. A direct debit stays in flight for a few business days.
Settled charges appear on List Payments as well.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `open` for the charges still in flight, or one settled status. Any other value answers `400`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns your statement for a period. It is the same statement the portal's
Statement page shows. It has the opening balance, then every invoice,
credit note, payment and reversal in date order with the running balance,
then the closing balance. Amounts include GST. A debit is what you owed us
more. A credit is a payment or credit note.

Dates are in your account's own time zone. Leave both out for the
portal's default period. A date that is not real, or a `from` after `to`,
answers `422`. Set `format=csv` for the portal's CSV export.

>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns your credit warning settings, as the portal's Credit Alerts page
holds them. They are whether warnings are on, the percentages of your
credit limit they are sent at, the channels, and who receives them. With
no recipients, warnings go to `fallbackEmail`, your billing contact.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Changes any of `enabled`, `thresholds` and `channels`. What you leave out
stays as it is. Thresholds come from `availableThresholds`. A setting the
portal would refuse answers `422`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Adds one person to receive credit warnings. Send `email` or `mobile`, not
both. A mobile that is not an Australian mobile answers `422`.

parameters.name: recipientId
parameters.description: The recipient's `id` (a uuid).

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Stops sending credit warnings to one recipient. A recipient that is not on
your account answers `404`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns the cards and direct debit authorities stored on your account, as
the portal's Payment Methods page lists them. Revoked ones are left out.
You add a method in the portal only, because it takes your card or bank
details on the payment provider's own page.

id.description: The method's public id.

autopayMethodId.description: The `id` of the method autopay charges, or null when autopay is off.

parameters.name: methodId
parameters.description: The method's `id` (a uuid) from List Payment Methods.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Removes a stored method, as the portal does. When it was the default,
another stored method becomes the default. A method that is not on your
account answers `404`. This never takes a payment.

parameters.name: methodId
parameters.description: The method's `id` (a uuid) from List Payment Methods.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Makes a stored method the default. A method that is not on your account
answers `404`. This never takes a payment.

200.description: The method, now the default, with the same fields as a List Payment Methods row, inside `result`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns every dispute you have raised on our invoices, newest first. While
invoice disputes are switched off, this answers `404`.

>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns the disputes on one invoice, and whether you can raise another. It
shows how much is still disputable and when the window closes. `refusal`
says why not when `canDispute` is false. While invoice disputes are
switched off, this answers `404`.

200.description: The disputes and what can still be disputed.

disputable.description: The most a new dispute may be for, with GST.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Disputes all or part of an invoice, or one line of it, as the portal does.
While the dispute is open, we hold the disputed amount off collection and
reminders, and we open a support ticket. Past the dispute window, or for
more than is disputable, this answers `422` naming `amount` or `reason`.
This never takes or refunds a payment.

amount.description: The amount disputed, with GST, up to two decimals.

lineId.description: The line disputed, by its `id` (a uuid) from the invoice's `lineItems`. Leave it out for the invoice as a whole.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns the groups that section our invoice to you, by name. Each group
prints as its own section with its PO number and subtotal. Lines in no
group print under Other.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Adds a group to our invoice. A name that is already used answers `422`.
Case does not matter. The group applies from the next invoice.

parameters.name: groupId
parameters.description: The group's `id` (a uuid).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns one group on our invoice, with the services in it.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Renames a group or changes its description, PO number or cost centre.
Only the fields you send change. The change applies from the next invoice.
Issued invoices keep the values they were issued with.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Removes a group with no services in it. A group that still has services
answers `422`. Move them to another group, or out of groups, first.

parameters.name: groupId
parameters.description: The group's `id` (a uuid).

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Makes the group's services exactly the list you send. A listed service
moves in from any other group, because a service is in at most one. A
service you leave off the list leaves its group and prints under Other.
An empty list empties the group. A service that is not on your account
answers `422`. The change applies from the next invoice.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns every live service on our invoice to you, with its invoice group
and its own billing label, PO number and cost centre.

parameters.name: serviceRef
parameters.description: The service's reference, as invoice lines' `serviceRef`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns one service's place on our invoice. A service that is not on your
account answers `404`.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Sets the service's own billing label, PO number and cost centre on our
invoice. Only the fields you send change. Null or blank clears one, and a
cleared PO or cost centre falls back to the group's. Place the service
in a group with `PUT /account/invoice-groups/{groupId}/services`. The
change applies from the next invoice.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Your partners' monthly commission runs, newest first, as the portal's
Partners page lists them. This is read only. Rates, finalising and
recording a payout stay in the portal. While partner commissions are
switched off, this answers `404`.

parameters.name: partner
parameters.description: One partner's user id. One that is not your partner answers `422`.

gstShown.description: Whether the portal shows these figures with GST.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: The run's `id` (a uuid).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

One run with its breakdown by client and product, and the clawbacks it
took. Another account's run answers `404`.

repayment.description: An invoice paid again after a clawback, earning its commission back.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Clawbacks still to come off your partners' commission.

parameters.name: partner
parameters.description: One partner's user id. One that is not your partner answers `422`.

parameters.name: partnerId
parameters.description: The partner's user id.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

One partner's commission rates: the default, any rate for a product type,
and any rate for one product. The most specific applies. A user who is
not your partner answers `404`.

>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Lists the invoices you issued to your end users, newest first. It
includes issued, paid and void invoices. An invoice held for approval is
on
[/end-users/invoice-approvals](#tag/End-User-Billing/operation/list_end_user_invoice_approvals)
until it is released. The invoices Check Networks issues to you are on
`/account/invoices`, and never here.

It answers 404 unless your account bills its end users.

`?format=csv` or `?format=ndjson` streams every matching invoice instead
of a page.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only this end user's invoices, by their number. An unknown number answers 422.

parameters.name: issuedFrom
parameters.description: Issued on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD. The day is the one the invoice shows, in the time zone it was cut in (its `timezone`). Send `CN-Time-Zone` to read the date in your own zone instead. You can leave either end open. A date that is not a real date, or a start after the end, answers `422`.

parameters.name: issuedTo
parameters.description: Issued on or before this date, the whole day included.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Invoice number contains this.

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: The end-user invoice's id.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns one invoice you issued to an end user, with its lines. It
answers 404 for an invoice Check Networks issued, a draft, an invoice
held for approval, or another account's invoice.

>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Downloads the PDF we sent the end user, under your brand.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Sends an issued or paid invoice again. It is the same email the bill run
sent. It goes to the end user's billing email address, or to their email
address if they have no billing one.

The call takes no address. A body that names one (`to`, `email`, `cc`,
`bcc` or `recipient`) answers 422, so an invoice never goes anywhere
else. You can resend an invoice three times an hour. A fourth resend
answers 422 and says when to try again.

For an end user with a family violence safety record, the email goes to
the safe email on that record. Where the method agreed with them does
not allow email, we send nothing and the call answers 422 saying so. We
tell our team to deliver the invoice the agreed way.

get.summary: List Payments on an End-User Invoice
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Lists the payments applied to this invoice, oldest first. Payments
settle an end user's invoices oldest first. One payment can therefore
be part-applied here and part to another invoice. `appliedToInvoice` is
this invoice's part. A payment that was later reversed is left off.

post.summary: Record a Payment on an End-User Invoice
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Records money the end user paid you outside the portal against an
issued invoice, as **Record Payment** does in the portal. It comes off
what they owe. Anything over the invoice's balance stays on their
account as credit. Send an `Idempotency-Key`. It names the payment, so a
retry with the same key records it once and answers 200 with
`duplicate: true`.

amount.description: Inc. GST, as a dollar string.

paidOn.description:
The day the money was received. It must be today or earlier,
on Brisbane's calendar. A later day answers 422 on `paidOn`.

amountDue.description: What is still owed on the invoice.
What is still owed on the invoice.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns how much of this invoice is left to credit. That is its total
less the credit notes already issued against it. It is zero on a void
invoice.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Issues a credit note against an issued or paid invoice. This is the one
way to correct an invoice, as **Credit** does in the portal. We raise
the credit note on our side, and the call answers 202. Once issued, it
is listed on
[/end-users/credit-notes](#tag/End-User-Billing/operation/list_end_user_credit_notes)
and we email it to the end user. Asking for more than is left to credit
answers 422 and names the amount left. 503 means billing could not be
reached, so retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

The decision is the API key's own. The key's scopes are its authority,
and the audit log names the key, not a user.

amount.description: Inc. GST, as a dollar string. At least 0.01.

reason.description: Printed on the credit note.

202.description: The credit note is being issued.

post.summary: Pause Payment Reminders on an End-User Invoice
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Pauses payment reminders for this issued invoice. We send none until
`until`, when reminders start again. The due date does not change, and
the invoice still shows as overdue. Pausing again replaces the date.

until.description: The day reminders start again. After today, on your calendar.

post.summary: Resume Payment Reminders on an End-User Invoice
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Lifts a pause at once. An invoice that is not paused comes back as it
is.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Lists the invoices the bill run held instead of sending, oldest first.
Each one is held because something on it had no price. While an invoice
is held, we post nothing to the end user's account and email nothing.
Release it as it stands, or price what is listed in `unpriced` and rerun
it.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Issues and sends a held invoice as it stands. What had no price is not
on it. The release runs on our side, and the call answers 202. The
invoice then appears on `/end-users/invoices`. An invoice that is no
longer held, or is already being released or rerun, answers 409. 503
means billing could not be reached, so retry. It is the API key's own
decision, and the audit log names the key.

202.description: Being released.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Rebuilds a held invoice with your current prices and sends it. If
something is still unpriced, we hold the invoice again. The rerun runs
on our side, and the call answers 202. An invoice that is no longer
held, or is already being released or rerun, answers 409. 503 means
billing could not be reached, so retry. It is the API key's own
decision, and the audit log names the key.

202.description: Being rerun.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Lists the credit notes you issued to your end users, newest first. The
credit notes Check Networks issues to you are on `/account/credit-notes`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only this end user's, by their number. An unknown number answers 422.

parameters.name: issuedFrom
parameters.description: Issued on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD. The day is the one the credit note shows, in the time zone it was cut in (its `timezone`). Send `CN-Time-Zone` to read the date in your own zone instead. You can leave either end open. A date that is not a real date, or a start after the end, answers `422`.

parameters.name: issuedTo
parameters.description: Issued on or before this date, the whole day included.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns one credit note you issued to an end user, with its lines.

>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Downloads the PDF we sent the end user.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.summary: Preview an End User's Next Invoice
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Shows what the bill run would put on this month's invoice if it ran now.
It is built from the bill run's own lines, and it saves nothing. Usage
runs to `usageTo`, so the figures can change before the invoice issues.
`held` says the bill run would hold the invoice for approval, with what
is `unpriced`.

A `status` other than `preview` says why there is nothing to show. The
month is already invoiced, there is nothing to bill, the end user is
suspended, or their final invoice has issued.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.summary: Check an End User's Final Invoice
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Checks whether the end user's final invoice can be issued now. It can
once every service assigned to them and every recurring charge of your
own has an end date. The usage window after the last of those dates must
also have passed. The window is three days by default, because usage
takes that long to arrive.

Otherwise `finalInvoiceReasons` says what is still open, each with a
stable `code`. `finalInvoiceEarliestDate` gives the earliest date it can
be issued, when that is known.

The codes are `final_invoice_already_issued`, `service_without_end_date`,
`charge_without_end_date`, `nothing_to_bill` and `usage_window_open`. We
may add new codes.

Sometimes your last invoice to the end user already billed everything
through the last end date, because the monthly bill run got there first.
Then `finalInvoiceAllowed` is true and `finalInvoiceReasons` holds one
reason, `already_billed_through_end`. Issuing makes no new invoice, and
marks the end user finally invoiced.

post.summary: Issue an End User's Final Invoice
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Bills the end user for everything since their last invoice, up to the
end of their last service or charge. It issues the invoice and emails
it now. The monthly bill run skips them from then on. You cannot undo
it. Correct it with a credit note.

It answers 201 with the invoice. The invoice `status` is `held` when
part of it had no price. Release or rerun a held invoice under
`/end-users/invoice-approvals`.

The call answers 422 when the invoice cannot be issued yet. The error
carries `reasons`, as the check above does, and `earliestIssueDate`. 503
means billing could not be reached, so retry. It is the API key's own
decision, and the audit log names the key.

When the last invoice already billed everything through the last end
date, we make no invoice. We mark the end user finally invoiced through
that date, and we refuse usage after it from then on. The answer is a
200 with `code` `already_billed_through_end` and a `message` saying so.

200.description: Nothing was left to bill. The end user is marked finally invoiced, with no new invoice.

finallyInvoicedThrough.description: The last service's end date, the day they are finally invoiced through.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Lists every invoice, payment, credit note and adjustment on the end
user's account between `from` and `to`, oldest first. The dates are on
your calendar. You also get the opening, running and closing balance.
The range defaults to the first of the month two months back, up to
today. The list pages by cursor. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor`
until it is `null`.

One request covers at most 12 months. `to` can be up to 12 months after
`from`, so 1 January to the next 1 January is the longest. A longer
range answers 400. Ask for it a year at a time.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

post.summary: Post an Adjustment to an End User's Account
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Changes what the end user owes without an invoice or credit note. Use
it, for example, to write off a small balance. A positive `amount` adds
to what they owe. A negative one takes off it and pays their oldest
unpaid invoice first. The amount includes GST. It shows on their
statement with your `reason`. Send an `Idempotency-Key`. It names the
adjustment, so a retry with the same key posts it once and answers 200.

amount.description: Signed, inc. GST, as a dollar string. Not zero.

date.description: The day it was posted, on your account's time zone.

balance.description: What the end user owes now.

date.description: The day it was posted, on your account's time zone.

balance.description: What the end user owes now.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:read

Lists your end users' financial hardship cases, newest first.
`assessmentDueBefore` lists the applications still to assess whose
deadline falls on or before that day.

**Your obligations.** A hardship case read or decided through the API
carries the same obligations under the Telecommunications (Financial
Hardship) Industry Standard 2024 as one in the portal. You are the end
user's supplier, and you are responsible for meeting them. They cover
the deadlines, the options you offer, and the notices.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only this end user's, by their number. An unknown number answers 422.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.summary: List an End User's Hardship Cases
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:read

Lists one end user's hardship cases, newest first.

**Your obligations.** A hardship case read or decided through the API
carries the same obligations under the Telecommunications (Financial
Hardship) Industry Standard 2024 as one in the portal. You are
responsible for meeting them.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

Records an arrangement agreed with the end user (`status: active`), or
an application to assess (`status: proposed`). An application has an
assessment deadline in business days on your calendar. We send the end
user the acknowledgement or the written confirmation under your brand,
as the portal does.

`options` must be ones you offer (`/retail/hardship-options`). A payment
plan needs `instalmentAmount` and `instalmentCount`. Fee or debt relief
needs `reliefAmount`.

An end user has one case at a time. While one is under assessment
(`proposed`) or `active`, opening another answers `409` and sends
nothing. Assess or close that case first.

An `Idempotency-Key` is required. A retry after a timeout replays the
first answer and never opens a second case or sends a second notice.

**Your obligations.** Opening a case through the API carries the same
obligations under the Telecommunications (Financial Hardship) Industry
Standard 2024 as opening it in the portal. You are responsible for
meeting them. We record the case as made by the user who created the
API key.

parameters.name: caseId
parameters.description: The case's `id` (a uuid).

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

Records the outcome of an application under assessment. Send `decision`
as `approve` to make it an active arrangement. We send the end user the
written confirmation. Send `decline` to close it. We tell the end user
the outcome. A case that is not under assessment answers 409.

**Your obligations.** An assessment made through the API carries the
same obligations under the Telecommunications (Financial Hardship)
Industry Standard 2024 as one made in the portal. You are responsible
for meeting them. We record it as the API key's own decision, with no
user.

parameters.name: caseId
parameters.description: The case's `id` (a uuid).

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

Closes a case as `completed`, `cancelled` or `declined`. A case that is
already closed answers 409.

**Your obligations.** Closing a case through the API carries the same
obligations under the Telecommunications (Financial Hardship) Industry
Standard 2024 as closing it in the portal. You are responsible for
meeting them. We record it as made by the user who created the API key.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:read

Returns the financial hardship assistance you offer your end users.

**Your obligations.** The Telecommunications (Financial Hardship)
Industry Standard 2024 applies to options set through the API as it does
in the portal. You are responsible for meeting it.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

Replaces the assistance you offer. Send at least six options, as s18(1)
of the Standard requires. Fewer is a 422. We store them in the
catalogue's order.

**Your obligations.** Setting these through the API carries the same
obligations under the Telecommunications (Financial Hardship) Industry
Standard 2024 as setting them in the portal. You are responsible for
meeting them.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:read

Lists the disputes your end users raised about charges on their
invoices, newest first. While a dispute is open, automatic payment does
not take the disputed amount, and payment reminders leave it out.

**Your obligations.** A dispute handled through the API carries the
same obligations as one handled in the portal. These are the
complaints-handling and financial hardship rules you are bound by as the
end user's supplier. You are responsible for meeting them.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only this end user's, by their number. An unknown number answers 422.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:read

Returns one dispute, with what the end user said and where your decision
stands.

**Your obligations.** A dispute handled through the API carries the
same obligations as one handled in the portal, and you are responsible
for meeting them.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

Shows the end user you are looking at an open dispute. The dispute stays
open, so the disputed amount is still held. The decision runs on our
side, and the call answers 202. A dispute that is not open answers 409.
503 means billing could not be reached.

**Your obligations.** A decision made through the API carries the same
obligations as one made in the portal. These are the complaints-handling
and financial hardship rules you are bound by as the end user's
supplier. You are responsible for meeting them. It is the API key's own
decision, and the audit log names the key.

202.description: The dispute, with the decision in progress.

post.summary: Credit and Resolve an End-User Dispute
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

Use this when the end user was right. We issue a credit note for
`amount` against their invoice, and the dispute is resolved. `amount` can
be up to the amount disputed.

The decision runs on our side, and the call answers 202. `resolution`
shows the outcome and the credit note. A resolved dispute, or one with a
decision already in progress, answers 409. 503 means billing could not
be reached.

**Your obligations.** A decision made through the API carries the same
obligations as one made in the portal, and you are responsible for
meeting them. We email the end user the decision. It is the API key's
own decision, and the audit log names the key.

amount.description: Inc. GST, as a dollar string.

notes.description: Shown to the end user with the decision.

202.description: The dispute, with the decision in progress.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

Resolves a dispute without a credit. Send `outcome` as `reject` when the
charge stands. Send `no_change` when nothing is owed either way, for
example when they withdrew it. Collection of the amount resumes.

The decision runs on our side, and the call answers 202. A resolved
dispute, or one with a decision already in progress, answers 409. 503
means billing could not be reached.

**Your obligations.** A decision made through the API carries the same
obligations as one made in the portal, and you are responsible for
meeting them. We email the end user the decision. It is the API key's
own decision, and the audit log names the key.

202.description: The dispute, with the decision in progress.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

Sends the last decision again, exactly as you asked for it. Use it after
`resolution.error` says the decision could not be completed. With no
failed decision to send, or one still in progress, it answers 409.

**Your obligations.** A decision made through the API carries the same
obligations as one made in the portal, and you are responsible for
meeting them.

202.description: The dispute, with the decision in progress.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Lists the groups that section the invoices you send this end user, by
name. Each group prints as its own section with its PO number and
subtotal. Lines in no group print under Other. It answers `404` unless
you bill your end users.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Adds a group to this end user's invoices. A name this end user already
uses answers `422`, ignoring case. The group applies from the next
invoice.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

parameters.name: groupId
parameters.description: The group's `id` (a uuid).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns one of this end user's groups, with the services in it.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Renames one of this end user's groups, or changes its description, PO
number or cost centre. Only the fields you send change. The change
applies from the next invoice. Issued invoices keep their values.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:delete

Removes one of this end user's groups that has no services in it. A
group that still has services answers `422`. Move the services first.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

parameters.name: groupId
parameters.description: The group's `id` (a uuid).

put.summary: Set End User Invoice Group Services
put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Makes the group's services exactly the list you send. It works as
`PUT /account/invoice-groups/{groupId}/services` does. You can list only
this end user's own services. Any other service answers `422`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Lists this end user's live services. Each one comes with its group and
its own billing label, PO number and cost centre on the invoices you
send.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns one of this end user's services and its place on their invoices.
A service that is not this end user's answers `404`.

put.summary: Set End User Invoice Service Details
put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Sets the service's own billing label, PO number and cost centre on this
end user's invoices. Only the fields you send change. Null or blank
clears one. The change applies from the next invoice.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns your markups and every product you have priced for your end users.
A product given to an end user bills at the first of these that applies:

1. The service's own price.
2. Its price here.
3. Its type's markup on what we charge you.
4. Your default markup.
5. Nothing. The end user's invoice is held for you to approve.

Only a call plan prices calls.

The call answers 404 unless your account bills its end users.

defaultMarkupPct.description:
Your default markup, a percentage of what we charge you.
Null when none is set.

markupsByType.description:
Your markups by product type (service category), each a
percentage of what we charge you. A type not listed uses
the default markup. Empty when none is set.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Sets or clears your default markup, your markups by product type, or
both. A product you have not priced bills at what we charge you plus
its type's markup, or else the default markup. With neither, a product
you have not priced bills nothing, and its end user's invoice is held for
you to approve. A price you set for a product or a service always wins
over a markup.

A call with no call plan bills at what we charged you for it plus its
call category's markup, such as `au_mobile_calls`, or else the default
markup. A call plan always wins. Send at least one of the two fields. A
field you leave out stays as it is.

While you bill your end users, clearing the default or a type's markup
is `422` on `defaultMarkupPct` when it would leave a live service of an
end user you bill with nothing to price it. The error counts those
services and names up to five. Nothing is changed. We check both fields
together, so a type's markup set in the same request counts.

defaultMarkupPct.description:
The markup, a percentage of what we charge you, as a number or
a numeric string ("30.00"), from 0 to 9999. Null clears it.

markupsByType.description:
Your markups by product type, the whole set. A type you leave
out, or send as null, uses the default markup. Key each markup
by the product's service category. Examples are `hosted_pbx`,
`data_and_internet`, `payg_sip_channels`,
`au_geographic_numbers`, `sms` and `au_mobile_calls`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Prices a product for your end users. The product must be one of ours on
sale, and not already in your book. If it is, change its price instead.

`price` and `setupFee` are **ex-GST** dollar amounts, as the portal takes
them. GST is added on the end user's invoice under your tax settings.

productId.description: The product's public id, as the unpriced queue and the price book return it.

price.description: The price each period, ex-GST, in dollars, up to two decimals.

setupFee.description:
The setup fee, ex-GST, in dollars. Leave it out, or send null,
for none set. 0 is a free connection.

effectiveFrom.description: The day the price applies from. It is today when you leave it out or send null.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: The price's `id` (a uuid), from the price book.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Changes a product's price. `price` is **ex-GST**. Every end user on the
product moves to the new price. There are no grandfathered prices. A
month already invoiced keeps what it was charged.

price.description: The price each period, ex-GST, in dollars.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:delete

Takes a product out of your price book. Its end users then bill at your
markup for its type, or else your default markup.

While you bill your end users, removing it is `422` on `itemId` when
nothing else would price a live service of an end user you bill. The error
counts those services and names up to five. Price them another way first,
or mark the service or the end user not billed.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: The price's `id` (a uuid), from the price book.

put.summary: Set a Product's Default Call Plan
put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Sets the call plan that prices a voice product's calls for end users whose
service has no plan of its own. It must be one of your own published call
plans. Send null to clear it.

While you bill your end users, clearing it is `422` on `planId` when no
markup would price those calls on a live service of an end user you bill.
The error counts those services and names up to five.

planId.description: The plan's `id` (a uuid) from List Retail Plans.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns the products you have given your end users that your price book
does not price. One billing at your default markup carries that price as
`proposedPrice`, which you can accept in one call. One that nothing prices
has `bills: false`. It holds its end users' invoices until you price it.

endUsers.description: How many live services of your end users are on it.

bills.description: True when it bills at your default markup. False when it holds invoices.

proposedPrice.description: The default markup's price, which becomes the product's price when you accept it. It gives the price ex-GST and its GST under the product's GST treatment. A GST-free product has no GST. It is null when nothing prices the product.

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: The product's `productId` (a uuid), from the queue.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Writes a queued product's proposed price into your price book from today,
as a price of your own. The proposed price is your default markup's. The
product leaves the queue. A product nothing prices has no proposal, so the
call is refused with 422. Price it with `POST /retail/price-book/items`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns a paginated list of your own call plans for your end users, by
name. Each comes with its versions and their state. The destinations of a
version are at
[List Plan Destinations](#tag/End-User-Call-Plans/operation/list_retail_plan_destinations).

This is only for an account that bills its end users. Otherwise it
answers `404`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to retrieve. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Number of plans per page. Defaults to `50`, maximum `200`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing call plans.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Creates a call plan as a draft, as the portal's New Plan page does. Pick
one of three modes:

- **`blank`** is an empty plan. Add destinations, or import a CSV.
- **`clone`** is a copy of a base card's version in effect, or its
  latest if none is in effect.
- **`margin`** works out your sell rates from a base card you are billed
  on, which gives your buy rates, with the `margin` you send. A `percent`
  margin marks up the connection fee too. A `fixed` margin adds to the
  per-minute rate only.

The base card is one from
[List Base Cards](#tag/End-User-Call-Plans/operation/list_retail_plan_base_cards).
It is one of your own plans, or a card you are billed on. Any other is
refused with `422`.

Nothing prices calls until you publish the draft with
[Publish a Call Plan](#tag/End-User-Call-Plans/operation/publish_retail_plan).

code.description: A code unique across all plans. Use letters, digits, underscore and hyphen. Leave it out, or send null, and we make one from your account number.

baseCardId.description: The card to start from, by its `id` from List Base Cards. Required for `clone` and `margin`.

margin.description: The margin over the base card. Send it with `margin` mode only. `value` is then required.

type.description: `percent` marks the per-minute rate and the connection fee up by `value` per cent. `fixed` adds `value` dollars to the per-minute rate.

value.description: Per cent for `percent`. Dollars per minute, ex-GST, for `fixed`. Up to 6 decimal places.

roundingStep.description: Sell rates round up to this step, in dollars, at most 5 decimal places. Defaults to `0.00001`.

minMargin.description: The least the per-minute sell rate is above the buy rate, in dollars ex-GST, applied after the markup.

201.description: The plan was created as a draft.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns the cards a new plan may start from, by name, in one response.
They are your own plans and the cards you are billed on. Pass one's `id`
as `baseCardId` to
[Create a Call Plan](#tag/End-User-Call-Plans/operation/create_retail_plan).

200.description: A JSON object containing the cards.

id.description: The card's public id.

ownPlan.description: True for one of your own plans. False for a card you are billed on.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The plan's `id` (a uuid).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns one of your own plans with its versions. `draftDrift` compares a
draft made from a rate deck with the deck's current buy rates, as the
portal's publish step does. It is null for any other plan. It is also null
when nothing is below cost.

Another account's plan, or a card that is not yours, answers `404`.

belowCost.description: Prefixes that sell below their buy rate.

belowFloor.description: Prefixes that sell above cost but below the margin floor.

orphaned.description: Prefixes with no buy rate in the deck.

acknowledgementNeeded.description: True when publishing needs `acknowledgeDrift: true`. That is when some prefix is below cost or below the floor.

buyPerMinuteExGst.description: The deck's buy rate per minute, ex-GST.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Changes the plan's name, code, description or currency. Send only the
fields to change. These belong to the plan, not a version. So the change
is live at once and opens no draft.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The plan's `id` (a uuid).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns a paginated list of one version's destinations, by name then
prefix. Without `version`, you get the working version. That is the draft,
or else the version in effect, or else the latest.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version number. An unknown one is refused with `422`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Only destinations whose name or prefix matches.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to retrieve. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Number of destinations per page. Defaults to `50`, maximum `200`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing destinations.

version.description: The version listed. It is null for a plan with no version yet.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Adds a destination to the plan's draft. When the plan has no draft, we
open one first as a copy of its latest version, because a published
version never changes. A prefix already on the draft is refused with
`422`.

Rates are dollar amounts, **ex-GST**, to at most 5 decimal places.

connectionFee.description: The charge for each answered call, ex-GST. Defaults to `0`.

minimumCharge.description: The least an answered call costs, ex-GST. Defaults to `0`.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The plan's `id` (a uuid).

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Loads a CSV into the plan's draft, opening the draft first when there is
none. The file has the portal's columns, with a header row, in any order:

```
name,prefix,per_minute_rate,connection_fee_rate,minimum_charge_rate,first_increment_seconds,subsequent_increment_seconds
Australia Mobile,614,0.03,0.05,0,60,60
```

`name`, `prefix` and `per_minute_rate` are required on each row. The fee
and minimum default to `0`, and the increments to `60`. Rates are dollars,
**ex-GST**, to at most 5 decimal places. The file can have at most 20,000
rows.

The import is all or nothing. A file with any bad row is refused with
`422`, which names the first ten bad lines. The draft is left as it was.

`mode` is `replace` or `merge`. With `replace`, the draft becomes exactly
the file. With `merge`, the file's rows are added, or replace those with
the same prefix, and the rest stay.

200.description: The file was loaded into the draft.

importedVersion.description: The draft the file was loaded into.

destinationCount.description: The draft's destinations after the import.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The plan's `id` (a uuid).

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: The destination's prefix, which names it on every version.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Changes a destination on the plan's draft, opening the draft first when
there is none. Send only the fields to change. The prefix cannot change.
Remove the destination and add the new prefix instead. A prefix not on the
working version answers `404`.

Rates are dollar amounts, **ex-GST**, to at most 5 decimal places.

connectionFee.description: The charge for each answered call, ex-GST.

minimumCharge.description: The least an answered call costs, ex-GST.

200.description: The destination as changed, on the draft.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Removes a destination from the plan's draft, opening the draft first
when there is none. The published versions keep it until the draft is
published. A prefix not on the working version answers `404`.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The plan's `id` (a uuid).

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Publishes the plan's draft as a version that never changes. It prices
calls from `effectiveFrom`, which is today when you leave it out, for
every service on the plan. A published version it replaces from that date
is marked `superseded`. It still prices the calls made before that date.

The call answers `422` in these cases:

- The plan has no draft, or the draft has no destinations.
- The draft was made from a rate deck and prices some prefix below
  the deck's buy rate or below its margin floor, and `acknowledgeDrift`
  is not `true`. See `draftDrift` on
  [Get a Call Plan](#tag/End-User-Call-Plans/operation/get_retail_plan).

effectiveFrom.description: The date the version prices calls from. It defaults to today when you leave it out or send null.

acknowledgeDrift.description: Publish although the draft prices below cost or below its floor.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

parameters.name: assignmentId
parameters.description: The service's `assignmentId` (a uuid), from List an End User's Services.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns the service's billing. You get the call plan pinned to the
service, its own price and setup fee, and whether it is billed. You also
get the price that will bill, and where that price comes from. It
answers 404 unless your account bills its end users.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Sets all four fields at once, as the portal's Service Billing dialog
does.

- `planId` is one of your own published call plans, or null for the
  product's default plan. Any other plan answers 422, and nothing
  changes.
- `price` and `setupFee` are this service's own price each period and
  setup fee. Both are **ex-GST** dollar amounts. Null goes back to your
  price book. 0 is free. The most is 999,999.99. A month already charged
  keeps its price.
- `notBilled` set to true leaves the whole service off the end user's
  invoices, with its fees and its usage. This starts from the next
  invoice we build.

While you bill this end user, clearing `price` or `planId` answers 422
on `price` when nothing else would price the service. Your price book, a
markup or a call plan could do that. Nothing changes. We check the four
fields together, so clearing the price with `notBilled` true is
allowed.

planId.description: The plan's `id` (a uuid) from List Retail Plans.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

parameters.name: assignmentId
parameters.description: The service's `assignmentId` (a uuid), from List an End User's Services.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Ends the end user's billing for the service today, on your account's
calendar. The end user is billed to the end of today and not after. We
do not cancel the service itself.

A service whose billing has already ended, today or before, keeps its
end date, so calling this again changes nothing.

200.description: The service's billing, with its end date.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.summary: List an End User's Own Charges
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Lists your own charges on the end user's bill, newest first, in one
response. It answers 404 unless your account bills its end users.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Adds a recurring or once-off charge to the end user's next bill. Send an
`Idempotency-Key`, so a retry does not add it twice.

`amount` is an **ex-GST** dollar amount, from 0.01 to 999,999.99. The
portal's form takes it the same way. We add GST on the invoice.

A recurring charge that starts in an earlier month must say what to do
with the months since then. Nothing back-bills by default. `billing`
`start` bills every month since `startsOn`. `billing` `later` bills from
`billFrom`, and it does not bill again the months you billed elsewhere.
Leaving `billing` out for such a charge answers 422. A charge that
starts this month or later bills from its start.

An archived end user answers 422.

amount.description: Ex-GST, in dollars, up to two decimals.

startsOn.description: The start date (recurring) or the date of the charge (once-off).

endsOn.description: Recurring only. The last day it bills.

billing.description: Recurring only. Required when `startsOn` is in an earlier month.

billFrom.description: With `billing` `later`, the first day to bill from. Not before `startsOn`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

parameters.name: chargeId
parameters.description: The charge's `id` (a uuid).

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Changes the fields you send. The rest stay. `amount` is **ex-GST**.

Once an invoice carries the charge, these limits apply.

- A **once-off** charge can no longer change. The call answers 422.
- A **recurring** charge can change only its `description`, `amount`
  (for months not yet charged) and `endsOn`. Sending `startsOn`,
  `billing` or `billFrom` answers 422.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:delete

Removes a charge that no invoice carries. An invoiced charge answers 422.
To end a recurring one, use `PATCH` with `endsOn` instead.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns the settings printed on every invoice to your end users. They are
the name and ABN you bill as, default payment terms and delivery, the copy
address, summary or detailed format, the number prefix and next number,
and how end users pay you outside a gateway.

This is only for an account that bills its end users. Otherwise it
answers 404.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Changes any of your end-user invoice settings. Send only the fields to
change. Send null to clear a field that can be blank. The next end-user
invoice uses the new values.

The running invoice number changes only when you send
`invoiceNextNumber`. Each bill run moves it on, so a PATCH of any other
field never winds it back.

abn.description: 11 digits that pass the ATO check digit. Spaces are allowed.

bpayBillerCode.description: Your own BPAY biller code, 3 to 10 digits. Spaces are allowed and removed, so `12 3456` is stored as `123456`.

200.description: The settings saved, all of them.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns when your end users are reminded of an overdue invoice. Company
Settings → Payment Reminders sets it in the portal.

This is only for an account that bills its end users. Otherwise it
answers 404.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Sets the whole schedule. Days are from 1 to 365, and the final notice
must come after the first reminder. The change applies from the next
nightly reminder run. We record it in your audit log, as we do a change
in the portal.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns the notices your end users receive that you may reword. They are
the compliance notices, such as complaints, and the end-user billing
emails. Company Settings → Notice Wording lists them the same way. You
get them all in one response, because the list is not paginated.

This is only for an account that bills its end users. Otherwise it
answers 404.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The notice's key, from List Notices.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns one notice's subject and body in effect, in Markdown, and the
Check Networks default wording.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Saves your own subject and body, in Markdown, for a notice. We check the
wording as the portal does. A 422 lists each problem. The wording is
refused when it does any of these:

- It drops a placeholder in `requiredContent`.
- It uses a placeholder the notice does not offer.
- It types a working-days timeframe as text where the notice has a
  placeholder for it.

We add a notice's statutory footer on every send. You cannot change it. To
test a notice, send it to yourself from the portal.

body.example:
Hi {{ customer_name }},

Invoice **{{ invoice_number }}** is attached.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Removes your own wording, so we send the notice with the Check Networks
default. A notice you have not reworded is unchanged.

200.description: The notice, back on the default wording.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns whether each payment gateway you take your end users' payments
through is connected and working. The gateways are Stripe, Square and
GoCardless. It also says which payment methods each is on for. You get one
row per gateway, connected or not. Use it to spot a broken gateway before
your end users fail to pay.

We check keys when they are saved in the portal or a gateway is switched
back on. This read does not call the gateway. No key, webhook secret or
callback address is returned. Connecting, changing and removing a gateway
stay in the portal.

This is only for an account that bills its end users. Otherwise it
answers 404.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns how much of the monthly spend limit you set on an end user is
used this month. You get the limit, the amount spent so far with and
without GST, the per cent, and the alert tiers already reached. The
amount spent is the end user's Next Bill Estimate. Their spend alert
emails and your portal show the same figure. Once the month's invoice is
issued, the estimate starts again from nothing.

An end user with no limit answers `result: null`. Set the limit on the
end user. `endUser.spendThreshold` tells you as each tier is reached.

200.description: The end user's spend this month.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.summary: List an End User's Own Usage
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Lists the usage you rated yourself for one end user, newest usage first.
Each record says whether it is billed yet. This works only for an
account that bills its end users.

parameters.name: billed
parameters.description: `true` for billed records only, `false` for those still to bill.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first usage date to list.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The last usage date to list.

200.description: A page of the end user's usage records.

post.summary: Add Own Usage for an End User
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Adds one record of usage you rated yourself, such as managed-service
hours, seats or a third-party feed. We bill it on the end user's next
invoice, at your unit price ex GST. It is locked once a held or issued
invoice carries it.

The call is refused when the usage date is in the future, or in a bill
period the end user already has a held or issued invoice for. It is also
refused for a `reference` you already added on your account.

Once the end user is finally invoiced, a usage date after their last end
date is refused too, because no invoice would bill it. The error says
"This end user has had their final invoice, so usage after ... can't be
added."

An `Idempotency-Key` is required. A retry with the same key returns the
first answer and never adds the record twice.

post.summary: Add Own Usage in a Batch
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Adds up to 500 records of usage you rated yourself, across your end
users. Each row names its end user.

It is all or none. If we refuse any row, nothing is added. The `422`
names every bad row by its index from 0 (`rows.3.reference`). The rules
for each row are those of `POST /end-users/{endUser}/usage`. We refuse a
reference repeated within the batch too.

An `Idempotency-Key` is required. A retry with the same key returns the
first answer and never adds the batch twice.

endUser.description: The end user's number.

201.description: Every record was added, in the order sent.

parameters.name: usageId
parameters.description: The usage record's `id` (a uuid).

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:delete

Removes a record that no held or issued invoice carries yet. A billed
record is refused with `422`. Correct the invoice with a credit note
instead.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:read

Shows whether your own Xero connection works, and why an end-user
invoice, credit note or payment has not reached Xero. It lists the
mapping problems still to fix and how many entries are waiting, waiting
on a contact or failed. It also gives the last push and the last error.
It answers whether or not Xero is connected.

This is for an account that bills its end users. Any other account gets
`404`. Connect and disconnect Xero from Integrations in the portal,
because both need a browser sign-in to Xero.

>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:read

The end-user ledger entries behind one of the counts in Get Xero Status,
newest first. Each shows the end user, the invoice, credit note or
payment it is for, and why it is not in Xero. Pick the list with `state`.

  - `waiting`: not tried yet. The nightly push, or Send to Xero, sends them.
  - `unmatched`: the end user has no Xero contact yet. Link one with Link
    Xero Contact, or create one.
  - `partial`: sent in part. The next push finishes them.
  - `failed`: Xero refused them, and `reason` says why. Fix it in Xero or
    here, and the next push tries again.

Answers `409` while the account has no working Xero connection.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Which list.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to retrieve. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Number of entries per page. Defaults to `50`, maximum `200`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:read

The accounts and tax rates your end-user documents go to in Xero, the
choices your chart of accounts offers for each, and what still stops a
push.

The call answers `409` while the account has no working Xero connection.
It answers `502` when we cannot read Xero just now.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:update

Chooses the accounts and tax rates your end-user documents go to, as Save
does on Integrations → Xero in the portal. Only the mappings you send
change. Send `null` or `""` to clear one.

Each value must be one your chart of accounts offers for that kind of
mapping today. See `choices` in Get Xero Mapping. We read your chart from
Xero again first. Any other value answers `422` and nothing is saved.

The answer is the mapping as saved, with `problems` listing what still
stops a push. The call answers `409` while the account has no working
Xero connection.

products.description: A sales account by product ID.

charges.description: A sales account by your own charge's ID.

pushPayments.description: Send payments you record to Xero too.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:update

Sends what is waiting to Xero now, rather than at the nightly push. It is
the same push as Send Now in the portal. It also retries anything failed,
sent in part or waiting on a contact.

The push is queued and the call answers `202` at once. Get Xero Status
shows the counts and any error once the push has run, usually within a
minute. A second call while one is queued is the same push. The account's
Audit Log records each call against the API key that made it.

The call answers `409` while the account has no working Xero connection.
It answers `503` when we could not queue the push just now. Nothing was
sent, so call again shortly.

202.description: The push is queued.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:read

Contacts in your Xero organisation, to link an end user to. With
`search`, you get the contacts whose name matches. Without it, you get a
page of 100 in name order. `endUser` names the end user already linked to
a contact.

The call answers `409` while the account has no working Xero connection.
It answers `502` when we cannot read Xero just now.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: A name, or part of one.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Without `search`, which page of 100. Defaults to `1`.

id.description: The contact's Xero ID. Link it with Link Xero Contact.

status.description: Xero's status for the contact, `ACTIVE` or `ARCHIVED`.

endUser.description: The number of your end user already linked to this contact.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:update

Links an end user to a contact in your Xero organisation. Their
invoices, credit notes and payments then go to that contact. Entries
waiting on a contact for them are sent on the next push.

- Send `contactId` to link a contact you chose. See Search Xero
  Contacts. A contact Xero does not have answers `422`.
- Send `create: true` to create them in Xero instead. As the portal
  does, a contact with their number, or exactly their name, is linked
  and no second one is made. An archived contact answers `422`.

It answers `409` while the account has no working Xero connection.

contactId.description: The Xero contact's ID. Needed unless `create` is `true`.

create.description: Create the end user as a new Xero contact.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:update

Removes an end user's link to their Xero contact. The next push matches
them again, by their number and then exactly by name. Otherwise it waits
for you to choose a contact. Nothing already in Xero changes.

200.description: The end user, now with no contact.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Pauses a trunk at once, as the portal's Suspend Trunk does. You might use
it to stop a compromised PBX. A suspended trunk makes and receives no
calls. New outbound calls are refused, and calls to its numbers are
refused before they reach your PBX. It **still places 000 (and 112 and
106) calls**. For an hour after one, calls to its numbers are delivered
so the emergency service can call back. Its PBX stays registered, calls
already up carry on, and billing is unchanged.
`POST /trunks/{username}/resume` reverses it.

Suspending a trunk that is already suspended answers `200` with the trunk
as it stands. The trunk then reads `status: suspended` and, when you
suspended it, `suspendedBy: account`.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Resumes a trunk you suspended, as the portal's Resume Trunk does. You can
resume only your own pause. A trunk Check Networks suspended answers
`409` with the reason. It reads `suspendedBy: checkNetworks`, for example
for non-payment. It stays suspended until we lift the hold.

Resuming a trunk that is already active answers `200` with the trunk as it
stands.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Cancels the plan or channel change booked for the trunk's next billing
cycle, which is its `pendingPlanChange`. The portal's Cancel does the
same. The next cycle keeps the trunk's current plan. The call answers
`404` when nothing is booked. We send a `trunk.planChangeCancelled` event.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's SIP digest username.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** secrets:read

Returns a trunk's current SIP username and password. Use it to set up a
PBX on an existing trunk without rotating its password.

Reading a secret has its own scope. `voice:read` does not reveal it. We
record each reveal in the trunk's history with the API key that read it,
as we do for a reveal in the portal. We never record the password itself.

A cancelled trunk answers 404. So does a trunk whose password cannot be
read back. Rotate it to get a new one.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's handle, as the portal shows it. A trunk with no credential has no SIP username yet. A SIP username is accepted too, but it answers 409, because that trunk already has a credential.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Gives its first SIP credential to a trunk that was set up without one,
which is an IP-only trunk. It can then register. We set the username and
password. We return the password **only once**, in the `201` answer, as
on a new trunk.

A trunk that already has a credential answers 409. Rotate its password
instead. A cancelled trunk answers 422. Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a
retry replays the first answer.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's SIP digest username.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Rolls a new, generated SIP password onto the trunk's credential and
returns it **once**. The username does not change.

**The old password stops working at once.** A PBX still using it fails
its next registration or call until it has the new one.

Send an `Idempotency-Key`. A retry with the same key replays the first
answer, with the same password, rather than rotating twice. A cancelled
trunk answers 422.

200.description: The trunk's SIP credential with its new password.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's SIP digest username.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns where the trunk's SIP credentials may be used from: source
addresses and countries. Both lists empty means no restriction.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Replaces both lists. Send both every time. Empty lists lift every
restriction you set. The change reaches the SBC on its next policy
reload. We record it in the trunk's history, with the entries it removed.

Entries Check Networks added, for example to stop fraud, are returned in
the lists but are not yours to remove. A replace keeps them, so they are
still in the lists it returns. Contact support about one.

Addresses must be public. Private, CGNAT and reserved ranges are refused.
A refused entry answers 422 naming the entry and its place in the list,
for example `cidrs.1` or `countries.0`. Nothing is changed.

A typo must not lock you out. So a `cidrs` list that is not empty and does
not hold the address this request came from answers 422 on `cidrs`,
naming the address. Nothing is changed. A source in an allowed country is
still accepted, but the check does not look the country up. Send
`confirmLockout: true` to save the list anyway. Empty lists always go
through.
