cidrs.description: Source addresses or CIDR ranges: IPv4 no wider than `/24`, IPv6 single hosts only.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, in any case.

confirmLockout.description: Save a `cidrs` list that leaves out the address this request came from. Without it, that list answers 422.

200.description: The source restrictions now in force.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update, and voice:delete for `release`

Releases, routes or re-addresses up to 100 numbers in one call. Each number
goes through the same checks as the single call and gets its own result.
One refused number never stops the rest.

- `release` works as `DELETE /numbers/{number}`, which says what a release
  does. Billing stops. The number cools off for 30 days before anyone
  can order it. The API has no undo. We skip a number Check Networks has
  suspended, one a trunk presents as its default caller ID, and one whose
  release is already asked for. Its result gives the reason. Each release
  then runs shortly after, as a single one does.
- `route` sends every number straight to `trunk`, a `sipUsername`. Each
  number gets its own routing, so the rest of its block is untouched. This
  replaces any failover, time-of-day or geographic routing the number had.
- `emergencyAddress` lists every number at `emergencyAddressId`. A spare
  number takes it at once. For a number in use, we change its IPND record
  shortly after, as with `PATCH /numbers/{number}`.

We skip a number that is not yours. `Idempotency-Key` is required. Without
one the call answers `400`. A retry with the same key returns the first
call's job instead of releasing or routing again.

The call does the work before it answers. It answers `202` with the job,
`done`, and every number's result. Read it again with
`GET /numbers/bulk/{jobId}`. We save the job as each number is done. A
call that stops part way leaves a job that reads `running`, with the
results of the numbers it reached.

numbers.description: The numbers, E.164 (`61299999999`, with or without `+`).

trunk.description: The trunk's `sipUsername`. Required for `route`, and only for `route`.

emergencyAddressId.description: One of your emergency addresses. Required for `emergencyAddress`, and only for `emergencyAddress`.

202.description: The job, with each number's result.

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: The `jobId` from `POST /numbers/bulk`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns what a `POST /numbers/bulk` call did to each number.

get.summary: Find the Numbering Area for an Address
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the numbering areas (SZUs) that serve a street address, best match
first. The portal's Order Numbers page finds them the same way. Use it to
order a local number for a customer's address. Search for the address with
`GET /addresses/search` and send its `fullAddress` as `address`. Pass the
first `szu` to `GET /numbers/available`.

This can take up to a minute. If the address is refused, the call answers
`422` with the reason. If the areas cannot be looked up just now, it
answers `503`.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: The `fullAddress` of a `GET /addresses/search` result.

200.description: The areas serving the address, best first. Empty when none was found.

percentMatch.description: How well the area matches the address, in percent.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns up to five numbers you can order now. For a block, it returns the
block you would get. Each comes with its monthly and setup price per
number, as the portal's Order Numbers page shows them. Our own stock comes
first. If we hold none for an Australian geographic number, you get an
`offer` instead. It reserves nothing until you order it with its
`offerId`. An offer is never made inside a bundle.

To reserve a single number of ours, hold it with `POST /numbers/holds`,
then order it.

parameters.name: szu
parameters.description: The numbering area, from `GET /numbers/areas`. Required for `fixed` and `nz_geographic`.

parameters.name: blockSize
parameters.description: `1`, or `10` or `100` consecutive numbers for a geographic type.

parameters.name: bundle
parameters.description: The bundle you will order into. Only numbers we hold are offered. A bundle that has been submitted answers `422`.

200.description: What you can order now. An empty `results` means nothing is available in this area.

blocksInStock.description: How many complete blocks we hold; null for a single-number search.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Holds one of our numbers from `GET /numbers/available` (a `stock` single)
for 24 hours while you finish the order. Picking a number in the portal
does the same. Nobody else can take it while it is held. Order it with
`POST /numbers` and the `holdId`. A hold cannot be extended. Once
`heldUntil` passes, the order answers `422` with the code `hold_expired`.
You can hold the number again if it is still free.

Your account may hold 50 numbers at once, counting numbers being
ordered. A hold past that answers `409` saying so. It keeps answering
that until one of them is ordered or its hold ends. Ask us if you need
more. A `409` also means somebody else has just taken the number.

201.description: The number is held for you.

holdId.description: The hold, to order the number by.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns your number orders, newest first. Each comes with its status, its
numbers once allocated, and its error if it failed.

>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns one number order. It is the `Location` an order answers with. Poll
it until it leaves `pending`. A `completed` order has each number and its
route. A `failed` order has `error`. An order in a bundle is `draft`
until the bundle is released.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Looks up a batch of Australian numbers, as the portal's Number Lookup
does. For each number it returns who it was assigned to, who serves it
now, its numbering area, whether it is already porting and whether we
already hold it. Use it as the first step of a port, before you ask the
end user for paperwork.

It only reads. A suspended account can still call it, as it can any
`GET`.

Each number counts against your account's daily lookup allowance. The
portal uses the same allowance. We refuse a batch that would go over it
whole, with `429`. The allowance is in `error.allowance`, and
`Retry-After` is the seconds until it resets at midnight Brisbane time.

429.description: Over the daily lookup allowance (`error.allowance`), or over the limit of requests per minute. Wait for `Retry-After` seconds.

error.reason: You have used 990 of your 1,000 daily number lookups, and this batch asks for 25 more. The allowance resets at midnight.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns every number port on your account, in and out, newest request
first, as the portal's Number Ports page lists them. A port-out
(`direction: out`) is a number leaving you for another carrier. It takes
its customer's calls with it when it goes. Filter on `direction=out` to
watch them.

You can filter by these:

- `direction`.
- `group`, which is the portal's tabs: `active`, `completed` and
  `rejected`.
- `state`.
- `number`, which is any number on the port, including one inside a CAT C
  range.
- `needsAttention=true`, which is ports stalled past their step's usual
  time, or past a date they carry. That is a cutover that passed or a
  verification code that lapsed.

For a download, set `format=csv` or `format=ndjson`. The response streams
every matching port instead of paged JSON, and `page` and `perPage` are
ignored. `csv` has the portal's export columns: `reference`, `requested`,
`direction`, `numbers`, `state`, `losing_provider`, `end_user`,
`scheduled_for` and `completed`. Dates are on your account's calendar. So
`group=active&format=csv` is the portal's export of its Active tab.
`ndjson` is one `results[]` item per line.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The portal's tab. `active` is ports in flight. `completed` is `activated` and `ported_away`. `rejected` is `rejected` and `cancelled`.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Ports carrying this number, in E.164 or national form.

parameters.name: needsAttention
parameters.description: `true` for only the ports that need a person to look at them (see `attention`).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Bulk export format. Leave it out for paged JSON. `csv` or `ndjson` streams every matching port as a download.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to retrieve. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Number of records per page. Defaults to `50`, maximum `200`.

200.description: A page of ports, or the download.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`: a header row with the portal's export columns, then one row per port.
Present only when `format=ndjson`: one JSON object per line, each identical to a `results[]` item.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Asks for numbers to be ported to you from another carrier. It is the
portal's port request form, with the same checks and the same refusals.

- `portType` picks the kind of port. `CatA` is one fixed-line number.
  `CatC` is a list of fixed-line numbers. An entry ending `#` is a range
  of 10, and `##` is a range of 100. `Mob` is one mobile number.
  `Inbound` is one 13, 1300 or 1800 number. Every type but `CatC` takes
  one number.
- `trunk` and `emergencyAddressId` are where the numbers land when the
  port completes. `trunk` is a `sipUsername` from `GET /trunks`.
  `emergencyAddressId` comes from `GET /emergency-addresses`.
- Attach the most recent bill from the losing provider as a PDF of up to
  8 MB. Send the request as `multipart/form-data` to attach it. Every
  port needs the bill except a prepaid mobile one. For that, the holder's
  `dateOfBirth` is the proof instead.
- A mobile port needs `accountType`. Send `postpaid` with the losing
  carrier's `accountNumber`, or `prepaid` with `dateOfBirth`.
- You must accept `consents.portingAuthority` and `consents.terms`.
  `consents.authorisedAgent` is recommended. We record your API key as
  the one who gave the consents, under the name it had then. We do not
  record a user.
- To have the number's holder give the Porting Authority instead, send
  `authorityHolder` with their `name` and `email`. Leave out
  `consents.portingAuthority`. This works for any port but `Mob`. We save
  the port in `awaiting_authority` and email the holder a link on your
  end-user portal. The link is `confirmAuthority` on
  `/ports/{reference}/delegations`. Their confirmation, with their name
  and position, becomes the port's Porting Authority and covers the Agent
  Authority. The port then moves to `requested` and we lodge it. We
  remind them after 7 days. We cancel the port after 14 days without a
  confirmation. An account with no end-user portal gets a `403` with
  `no_end_user_portal_access`.

A mobile port sends a verification code to the number straight away.
Confirm it with `POST /ports/{reference}/confirm` within 30 minutes.
`verificationCodeSent: false` means we could not send it yet. Send one
with `POST /ports/{reference}/verification-code`.

A number the account may not port is a 422 on `numbers.0`. That is a
number that does not match the port type, a mobile number already on
another open port, or one whose verification failed in the last day. An
account that may not place orders gets a 403.

recentBill.description: The losing provider's most recent bill, PDF, up to 8 MB.

201.description: The port, in state `requested` (or `ppv_sent` once a mobile port's code has gone, or `awaiting_authority` when sent to the number's holder).

verificationCodeSent.description: On a mobile port, whether the verification code went to the number. Null on every other port.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns one port, as the portal's port page shows it. You get these
fields:

- Its real `state`.
- Who it is `waitingOn`, and the `nextStep`.
- Whether it needs `attention`, and why.
- Its `history`, step by step with dates.
- The cutover you asked for (`preferredCutoverOn`) and the booked one
  (`scheduledFor`).
- Why it stopped (`statusReason`).

A mobile port also carries its `verificationCode` dates and the number of
wrong codes it can still take.

post.summary: Confirm a Mobile Port's Verification Code
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Confirms the six-digit code we sent the mobile number's holder, for a port
in state `ppv_sent`. A correct code moves the port to `ppv_validated` and
we lodge it with the carrier.

A refusal is a 422 on `code`. Its message says what to do. The code is
wrong, and the message gives the attempts left. Or it has lapsed, and you
send a fresh one with `POST /ports/{reference}/verification-code`. Or the
port is not waiting for a code. Five wrong codes per port, counted across
every code sent, reject the port. A 503 means we could not check the code
just then, and the attempt was not counted.

post.summary: Resend a Mobile Port's Verification Code
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Sends a fresh verification code to the mobile number being ported, when
the last one lapsed or never arrived. The port stays waiting for the
code (`ppv_sent`). A code lasts **30 minutes**. The new one replaces the
old, which no longer works.

We count the five wrong codes a port can take across every code sent. A
resend does not give more tries. `verificationCode.attemptsRemaining` on
the port says how many are left. Resends count against your API rate
limit like any other write.

A port that is not a mobile port waiting for its code is a 422 on
`reference`. So is a number the code cannot be sent to. The message says
why.

>**Required Scope(s):** voice:delete

Withdraws a port-in you no longer want, before its cutover is locked in.
The port-in terms allow this, and the portal offers it. The port moves to
`cancelled`, and `statusReason` says you withdrew it. We send the step as
`order.statusChanged` like any other.

You can withdraw a port in these states:

- `requested`, `submitted` and `confirmed` for a fixed line or a
  13, 1300 or 1800 number.
- `ppv_sent` and `ppv_validated` for a mobile number.

Once the port is `scheduled`, or a mobile port is `submitted_upstream`,
the cutover is locked in. That is a 409 with the reason. So is a port that
is complete, rejected or cancelled by us. A port-out is worked by our team
and cannot be withdrawn here. That is a 409 too. Withdrawing a port you
already withdrew answers 200 with the port.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the figures the portal's call history shows above its table. They
cover the same window and filters as `GET /voice/cdrs`. You get calls,
answered calls, minutes, cost, answer rate and average call length.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: On or after this datetime (ISO 8601). Defaults to 31 days before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: On or before this datetime (ISO 8601). Defaults to now.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: `unbilled` means the calls since the start of this month that are not on an invoice yet. Do not send it with `from`.

parameters.name: trunk
parameters.description: Only this trunk's calls, by sipUsername.

parameters.name: invoice
parameters.description: Only the calls billed on this invoice of ours to you, by its `id` in your invoice list. Not one of yours is a 422.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search the source and destination numbers.

answerRate.description: Answered calls as a percentage of calls.

averageSeconds.description: The average length of an answered call.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the scheduled call record exports, daily and monthly, each on or
off, as the portal's SFTP Access card shows them. Exports land on our
SFTP server under your SFTP login.

`sftpLogin` says whether you have a login and gives its username. You
create, rotate and withdraw the login in the portal only. The password is
never returned. When we cannot read the login's state right now, `exists`
and `username` are `null`.

200.description: The exports and the SFTP login.

put.summary: Turn a Scheduled Call Record Export On or Off
put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Turns the daily or monthly export on or off, as the portal's SFTP Access
card does. We audit the change with the API key that made it. You manage
the SFTP login itself in the portal only. An unknown cadence is a `404`.

200.description: The export as it now stands.

parameters.name: cgrid
parameters.description: The call's `cgrid`, as `GET /voice/cdrs` lists it.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns one call detail record. Another account's call and an unknown id
both answer `404`.

>**Required Scope(s):** recordings:read

Returns the recordings of calls on your trunks, newest first, as the Call
Recordings page of the portal lists them. Follow `nextCursor` for the next
page until it is `null`. The call answers `403` while call recording is
not available on your account.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Recorded on or after this datetime (ISO 8601), or from the start of this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Recorded on or before this datetime (ISO 8601), or to the end of this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

parameters.name: trunk
parameters.description: Only this trunk's recordings, by sipUsername. A trunk that is not yours is a 422.

parameters.name: trigger
parameters.description: What started the recording. An unknown value is a 422.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search the caller ID number and name.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The recording's `id` (a uuid).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** recordings:read

Returns one recording, with `downloadUrl`. That is a link to the audio that
works for **5 minutes**. Fetch the recording again for a fresh link. We
audit every fetch with the API key that made it.

Another account's recording, an unknown id and a recording whose audio is
no longer stored all answer `404`.

200.description: The recording and its download link.

downloadUrl.description: The audio file. Works for 5 minutes.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the calls up now on your trunks, oldest first. The trunk page of
the portal lists them under Concurrency. Filter to one trunk with `trunk`.

A call to an emergency number (000, 112 or 106) is listed with
`emergency: true`. It is never hung up. `POST /voice/calls/{callId}/hangup`
refuses it with `422 emergency_call`.

Follow `nextCursor` for the next page until it is `null`.

parameters.name: trunk
parameters.description: Only this trunk's calls, by its sipUsername. A trunk that is not yours is a 422.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Number of calls per page. Defaults to `50`, maximum `200`.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page. It is `null` on the last page.

callId.description: The call's id; hang it up with `POST /voice/calls/{callId}/hangup`.

trunk.description: The sipUsername of the trunk the call is on.

answeredAt.description: Null while the call is ringing.

emergency.description: True for a call to 000, 112 or 106, which is never hung up.

parameters.name: callId
parameters.description: The live call's `callId`, as `GET /voice/calls/active` lists it.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Ends one live call on one of your trunks. Both parties are disconnected.
The call is billed for the time it was up. We audit the hang-up with the
API key that sent it.

**An emergency call (000, 112 or 106) is never hung up.** It answers
`422` with `error.code` `emergency_call`, and nothing is sent to the
network.

A call that has already ended, or is not on one of your trunks, answers
`404`.

202.description: The call has been ended.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username.

post.summary: Hang Up a Trunk's Live Calls
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Ends every live call on one of your trunks in one step. You might use it
to stop fraud. Both parties are disconnected on each call. Each call is
billed for the time it was up. We audit the request once, with the API key
that sent it and the counts. To stop new calls too, suspend the trunk
first with `POST /trunks/{username}/suspend`.

**An emergency call (000, 112 or 106) is never hung up.** It is left up
and counted in `skipped`.

`failed` counts calls the network could not end. Send the request again
with a new `Idempotency-Key` to retry them. A trunk with no live calls
answers `202` with every count `0`. A trunk that is not yours answers
`404`.

202.description: The trunk's calls have been ended, emergency calls aside.

trunk.description: The trunk as `GET /trunks` names it (its SIP username, else its `id`).

failed.description: Calls the network could not end.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The message's id, the `messageId` that `POST /sms` returned.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** sms:read

Returns one message on your account, with its `status`. The `Location`
header of `POST /sms` points here. Send, then poll this until the message
is `delivered` or `failed`. A message held for review reads `pending`
with a `statusReason` until it is released or blocked.

A message on another account answers `404`. So does an inbound message
held as a suspected scam, which you never received. We audit reads with
the message id, never the text.

A key limited to one end user reads only that end user's messages. Your
own and your other end users' messages answer `404`, as a missing one does.

>**Required Scope(s):** sms-senders:read

Returns every sender your account has asked for or holds, with its status.
It is the portal's **Approved Senders** list. Numbers you hold with us are
approved automatically and appear here too.

A key limited to one end user lists only that end user's senders. Those
are the senders they asked for and the mobile numbers they hold.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** sms-senders:create

Asks for a sender that `POST /sms` refused with `sender_not_approved`. The
sender is a number you control, such as one ported elsewhere, or a sender
ID of 3 to 11 letters and digits. It lands as `pending`. You can use it
once our team approves it. Sending again for your own pending or rejected
request updates it.

The call answers `422` when the sender is malformed, already approved, or
held by one of your end users.

A key limited to one end user asks for the sender as that end user, as
their portal does. Our team approves it as any other request. Once
approved, that end user's keys may send from it.

sender.description: An E.164 number, or a sender ID of 3 to 11 letters and digits.

notes.description: What the sender is for, for our team's check.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The request's `id` (a uuid), from `GET /sms/senders`.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** sms-senders:delete

Takes back one of your own pending requests. It then reads `withdrawn`. A
request our team has already decided, or one an end user made, answers
`409` and is unchanged.

A key limited to one end user withdraws only that end user's own requests.
Any other request answers `404`, as a missing one does.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** fax:read

Returns every fax sent and received on your numbers, your end users'
included, newest first. It is the portal's **Fax History**. You get
metadata only, never the document.

A key for one end user gets only that end user's faxes.

A page carries `perPage`, `nextCursor` and `results`. Pass `nextCursor`
back as `cursor` for the next page. Stop when it is `null`.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: One of your numbers. Only faxes received on or sent from it are returned.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of the other party's number, as the portal's search.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Faxes received or queued at or after this time. A date alone means the start of that day.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Faxes received or queued at or before this time. A date alone means the end of that day.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page. It is `null` on the last page.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** fax:send

Sends a fax from one of your numbers that is on a fax plan. Send to one
or more Australian landlines, mobiles and 13, 1300 and 1800 numbers. We
send one fax per destination and bill each per page. A fax cannot be
recalled.

A key for one end user sends only from a number on one of that end user's
fax plans. Any other number is refused as a number on no plan. We record
each fax against that end user and bill it to you as usual.

Send `multipart/form-data`. Documents are PDF or TIFF only, at most 5 of
them, each at most 10 MB. If the cover page is on in your fax settings, it
goes first and shows the subject, note and `replyEmail`.

`Idempotency-Key` is required. Without one the call answers `400`. A retry
with the same key returns the first send's faxes instead of faxing again.

The call answers `202` with one fax per destination, each `pending`.
Follow each one with `GET /fax/documents/{id}` or the `fax.sent` and
`fax.failed` webhook events.

The call answers `422` in these cases:

- The number is not yours or not on a fax plan.
- A destination cannot be faxed.
- A document is the wrong type or too large.
- There are too many documents.
- A document fails the virus scan.

from.description: One of your numbers on a fax plan.

replyEmail.description: Shown on the cover page as who the fax is from, and sent the result by email. Leave it out for no result email.

documents.description: PDF or TIFF files, as `documents[]`, each at most 10 MB.

202.description: One fax per destination, queued.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** fax:read

Returns one fax on your account. Use the id from `GET /fax/documents`,
`POST /fax/documents` or the `fax.*` webhook events. You get metadata
only, never the document. Any other id is `404`.

A key for one end user gets only that end user's faxes. Any other fax is
`404`.

>**Required Scope(s):** fax:read

Returns your fax domain and cover page. They are the portal's **Fax
Settings**.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** fax:update

Sets your fax domain or cover page. A field you leave out keeps its
value. Send `domain: null` to go back to the platform's domain. Check a
new domain with `POST /fax/settings/domain-check`.

The call answers `422` when the domain is not a hostname, is a shared
platform domain, or is held by another account.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** fax:read

Checks your fax domain both ways, as **Check domain** does in the portal.
It checks your saved domain, or the one you send. Nothing is stored, so
run it again after you change your DNS. The call answers `422` when there
is no domain to check.

It only reads. A suspended account can still call it, as it can any
`GET`.

domain.description: A domain to check instead of the saved one.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns your account's list of countries its SIP trunks may call when
`International` is in their calling permissions. Every trunk follows it
unless the trunk has its own `allowedCountries`. A new trunk follows it
too. An account that has never set a list allows every country.

The list applies to international calls only. Calls to Australia and New
Zealand follow each trunk's calling permissions. High-risk destinations
stay blocked whatever the list says. 000 always connects. New Zealand is
not in the list. A call to it is `NZMobile` or `NZNational`, never
international. To stop those calls, take them out of a trunk's
`callingPermissions`.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Replaces your account's list. Every trunk that follows it uses the new
list from its next call. A trunk with its own `allowedCountries` keeps
its own. The list needs at least one country. To stop every international
call, take `International` out of the trunk's calling permissions instead.
A list naming `NZ` is a `422`, because New Zealand follows `NZMobile` and
`NZNational`.

allowedCountries.description: ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes, each one of `availableCountries`. The United Kingdom is `GB`, not `UK`.

200.description: The list as it now stands.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's SIP digest username.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Lifts the hold on a trunk that reached its daily spend cap. Its outbound
calls then connect again now, rather than at midnight Brisbane time. The
trunk runs for the rest of the day at the same cap. Changing the cap arms
it again. Raising `dailySpendCapExGst` above `spendTodayExGst` also lifts
the hold. A trunk that is not held is a 422. The hold never stopped 000
or inbound calls.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns a paginated list of your residential lines, oldest first. A line
with `awaitingNumber: true` is billing but has no number yet, so it can
make and receive no calls. Filter by `endUser` for one end user's lines.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the lines of this end user, by its public number. A number that is not one of your end users is a 422, not an empty list.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to retrieve. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Number of records per page. Defaults to `50`, maximum `200`.

200.description: A paginated list of residential lines.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Orders a residential line on a plan. We lodge every residential number
with the emergency register against a service address. So the order needs
one of your emergency addresses. The answer gives it back for ordering the
line's number.

**The line bills from now.** It cannot make or receive calls until its
number is ordered. It reads `awaitingNumber: true` until then. The answer
carries the line's SIP password once. You cannot read it again.

name.description: A friendly name for the line.

emergencyAddressId.description: One of your emergency addresses, from `GET /emergency-addresses`. It is where the line's number will be lodged. Another account's address, or an unknown one, is a 422.

endUser.description: The end user this line is for, by its public number. It must be one of your end users, and not archived. Any other number is a 422. Leave it out, or send null, to make the line your own.

201.description: The line was ordered. Includes the one-time SIP password.

sipPassword.description: The line's SIP password. Shown only in this response.

emergencyAddressId.description: The address sent, to order the line's number against.

notice.description: That the line bills now and takes no calls until its number is ordered.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The line's SIP username, as call records and numbers name it in `trunk`. A SIP trunk's username is a 404.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns one of your residential lines, with its live numbers.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Moves an active line to the other plan, from today. The old plan's
monthly charge still applies to this billing period. The new one starts
today. A line that is not active is a 422. So is a change onto the plan
it is already on.

200.description: The line, on its new plan.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The line's SIP username. A SIP trunk's username is a 404.

get.summary: Get a Residential Line's Call Settings
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the line's call forwarding, Do Not Disturb, anonymous call
reject and call waiting, and the kinds of number it may call.

patch.summary: Update a Residential Line's Call Settings
patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Changes any of the line's call settings. A setting you leave out keeps its
value. Turning forwarding on needs a `destination` of 6 to 15 digits.
The change reaches the line within a minute. The portal and the end
user's star codes see the same settings. You cannot change
`callingPermissions` here.

destination.description: Never 000, 112 or 106, in any form; that is a `422`, "Calls can’t be diverted to an emergency number (000, 112 or 106)."

200.description: The line's call settings as saved.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The line's SIP username. A SIP trunk's username is a 404.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns whether the line's mailbox is on, where its messages are
emailed, and what happens to a message once it is emailed. The PIN is
the end user's own, so it is not returned.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Turns the mailbox on or off and sets where messages are emailed. A field
you leave out keeps its value. Send `email: null` to stop emailing. You
cannot set the PIN here. Sending `pin` is a 422.

200.description: The line's voicemail settings as saved.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns your caller ID authorisation requests, newest first. Filter by
`status` for, say, the ones still pending.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to retrieve. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Number of records per page. Defaults to `50`, maximum `200`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Ask to present a number your account does not hold as a trunk's caller
ID. Send `multipart/form-data` with the number, why you need it, and
proof that you may use it. The proof is a PDF, PNG or JPEG up to 8 MB,
such as a recent bill for the number. We review it and email the
account's technical contact, or its notification address, with the
outcome. The decision also sends `callerId.statusChanged`.

A 422 on `number` means one of three things. The number is a 13, 1300,
1800 or 1900 number, which can never be presented. Or your account can
already present it. Or a request for it is already pending.

reason.description: Why you need to present this number.

evidence.description: Proof you may use the number. PDF, PNG or JPEG, up to 8 MB.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The request's `id` (a uuid).

get.summary: Get a Caller ID Authorisation Request
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns one request: its status, when it was made and decided, and the
reason for a rejection.

delete.summary: Cancel a Caller ID Authorisation Request
delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:delete

Withdraw a request we have not decided yet. It stays in the list as
`cancelled`. A request already approved, rejected or cancelled is a 422.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Lists your qualification batches, newest first. That includes the ones
you sent here and the ones you uploaded on the portal's Batch
Qualification page. `q` searches the batch's reference. Each batch's rows
are on `GET /data/sq/batches/{id}`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `createdAt` or `updatedAt`, `-` in front for descending.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Qualifies up to 2,000 premises as one job, as the portal's Batch
Qualification page does with a CSV. Each row is a location id (`locId`,
LOC… or OPC…) or a street `address`, with your own `reference` for it.
For a premises whose port or line is in use, `avc` and `authorityDate`
carry the service id and customer authority date for a transfer. The
CSV's `avc` and `authority_date` columns do the same.

We accept the batch at once (`202`) and qualify each row on our side,
usually within minutes. Follow it with `GET /data/sq/batches/{id}` until
its `status` is `completed`. An address that does not resolve to one
location is `unresolved`. It does not refuse the batch.

Batches share the portal's allowance, which is ten batches an hour and a
number of rows a day. A batch over either is refused whole with
`409 - sq_batch_allowance_exceeded`. The portal's words are in `reason`,
and the rows left today are in `remainingRows`. Nothing in the refused
batch is qualified or counted. You can't create orders from a batch.

If we can't start the batch just then, the answer is `503`. We keep and
count nothing, so send the same request again shortly.

reference.description: Your name for the batch. The portal shows the batch by it.

items.description: One premises. Give `locId` or `address`, not both.

locId.description: An NBN Location ID or an Opticomm Property ID.

address.description: A street address, resolved to its location first.

reference.description: Your reference for the row, given back with its result.

avc.description: For a transfer, the service in use at the premises, in any case.

authorityDate.description: For a transfer, the date the end user gave authority.

202.description: The batch is accepted and its rows are being qualified.

409.description: The batch is over your account's batch allowance.

error.reason: This batch has 500 rows, and this account has 120 of its 5000 rows a day left. Upload a smaller batch, or the rest tomorrow.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The batch's id.

get.summary: Read a qualification batch and its results
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Returns one batch, its progress, and one page of its rows in the order
you sent them. Each row has its result once qualified. `page` and
`perPage` page the rows. Another account's batch answers `404`.

rows.description: One page of the batch's rows.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** colocation:read

Your colocation services, newest first, as the portal's My Colocation
page lists them. `q` searches the service number.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `createdAt` or `updatedAt`, `-` in front for descending.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The colocation service's id.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** colocation:read

One of your colocation services. Another account's service answers `404`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The colocation service the work is at.

post.summary: Ask for remote hands at a colocation service
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** colocation:create

Asks our technicians for work at your rack, as the portal's Remote Hands
request does. Remote hands is billed per incident.

The request is a support ticket with the service linked. The call
answers with the new ticket, which you follow and reply to on
`/tickets`. It also shows on the portal's Support page.

Another account's service answers `404`. A decommissioned service
answers `409`.

description.description: The work needed at the rack.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The colocation service the extra is for.

post.summary: Ask for an extra on a colocation service
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** colocation:create

Asks for another power outlet, cross-connect or network port, or a
bandwidth uplift, as the portal's Extras request does. We quote and
bill it.

The request is a support ticket with the service linked. The call
answers with the new ticket, which you follow on `/tickets`. It also
shows on the portal's Support page.

Another account's service answers `404`. A decommissioned service
answers `409`.

get.summary: List the sites you can order colocation at
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** colocation:read

The sites that offer colocation, as the portal's order form lists them.
Pass a site's `id` as `siteId` on `POST /colocation/orders`.

id.description: The site's code.

label.description: The site as the portal names it.

defaultPowerAmps.description: The power a new service at this site includes, in amps, when the tier does not say.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** colocation:create

Orders rack space at a site, as the portal's Order Colocation page does.
We record the order at once and assign the rack and rack units. The
service then appears on `GET /colocation/services`.

An account that may not place orders is refused with `403 - forbidden`
and the reason, as a data order is. That covers its credit, an
onboarding check, or a prepay balance short of the order. A site that
does not offer colocation answers `422` naming `siteId`.

requestedPowerAmps.description: The power you need, in amps, when more than the tier includes.

201.description: The order, waiting for us to assign rack space.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create

Use this when the end user has moved into premises whose line or port is
still in use by someone else, and you can't give the old service's id.
Order a Connect Outstanding with a proof of occupancy instead. That is a
lease, a utility bill or similar showing the end user occupies the
premises.

Send `multipart/form-data` with the document as `file`. It must be a
PDF, JPEG or PNG up to 10 MB. Put the answer's `id` on the order as
`occupancyDocumentId`, on `POST /data/orders` or the NBN Connect routes.
Each document is used by one order. We keep it with the order as
evidence, for as long as we keep the order record. We store it privately
against your account and never serve it to anyone outside it.

A file of another type or over 10 MB is a `422`.

file.description: The document, a PDF, JPEG or PNG up to 10 MB.

201.description: The document, ready for an order to use.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Your bundles, newest first, each with its items in order. `q` searches
the reference and title.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `createdAt` or `updatedAt`, `-` in front for descending.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create

Starts an empty bundle, as the portal's Start a bundle does. Add to it
through each item's own order route, with the bundle's id. Send
`bundleId` on `POST /data/orders` and `POST /trunks`, and `bundle` on
`POST /numbers`. Each joins as a draft. Nothing is sent until you submit
the bundle with `POST /bundles/{id}/submit`.

Numbers and a trunk added after a data order start once the items above
them have completed. Nothing then rings or bills before the service it
runs over. Change that, and the order, with
`PATCH /bundles/{id}/items/{itemId}`.

A bundle is submitted as a data order. An account that may not order
data services is refused with `403` here, before anything is added.

endUser.description: The end user the bundle is for, by its public number.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bundle's id.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

One of your bundles, with its items in order, each with its state and
what it is still waiting on. Another account's bundle answers `404`.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:delete

Cancels a bundle that nothing has left. Its drafts are discarded and
nothing in it is sent. A bundle that has been submitted, or has an item
already sent, answers `409`. Contact support for that.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bundle's id.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: The item's `id`, as the bundle read shows it.

patch.summary: Move a bundle item, or set when it starts
patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Puts an item at a place in the bundle with `position`. 1 is first, and a
position past the end puts it last. Say whether it starts only once
every item above it has completed with `waitsForPrevious`.

The first item waits for nothing. Numbers on the bundle's own trunk
always stay after it and wait for it. A change that breaks either rule
answers `422` and changes nothing. A bundle that has been submitted
answers `409`.

`acceptNewPrice: true` accepts the price a draft data order costs today
when its `checkoutBlockedReason` is `price_changed`, as the portal's
Accept New Price does. The draft then checks out at that price, which
shows as its `price` on the item. It works on a draft still in a
submitted bundle too, but not on one already checked out, which answers
`409`. A draft whose price has not risen is left as it is. Send it on
its own, or with a move.

acceptNewPrice.description: `true` to accept a draft data order's new, higher price (`checkoutBlockedReason` `price_changed`), so it can be checked out.

200.description: The item as it now stands.

delete.summary: Remove a draft from a bundle
delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:delete

Drops a draft from the bundle and discards it. The draft can be a data
order, numbers or a trunk. Numbers have their hold freed. Remove the
numbers ordered for the bundle's trunk before the trunk itself. Something
already sent, or a bundle that has been submitted, answers `409`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bundle's id.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Submits the bundle, as the portal's Submit All does. Every item that is
ready is sent now, each on its own. The items that wait are sent as the
items above them complete. Read the bundle to follow each item. Submit
again to send anything added or made ready since.

To check out only some of the draft data orders, list their ids in
`orders`, as the portal's ticked rows. Only those are checked out. Every
other draft stays in the bundle as a draft, to check out later, change or
remove. Without `orders`, every draft that is ready is checked out.

Each draft the submit was for is answered in `orders`. It is `submitted`
(`scheduled` with `sendAt`), or `refused`. A refusal carries the
`checkoutBlockedReason` its item shows on the bundle read, and the words
for it. One refusal does not stop the rest, and a refused draft stays a
draft in the bundle.

A draft whose price has gone up since it was added is refused with
`price_changed` and its `price` today. Accept it with `acceptNewPrice` on
`PATCH /bundles/{id}/items/{itemId}`, and submit again.

An id in `orders` that is not a data order in this bundle answers `422`
on that place in the list, and nothing is sent.

A bundle with nothing ready to send, or one that has finished, answers
`409`. Its data orders go to the carrier. The `Idempotency-Key` is
required, and the call counts against the write limit.

On a prepaid account, the chosen ready data orders' up-front cost
together must fit your balance less what orders already sent hold. That
cost is each one's setup and first charge, ex GST. If it does not fit,
the call answers `422` and nothing is sent. The `reason` names the total,
the shortfall and what is held.

To send the bundle later instead, give `sendAt`. It must be at least 15
minutes and at most 30 days away. The whole bundle waits for that time.
Each draft is held for it, and its number orders and trunk wait with
them. Nothing goes to a carrier and nothing is provisioned until then.
`released` is empty, except for the drafts placed now (see below). The
waiting items are in `waiting`, and the bundle's `sendAt` is the time.

We make the prepay check once, now, for the whole checkout. At the time,
the drafts go. We check each again as a delayed order is checked, then
release the numbers and trunk as an immediate submit would have. One
that fails is held for a person with the reason, and the rest still go.

Change the time for all of them with `PATCH /bundles/{id}/send-time`.
Cancel it with `DELETE /bundles/{id}/send-time`, which returns the bundle
to how it was before the submit. A time outside the window answers `422`
on `sendAt`.

An nbn draft a technician attends is not held for `sendAt`. That is a new
NTD, a Fibre Uplift, or no NTD chosen. Its day is its install
appointment, so we place it with nbn now with the appointment booked on
it, which locks the slot in, as `POST /nbn/orders/delayed` places one.
It is answered `placed` in `orders` and listed in `released`. The rest
are held.

If such a draft has no appointment booked, the call answers `422` naming
the drafts that need one, and nothing is held or placed. Book the
appointments and submit again.

The bundle's send time changes and cancels only the drafts it holds. A
placed order is with nbn. Move its appointment to change its day.
Cancelling it asks our team, who withdraw it with nbn by hand.

sendAt.description: When to send the bundle, its drafts, number orders and trunk alike, at least 15 minutes and at most 30 days away. Left out or null, they are sent now.

orders.description: The ids of the draft data orders to check out, as the bundle read shows them. Left out or null, every ready draft is checked out.

202.description: The ready items are on their way.

released.description: The ids of the items sent now.

waiting.description: The ids of the items that follow once the items above them complete.

orders.description: One answer for each draft data order the submit was for: those in `orders`, else every draft in the bundle.

id.description: The draft's id, as given.

outcome.description: `submitted`: checked out, and sent as the bundle's order allows. `scheduled`: checked out and held for `sendAt`. `placed`: with `sendAt`, an nbn draft a technician attends, placed now with its booked appointment rather than held. `refused`: not checked out, and still a draft in the bundle.

reason.description: Why it was refused, or null.

message.description: What to do about `reason`, in words for this draft.

price.description: For `price_changed`, the price today to accept; else null. Null too for a key without `billing:read`.

422.description: A prepaid balance, less what sent orders hold, does not cover the chosen ready data orders together; or an id in `orders` is not a data order in this bundle (named in `fields`); or, with `sendAt`, an nbn draft a technician attends has no install appointment booked (the `reason` names the drafts). Nothing was sent.

error.reason: Your prepaid balance does not cover this checkout: the chosen drafts cost $348.00 up front, ex GST (short by $48.00). Check out fewer drafts, or top up. Nothing was sent.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bundle's id.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Moves everything a bundle's submit holds for later to a new time, all
together. That is its orders, number orders and trunk, held with `sendAt`
on `POST /bundles/{id}/submit`. The new time must be at least 15 minutes
and at most 30 days away. Nothing goes to a carrier and nothing is
provisioned. An order already sent is left as it is.

A bundle holding nothing for a later time answers `409`. A time outside
the window answers `422` on `sendAt`.

sendAt.description: The new time, at least 15 minutes and at most 30 days away.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:delete

The bundle goes back to how it was before its submit. Every order it
holds for later goes back to being a draft in the bundle, and its number
orders and trunk stay drafts. Nothing has been sent, so there is no
charge. The drafts stay in the bundle until you submit them again or
remove them. An order already sent is left as it is.

A bundle holding nothing for a later time answers `409`.

200.description: The bundle, its items drafts again and its `sendAt` null.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bundle's id.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

We remove a draft data order that has not been checked out on its
`draftRemoval.removesAt`, 30 days after it was made. Keep gives every
draft in the bundle that can still be kept another 30 days, but never
more than 90 days from when it was made.

Each draft's `draftRemoval.keepLimit` is the latest date Keep can take it
to. `canKeep` says whether Keep would move it. Nothing goes to the
carrier.

We never remove a delayed order, an order the carrier already has, or a
draft that has been checked out. They show no `draftRemoval`.

A bundle none of whose drafts can be kept any longer, or one that has
finished, answers `409`.

200.description: How many drafts were kept, and the bundle with their new removal dates.

get.description:
Your VPN access groups, by name, with what each allows and how many
users it has.

post.description:
Creates an access group. A `split` group needs at least one destination.
No destination may name a reserved or Check Networks network. Such a
destination answers `422` naming `destinations`. A `full` group keeps no
destinations.

destinations.description: For a `split` group, the networks it reaches, as CIDRs or bare addresses.

patch.description:
Changes a group's name, access mode, destinations or notes. A field you
leave out is kept. Every user in the group takes the change, and no
profile has to be downloaded again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The group's id.

delete.description:
Deletes a group whose users are all removed or moved. Removed users
don't hold a group. A group that still has a live or suspended user
answers `409` with the reason.

A group with a dedicated egress IP has the IP released, and its monthly
charge ends on the day of the delete. If we can't release the IP just
now, the delete answers `503` and nothing changes. The group, its IP and
its charge stay until you try again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The group's id.

get.description: Your VPN users, by name. Removed users are not listed.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Only this group's users, by the group's id. A group not on your account is `422`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only this end user's, by its number. An unknown number is `422`.

post.description:
Orders up to 50 users in one of your groups, optionally for one of your
end users, as the portal's order form does. Each is billed monthly from
issue at your seat price, which the answer shows.

An account that may not order answers `403` with the reason. That is an
account your account manager has not enabled for VPN, or one at its
credit limit. A staff hold on the end user answers `409`.

While you bill your end users, seats for an end user you bill need a
retail price for VPN users, either a price or a markup. Until you set
one, the call answers `422` on `endUser`, saying what to set.

We issue the users in the background, so the answer is `202`. They
appear on `GET /vpn/users` as `provisioning` shortly after, and each
profile is ready to download a minute or so later (`profileReady`).

names.description: Each user's name, one user per name.

endUser.description: The end user the seats are for, by its number. They then appear on that end user's own portal, where it downloads and resets its profiles.

202.description: The users are ordered.

endUser.description: The end user's number; null when none.

seatPriceExGst.description: Each user's monthly price, ex GST. Null when no price is set for your account.

monthlyPriceExGst.description: What this order adds to your monthly bill, ex GST.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user's id.

patch.description:
Renames a user, moves it to another of your groups, or gives it to
another end user (null for none). A field you leave out is kept. Its
certificate, address and profile stay the same, so nothing needs
downloading again.

A suspended user answers `409`. So does a move to an end user you bill
while nothing prices a VPN user for them, such as a retail price or a
markup.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user's id.

endUser.description: The end user's number, or null for none.

delete.description:
Revokes the user's certificate and stops its monthly charge, as the
portal's Remove does. This cannot be undone. Order a new user to replace
it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user's id.

get.description:
A link to download the user's OpenVPN profile (`.ovpn`). The link works
for 5 minutes. The profile holds the user's private key, so it needs its
own scope, `vpn:credentials`, and we record each link we give.

The call answers `409` while the profile is still being made
(`profileReady` is false), or while the user is suspended.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user's id.

id.description: The user's id.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns what your usage has added to your bill with us for one month so
far. It covers call charges, data and numbers, grouped as the bill groups
them, with each group's items. It also gives the month's usage in real
units. These are the figures the Usage page in the Wholesale Portal shows,
worked out the way the bill run will charge them. Once the bill is issued,
find it on [List Invoices](#tag/Account/operation/list_invoices).

Months run on your bill's calendar. That is your account's time zone, the
zone your invoices are cut in. You set it in the Wholesale Portal's Company
Settings, and it is Brisbane until you set another. A month already billed
stays on the zone its invoice was cut in. You can ask for this month or any
of the eleven before it. `daysRemaining` is how many days of the month are
left after today, and `0` for a past month.

Amounts are dollars as decimal strings. Each comes three ways: without GST,
its GST, and with GST (`...ExGst`, `...Gst`, `...IncGst`).

The units count every answered call, including inbound and free ones.
The charges leave those out.

Set `format=csv` for the Usage page's charges CSV. It has one row per item,
then each group's subtotal.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Omit it for JSON. `csv` downloads the charges as CSV.

daysRemaining.description: Days of the month left after today. `0` for a past month.

groups.description: The charges, by the group the bill puts them in. Groups with nothing in them are left out.

smsMessages.description: SMS messages sent, counting each part of a long message.

schema.description: Sent only when `format=csv`. Columns `group`, `item`, `quantity`, `excl_gst`, `gst` and `incl_gst`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns one month's usage for each of your end users, in real units. It
also shows what each has added to your bill with us so far. Every end user
is listed alphabetically, including those with no usage. Your own services,
the ones you have not resold to an end user, come last with
`endUser: null`, when they have any usage. These are the Usage page's
"Usage by End User" figures.

Set `format=csv` for the Usage page's CSV of the same table. It has units
only.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Omit it for JSON. `csv` downloads the table as CSV.

endUser.description: The end user's number, as `/end-users` names it. `null` for your own services.

chargesExGst.description: What this usage has added to your bill so far, without GST.

schema.description: Sent only when `format=csv`. Columns `end_user`, `voice_minutes`, `voice_calls`, `data_down_bytes`, `data_up_bytes` and `sms_messages`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns the data your services moved each day of one month. It is the
curve behind the Usage page's bar chart. Only days with usage are listed,
oldest first. Each day is a day on your bill's calendar, as
`GET /account/usage` describes it.

Set `format=csv` for the Usage page's CSV of the same days.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Omit it for JSON. `csv` downloads the days as CSV.

schema.description: Sent only when `format=csv`. Columns `date`, `down_bytes`, `up_bytes` and `total_bytes`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns the business reports you can run. They are the ones on the Reports
page of the Wholesale Portal. Run one with
[Get Report](#tag/Account/operation/get_account_report). A report that
`takesPeriod` is worked out over a date window. The others are as at now.

key.description: The report's key, for Get Report.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Runs one business report for your account. It is the same document the
Reports page downloads, as JSON, CSV or PDF. A key that is not on
[List Reports](#tag/Account/operation/list_account_reports) returns
`404`.

In JSON the report is a table. `columns` are its headings. Each of
`rows` is one row of cells, formatted as the download shows them, with
dollars as decimal strings such as `"1234.50"`. `moneyColumns` lists
the indexes of the dollar columns. `kpis` are the headline figures.
`sections` are any small tables shown ahead of the main one.

Only a report that `takesPeriod` reads `from` and `to`. Without them it
runs from the first of this month to today. They are calendar dates in
your account's time zone, whatever `CN-Time-Zone` says. The zone is
Brisbane until you set one. A day runs from midnight to midnight there,
so the end-user bill run at 04:00 on the 1st is in that month. `from` and
`to` come back as the dates you asked for.

Only `aged_receivables` reads `asAt`. The report is as at the end of that
day in your account's time zone. It leaves out invoices, payments and
credits dated after it. Without `asAt` the report is as at now.

`estimateRows` lists the indexes into `rows` of the rows that are an
estimate, not invoiced figures. In the margin report they are the "Usage
so far (not yet billed)" rows and the "Total with usage so far" row, which
adds them. It is empty when no row is an estimate.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The report's key, from List Reports.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first day of the window, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The last day of the window, `YYYY-MM-DD`, included.

parameters.name: asAt
parameters.description: For `aged_receivables` only. The day the report is as at, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Omit it for now.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Omit it for JSON. `csv` or `pdf` downloads the report.

subtitle.description: The period or as-at date the report covers.

from.description: The window's first day. `null` for a report that is as at now.

asAt.description: The day `aged_receivables` is as at. `null` for every other report.

estimateRows.description: Indexes into `rows` of the rows that are an estimate, not invoiced figures.

schema.description: Sent only when `format=csv`. Any sections, then the main table.
Sent only when `format=pdf`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns the usage alerts on your account. They are the ones under
Notifications in Company Settings. A usage alert watches your call spend
today or this month, your minutes this month or your SMS this month. It
watches the whole account or, for calls, one trunk. When it reaches its
threshold we tell the alert's own recipients, once for that day or month.
We also send a
[Usage Alert Triggered](#tag/Webhook-Events-Usage/operation/webhook_usage_alert_triggered)
event. We check alerts every 15 minutes.

Usage alerts are notices only. They never stop calls. Your credit limit
is what stops calls.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Adds a usage alert. An account can have up to 25. `recipients` lists who
the alert goes to, up to 10 addresses and 10 mobiles. Only they are told.
One bad recipient refuses the whole request with `422`. Each channel in
`channels` needs someone on it. `email` needs at least one address and
`sms` needs at least one mobile, or the request is `422`. If you leave
out `channels`, it is the channels your `recipients` reach. An empty list
sends only the webhook event.

trunk.description: One of your SIP trunks, by its `sipUsername`. Use it for a call metric only. Omit it or send `null` for the whole account.

threshold.description: Dollars without GST for a spend metric, such as `"50.00"`. Otherwise a whole number, such as `"1000"`. It is at least one cent or one unit. We take a JSON number too, such as `1000`. A string keeps the cents exact.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Changes a usage alert. Send only the fields you change. `trunk: null`
moves it back to the whole account.

A new `metric` in another unit needs a new `threshold` in that unit. That
is a change from spend to minutes or SMS, or back. Without the new
threshold the request is `422` and the alert is left as it was. Between the
two spend metrics, or the two counts, we keep the threshold.

`recipients`, when you send it, replaces the alert's whole list. `[]`
empties it. To add or remove one person, use the alert's `recipients`
routes. A change to `channels` or `recipients` that leaves a channel with
nobody on it is `422`. That means `email` with no address, or `sms` with no
mobile.

parameters.name: alertId
parameters.description: The alert's `id` (a uuid).

threshold.description: As on create. We take a JSON number too.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Removes a usage alert and its history.

parameters.name: alertId
parameters.description: The alert's `id` (a uuid).

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Adds one person to a usage alert. Send `email` or `mobile`, not both. An
alert takes up to 10 addresses and 10 mobiles. Someone already on the
alert answers `422`, and so does a mobile that is not an Australian
mobile. An alert that is not on your account answers `404`.

parameters.name: alertId
parameters.description: The alert's `id` (a uuid).

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Stops sending one usage alert to one recipient. A recipient that is not
on this alert, or an alert that is not on your account, answers `404`.
The last address of an alert sent by email, or the last mobile of one
sent by SMS, answers `422`. Take that channel off the alert first.

parameters.name: alertId
parameters.description: The alert's `id` (a uuid).

parameters.name: recipientId
parameters.description: The recipient's `id` (a uuid).

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Changes the address printed on our invoices to you, your billing contact,
or both. It works as the Company Details page does in the portal, with the
same rules. A state is one of ACT, NSW, NT, QLD, SA, TAS, VIC or WA. A
postcode is four digits. An email is a valid address.

Only what you send changes. A field you leave out of `billingAddress` or
`billingContact` keeps its value. A field you send as `null` is cleared. A
billing contact with every field cleared is removed. We record each change
in your account's audit log against this API key.

You change your legal name, ABN, ACN and trading name through support, not
here. Sending `entityDetails` is refused with 422.

country.description: If you leave it blank, we save the address as in Australia.

200.description: Your billing details as they now stand.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Lists the Points of Interconnect where your account has a live data
service. Each shows how many of your services are live there, as the
portal's Utilisation page lists them. Read a POI's utilisation with
[Get POI Utilisation](#tag/Data-Utilisation/operation/get_data_poi_utilisation).

code.description: The POI's code, as NBN names it (`4IPS`), or `OPC-<state>` for Opticomm.

liveServices.description: How many of your data services are live at this POI.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Returns a POI's utilisation over a window. It is the series the portal's
Utilisation chart draws, in Mbps. It has the NNI's traffic (every
supplier link into the POI, summed) and the POI's traffic on its outer
tag on our BNG. It also has the NNI's planned capacity. Both traffic
figures cover the whole POI and every customer's traffic. You can use
them to see whether congestion is ours before you raise a fault.

The window is the last 24 hours unless you send `from` and `to`. It can
reach back at most 30 days. Its points are as far apart as the portal's
chart for that length: 5 minutes up to 24 hours, 30 minutes up to 7
days, 2 hours up to 30 days.

A POI where your account has no live data service answers 404. When we
can't read our monitoring, the call answers 503. Try again shortly.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The POI's code, from [List POIs With Your Services](#tag/Data-Utilisation/operation/get_data_pois).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The window's start, ISO 8601. At most 30 days ago. Default 24 hours before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The window's end, ISO 8601, not in the future. Default now.

capacityMbps.description: The NNI's planned capacity. Null when none is recorded.

currentNniPercent.description: The NNI's busier direction at the latest point, as a percent of capacity. Null without a capacity or a latest point.

currentBngPercent.description: The POI's BNG traffic, busier direction at the latest point, as a percent of capacity.

points.description: One point per step, oldest first. A value is null where nothing was recorded, never zero.

nniDownloadMbps.description: NNI traffic toward your end users.

nniUploadMbps.description: NNI traffic from your end users.

bngDownloadMbps.description: The POI's outer-tag traffic on the BNG, toward your end users.

bngUploadMbps.description: The POI's outer-tag traffic on the BNG, from your end users.

get.description:
Returns your account's audit trail, newest first. It shows what your
portal users did and what your API keys did, named by the key. It shows
what each OAuth app you connected did on your account. Those entries show
as `apiKey`, named by the app, and appear only on your account's trail. It
also shows what our support staff did on your behalf. Those show as
`Support`, and we never name the staff member. The entries are the same as
the portal's Audit Log page. Use them to feed a security log system.

Page with `page`, or follow `nextCursor` by passing it back as `cursor`
until it is `null`. Following the cursor reads every entry exactly once
while new ones are written. A cursor page carries `perPage`, `nextCursor`
and `results` only. `q` searches the action key and the IP address.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only entries at or after this time, as an ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone means the start of that day.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only entries at or before this time. A date alone includes that whole day. Not before `from`.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Only these actions. Send one or several action keys, comma-separated, such as `user.login,user.password_changed`. The most you can send is 50.

parameters.name: actor
parameters.description: Only entries by this actor. Send a user's id as `GET /account/users` names it, an API key's id, or `support` for our support staff. Anything else matches nothing.

total.description: Entries matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass it back as `cursor` for the next page. It is `null` on the last page, or on a page that was not full.

get.description:
Returns the calls your API keys made in the last 30 days, newest first.
Use it to debug an integration. It shows which calls failed, how long each
took, and which addresses used each key. It is the same list as the Recent
API Calls panel on the API Keys page. A call refused for its key is listed
too. That covers a revoked key, a missing scope, and an address not on the
key's allowlist. A call with no valid token belongs to no account, so it is
not listed.

Each entry is a summary only. It never holds the request or response body,
the query string or a header. Page with `page`, or follow `nextCursor` by
passing it back as `cursor` until it is `null`. A cursor page carries
`perPage`, `nextCursor` and `results` only.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only calls at or after this time, as an ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone means the start of that day.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only calls at or before this time. A date alone includes that whole day. Not before `from`.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Only calls by this key, by its `client_id`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only calls answered with these statuses. Send one or several, comma-separated. Each is a status such as `404`, or a class such as `4xx` or `5xx`. Anything else is `422`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Only calls whose path starts with this, with or without the `/v2` prefix. For example, `/tickets` matches `/v2/tickets/TKT-10234`.

total.description: Calls matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass it back as `cursor` for the next page. It is `null` on the last page, or on a page that was not full.

get.description:
Every webhook event of the last 30 days on your account that one of your
endpoints subscribed to when it happened. Events come oldest first, in
the body a delivery carries. Use it to catch up after your receiver was
down.

We do not keep an event that no endpoint subscribed to, of any type, so
it never appears here. An endpoint that is turned off still counts.

To catch up, pass the `eventId` of the last event you handled as
`after`. Follow `nextCursor` until it is `null`, passing it back as
`cursor`. Events then arrive in the order they happened. Each carries
the same `eventId` as its deliveries, so a handler that de-duplicates on
`eventId` treats an event read here and one delivered as one. An event
older than 30 days is gone.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only these event types. Send one or several, comma-separated. Each is a type (`ticket.replied`) or a family (`ticket.*`). A type that does not exist answers `422`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only events at or after this time, an ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone means the start of that day.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only events after this one, by its `eventId`. An `eventId` that is not your account's, or is older than 30 days, answers `422`. Start again with `since`.

total.description: Events matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass it back as `cursor` for the next page. It is `null` on the last page, or a page that was not full.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event's `eventId`, from `GET /events` or a delivery.

get.description: One event of the last 30 days, in the body a delivery carries. An event that is not your account's, or is older than 30 days, is `404`.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event's `eventId`, from `GET /events` or a delivery.

post.summary: Send an Event to an Endpoint
post.description:
Limit: 10 per minute for the account (webhook send), shared by test, redeliver, replay-dead and event re-send.

Sends one event of the last 30 days to one of your webhook endpoints, as
a new delivery. Use it for an event your receiver missed.

We keep only an event that one of your endpoints subscribed to when it
happened, so only such an event can be sent. It can go to any of your
endpoints, including one registered since.

The delivery carries the event's **own `eventId`** and its original
`occurredAt`, so a handler that de-duplicates on `eventId` sees the same
event. It carries the endpoint's next `sequence`. We send it whether or
not the endpoint subscribes to the event's type, and while the endpoint
is disabled, as a redelivery is.

An endpoint that is not your account's answers `404`. The call answers
`409` while the endpoint holds 100 queued deliveries.

202.description: Queued

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns every time a step of this port was handed to a person by a link,
newest first. Each shows whether the link was used, cancelled or has
expired.

200.description: A page of the port's delegations.

post.summary: Hand a Port's Step to a Person
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Emails a named person a one-use link to do one step of this port, when
you cannot do it yourself. `action` says which step.

- `confirmPort`: the holder of the mobile number being ported enters the
  verification code texted to it, as `POST /ports/{reference}/confirm`
  does. It works only for a mobile port-in waiting for its code
  (`ppv_sent`).
- `confirmAuthority`: the holder of the fixed-line number reads the
  Porting Authority and confirms it with their name and position. That
  becomes the port's Porting Authority and covers the Agent Authority. It
  works only for a port waiting for it (`awaiting_authority`), which you
  get by sending `authorityHolder` on `POST /ports`.

Any other port is a `409`.

The link opens a page on your end-user portal, in your branding. The
person is emailed a code there first. They then see only the numbers being
ported and the step, and they do it once. The link works for 7 days. When
it is used you get `delegation.used`.

The call answers `403` with the code `no_end_user_portal_access` when your
account has no end-user portal. That is when it is turned off, or has no
domain.

The `Idempotency-Key` is required. A retry after a timeout answers with
the first delegation and sends no second email.

One link is open per step at a time. While one is open (`sent` and not
expired), another for the same step is a `409`, to any address, and sends
nothing. Resend it, or cancel it and hand the step over again.

name.description: The person's name, used in the email.

email.description: Where the link, and then the code, are sent.

Emails the same person a new link, which works for 7 days from now. The
old link stops working at once, and so does any code sent for it. You can
resend an expired link. You cannot resend a used or cancelled one, or one
whose step is no longer open. Each of those is a `409`. A resend within 5
minutes of the last email, or a sixth in a day, is a `429` with
