post.summary: Hand an Order's Step to a Person
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Emails a named person a one-use link to do one step of this order, for
when you cannot do it yourself. The one step is `pickAppointment`.
Someone at the site picks the technician's install time from the
carrier's free slots. They also give the name and phone number the
technician should call. You can offer it on an NBN or Opticomm connect
with no appointment yet. That includes an order waiting for your
appointment (`order.appointmentRequired`). Any other order is a `409`.

The link opens a page on your end-user portal, in your branding. The
person is first emailed a code there. They then see only the site's
address and the free install times, and book one once. We put the
appointment on the order as the portal's Appointment card does. An order
waiting for its appointment is then sent to the carrier. The link works
for 7 days. When it is used, you get `delegation.used`.

You get a `403` with the code `no_end_user_portal_access` when your
account has no end-user portal. That is when it is turned off, or has no
domain.

The `Idempotency-Key` is required. A retry after a timeout answers with
the first delegation and sends no second email.

One link is open per step at a time. While one is open (`sent` and not
expired), another for the same step is a `409`, to any address, and
sends nothing. Resend the open link, or cancel it and hand the step over
again.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** none. Any token reads the key it was issued to.

Returns the key the calling token belongs to. You get its name, scopes, IP
allowlist and end date. While a rotation's overlap runs, you also get when
the old secret stops working. You never get a secret, and never another
key.

A key belongs to your account, not to the user who made it. It keeps
working when that user leaves or changes role. An Owner or Admin creates,
rescopes and revokes keys under API Keys in the portal.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** none. Any token rotates the key it was issued to.

Gives the calling key a new secret. The secret is returned in this
response only, so store it before anything else. Use this to roll a secret
on a schedule without an outage.

`rotationOverlapHours` is 0 to 168, and the default is 24. It keeps the old
secret working for that long. Both secrets mint tokens, and tokens from
before the rotation keep working, until `result.previousSecretExpiresAt`. A
token the old secret mints in the overlap ends with it. With `0`, the old
secret and every token minted with it stop at once, including the token
that asked. Rotating again ends the earlier overlap. Only the secret just
replaced still works.

We email the account's Owners each time a key rotates itself.

An `Idempotency-Key` is required. A retry with the same key returns the
same new secret and does not rotate again.

rotationOverlapHours.description: How long the old secret keeps working, in hours.

200.description: The key, and its new secret.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Clears a staff user's second factor, for someone who has lost their
device. They set it up again the next time they sign in. On an account
that requires two-factor, they cannot go further until they do.

You cannot reset an Owner's two-factor through the API. It answers `403`
with `owner_protected`. Another Owner resets it in the portal. `reset` is
`false` when the user had no second factor.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The user's `id`.

reset.description: Whether there was a second factor to clear.

Returns the staff invitations not yet accepted, newest first. Expired ones
are included, with `status: expired`, so you can resend them.
`POST /account/users` sends one, and its `inviteId` is the `id` here.
Partner invitations are under `/partners/invites`.

parameters.name: inviteId

Emails the invitation again with a fresh link, and starts its expiry
again. The old link stops working.

parameters.name: inviteId

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Returns whether staff must use two-factor, and the addresses they may sign
in to the portal from. They are under Company Settings > Security. You can
only read them here. An Owner or Admin changes them in the portal. Each API
key's own IP allowlist is on `GET /account/api-keys/self`.

>**Required Scope(s):** `data:read` for disconnects, `voice:read` for plan changes; at least one

Returns every change booked on your account for a later date, in one list,
soonest first. That covers a data service disconnect booked for a later
day, and a trunk plan or channel change waiting for the start of the next
billing cycle. You can cancel each with `DELETE /account/booked-changes/{id}`
before its date. A change that has taken effect, been cancelled or failed
on its date is no longer listed. `bookedChange.applied`,
`bookedChange.cancelled` and `bookedChange.failed` say when that happens.

A key lists only the kinds it may read. Without `voice:read` there are no
plan changes, and without `data:read` there are no disconnects. Asking for
a `kind` the key may not read is a `403`. The same change shows on the data
service and the trunk reads, as their `bookedChange`.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: One or both kinds, comma-separated. A value outside the set is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The booked change's id, as `GET /account/booked-changes` returns it.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** `data:delete` to cancel a disconnect, `voice:update` to cancel a plan change

Cancels a booked change before its date, so it does not apply. It can
cancel a disconnect booked for a later day, and the service stays live and
billed. It can cancel a trunk plan change booked for the next billing
cycle, and the trunk keeps its current plan. It is the same cancel as the
data service's and the trunk's own, `DELETE /trunks/{username}/plan-change`.
It sends `bookedChange.cancelled`, and for a plan change it also sends
`trunk.planChangeCancelled`.

A key without the scope for the kind of change gets `403`. Another
account's change, and one already applied or cancelled, are `404`, as an
unknown id is. A disconnect that can no longer be cancelled is `409` with
the reason.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** the read scope of each type listed (`voice:read`, `sms:read`, `billing:read`, `data:read`); at least one

The account's background exports from the last 14 days, newest first. It
lists only the types the key may read. Without `voice:read`, no `cdrs`
exports are listed, and so on. A ready export carries a fresh
`downloadUrl`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: One or more states, comma-separated. A value outside the set is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** the read scope of the type: `voice:read` for `cdrs`, `sms:read` for `sms`, `billing:read` for `invoiceLines`, `data:read` for `dataUsage`

Writes a large export in the background instead of one long streamed
response. The call answers `202` with the export at once. Follow it with
`GET /exports/{exportId}`, or wait for `export.ready` or `export.failed`.
A ready export carries a signed `downloadUrl`, good for an hour. We keep
its file for 7 days.

The rows are the streamed reads' own. A file holds what `?format=` on
the list would have streamed for the same window and filters:

- `cdrs`: `GET /voice/cdrs`. Filters `trunk`, `endUser`, `direction`,
  `disposition`, `q`, `invoice`, `sort`.
- `sms`: `GET /sms`. Filters `direction`, `status`, `q`, `sort`.
- `invoiceLines`: each invoice issued in the window, one row per line as
  `GET /account/invoices/{invoiceId}?format=csv` has it. No filters.
- `dataUsage`: one row per data service per day, as
  `GET /data/services/{ref}/usage` buckets it (`serviceId`, `date`,
  `downloadBytes`, `uploadBytes`, `totalBytes`). Filter `serviceId`.
  Each day is a day on your account's time zone, the zone your bills
  are cut in. The export runs in the background, so `CN-Time-Zone`
  sets how `from` and `to` are read, not the days.

`from` is required and `to` defaults to now. The window is at most 93
days. A filter the type does not take, or a value the list would refuse,
answers `422`. At most 3 exports run at once on an account. A fourth,
while 3 are queued or running, answers `409`.

to.description: The window's end. Now when absent.

filters.description: The list's own filters, by its query parameter names.

202.description: Accepted. The export is queued; `Location` names its read.

parameters.name: exportId
parameters.description: The export's id, as `POST /exports` returned it.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** the read scope of the export's type (`voice:read`, `sms:read`, `billing:read` or `data:read`)

The export's state, row count and size. While it is `ready` and its file
is kept (7 days), `downloadUrl` is a signed link to the file. The link is
good for one hour. Each read gives a new one, so read the export again
when a link has expired.

Another account's export answers `404`, as an unknown id does. A key
without the type's read scope gets `403`.

parameters.name: exportId
parameters.description: The export's id.

get.description:
The file of a ready export, through the signed `downloadUrl` that
`GET /exports/{exportId}` gives you. It needs no token. The signature is
the authority, and it lasts one hour. An expired or altered link answers
`403`, so read the export again for a new one. A file past its 7 days
answers `410`.

parameters.name: expires
parameters.description: When the link stops working, as a Unix time. Part of the signed link.

parameters.name: signature
parameters.description: The link's signature.

410.description: The export's file has been removed after its 7 days.

Replaces what a partner may reach. `endUsers` and `products` are both

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

**Sandbox only.** Call it on `https://api.checknetworks.dev`. Production
answers `404`.

Wipes your sandbox account's orders, services, bills and callbacks, and
starts its test addresses again. A test run then starts clean. Its users,
API keys and addresses are kept.

You can reset a sandbox 3 times in any 24 hours, counting resets from
here and from API Keys in the production portal together. Past that we
refuse the reset with `429`. `Retry-After` gives the seconds until the
next one is allowed.

resetsPerDay.description: How many resets are allowed in any 24 hours.

post.description: Sent when you call `POST /webhooks/{webhookId}/test` with no `eventType`, so you can check your endpoint receives and verifies deliveries. With an `eventType`, the test sends a sample of that event instead, in its own shape, with `test: true`.

It comes with `ticket.statusChanged`. A ticket set to `pending` any other way sends only `ticket.statusChanged`. Reply to the ticket to send it back to us.

A hold never stops a 000 call, and inbound calls are not affected. Sent once per hold.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a booked change reaches its date but cannot be made: the carrier refuses a booked data disconnect, or a trunk plan change cannot be applied (for example, the trunk was cancelled first). The change is no longer listed and nothing changed; book it again if you still want it. `data` is the entry `GET /account/booked-changes` listed, plus the `reason`.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when Check Networks moves a data disconnect booked for a later day to another day, at your request or after its day came and it was held for us to check. It is the same booking, with the same `id`; nothing was cancelled. `data` is the entry `GET /account/booked-changes` now lists, with its new `effectiveOn`, plus `previousEffectiveOn`.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a background export (`POST /exports`) has its file. `data` is the export without its link: read `GET /exports/{exportId}` (the `resourceUrl`) for a signed `downloadUrl`, good for an hour.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a background export could not be written. `failureReason` says what to do; start it again with `POST /exports`.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when Check Networks issues an invoice to your account. `data` carries the invoice summary. Invoices you raise to your own retail customers do not send this.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when one of your invoices is settled in full. `occurredAt` is when it cleared. Fires once per invoice, when the last of its balance is covered.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description:
Sent when one of your invoices is cancelled and its charges unwound — the counterpart to `invoice.issued`. The invoice is no longer owed: clear it from your receivables rather than carrying it as an open debt that nothing will ever settle.

`data.voidedAt` is when it was cancelled. A paid invoice is never voided — that is a refund or a credit note — so this only ever follows an `invoice.issued` you have already seen, and it fires once per invoice however many times a void is attempted.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description:
Sent whenever a payment lands on your account, whether or not it settles an invoice — a part payment, an overpayment and a payment made before an invoice is issued all fire this.

`invoice.paid` only fires on FULL settlement, so this is the event to post receipts against if you are keeping a receivables ledger in step. `data.amount` is the payment and `data.balance` is your account balance after it, so you can reconcile without calling `GET /account/balance`.

amount.description: The payment amount, as a decimal string.

balance.description: Your account balance after this payment.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a card or direct-debit payment on your account succeeds, including a credit top-up. `data.source` says which; a charge's `data.invoiceNumber` links it to the invoice it paid, and a top-up's is null.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a card or direct-debit payment on your account is declined or errors. `data.failureCode` / `data.failureMessage` carry the reason.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a payment that succeeded is taken back: a direct debit dishonoured or a card charged back. The invoices it paid are owed again, and `data.failureCode` / `data.failureMessage` carry the reason.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when we issue a credit note against one of your invoices, including one that decides a dispute in your favour.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when one of the usage alerts you set (`/account/usage-alerts`) passes its threshold, once per period. An alert is a warning only: it never blocks a call or a message.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a PPPoE realm you requested is approved. The realm is live from that moment: logins are namespaced into it and PPPoE services can be provisioned.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a PPPoE realm you requested is not granted. `data.reason` carries why; the name is free for someone else, and you are welcome to request a different one.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when Opticomm reports the session of one of your RADIUS users on Opticomm's RADIUS. Opticomm gives it a minute or two after we ask, so when *Check Whether a User Is Online* or *Retrieve the Current Session* answers `202`, this event carries the answer and you need not poll. `data.session` is null when nothing is connected.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description:
Sent when one of your orders changes status, so you do not have to poll `/data/orders`. `data.from` / `data.to` carry the transition in the same words that endpoint publishes.

Orders move through more internal steps than the API publishes, and this event follows the published status — several internal steps share the status `InProgress`, and moving between them does not emit. You get one event per status change you can actually see.

Draft orders do not emit: they are not visible on `/data/orders` and have no order id to correlate against, so the first event for an order is the one where it becomes `InProgress`. The exception is an order waiting for your appointment or port (`order.appointmentRequired`, `order.ntdFull`): it is public under its PND, so if it is cancelled after 7 days unanswered, this event names that PND, with the reason. An order held for later (`order.delayed`) is public under its PND too: cancelling it sends this event naming the PND, `to: Failed`, with the reason.

Number ports (`orderType: numberPort`) are the exception to one event per status: a port sends this event on **every** step it takes, and again when its cutover moves, as our emails tell you. `step` is the port's real state (as `GET /ports/{reference}` reads it), `waitingOn` who it waits on, `scheduledFor` the booked cutover and `statusReason` why it stopped. A step that waits on you also sends `port.actionRequired`.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent for an order a person holds for a later submit time: when the hold starts, when its time changes, and when we hold it for you at its time because it could not be sent (for credit, because it was not ready, or because another order is open at the location). Nothing has been sent to the carrier. An order we are still trying to send to the carrier does not send it.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description:
Sent when an order you placed with POST /data/orders needs a technician and no appointment was attached. The order is accepted and waits on our side; nothing is sent to the carrier until it has an appointment.

Read the order's timeslots (GET /data/orders/{orderId}/timeslots), reserve one on the network's appointment endpoint, and attach it with PATCH /data/orders/{orderId}. An order still waiting after 7 days is cancelled.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description:
Sent when an order you placed with POST /data/orders named no port and every port on the installed NTD is in use. We never order another NTD unasked, so the order waits on our side for you to choose:

- **A new NTD:** reserve an appointment from the order's timeslots and
  attach it with PATCH /data/orders/{orderId} (`appointmentId`).

- **Take over a port:** PATCH /data/orders/{orderId} with the port
  (`resourceId`), the service on it (`serviceId`, the AVC on NBN) and
  the `customerAuthorityDate`.


An order still waiting after 7 days is cancelled.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a number port arrives at a step only you can move: today, a mobile port-in waiting for the verification code its number's holder was sent (`action: enterVerificationCode`). Confirm it with `POST /ports/{reference}/confirm`, or send a fresh code with `POST /ports/{reference}/verification-code` once it lapses. The same step also arrives as `order.statusChanged`.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description:
Sent when a service first comes up — a data service going live, or a SIP trunk becoming active. This is the event that tells you an order has turned into something usable.

`data.serviceType` says whether to read `data.serviceId` as a data service id or a trunk's `sipUsername`. Services migrated onto the platform from an existing environment do not emit this: they were already live for you, and the import is our records catching up.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a service is suspended and stops carrying traffic — including a suspension for non-payment, which is the most common reason a working service stops. Pair it with `service.resumed`.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a suspended service is restored. Only emitted coming out of a suspension — a service going live for the first time sends `service.provisioned` instead.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a service is cancelled or terminated for good. Unlike `service.suspended` this is final — the service will not resume, and a replacement means a new order.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description:
Sent when the carrier tells us it will cease one of your data services on a future date, and no cease order of yours asked for it. Most are churns: the end user has moved to another provider. The service stays live, and billed, until `data.ceaseAt`, so there is time to warn your end user or reorder.

Sent once per date; if the carrier moves the date, it is sent again with the new one. `service.disconnected` follows on the day. A cease you ordered sends no `service.ceaseScheduled`.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent once when a line test on one of your data services finishes: completed, cancelled or rejected. The carrier tells us when a test ends, so after `POST /nbn/diagnostics/avc/service_test` or `POST /opticomm/serviceTest` you need not poll. `data.result` is `Passed` or `Failed` where the carrier gives one; read the test by `data.testId` on `data.network`'s diagnostics endpoints for its measurements. A test still running sends nothing.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

A submitted change then follows as any speed change does. The same outcome is emailed to your users who have the ONT upgrade notice on.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a technician appointment is committed to one of your orders. This is the first event for any appointment: a reserved slot is a hold that has not been committed and routinely lapses, so it is not announced, and every later appointment event follows a booking you have already been sent.

post.description:

Worth wiring up before anything else on this list: a reschedule most often originates with the carrier rather than with you, and a missed one means the technician arrives at an empty premises — a missed-appointment fee and a week's slip on the order.

post.description:
Sent when a network outage affecting services on your account reaches the register. `data` is the same body `GET /outages` returns, plus `yourAffectedServiceCount` and `yourAffectedServiceTypes`.

You are only sent outages that match your own services — the same matching `GET /outages` performs — so this and the read endpoint can never disagree about whether you are affected. Only reviewed, published entries are sent.

Planned maintenance is sent too, with `data.planned` true: when we first send its notice to your account.

post.description: Sent when something a customer would be told about a running outage changes — the estimated restoration time, the affected area, the cause, the notes. OAuth2.description:
Every call carries an OAuth2 access token. An API key gets one with the client credentials flow.
A registered OAuth app uses the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256) and its client secret. An Owner or Admin approves it on the consent screen in the wholesale portal. Its tokens act for that account within the scopes approved, until the account revokes the app under Connected Apps. An app never gets a `safety:*` scope.
Access tokens last an hour. An app's refresh token is replaced on every use and lasts 30 days from that use, so an app left idle for 30 days must be connected again. Send a replaced refresh token again within 60 seconds and we refuse it as `temporarily_unavailable`, which you can retry. After that it disconnects the app from the account.
See https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/guides/oauth-apps/.
