status.description: HTTP status code for the error.

code.description: A stable code to branch on. `reason` is free text and may change. Each code has an entry at `docUrl` saying what to do. A refusal says why. `key_revoked`, `key_expired`, `secret_rotated`, `scopes_changed` and `missing_scope` need a new key, token or scope. `ip_not_allowed` needs the caller's address on the key's allowlist. `account_suspended` and `account_inactive` need a person on your side. `end_user_keys_off` is a key limited to one end user while their provider has API keys switched off for them. `owner_protected` is a change to an Owner, which a key, acting as an Admin, may never make. That covers an Owner's name, email, role, two-factor or removal. `app_disabled` and `app_access_revoked` mean the app must be connected again. Both come from an OAuth app's token. `idempotency_in_progress` comes with `Retry-After` and means retry later. `idempotency_key_reused` means send the new request under a new key. The `carrier_` codes and the five before them are the canonical carrier errors. They are the same whichever carrier refused. `address_not_serviceable`, `duplicate_order`, `insufficient_capacity`, `auth_validation_failed`, `customer_authority_required` and `charge_acknowledgement_required` mean a carrier refused the request on its merits. `carrier_bad_request` means a carrier refused it for any other reason, and its own code is in `carrierCode`. `carrier_unauthenticated`, `carrier_rate_limited` and `carrier_unavailable` mean our link to the carrier failed, so retry later. `carrier_unknown` is a carrier failure we could not classify. `caller_id_authorisation_required` means a trunk's caller ID is one your account neither holds nor has had approved. Ask for it with `POST /caller-id-authorisations`. `hold_expired` means a number order named a hold that has run out. Hold the number again. `no_end_user_portal_access` means you asked for a sign-in link for an end user who cannot use the end-user portal. `sender_not_approved` means a `POST /sms` or `POST /sms/bulk` used a sender your account has no approval for. Request one with `POST /sms/senders`. `emergency_call` means we refused a hang-up because the call is to 000, 112 or 106. `sq_batch_allowance_exceeded` means a qualification batch is over your account's allowance. `remainingRows` says how many rows you may still send today. `no_live_session` means you asked for a session reset with nothing connected to drop. `session_not_resettable` means you asked for one on a network where a reset is not possible. `res_line_needs_number` means a change would leave a Res Line with no number. `resLines` names each line. Send the request again with a `resLineResolutions` choice for each. `bundle_draft_limit` means you sent a data order for a bundle that already holds as many draft orders as one may. Send or remove some of its drafts, or start another bundle. We may add codes. Treat an unknown code by its `status`.

reason.description: Client-friendly reason for the error.

messageId.description: This request's id, the same as the `CN-Message-Id` response header. Quote it to support.

docUrl.description: The `code`'s entry on the developer site's errors page.

carrierCode.description: The carrier's own error code, where the failure was a carrier rejection of the request. Examples are NBN's RJ002003 and 001013. Absent when the error did not originate at a carrier.

remainingRows.description: On a `sq_batch_allowance_exceeded` error, the rows your account may still qualify by batch today. Null when the day has no row limit and the refusal is the hourly batch count. Absent on every other error.

charge.description: On a `charge_acknowledgement_required` error, the charge the request would incur. Repeat the request accepting it to go ahead. Absent on every other error.

amount.description: The charge as a decimal dollar amount, without GST. Deprecated. Read `amountExGst`, `amountGst` and `amountIncGst` instead.

amountExGst.description: The charge without GST, as a decimal dollar amount.

amountIncGst.description: The charge with GST. This is what the invoice will show.

contractEndsOn.description: When the contract the charge comes from ends.

period.description: On a recurring charge, such as call recording, how often we bill it. The amounts are per period.

consent.description: On a `charge_acknowledgement_required` error for call recording, the consent you accept by sending `acknowledgeRecording: true`. Absent on every other error.

holdId.description: On a `POST /numbers` that took an offered number but could not place the order, a hold on that number, until `heldUntil`. Order again with this `holdId` and the same `type`, `szu` and `blockSize`. That order takes the same number. Absent on every other error.

heldUntil.description: When the `holdId` beside it runs out. Absent on every other error.

allowance.description: On a `rate_limited` error from `POST /numbers/lookup`, the account's daily number lookup allowance. It says how many lookups the account is allowed, how many it used today, and how many the refused batch asked for. It resets at midnight Brisbane time. `Retry-After` gives the seconds until then. Absent on every other error.

resLines.description: On a `res_line_needs_number` error, each Res Line the change would leave with no number, and the choices for it. Send the request again with `resLineResolutions` holding one choice per line. Absent on every other error.

username.description: The line's SIP username, as `/residential-lines/{username}` names it.

existingWebhookId.description: On a `409` from `POST /webhooks`, the endpoint already registered at that URL. Absent on every other error.

fields.description: On a `validation_failed` error, one entry per failed rule, naming the input it was about. Absent on every other error.

field.description: The input's name. A nested input uses dots, such as `address.postcode`.

reason.example: The location id field is required.

AddressMatch.description: An address from our copy of G-NAF.

gnafId.description: The G-NAF address id (`address_detail_pid`). Pass it to `GET /nbn/address/search?gnaf=` to find the NBN location.

roadNumber2.description: The end of a number range, such as 14 in 12-14.

confidence.description: G-NAF's confidence in the address, from -1 to 2. 2 means three or more contributing sources agree.

nbnLocId.description: The NBN location id, when we already know it.

opticommOpcId.description: The Opticomm property id, when the address is on Opticomm's network.

AccountBillingAddress.description: The address printed on our invoices to you, in the same shape as the account's `address`. Each line is null when not on file.

state.description: The state or territory. A change you make by API must be one of ACT, NSW, NT, QLD, SA, TAS, VIC or WA. An address our staff entered may hold another.

postcode.description: Four digits when changed by API.

country.description: Australia when an address is saved without one.

AccountBillingContact.description: Your billing contact, where invoices and billing notices go. Each field is null when not on file.

CreditPosition.description: Where your account stands with us. It means the same on a prepaid and a postpaid account. `amountOwed` includes GST, as your invoices do. The credit line is read as credit control reads it and the portal dashboard shows it. It is without GST, and credit used is what you owe plus usage not yet invoiced. Your services are held when `availableCredit` reaches zero.

amountOwed.description: What you owe us on invoices, less payments and credits, with GST. Positive when you owe us. Negative when you hold credit with us.

creditLimit.description: Your credit limit with us, without GST. Two decimals.

creditUsed.description: How much of the credit limit is used, without GST. It is what you owe plus usage not yet invoiced. Never below `0.00`.

availableCredit.description: The credit limit less credit used, without GST. Below zero when you are over your limit.

creditUsedPercent.description: Credit used as a whole percentage of the limit. We send credit warnings at 80, 90, 95 and 100% of this figure.

Notice.description: A notice we sent you or one of your end users, and what happened to it. No message body is kept, so a notice is told by its kind and what it was about.

createdAt.description: When we sent it (or tried to).

kind.description: What the notice is, e.g. `invoice_issued`, `overdue_notice`, `outage_started`. New kinds may be added.

recipient.description: The address it went to. `Suppressed` for an end user whose contact details are withheld under a family violence record.

endUser.description: The number of the end user it went to, or null for a notice to you.

about.description: What the notice was about, or null.

type.description: `invoice`, `creditNote`, `outage` or `payment`; other notices name their own kind of record.

reference.description: The invoice or credit note number, the outage reference, or the payment's amount and date.

status.description: `suppressed` means not sent, because an earlier notice to the address bounced hard or was marked as spam.

error.description: Why it failed, bounced or was suppressed.

lastEventAt.description: The mail service's latest report on it (delivered, bounced).

BillingInvoice.description: One of our invoices to your account, as List Invoices returns it. Money is a decimal dollar string in `currency`. A priced figure comes as three fields: without GST, the GST, and with GST.

id.description: The invoice's id, as `GET /account/invoices/{invoiceId}` takes it. It is opaque. Compare it, never parse it.

createdAt.description: When the invoice was created, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the invoice last changed, in UTC.

type.description: Always `invoice`. It matches the `type` field on `/account/credit-notes` rows, so you can tell the two apart.

total.description: This invoice's new charges with GST. Deprecated. Read `totalIncGst`.

totalExGst.description: This invoice's new charges without GST.

totalGst.description: The GST on this invoice's new charges.

totalIncGst.description: This invoice's new charges with GST.

currency.description: The currency of the invoice amounts.

periodStart.description: The first day of the period the invoice bills.

periodEnd.description: The last day of the period the invoice bills.

previousBalance.description: The balance carried onto this invoice from before it, with GST, as the invoice prints it.

amountPaid.description: The payments applied to this invoice so far, with GST, as the portal's invoice page lists them.

amountDue.description: What is still owed on this invoice now, with GST. `0.00` once it is paid or void. A part-paid invoice shows what is left.

amountDisputed.description: The part of `amountDue` an open dispute holds off collection and reminders, with GST. `0.00` when nothing is disputed.

paidAt.description: The date the invoice settled. `null` while any amount is still outstanding. It is cleared again if a payment is later dishonoured and the invoice reopens. It is the settlement date of the payment that closed the invoice, not the time we recorded it.

PaymentCharge.description: A card or direct debit charge we started on your account, from autopay or Pay Now in the portal. While `inFlight`, it has not reached your balance yet. Do not pay the same invoice again.

id.description: The charge's public id.

invoiceId.description: The invoice the charge pays, when it pays one.

methodLabel.description: The stored method as the portal names it.

amount.description: The charge, with GST like the invoice it pays.

status.description: `initiated` and `pending` are in flight. `succeeded` moves to List Payments once it settles. `errored` means we lost the provider's answer. We retry the charge with the same key, so it cannot be taken twice.

BillingLineDetailRow.description: One row behind an invoice line. `kind` says which fields it has. A `call` is one of the calls a usage line charges. A `burst_settlement` is the 95th percentile behind a transit burst line.

dialled.description: The number dialled, E.164 without the `+` (`call`).

included.description: The call was inside an included allowance, so it charged nothing (`call`).

chargeExGst.description: The call's charge without GST, to 4 decimal places as rated (`call`).

billedMbps.description: The whole Mbps above the commit that was billed.

BillingInvoiceLine.description: One line of an invoice: what it charges, the service, end user and period it bills, and the rows behind it.

id.description: The line's public id, for its detail route and a dispute's `lineId`.

product.description: The product the line charges for, as the invoice names it.

unitPrice.description: The unit price without GST, to up to 5 decimal places. Deprecated. Read `unitPriceExGst`.

unitPriceExGst.description: The unit price without GST, to up to 5 decimal places.

unitPriceGst.description: The GST on one unit. `0.00` on a GST-free line.

total.description: The line total with GST. Deprecated. Read `totalIncGst`.

tax.description: The GST on the line. Deprecated. Read `totalGst`.

totalGst.description: The GST on the line, as the invoice charged it.

totalIncGst.description: The line total with GST. Lines add up to the invoice's `totalIncGst`.

serviceType.description: The kind of service the line bills. Null for an account-level line or a service the API does not read.

serviceRef.description: The service, named as its own routes name it. For a data service that is the `{ref}` in `GET /data/services/{ref}`. For a trunk it is the SIP username. For a fax plan or VPN user it is the id. For a transit service it is the number. Null for an account-level line.

serviceCategory.description: The broad category the line bills under.

endUser.description: The end user's number when the service belongs to one of your end users.

group.description: The section of the invoice the line prints under.

invoiceGroup.description: The name of the invoice group you placed the line's service in, as it stood when we built the invoice. Null for a line in no group. That line prints under Other.

invoiceGroupId.description: The invoice group's public id, as `GET /account/invoice-groups` names it. Null once the group has been removed.

invoiceLabel.description: The service's own billing label when the invoice was built.

poNumber.description: The purchase order number in effect for the line. It is the service's own, or else its group's.

costCentre.description: The cost centre in effect for the line. It is the service's own, or else its group's.

periodStart.description: The first day the line bills for. Null for a one-off charge.

periodEnd.description: The last day the line bills for.

detail.description: The rows behind the line, as the portal opens them. For a usage line these are the calls it charges. For a transit burst line it is the burst settlement. At most 50 come here. `detailHref` pages the rest.

detailTotal.description: How many rows are behind the line in all.

detailHref.description: Where to page every row when there are more than `detail` carries. Null otherwise.

InvoiceGroupSection.description: One section of an issued invoice. It holds an invoice group's lines and subtotal, as the group stood when we built the invoice. Lines in no group are the Other section, with a null `groupId`. Money is in dollars. The subtotal comes as ex GST, GST and inc GST.

groupId.description: The group's public id. Null for Other.

lineIds.description: The public ids of the section's lines, as `lineItems[].id`.

BillingPayment.description: A payment we received on your account, with the invoices it settled.

id.description: The payment's id, as the `payment.*` webhook events name it in `paymentId`. It is opaque. Compare it, never parse it.

createdAt.description: When the payment was recorded, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the payment last changed, such as by a reversal, in UTC.

type.description: Always `payment`. Invoice rows have `type` `invoice` and credit-note rows have `type` `credit_note`. `amount` is unsigned. Treat a payment as a credit by its `type`, not its sign.

status.description: `applied` once the payment is on your account. `reversed` when your bank later dishonoured it and we took the amount back off.

amount.description: The payment in dollars, as a decimal string with two decimals. A payment has no GST of its own. It pays invoices whose totals include GST, so read it as GST-inclusive.

method.description: How it was paid. For a payment our billing team recorded, this is `bank_transfer`, `bpay`, `cheque`, `cash`, `offset` or `other`. Otherwise it is the direct-debit gateway that reported the payment.

reference.description: The payment reference as it reached us, if any.

invoices.description: The invoices this payment settled, oldest first, and how much of each.

invoiceId.description: The invoice's `id`, as on List Invoices.

amount.description: The part of this payment applied to that invoice, in dollars with GST.

receiptHref.description: Our receipt for this payment as a PDF (Get Payment Receipt).

PricingItem.description: One product at the price you pay us, as the portal's Pricing page shows it, with any volume tiers and the tier your current quantity sits in.

displayName.description: The Friendly/Display Name of the Product/Service

setup.description: The upfront price without GST. Deprecated: read `setupExGst`.

rate.description: The recurring price without GST. Deprecated: read `rateExGst`.

rateExGst.description: The recurring price without GST. On a tiered product, the first tier's price; `tiers` has the rest.

increment.description: The Billing Interval/Period for the Product/Service

tiers.description: Volume tiers, lowest first. Empty for a flat price.

from.description: The first quantity this tier's price applies to.

to.description: The last quantity, or null for the top tier.

heldQuantity.description: How many you hold now, on a tiered product; null otherwise.

currentTier.description: The tier `heldQuantity` sits in, counting from 1; null for a flat price.

AccountUser.description: A staff login on your wholesale account.

id.description: The user's id, for the user's own routes.

twoFactorEnabled.description: Whether the user has a second factor set up.

lastLoginAt.description: When the user last signed in to the portal, in UTC.

createdAt.description: When the login was created, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the login last changed, in UTC.

Layer2Destination.description: A Layer 2 link destination. It is one of your active customer-interconnect outer VLANs (S-Tags), where we can hand a Layer 2 service off to you.

interconnectRef.description: The customer interconnect this destination belongs to.

outerVlan.description: The POI's tag on the interconnect port, for a per-POI destination. Null for a `0NAT` destination. On a single-tag interconnect each service has its own tag on the port, which we give when we build the service.

poiCode.description: The Point of Interconnect code. `0NAT` is a reserved code for a single-tag interconnect. One outer VLAN carries all your services across every POI and carrier, instead of a separate tag per POI. It therefore serves both NBN and Opticomm.

poiName.description: The Point of Interconnect name. Null for a `0NAT` destination.

carriers.description: The carrier networks this destination serves.

isDefault.description: Whether this is the default destination on its interconnect.

portState.description: The interconnect port's own state, which we read from our switch every minute. It is `waiting_for_link` until the port is first up, then `up`, or `down` if it drops. You can order services while it waits for link.

lldpNeighbour.description: The system name your device on the port sends over LLDP, while the port is up. Null when the port is not up or no name is sent.

SuspensionTakesEffect.description: On a suspended data service, how soon the suspension takes effect. It is `within 15 minutes` for a service we cut, which includes a service handed to you at layer 2 on your interconnect. It is `within 1 business day` for an Opticomm L3 service, which the carrier suspends for us. Null while the service is not suspended.

ExternalRef.description: Your own reference for this object, such as your customer or job id. It saves you keeping a map from our ids to yours. It can be up to 64 letters, digits, `_`, `.` or `-`. It is unique on your account for each kind of object. Two trunks cannot share one, but a trunk and a ticket can. The list's `externalRef` filter matches it exactly. Set it on create or with PATCH. Send null to clear it. Null when none is set.

Metadata.description: Your own key-value pairs on this object. You can set at most 20 keys. Each key can be up to 40 letters, digits, `_`, `.` or `-`. Each value is text of up to 255 characters. We store them and send them back on reads and webhooks. We never act on them. A map you send replaces the one we hold. Send `{}` or null to clear it. An empty object when none is set.

BookedChangeRef.description: The change booked on this service or trunk for a later date, or null when there is none. `GET /account/booked-changes` lists it in full. `DELETE /account/booked-changes/{id}` cancels it.

id.description: The booked change's id.

DataService.description: One of your data services, on any network, in one shape. Fields we do not hold for a service are null.

id.description: The product reference. It is an NBN PRI or an Opticomm product. Use it, or `serviceId`, to address the service.

href.description: Link to this service on the Check Networks API.

network.description: The network that delivers the service.

serviceId.description: The service reference on the network, such as an NBN AVC.

status.description: Where the service is up to. A connect still in flight is an order, not a service.

speed.description: The speed of the service's plan, in Mbps.

locationId.description: The premises the service is at, an NBN location id or an Opticomm one.

poi.description: The NBN point of interconnect the service is carried through, where we hold it.

plan.description: The plan you are billed for, by our SKU and name. Before the service has a plan, this is the SKU it was ordered on, with `name` null.

customerReference.description: Your own reference for the service.

tags.description: Your own tags on the service, in the order you set them with `PUT /data/services/{ref}/tags`. A Connect's tags carry over to the service it builds.

radiusUser.description: The service's RADIUS user reference, for the RADIUS endpoints such as `GET /data/radius/{ref}`.

endUser.description: The retail customer you assigned the service to, by its public number, or null.

endUserName.description: That end user's name, or null.

endUserDetail.description: Present only with `expand=endUser`. It is the end user in full, or null when the service has none.

endUser.description: The end user's public number, as `endUser`.

externalReference.description: Your own reference for the end user.

requestedAt.description: When the service was ordered. The list opens newest first on this.

updatedAt.description: When the service last changed.

DataOrderSummary.description: One order as a row of `GET /data/orders`. It has enough to act on without reading each order. Read the whole order at `GET /data/orders/{orderId}`, which is its `href`.

id.description: The order ID. This is the carrier's ID, or a Check Networks PND for an order the carrier does not have yet. The order read takes the same ID.

href.description: Link to the whole order.

status.description: "InProgress" covers everything still moving, including an order waiting for you.

statusReason.description: Why a failed order failed, or what an order waiting for you or for Check Networks needs. It is the same as on the order read.

locationId.description: The premises the order is for, as a LOC or OPC id.

orderReference.description: Your own reference, as you sent it when you placed the order.

salesReference.description: The same value as `orderReference`, the order's sales reference.

serviceId.description: The service the order produced, as an AVC or OVC id, once the carrier has assigned one.

endUser.description: The end user the order is for, by its public number, or null.

endUserName.description: That end user's name, or null.

actionRequired.description: What the order waits for from you, `appointmentRequired` or `ntdFull`, or null. The order read has the detail.

tags.description: Your own tags on the order.

updatedAt.description: When the order last changed.

service.description: Present only with `expand=service`, the order's service in the shape of the service list, or null before there is one.

MetadataInput.description: Your own key-value pairs, as `Metadata` describes them. The map you send replaces the one we hold. `{}` or null clears it.

DataOrderCreate.description: A Connect order for any data network. Take each value from the Service Qualification for the location, from `GET /data/sq/{locId}`.

locId.description: The premises. It is an NBN Location ID (LOC…) or an Opticomm Property ID (OPC…). The location decides which network and product the order is placed as.

bandwidthProductSku.description: One of the `availablePlans` SKUs from the Service Qualification.

orderReference.description: Your own reference for the order. Sending the same reference again returns the order it already placed rather than placing a second one.

tags.description: Your own tags on the order. They carry over to the service the order builds. See `PUT /data/services/{ref}/tags`. We trim each tag. A tag can be at most 255 characters, and tags match ignoring case. You can send at most 20. We check them before anything is sent to the carrier. A retry under the same `orderReference` keeps the tags the order was placed with.

externalRef.description: Your own reference for the data service this order builds. We hold it on the order and set it on the service when the service is built. See `PATCH /data/services/{ref}`. A reference that another of your data services holds, or another open order holds for its service, is a 422 before anything is sent to the carrier. A retry under the same `orderReference` keeps the reference the order was placed with.

metadata.description: Your own metadata for the data service this order builds, set on it when it is built.

informedConsent.description: Confirms the End User has given Informed Consent for the order.

resourceId.description:
Optional. One of the `resources` from the Service Qualification. It is the NTD or OTD port, or the copper pair, the service runs on.
Leave it out and we choose. We take the next free port on an installed NTD. On copper we take the one spare pair, or a new line where there is none. Where no NTD is installed, the order waits for an appointment (`order.appointmentRequired`). Where every port is in use, the order waits for you to choose a new NTD or a port to take over (`order.ntdFull`). We never order a second NTD unasked. Required on copper with more than one spare pair.

appointmentId.description: Optional. An appointment you reserved for this location, for an order that needs a technician. Without one, such an order waits for it (see `order.appointmentRequired`).

preferredAppointmentDate.description: Optional. The first day you would like a technician, if the order needs one. It is today or later, in your account's time zone, or the one you sent in `CN-Time-Zone`. The order's timeslots read (`GET /data/orders/{orderId}/timeslots`) starts here.

potsInterconnect.description: Copper only. The Full National Number (FNN) or Unconditioned Local Loop (ULL) of the phone service being transitioned. Required for an Active Service Class 12 pair. Do not send it otherwise.

priorityAssist.description: Optional. We send it to the carrier as its priority assist flag. We accept `true` only for an `endUser` on our Priority Assistance register. With no `endUser`, we accept it for your own account or your own end user, which we make when you register yourself, and never for another end user's. Otherwise we refuse the order with a 422 on `priorityAssist` before anything is drafted. A `newEndUser` is never on the register.

endUser.description: Optional. The end user the service is for, by its public number. The service, its charges and its usage are then theirs, as for an order placed in the portal for them. It must be one of your end users and not archived. Any other number is a 422 and we place no order.

occupancyDocumentId.description: Optional. For an NBN Connect Outstanding, the `id` of a proof of occupancy you uploaded with `POST /data/occupancy-documents`. Send it instead of the old service's id. It is evidence that the end user occupies the premises. We keep it with the order, and one order uses each document. A retry with the same `orderReference` may name it again. A retry after a call that stopped before the order was sent keeps it with the order before sending the order, unless the order already keeps one. Do not send it with `serviceRef`. Another account's document, or one another order used, is a 422.

bundleId.description: Optional. An open bundle to add the order to. The order goes in as a draft, and we place it when the bundle is submitted. A bundle that has been submitted, or is not yours, is a 422. A bundle already holds 200 draft orders at most. Past that it is a 422 with code `bundle_draft_limit`, and we make no draft.

newEndUser.description: Optional. A new end user to make and order for in this one call. Send it instead of `endUser`, never both. It takes the same fields and rules as creating an end user. We check both parts before we make anything. If we refuse the order, we do not keep the end user, and the answer is the order's 422. The end user's welcome email goes only once we accept the order. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same end user and order. The response's `endUser` is the new end user's number.

endUserType.description: Optional. What we tell the carrier the premises is. Left out, it is taken from the end user's own type, as the portal does.

addons.description: Optional. The add-on products to sell with the service, each with a quantity. You can send only the add-ons the portal offers for the chosen plan. Any other is a 422. Left out, the order carries the plan's default add-ons, as the portal ticks them. An empty list carries none. Each starts billing when the carrier accepts the order.

productId.description: The add-on product's public id, as an order's `addons` show it in `GET /data/orders/{orderId}`.

restorationSlaSku.description: Optional, NBN only. The restoration SLA. It must be one the chosen plan allows at this location. The standard SLA applies when you leave it out. We refuse it on an Opticomm order.

staticIp.description: Optional. A static IPv4 address, rather than one from the dynamic pool. A monthly charge applies.

ipv6.description: Optional. IPv6, with a framed /64 and a delegated prefix. It is free, and on unless you turn it off.

install.description:
Optional. How the service reaches the premises.

- `existing` is a port or pair already there. Name it in `resourceId`, or we choose.
- `new` is a new NTD, OTD or copper pair, where the Service Qualification offers a new install.
- `additional` is another NTD, OTD or pair beside the ones in use, where the Service Qualification offers an additional install.
- `fibreUplift` is NBN only. It is a Fibre Uplift, where the Service Qualification says `upliftAvailable`. nbn replaces the premises' copper access (FTTN, FTTB or FTTC) with fibre, on a new NTD. A 12-month term applies.

A `new` or `additional` install takes no `resourceId`. It needs a
technician appointment, on NBN and Opticomm alike. Without an
`appointmentId` the order waits for one (`order.appointmentRequired`).
It is a 422 where the location does not offer it.

A `fibreUplift` takes no `resourceId`, `transferType` or `serviceRef`.
You order it on an uplift plan, which is a `bandwidthProductSku` ending
`-UPL`. Any other plan is a 422. An uplift plan on any other order is
a 422 too. We read nbn's own uplift qualification
(`GET /nbn/service_qualification/fibre_uplift`) again before we draft
the order. A location it no longer offers is a 422. A technician
installs the NTD. Without an `appointmentId` the order waits for one
(`order.appointmentRequired`). The timeslots from
`GET /data/orders/{orderId}/timeslots` are the uplift's own. Reserve
one with `alternativeTechnology` `Fibre` on
`POST /nbn/appointments/reserve`.

transferType.description: Optional. Takes over a service another provider has at the premises, in this one call. On NBN, send it as the NBN order routes take it, with `serviceRef` and `customerAuthorityDate`. On Opticomm, send `Service Transfer` or `Service Transfer Reversal` with `customerAuthorityDate` and no `serviceRef`.

serviceRef.description: The AVC of the service being taken over. For an NBN transfer only.

customerAuthorityDate.description: The day the end user authorised the transfer. Required with `transferType`. It is today or earlier, in your account's time zone, or the one you sent in `CN-Time-Zone`.

DataOrder.description: An order for a data service, in carrier-agnostic form.

id.description: The order ID. This is the carrier's ID, or a Check Networks PND for an order the carrier does not have yet. That is an order waiting for your appointment or port (see `actionRequired`), or an NBN order awaiting Check Networks validation (see `statusReason`). The PND keeps finding the order after the carrier gives it an ID.

href.description: Link to this order on the Check Networks API.

type.description: What the order does.

status.description: Where the order has got to. "InProgress" covers everything still moving, including an order awaiting an appointment.

statusReason.description: Why a failed order failed. For an InProgress NBN order that NBN could not accept as Check Networks sent it, this is "Awaiting Check Networks validation". The fault is ours and nothing is needed from you. We correct and resubmit the order. It ends Failed only if we cannot place it. For an order waiting for you, this says what it needs (see `actionRequired`). Null otherwise.

actionRequired.description: What an order waiting for you needs, or null. Nothing has been sent to the carrier. Answer it with `PATCH /data/orders/{orderId}`.

reason.description: "appointmentRequired" means a technician is needed. Attach an appointment. "ntdFull" means every port on the NTD is in use. Attach an appointment for a new NTD, or name a port to take over.

demandType.description: The appointment type a technician visit for this order needs.

expiresAt.description: When the order is cancelled if it is still waiting.

preferredAppointmentDate.description: The first day you would like a technician, as you placed the order.

locationId.description: The premises the order is for, as a LOC or OPC id.

orderReference.description: Your own reference, as you sent it when you placed the order.

salesReference.description: The same value as `orderReference`, the order's sales reference.

serviceId.description: The service the order produced (AVC # or OVC #), once the carrier has assigned one.

appointmentId.description: The appointment attached to this order, if any.

tags.description: Your own tags on the order, as you sent them with `POST /data/orders`. They carry over to the service the order builds.

endUser.description: The end user the order is for, by its public number, or null.

endUserName.description: That end user's name, or null.

endUserType.description: What the carrier was told the premises is.

address.description: The premises as qualified, or null where we hold no address for the location.

poi.description: The Point of Interconnect the service is delivered through.

name.description: Our product's name for the plan, as the portal names it. Null where no product sells the SKU.

restorationSlaSku.description: The restoration SLA ordered, for NBN. Null for the standard one.

addons.description: The add-ons sold with the service.

staticIp.description: Whether a static IPv4 address was ordered.

ipv6.description: Whether IPv6 was ordered. Null where the order does not say.

price.description: The monthly charge and the one-off charges the order will start. It adds the plan and each add-on times its quantity, at your prices. Null for a key without `billing:read`, or where the plan is not priced for you.

contacts.description: The contacts given for the install. Null where the order holds none.

customerRequiredDate.description: The carrier's customer required date, where it has one.

events.description: The order's timeline, oldest first. It holds the order's state changes, the carrier's progress and appointment updates, and its notes.

createdBy.description:
Who placed the order. It is the portal user's name, or the name of the
API key that placed it through `POST /data/orders`. Null where we hold
neither, as for an API order placed before 21 Nov 2026.

service.description: Present only with `expand=service`. It is the service the order is for, in the shape of the service list (`GET /data/services`), or null before there is one.

DraftOrderPrice.description: A draft data order's price today. It holds the monthly charge and the one-off charges the order will start, at your prices. Each comes as ex GST, GST and inc GST, as on a data order's `price`.

CheckoutBlockedReason.description: Why a draft data order in a bundle cannot be checked out now. It is one of a closed set, and the first that applies in this order wins. `refused_by_rules` means the order is no longer a draft, the plan is no longer offered, your account cannot place orders, or another order is open at the location. `incomplete` means there is no plan, no NTD port or no informed consent. `needs_appointment` means a technician is needed and no appointment is booked, or its reservation has lapsed. `qualification_expired` means the site was qualified too long ago. Qualify it again and add a new draft. `price_changed` means the price today is above the price the draft was added at. Accept it with `acceptNewPrice` on `PATCH /bundles/{id}/items/{itemId}`. A price that fell is not a block. The draft goes at the lower price.

BundleItem.description: One item of a bundle, in the bundle's order. It is a data order, a number order or a voice trunk.

id.description: The item's own id. For a data order it is the carrier order id once placed, and its `PND` reference before then. For a number order it is the order's `id`. For a trunk it is the trunk's id in the bundle. Send that id as `trunk` to `POST /numbers` to put numbers on the trunk.

href.description: Where you read the item on its own. That is the data order once the carrier has it, the number order, or the trunk once it is set up. Null until then.

label.description: What the portal calls the item.

position.description: Its place in the bundle. 1 is first.

waitsForPrevious.description: Whether it starts only once every item above it has completed. Numbers on the bundle's own trunk always do.

state.description: `draft` until it is released. `inProgress` once it has been sent, and also while we resend an order the carrier asked us to try again. Then `completed`, or `failed` when it ended without completing.

waitingFor.description: The ids of the items above it it is still waiting on.

outcomeReason.description: Why it ended without completing, or null.

price.description: A draft data order's price today. When `checkoutBlockedReason` is `price_changed`, this is the new price to accept. Null for any other item, for a draft with no plan or one your prices do not cover, and for a key without `billing:read`.

canCheckout.description: Whether this draft data order can be checked out now. Null for any item that is not a draft data order still to be sent.

checkoutBlockedReason.description: Why it cannot be checked out now. A submit that names the item refuses it with this reason. Null when it can be, and for any item that is not a draft data order still to be sent.

checkoutBlockedMessage.description: What to do about `checkoutBlockedReason`, in words for this draft.
checkoutBlockedMessage.example: The price has gone up since this draft was added. Accept the new price to check it out.

draftRemoval.description: When this draft is removed if you do not check it out. Null for anything we never remove. That is a delayed order, an order the carrier already has, a draft that has been checked out, a number order or a trunk.

keepLimit.description: The latest date Keep (`POST /bundles/{id}/keep`) can move it to. That is 90 days from when the draft was made.

id.description: The Check Networks Delayed Order Reference #.

carrier.description: The network the order will be placed on when it submits.

status.description: The status of the Delayed Order.

submitDateTime.description: When this Delayed Order submits. Null while it is held for you. That means it was not sent at its time and needs you (see `heldForAction` on `order.delayed`). Submit it now, give it a new time, or cancel it.

endUser.description: Optional. The end user the service is for, by its public number. The service, its charges and its usage are then theirs, as for an order placed in the portal for them. It must be one of your end users and not archived. Any other number is a 422 and we place no order.

addons.description: Optional. The add-on products to sell with the service, each with a quantity. You can send only the add-ons the portal offers for the chosen plan. Any other is a 422. Left out, the order carries the plan's default add-ons, as the portal ticks them. An empty list carries none. Each starts billing when the carrier accepts the order.

productId.description: The add-on product's public id, as an order's `addons` show it in `GET /data/orders/{orderId}`.

opcId.description: The Opticomm Property ID (OPC #) for the premises the order is for. Find it for an address with a `/opticomm/address/search` request.

bandwidthProductSku.description:
The product SKU of the Bandwidth Product you are ordering.
Find the options for the property (OPC #) in the `productAvailability` list of an Opticomm Service Qualification request.

orderReference.description:
Your reference number for this order. It can be up to 45 characters.
You can use letters ("a-Z"), numbers ("0-9"), underscores ("_"), hyphens ("-") and periods (".").

portId.description: Optional. The NTD UNI-D port to deliver the service on. Find a free port in the Service Qualification response's `ntd.dataPorts`. When you leave it out, we pick the first free port.

appointmentId.description: A reserved installation appointment for the property. Required when the Service Qualification response shows `appointmentRequired`. That is typically Service Class 2 premises.

transferType.description: Send this for a service-transfer (churn) order, which takes over an active service at the property from another provider.

customerAuthorityDate.description: The date you obtained Customer Authority from the end user. Required for Service Transfer orders, and only used by them. It must be less than 45 days old.

plannedCompletionDate.description: Optional. The earliest date the order should complete. When you leave it out, the order completes as soon as possible.

endUserType.description: Optional. The end-user type for the service. Left out, it is taken from the end user's own type, as the portal does.

priorityAssist.description: Optional. We send it to the carrier as its priority assist flag. Defaults to false. We accept `true` only for a customer on our Priority Assistance register. That is the `endUser`. When you name none, it is your own account or your own end user, never another end user's. Otherwise we refuse the order with a 422 on `priorityAssist` before we hold anything.

DataDelayedOrder.description: A held (Delayed) order in full. It has the fields you sent when you created it, plus the scheduled submission time. We hold the order ourselves. Nothing has gone to any carrier. That is why the reference is a Check Networks pending reference and not a carrier order id.

id.description: The Check Networks Delayed Order Reference #.

carrier.description: The network the order will be placed on when it submits.

state.description: Always Delayed while the order is held.

orderReference.description: The reference you sent when you created the order.

salesReference.description: The same value as `orderReference`, the order's sales reference.

propertyId.description: The network's reference for the property the order is for. It is an Opticomm Property ID (OPC #) or an nbn Location ID (LOC #).

submitDateTime.description: When the order is scheduled to submit. Null while it is held for you. That means it was not sent at its time and needs you. Submit it now, give it a new time, or cancel it.

DataOrderAnswer.description: What an order waiting for you needs. That is an appointment, or a port to take over. Send `appointmentId` or `resourceId`.

appointmentId.description: An appointment you reserved from the order's timeslots, from `GET /data/orders/{orderId}/timeslots`. On an NTD with no free port, a technician installs another NTD.

resourceId.description: For an NTD with no free port, the port to take over. Take it from the Service Qualification's `resources`.

serviceId.description: The service on that port, which this order takes over. On NBN it is the AVC.

customerAuthorityDate.description: The date the End User authorised you to take the service over. Required with `serviceId`.

DataProvisioningRecord.description: A provisioning request: what was configured for a service, what we allocated for it, and whether it is live yet.

id.description: The provisioning request reference.

href.description: Link to this provisioning request on the Check Networks API.

orderId.description: The order this provisioning belongs to.

status.description: Pending while the carrier is still working the order. Complete once the service is built and everything below is final.

deliveryMode.description: How the service is handed to you.

protocol.description: The Layer 3 session protocol. Null for Layer 2.

staticIp.description: Whether the IPv4 address is held stable. Null for Layer 2.

ipv6.description: Whether IPv6 is provisioned. Null for Layer 2.

handoff.description: Layer 2 only. The interconnect this service hands off on.

cTag.description: Layer 2 only. The inner VLAN. It is the one you chose while pending, and the one we allocated once complete.

pppoeUsername.description: PPPoE only. The login the CPE dials with, once it exists.

serviceId.description: The service this produced, as an AVC or OVC id, once assigned.

id.description: The provisioning request reference. Track it with `GET /data/provisioning/{ref}`.

orderNumber.description: The order the configuration was applied to.

deliveryMode.description: How the service will be handed to you.

protocol.description: The Layer 3 session protocol. Null for Layer 2.

staticIp.description: Whether the IPv4 address is held stable. Null for Layer 2.

ipv6.description: Whether IPv6 will be provisioned. Null for Layer 2.

pppoeUsername.description: PPPoE only. The full login the CPE dials with, once it exists. Null until the carrier accepts the order and the service is built.

sTag.description: Layer 2 only. The outer VLAN (S-Tag) your service is handed off on.

cTag.description: Layer 2 only. The inner VLAN (C-Tag) for this service. Null until we allocate it, unless you chose one.

status.description: Whether the service is built. Pending while the carrier is still working the order. Complete once it is done and the tags are final.

handoff.description: Layer 2 only. The interconnect in use, or the string `accountDefault` when we used your default destination for the POI.

DataServiceDetail.description: One of your data services, with its live status.

contract.description: The service's contract term, as the portal's Contract Term card shows it. It says when the term ends, and what disconnecting today would charge, with the plan's and every add-on's charge together. Null for a service with no term. For another cease date, use `GET /data/services/{ref}/disconnect-quote`.

earlyTerminationChargeExGst.description: Dollars, ex GST. `0.00` once the term has ended, or when the charge was waived.

earlyTerminationChargeWaived.description: True when we waived the early termination charge. The charge is `0.00` though the service is still in its term, and a disconnect charges nothing.

session.description: Whether the service is connected right now. Null for a service that is not Live.

status.description: `Available` means `online` answers. `Unavailable` means the network did not answer just now. Try again. `OnRequest` means this network has no live status we can read without starting a test there. Ask `GET /data/radius/{ref}/online` with the service's `radiusUser`. `NotOnOurRadius` means the service is handed to you at layer 2 on your interconnect and never logs on to our RADIUS, so it has no live status here.

online.description: Whether a session is up. Null unless `status` is Available.

DataServiceUsage.description: One month of a service's data usage, by day. Usage is reported, never charged.

id.description: The service's product reference.

from.description: The start of the billing month, in your bill's time zone or the one you sent in `CN-Time-Zone`. It carries the zone's offset.

to.description: The end of the billing month, or now for the current month, in the same zone as `from`.

complete.description: False for the current month, which is still counting.

allowanceBytes.description: The plan's included data, if it has a figure. Null for unlimited.

days.description: One entry per day with usage, oldest first.

date.description: The day, in the same zone as `from`.

NetworkOutage.description: One entry from the Check Networks outage register, as published under the Telecommunications (Customer Communications for Outages) Industry Standard 2024 (Part 4), or a planned maintenance window you were sent notice of. Field values match the public register at https://status.checknetworks.tools. For a planned window, `startedAt` and `estimatedRestorationAt` are the window's start and end, and `additionalInfo` describes its impact.

reference.description: The Check Networks outage reference

title.description: Short plain-English description of the outage

type.description: Whether the outage is planned maintenance or an unplanned outage

severity.description: For an unplanned outage, its class under the Standard. `major` is at least 100,000 services or a whole State, for more than 60 minutes. `significant_local` is at least 1,000 regional or 250 remote services, for more than 6 or 3 hours. Null for planned maintenance.

status.description: Whether the outage is still in progress or has been resolved

startedAt.description: When the outage began, in UTC like every time the API returns

resolvedAt.description: When service was restored. Null while the outage is open.

estimatedRestorationAt.description: The current estimate for restoration. Null when there is no estimate yet. That is meaningful, not a placeholder.

timezone.description: IANA timezone of the affected area, for showing the UTC times in local time

affectedSites.description: Our own sites affected (a data centre or exchange), by name. Absent for planned maintenance.

premisesAffected.description: Number of premises affected. Null where Check Networks has no technical visibility of the count, and always null for planned maintenance.

responsibleParty.description: The carrier or carriage service provider responsible for resolving the outage. Null where Check Networks is itself responsible.

cause.description: High-level cause. The literal value `withheld` means a cause is known but has been withheld from publication; null means no cause is recorded yet.

causeNatural.description: Whether the cause relates to a natural event or weather

additionalInfo.description: Any further published detail about the outage

firstPublishedAt.description: When this register entry was first published

lastRectifiedAt.description: When this register entry was last corrected, if it has been

yourAffectedServiceCount.description: How many of your services this outage hit, from the footprint we recorded when we published it. It is 0 when the outage reaches your area but none of your services. Null for planned maintenance, because we do not record which services a window touches.

yourAffectedServices.description: Each of your services this outage hit, including your end users' services. Use it to tell them. Null for planned maintenance.

service.description: The service's reference (a data service id, trunk or number).

address.description: The service address. Null when it is masked (`addressMasked`), or when we hold none.

addressMasked.description: True when we withhold the address because the end user has a family violence safety record. The End Users list in the portal withholds their contact details the same way.

endUser.description: The end user the service belongs to, by its public number. Null for a service you hold yourself.

ServiceDegradation.description: A Potential Service Degradation. The link at the service's point of interconnect is near capacity. The service may be slower at peak, but it is not down. It is not an outage under the Standard, so it carries no register fields.

startedAt.description: When we opened it, in UTC.

estimatedRestorationAt.description: When we expect the extra capacity to be in place. Null until we have a date.

area.description: The affected points of interconnect, e.g. `Sandbox (0SND)`.

additionalInfo.description: What end users may notice until the capacity is added.

url.description: Where the status site lists it.

id.description: The test's id, the carrier's reference for it.

test.description: The test's code, as `GET /data/services/{ref}/diagnostics/types` lists it.

status.description: Where the test is, taken from either carrier's own states. `accepted` means it was asked for and has not started. `in_progress` and `completed` are what they say. `cancelled` also covers a test whose result never came. `rejected` means the carrier refused it.

result.description: `passed` or `failed` once the carrier says. `none` until then, or for a test with no pass or fail.

DataServiceHealthReport.description: One health report on a data service, in the same shape on every network. `overall` is the result the portal's service page shows.

id.description: The report's id. Read it again with `GET /data/health/{id}`.

serviceId.description: The service's product reference. It is a PRI or an Opticomm product.

network.description: The access network the service is on.

status.description: `pending` until the carrier answers. The `serviceHealth.reportReady` webhook says when a report is complete.

overall.description: The report's overall result, as the portal shows it. Null while pending, or when the carrier gave none.

summary.description: The carrier's summary of the report, when it gives one.

alertMessage.description: The carrier's alert, when the report raised one.

requestedAt.description: When the report was asked for.

checks.description: Each measurement in the report. Empty while pending. An NBN report lists its Connectivity, Performance and Stability roll-up first, under `Overview`.

category.description: The group the measurement is in, as the carrier names it.

name.description: The measurement, as the carrier names it.

result.description: The measurement's result. Null when the carrier gave none.

unit.description: The value's unit, when it has one.

DataRadiusUser.description: A RADIUS user. There is one per service.

id.description: The RADIUS user reference.

href.description: Link to this user on the Check Networks API.

username.description: The username the service authenticates with.

realm.description: The realm the username sits in. Null where the service authenticates on its access circuit rather than a login.

authentication.description: How the service authenticates. An IPoE service has no password. The access circuit is the identity.

serviceId.description: The service this user belongs to.

detailSource.description: Whose RADIUS authenticates the service, and so where the detail below comes from. `checknetworks` is our own RADIUS. For some services the detail is read live on every request. `carrier` is another carrier's RADIUS. We cannot read it, so the detail is unavailable. `handoff` means the service is handed to you at layer 2 on your interconnect and never logs on to our RADIUS. There is no detail and `online` is null.

detailAvailable.description: False when we could not read the detail, because a live read failed or the carrier's RADIUS cannot be read. The detail fields are then null. The rest of the record is still given.

online.description: Whether the user has a session up right now. Null when the detail is unavailable.

ipAddress.description: The IPv4 address assigned to the service. Behind CGNAT this is the inner 100.64.0.0/10 address. See `publicAddress`.

staticIp.description: Whether the IPv4 address is static.

publicAddress.description: The shared public IPv4 address, when the service is behind CGNAT. Null for a service with its own public address.

publicPortRange.description: The ports of `publicAddress` this service holds, when behind CGNAT.

ipv6Address.description: The IPv6 WAN address. On our own RADIUS the service gets a WAN /64 instead, shown here in CIDR form.

ipv6DelegatedPrefix.description: The IPv6 prefix delegated to the service's router.

lastAuthentication.description: The latest authentication. Null when none is recorded.

reason.description: Why a reject happened on our own RADIUS, such as `no_live_service` or `bad_credential`. Null on an accept, and for a service read live.

recentDropouts.description: Sessions that ended within the recent window of five days.

DataRadiusNotChecked.description: The service is on Opticomm's RADIUS and we hold no session check for it. A read never asks Opticomm. Ask for a check with `POST /data/radius/{ref}/session-check`, then read again once it completes.

retrievedAt.description: Always null, as no check is held.

message.example: This session has not been checked at Opticomm recently. Ask for a check with POST /data/radius/{ref}/session-check, then read it here once it completes.

DataRadiusNotOnOurRadius.description: The service is handed to you at layer 2 on your interconnect and never logs on to our RADIUS. There is no session here to read, so it is neither online nor offline.

message.example: This service is handed to you at layer 2 on your interconnect and never logs on to our RADIUS, so we hold no session for it.

DataRadiusSession.description: A live RADIUS session. Traffic is named from the end user's point of view. What they sent is the upload.

id.description: The RADIUS user reference this session belongs to.

username.description: The username the session authenticated with.

source.description: Where we read the session from. `checknetworks` is our own RADIUS. For some services it is read live on this request. `opticomm` is Opticomm's session history from the latest session check, as at `lastSeenAt`.

startedAt.description: When the session came up. Null if the carrier does not give it.

lastSeenAt.description: When we last heard accounting for the session. For a session read live this is the time of the read. For an `opticomm` session it is when Opticomm reported the session.

durationSeconds.description: How long the session has been up. For a session read live we count it from `startedAt`, and it is null when `startedAt` is. For an `opticomm` session it is as Opticomm reported it.

ipAddress.description: The address assigned to the session.

uploadBytes.description: Traffic sent by the end user. For a session read live, traffic is reported to two decimal places of a unit, such as 27.38 GB, and this is that amount in bytes, with GB taken as 10^9. Null if there is no figure.

downloadBytes.description: Traffic sent to the end user, converted the same way as `uploadBytes`.

id.description: The service's product reference. It is a PRI or an Opticomm product.

endUser.description: The end user's public number, or null when none is assigned.

downloadBytes.description: Bytes sent to the end user in the month.

uploadBytes.description: Bytes the end user sent in the month.

allowanceBytes.description: The plan's monthly allowance, or null for an unlimited plan.

percentUsed.description: The total as a percentage of the allowance, to one decimal place. Null with no allowance.

complete.description: False for the current month, which is counted up to now.

id.description: The location ID as queried (LOC… or OPC…).

href.description: URL of this qualification.

network.description: The access network the qualification ran against.

locId.description: The premises' NBN Location ID. For NBN queries it equals `id`. For Opticomm queries we resolve it from the address. It is null when the premises has no NBN footprint we can resolve.

serviceable.description: Whether the premises can be served on the network.

status.description: The carrier's own serviceability status for the premises.

serviceClass.description: The carrier's serviceability class, where reported.

primaryAccessTech.description: The primary access technology, such as FTTP, HFC or FTTC.

alternativeTech.description: NBN only. The alternative technology the carrier plans for the premises, where reported. An example is Fibre at an upgrade-programme FTTN or FTTC premises.

upliftAvailable.description: True when the premises is FTTN or FTTC with Fibre as the alternative technology, and the carrier confirms Fibre Uplift eligibility. The full uplift document is at `/nbn/service_qualification/fibre_uplift`.

additionalInstallAvailable.description: True when every port or copper pair at the premises is in use and the carrier will install another device or pair for a further service. On NBN, order a connect with `ntdId` (or `copperPairId`) set to `NEW` and a Standard Install appointment. On Opticomm, order a connect that names no OTD, with an Additional Install appointment. The subsequent installation charge applies.

newDevelopmentChargeApplies.description: NBN only. True when the carrier's New Development Charge applies at the premises. Null where the network does not report it.

region.description: NBN only. The carrier region, where reported.

poi.description: NBN only. The Point of Interconnect serving the premises.

resources.description: The in-ground access resources a service can be provisioned on. These are NTD and OTD ports and copper pairs. Empty when the technology needs no resource pick, such as a new-install fibre premises.

status.description: A port is `Free` or `Used`. A copper pair is `Line In Use`, which means a service runs on it, or `Line Not In Use`, which means it is a spare pair. These are nbn's own words.

installFeeApplies.description: Copper pairs only. True when a subsequent installation charge applies to activating this pair.

serviceIdMatch.description: Present on NBN Service Transfer queries. It is true on the one resource that carries the `serviceRef` you supplied.

siteRestrictionError.description: NBN Service Transfer only. The carrier's rejection of the `serviceRef` you supplied, with a code such as RJ002003. Null when the transfer validated or you supplied no `serviceRef`.

enterpriseEthernet.description: The NBN Enterprise Ethernet check at the premises. Null when we cannot resolve an NBN footprint or the check was unavailable.

availablePlans.description: The bandwidth products the carrier sells at the premises. These are the SKUs the order endpoints accept. Empty when the lookup is unavailable.

otherNetwork.description: The same premises on the other network, where both NBN and Opticomm serve it. It is that network's qualification exactly as `/data/sq/{locId}` answers for its own ID, without an `otherNetwork` of its own. Null when the premises is on one network only, when that network does not answer, or on a transfer check (`serviceRef`), which covers the network you asked about only. Order on whichever network is serviceable with the plan you want.

GeographicAddress.description: An nbn address in nbn's own shape. Each field appears only when nbn holds it. Coordinates are strings.

id.description: The NBN Location ID.

href.description: Link to this address, `/nbn/address/{locId}`, on this API. Present only when the carrier sent a link.

formattedAddress.description: The address on a single line, for a person to read.
formattedAddress.example: Lot 708 16 De Vecchi Cl, Edmonton, QLD

lotNumber.description:
The Lot number. It is a reference number allocated to a property for subdivision administration before road numbering.

Where an official Road number has not been assigned, this field can be used for postal purposes and to identify the address site.

planNumber.description: The deposited plan number allocated to a property for subdivision administration before road numbering, in addition to the Lot number.

roadNumber1.description:
The number of the address in the road or thoroughfare. For a ranged address it is the start number.
It can include an alphabetic prefix and an alphabetic suffix.

roadNumber2.description:
The last number for a ranged address in the road or thoroughfare.
It can include an alphabetic prefix and an alphabetic suffix.
It is used for ranged street numbers. Otherwise it is blank.

roadName.description:
The name of the road or thoroughfare for the address site or complex.
It holds only the road name.

roadTypeCode.description: The abbreviation code for the type of road or thoroughfare for the address site or complex.

roadSuffixCode.description: The abbreviation code for the suffix of the road or thoroughfare for the address site or complex.

localityName.description: The name of the locality or suburb of the address.

postcode.description:
The Australian numeric descriptor for a postal delivery area, aligned with locality, suburb or place.

Required if `stateTerritoryCode` is not provided.

stateTerritoryCode.description:
The State or Territory code of the address.

Required if `postcode` is not provided.

gnafId.description: The Geocoded National Address File (GNAF) ID.

secondaryComplexName.description:
The name of a building or area within a complex site.
It can be the name of an entire building within an address site that has its own separate address.

unitTypeCode.description:
The sub-dwelling unit type code.
Within a complex, an abbreviation for the type of an address found within a building, sub-complex or marina.

unitNumber.description:
The sub-dwelling unit number.
Within a complex, a number that identifies an address found within a building, sub-complex or marina.
It can include a leading alphabetic prefix and a trailing alphabetic suffix.

levelTypeCode.description: Within a complex, an abbreviation for the floor or level of a multi-storey building or sub-complex.

levelNumber.description:
Within a complex, the number of the floor or level of a multi-storey building or sub-complex.
It can include a leading alphabetic prefix and a trailing alphabetic suffix.

addressSiteName.description:
Also known as the Building property name or Primary Complex name.

The official place name, or the name in common use, for an address site. That includes the name of a building, homestead, building complex, agricultural property, park or unbounded address site. It is the name of an entire building or address site.

complexRoadNumber1.description: Within a complex, the number of the address in the road or thoroughfare. For a ranged address it is the start number.

complexRoadNumber2.description: Within a complex, the last number for a ranged address in the road or thoroughfare.

complexRoadName.description:
Within a complex, the name of the road or thoroughfare of the address. A road name can look as if it holds a road type, such as The Boulevard.
The road type can also be null.

complexRoadTypeCode.description: Within a complex, an abbreviation for the type of road or thoroughfare of the address.

complexRoadSuffixCode.description: Within a complex, an abbreviation for the suffix of the road or thoroughfare of the address.

locationDescriptor.description: An extra descriptor that further identifies the location.

geographicDatum.description: The geographic datum of the address.

latitude.description: The latitude of the address, as a decimal string.

longitude.description: The longitude of the address, as a decimal string.

id.description: Unique NBN Reference for the location

pri.description: The Primary Reference Identifier for the NBN Service.

avc.description: The AVC Reference Identifier for the NBN Service.

bandwidth.description: The bandwidth of the NBN Service. Null when the service carries no plan.

reference.description: Your reference for the NBN Service. Null when you have not set one.

requestDateTime.description: Date and time that this request was received

startDateTime.description: Date and Time the period starts

endDateTime.description: Date and Time the period ends

reason.description: The reason provided as a string

tradingName.description: The name that the organization trades under.

inductionRequired.description: Is site induction required to access the site?

securityRequired.description: Is security required to access the site?

currentWhiteCard.description: Is a white card required to access the site?

securityClearance.description: Is security clearance required to access the site?

siteAccessClearance.description: Is site access clearance required to access the site?

additionalDetails.description: Additional details that may be required for on site.
additionalDetails.example: Enter through the door at the end of the rainbow. Knock four times.

role.description: The role this entity plays in relation to this record.

@referredType.description: The type of this Related Entity

contactName.description: Name of Access Seeker contact person

phoneNumber.description: Phone Number for Access Seeker contact

emailAddress.description: Email Address of Access Seeker contact

validFor.description: Time period for the appointment time slot

appointmentSlotType.description:
Appointment Slot Type.
- AM - Morning
- PM - Afternoon
- AHA - After-Hours Appointment
- CA - Customer Appointment

withinTimeWindow.description:
Is the timeslot is within the Order/Incident SLA period?.

type.description: The Type of History Item

party.description: The party responsible for the History Event

id.description: NBN Reference ID for the appointment

queryDateTime.description: When the query request was received

href.description: Link to get appointment details from NBN

externalId.description: RSP Reference ID provided in the request

creationDate.description: Date the appointment record was created

lastUpdate.description: Date the appointment record was last updated

status.description: The status of the appointment

appointmentHistory.description: History of changes to the appointment slot

id.description: NBN Appointment ID

href.description: Link to get appointment details from NBN

externalId.description: RSP Reference ID provided in the request

status.description: The status of the appointment

id.description: Unique Identifier for the nbn Location

region.description: Region the zone is located in

appointmentSlotType.description:
The type of appointment slot.
- AM - Morning

validFor.description: The period the time slot covers.

appointmentLeadTime.description: The lead time for this time slot.

comments.description: Comments, given when no forecast upgrade date is provided.

forecastDate.description: The date nbn is likely to do the physical or technical upgrade to the backhaul link. It also shows whether the LOC ID is served by a Priority Upgrade Link, which has an Average 28 Day Busy Hour Link Packet Loss of 0.25% or greater. Not provided when `priorityLink` is No.

comments.description: Comments, given when no backhaul forecast date is available. Not provided when `priorityLink` is No.

id.description: The Access Virtual Circuit ID. The Access Virtual Circuit is an Ethernet-based Layer 2 virtual connection across the nbn™ network. It is provided by the 1:1 Unicast data service construct and carries customer traffic between a single UNI and E-NNI. Only returned when you query by AVC ID. Not returned when you query by Location ID.

overallStatus.description: Provides an indication of the performance of cells on the tower that the Network Termination Device (NTD) is provisioned to, measured across a rolling 7 days. Valid values: No Issue Detected, Potential Issue Detected, Issue Detected.

id.description: The unique Cell ID nbn assigns. For Service Class 5 locations it is the predicted Cell ID.

siteName.description: The site name for the base station. For Service Class 5 locations it is the predicted site name.

category.description:
The type of cell. It is one of two values.
- "Predicted" is for service class 5.
- "Serving" is for service class 6.

wirelessServingArea.description: The Fixed Wireless Network nodes in a specific area, connected through a backhaul network to a fibre access node. It applies to service class 6 only.

averageBusyHourThroughputCategory.description: The Average 30 Day Downlink Throughput category of the cells during busy hour. When the value is 'less than 3Mbps' or '3 Mbps to less than 6 Mbps', we give either a Forecast Date or a Comment. When the value is 'Above 6 Mbps', we give neither.

priorityLink.description: Whether the cell is connected through a priority upgrade link. The values are Yes, No and Upgrade. When the value is No, `forecastDate` and `comment` are not required. Upgrade means the upgrade is complete but the link still reports an Average 28 Day Busy Hour Link Packet Loss of 0.25% or greater. That is typically because the 28 day average does not yet reflect the post-upgrade link performance.

id.description: The line item's identifier. It is usually a sequence number, such as 01, 02 or 03. The default is "01".

action.description: The action to be carried out on the Product.

id.description: The unique NBN Order ID. While nbn does not hold the order, it is one of our PNDs. That is the case when the order is Acknowledged before it reaches nbn, or is PendingReview.

href.description: Link to this order on this API.

orderType.description: The type of order. It is Connect a new service, Modify an existing service, or Disconnect an existing service.

state.description: The current state of the order, from the nbn Product Order state model, plus one state of ours. `PendingReview` means the order passed our checks but nbn could not accept it as we sent it. The fault is ours and we need nothing from you. We correct and resubmit it. Until nbn gives it an Order ID, its id is one of our PNDs. `GET /nbn/orders/product/{orderId}` accepts the PND, and keeps accepting it afterwards. The order ends `Cancelled` if it cannot be placed. A genuine refusal is never `PendingReview`. Examples are informed consent not evidenced, or no NTD capacity. The order is refused with a 422.

subState.description: The current substate of the order as per the nbn Product Order state model.

completionDate.description: Date when the order was completed

plannedCompletionDate.description: Date when all appointments and the order expected to be completed

plannedExpiryDate.description: When time to complete the assistance requested is required by

infrastructurePlannedDate.description: Date when the infrastructure will be available

count.description: Number of Delayed Orders in the results
