bandwidthProductSku.description:
The product SKU of the Bandwidth Product you are ordering.
It sets which Service Layer (Layer 2 or Layer 3) the order can be provisioned with.
Use the Product Qualification > Eligible Bandwidth Products API to find the options for the Location (LOC #).

restorationSlaSku.description:
Optional. The product SKU of the Service Restoration SLA.
If you leave it out, the Standard SLA ("NBN-SLA-TC4-STD") applies.
The SLA sets how quickly NBN responds when an issue affects the service. It depends on the SLA Region.
Response times are Business Hours unless you pick a (24/7) SLA.
Enhanced or Premium SLAs may cost an additional monthly amount.
A bundled SLA Product SKU is accepted only with an eligible Bandwidth Product SKU.
Use the Product Qualification > Eligible Restoration SLA Products API to find selectable options for the Location (LOC #).

orderReference.description:
Your reference number for this order, up to 35 characters.
Use only letters ("a-Z"), numbers ("0-9"), underscores ("_"), hyphens ("-") and periods (".").

EXAMPLES:
 - "New.Foo_BAR-2020-09-20"
 - "ExampleCompanyName"
 - "JaneCitizen-123456"
 - "Reseller.EndUser.123456"

endUserRef.description:
Not accepted. Sending this field returns 422. We assign the End User, and this API has no End User (Party) records.
It is the carrier's reference (EUP #) of the End User to associate the order with.

EXAMPLES:
 - "EUP000000000000"

priorityAssist.description:
Optional. Whether Priority Assistance is required.
It defaults to "false".
Send "true" only where the end user is eligible for a Downstream Priority Assistance Service under NBN Co's Wholesale Broadband Agreement.
We accept "true" only for a customer on our Priority Assistance register. That is the end user named in `endUser`. When none is named, it is the account or your own end user, never another end user. Any other order is refused with a 422 on `priorityAssist` before anything is drafted.

endUser.description: Optional. This is our end user number, not the carrier's `endUserRef`. It is the number of the end user the order is for, as `POST /data/orders` takes it. The order and its service belong to that end user. With `priorityAssist` true, that end user's registration is the one that counts. An end user that is not on this account is refused with a 422 on `priorityAssist`, or on `endUser` when the flag is not set.

ntdId.description:
The reference number of the Network Termination Device (NTD) to place the order against.
Send "NEW" to order a new NTD. Do that only when no existing NTD at the premises has a free port.

appointmentId.description:
The NBN Appointment ID to attach to this order. Required when `ntdId`
is "NEW", because a technician attends to install the NTD. It must be
an Appointment with Demand Type "Standard Install". Taking a port on
an NTD that is already installed needs no appointment.

unidPortId.description:
The Port ID for the UNI-D Resource. Required for Service Transfers, or when you want an exact port.
NBN assigns the next available port when you leave this out or send `null`.

transferType.description:
The Service Transfer type. It applies only to Service Transfers, and
is required for them.
 - "Service Transfer" - transfer an existing nbn service from another provider to you.
 - "Service Transfer Reversal" - recover an existing service that was incorrectly transferred away from you.
 - "Connect Outstanding" - connect a new service over a line that still has an existing active service not controlled by the End User.  This needs time to legally cancel the existing service.

occupancyDocumentId.description: Optional, and ours. On a Connect Outstanding, send the `id` of a proof of occupancy you uploaded with `POST /data/occupancy-documents`. It is evidence that the End User occupies the premises. We keep it with the order, and only that order may use it. A retry with the same `orderReference` may name it again. A document from another account, or one that another order used, is a 422.

serviceRef.description:
The Service ID (AVC #) for a Service Transfer. It applies only to Service Transfers, and is required for them.

Validate the AVC # against the CPI # or NTD + UNI Port with the SQ Single Site API first.

customerAuthorityDate.description:
The date the Customer authorised this order, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. A date-time is read as its date. It must be within the last 45 calendar days.
It applies only to Service Transfers. It is required when `transferType` is "Service Transfer" or "Connect Outstanding".

informedConsent.description: Confirms the End User has given Informed Consent for this order.

overlapPeriod.description:
Optional. The overlap period for Service Transfers.
Use it when you transfer a service to a new UNI-D Port. It is the number of hours after Order Completion during which the service is active on both the old and new ports. Update the End User's infrastructure in that time.
It applies only to Service Transfers.

fromPortId.description:
The UNI-D Port ID of the existing service. Send the new Port ID in `unidPortId`.
It applies only to Service Transfers. It is required when `overlapPeriod` is "4".

vlanMode.description:
Optional. The VLAN Mode sets which Product Template is used when ordering this connection.

Do not send it unless you need it.

When you leave it out, we assume "Default-Mapped".
It is meant mainly for moving existing "Tagged" PPPoE services without changing the client CPE configuration.

You cannot change this value with a Modify Order. You must cancel and reorder the service, which can bring it down for 24-48 hours.

uniVlanId.description:
The UNI VLAN ID # used to tag the service traffic. Required when
`vlanMode` is "Tagged". Send a value from 1 to 4094.

locId.description: The NBN Location ID for the premises the order is for.

bandwidthProductSku.description:
The product SKU of the Bandwidth Product you are ordering. It decides which Service Layer (Layer 2 or Layer 3) the order can be provisioned with.
Find the options for the Location (LOC #) with the Product Qualification > Eligible Bandwidth Products API.

restorationSlaSku.description:
(Optional) The product SKU of the Service Restoration SLA. It sets how quickly nbn responds if an issue affects the service, depending on the SLA Region.
If you leave it out, we apply the Standard SLA ("NBN-SLA-TC4-STD").
Response times are Business Hours unless you pick a (24/7) SLA. Enhanced or Premium SLAs may cost extra each month.
A bundled SLA product SKU is accepted only with an eligible Bandwidth Product SKU.

deliveryPostcode.description:

occupancyDocumentId.description: (Optional, ours) On a Connect Outstanding, the `id` of a proof of occupancy you uploaded with `POST /data/occupancy-documents`. It is evidence that the End User occupies the premises. We keep it with the order, and only that order may use it. A retry with the same `orderReference` may name it again. A document from another account, or one another order used, is a 422.

serviceRef.description:
(Conditional) The Service ID (AVC #) for a Service Transfer. It applies to Service Transfers only, and they must send it.
Check the AVC # against the CPI # or NTD + UNI Port first, with the SQ Single Site API.

customerAuthorityDate.description:
(Conditional) The date the Customer authorised this order, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. We read a date-time as its date. It must be within the last 45 calendar days.
It applies to Service Transfers only. Send it when `transferType` is "Service Transfer" or "Connect Outstanding".

informedConsent.description: Confirms that the End User has given Informed Consent for this order to be placed.

overlapPeriod.description:
(Optional) The overlap period for Service Transfers.
Use it when you move a service to a new UNI-D Port. It is the number of hours after Order Completion during which the service is active on both the old and new ports. Update the End User's infrastructure in that time.
It applies to Service Transfers only.

fromPortId.description:
(Conditional) The UNI-D Port ID of the existing service. Send the new Port ID as `unidPortId`.
It applies to Service Transfers only. It is required when `overlapPeriod` is "4".

installationWorkforce.description:
(Conditional) Who installs the NTD and/or antenna device. It
applies only when `ntdId` is "NEW", as an installed NTD needs no
installation.

It defaults to "NBN Co Install".

vlanMode.description:
(Optional) The VLAN Mode decides which Product Template is used for this connection.
Send it only when you need it. If you leave it out, we use "Default-Mapped".
It is mainly for moving existing "Tagged" PPPoE services over without changing the client CPE configuration.
You cannot change it with a Modify Order. To change it, cancel the service and order it again. That can bring the service down for 24 to 48 hours.

uniVlanId.description:
(Conditional) The UNI VLAN ID # that tags the service traffic.
Send it when `vlanMode` is "Tagged".
It must be between 1 and 4094.

locId.description: The NBN Location ID for the premises the order is for.

bandwidthProductSku.description:
The product SKU of the Bandwidth Product you are ordering.
It sets which Service Layer (Layer 2 or Layer 3) the order can be provisioned with.
Use the Product Qualification > Eligible Bandwidth Products API to find the options for the Location (LOC #).

orderReference.description:

Use only letters ("a-Z"), numbers ("0-9"), underscores ("_"), hyphens ("-") and periods (".").

serviceabilityClass.description:
The servicability classes are:

0 - Planned to be serviced by Fibre in the future (boundary status isnt In Service yet)
1 - Serviceable by Fibre, no drop or NTD in place
2 - Serviceable by Fibre, drop in place, no NTD in place
3 - Serviceable by Fibre, drop and NTD in place
4 - Planned to be serviced by Wireless
5 - Serviceable by Wireless, CPE not installed
6 - Serviceable by Wireless, CPE installed
7 - Planned to be serviced by Satellite
8 - Serviceable by Satellite, Satellite - NTD not installed
9 - Serviceable by Satellite, Satellite - NTD installed
10 - Planned to be serviceable by Copper
11 - Serviceable by copper, active node present
12 - Serviceable by copper, jumpering is required
13 - Serviceable by copper, infrastructure in place
20 - Planned to be serviced by HFC, outside plant does not exist
21 - Serviceable by HFC, the location has a street TAP but requires a lead-in, PCD, internal tie cable, and wall-plate/socket
22 - Serviceable by HFC, the location has a street TAP, lead-in & PCD in place, but no internal tie-cables with wall plates/sockets
23 - Serviceable by HFC, the location has a wall-plate/socket but no HFC NTD
24 - Serviceable by HFC, Location has a wall-plate/socket & HFC NTD and is Ready to Connect
30 - Planned to be serviceable by FTTC
31 - Serviceable by FTTC, no line available (NCD required)
32 - Serviceable by FTTC, cut-in required (NCD required)
33 - Serviceable by FTTC, cut-in complete (NCD required)
34 - Serviceable by FTTC, infrastructure in place (Check NCD status)

id.description: Identifier of the entry (sequence number where the carrier assigns one).

bandwidthProfile.description: The requested Bandwidth Product SKU (service entries).

OpticommProductOrder.description: An Opticomm product order. It is the carrier's own `ProductOrder` document (npis-product-order), relayed as Opticomm produces it. It differs from the carrier's response in two ways. We remove our account and interconnect identifiers. Hyperlinks point at this API instead of the carrier. `externalId` carries your reference. We hold our own reference with the carrier, so two customers can never collide on one value.

id.description: The Opticomm Order ID (OPO #). It is the order key across this API.

href.description: Link to this order on this API.

orderType.description: The type of order: Connect a new service, Modify an existing service, or Disconnect an existing service.

state.description: The current state of the order, from the Opticomm Product Order state model, verbatim. That includes the space in `In Progress`.

subState.description: The current substate, when Opticomm has the order Held or Pending.

externalId.description: Your reference, supplied when the order was created.

reasonCode.description: The carrier's business-process event on the order, when one applies.

note.description: Notes on the order, as the carrier holds them.

appointment.description: The installation appointment attached to the order, if any.

href.description: Link to the appointment on this API.

relatedPlace.description: The property the order is for.

id.description: The Opticomm Property ID (OPC #).

href.description: Link to the property on this API.

realizedResource.description: The physical resources the order realises (NTD, NTD port).

realizedService.description: The access services the order realises.

OpticommProductOrderCreate.description: The Opticomm `ProductOrder` create body, as the carrier's own API takes it. An integration built against npis-product-order submits the same document here. We set the carrier account fields ourselves. They are `billingAccount`, `accessSeekerContact`, `productOffering`, `relatedParty`, and interconnect identifiers such as `ovcId`. A request carrying any of them is rejected with `400`. We never silently override them. `externalId` is your reference. We present our own reference to the carrier.

orderType.description: Connect a new service (including a Service Transfer), Modify an existing service's bandwidth product, or Disconnect an existing service. A Disconnect also needs the `data:delete` scope.

endUser.description: Optional, and for a Connect only. This is our end user number, not the carrier's. It is the number of the end user the order is for, as `POST /data/orders` takes it. The order and its service belong to that end user. With `orderItem.product.priorityAssist` "Yes", that end user's registration is the one that counts. An end user that is not on this account is refused with a 422 on `priorityAssist`, or on `endUser` when the flag is not set.

relatedPlace.description: The property (required for a Connect): the Opticomm Property ID.

appointment.description: A reserved appointment to attach (new installs require one).

orderItem.description: The order line item. A Connect carries the end-user facts; a Modify or Disconnect names the Product Instance (OPI #) in `product.id`.

realizedResource.description: Physical resource requests. A Connect may name the NTD port with productSpecification `OUID` and `portId`.

realizedService.description: Service requests. A Connect or Modify names the requested `bandwidthProfile`, which is the Bandwidth Product SKU, here.

OpticommChangeRequest.description: A planned outage (change work). It is the carrier's own npis-networkoutage `ChangeRequest` document, verbatim. `oacIds` names only your own affected services.

oacIds.description: Your affected services (OAC ids). Only yours are listed.

OpticommTroubleTicket.description: An unplanned outage. It is the carrier's own npis-networkoutage `TroubleTicket` document, verbatim. With `?extended=true` you get the fuller record, as upstream answers it. That adds the condition, reason, estimated restoration and comments. `oacIds` names only your own affected services. Comment authors are left out.

comments.description: As upstream sends them. They are strings on the extended record and objects (dateCreated, text) otherwise. Authors are left out either way.

oacIds.description: Your affected services (OAC ids). Only yours are listed.

OpticommOutagePosition.description: The carrier's own npis-networkoutage position answer for a service. It is upstream's `NoOutage`, `CurrentOutage` or `FutureOutage` body, verbatim. A service with no outage carries only `currentOutage: false`. The id arrays appear only when the carrier sends them.

OpticommProductRecord.description: A product record inside an Opticomm inventory document. It has the carrier's own shape, without our account and interconnect identifiers. Records nest. An NTD (OTD) record carries its ports (OUI) as `productRef` entries of its own.

id.description: The record's identifier. It is the Product Instance (OPI #), access service (OAC #), NTD (OTD #) or NTD port (OUI #).

connectedToOui.description: The NTD port (OUI #) the access service rides.

id.description: e.g. FTTP, OACD, OTD, OUID.

OpticommProduct.description: An Opticomm service. It is the carrier's own npis-product-inventory `Product` document, relayed as Opticomm produces it. It differs from the carrier's response in three ways. We remove our account and interconnect identifiers. Hyperlinks point at this API. A service we hold suspended carries `suspensionTakesEffect`. `name` carries your reference, not the name we use with the carrier.

id.description: The Product Instance (OPI #). It is the product key across this API.

href.description: Link to this product on this API.

@type.description: The product class. For an end-user service, it is the access technology.

status.description: The product lifecycle status, as the carrier holds it.

suspensionTakesEffect.description: Our own field. It is present only while we hold the service suspended, and says how soon the suspension takes effect. It is `within 1 business day` for an Opticomm L3 service, which Opticomm suspends for us. It is `within 15 minutes` for a service we cut ourselves. Absent otherwise.

name.description: Your reference for the service.

productRef.description: The realised records under this product. They are the access service (OAC), the NTD (OTD) and, nested within it, the NTD ports (OUI).

place.description: The property the service is delivered at.

id.description: The Opticomm Property ID (OPC #).

href.description: Link to the property on this API.

OpticommServiceHealthAck.description: The carrier-style acknowledgement for a requested health report. The RAG report arrives later. Read it at `/opticomm/service_health/{hrId}` or in the service's reads.

id.description: The health report reference (OHR #).

OpticommServiceHealthReport.description: The carrier's own npis-service-health report fields, from the latest callback. We leave out the key we use with the carrier. The wrapper carries your reference.

id.description: The health report reference (OHR #).

OpticommHealthCategory.description: One health category from the carrier's report, verbatim.

status.description: RAG.

OpticommServiceHealth.description: One service-health request. It wraps the carrier's own report with our tracking fields. Upstream has no way to read a report, because reports arrive only by callback. So this read is our extension. `serviceHealth` and `healthCategory` are absent until the report lands. `requestStatus` is our own request lifecycle. Upstream has no failure state, so a failed request shows here instead of looking like InProgress.

id.description: The health report reference (OHR #).

externalId.description: Your reference for the request, when supplied on create.

OpticommSiteRestriction.description: The qualification body. It holds the property's serviceability, features, charges, boundaries, NTD/port inventory and technology, exactly as the carrier answers them. We omit upstream resource links that do not resolve here. They are `supportingProduct[].href`, `supportingResource[].href` and product catalog hrefs. `siteRestriction.href` points at this API's own address resource.

href.description: The qualified property on this API.

name.description: The property's display address.

serviceabilityStatus.description: Serviceable / Rejected, as upstream enumerates it.

supportingProduct.description: Product instances already at the property. `serviceProviderId` names the RSP the end user deals with today, and we keep it. We omit the upstream `href`, which does not resolve here.

supportingProductFeatures.description: Feature availability at the property, as one object. The carrier's swagger declares an array, but the live carrier sends one object, and this API relays what the carrier sends. `productAvailability` is present only when you ask for it with `?productAvailability=true`.

productAvailability.description: The bandwidth products orderable at the property, by Opticomm's product code.

supportingRelatedLocationFeatures.description: Charges, activity flags and demand/transfer availability.

supportingResource.description: The NTD (OTD) inventory. It covers the device, bandwidth and UNI ports.

OpticommSiteQualification.description: The carrier's own npis-service-qualification `SiteQualification` document. An integration built against Opticomm reads it unchanged. We serve it from our qualification cache, which is fresh until 01:00 Sydney the next day. A request carrying `customerAuthorityDate` is always answered live. `href` points at this API's own resources.

id.description: The qualified Opticomm Property ID (OPC #).

href.description: This qualification on this API.

NumberRoutingStep.description: One route in a number's routing chain. The first step takes the call. Each step with a `failover` hands the call to the next step when it fails. A chain has at most 4 steps. A `time_of_day` step picks a destination by the time. A `geographic` step picks one by where the caller is, on 13, 1300 and 1800 numbers only. Each falls back to `fallback`. Their destinations are plain routes, not another time-of-day or geographic step. A step you read back always carries `routeType`, `routeTarget`, `disconnectResponse`, `redirectCallerId`, `label` and `failover`. A step you send needs only `routeType`. A field you leave out is read as null, and `disconnectResponse` as `hangup`.

routeType.description: Where this step sends the call. Only we set `route_to_server`. You can read a chain that has one, but you cannot send it back. `fax2email` needs the number on a fax plan.

routeTarget.description: What it holds depends on `routeType`. It is a trunk's `sipUsername` or its `id`, a phone number, a SIP URI, or an email address. You can send either the `sipUsername` or the `id` of a trunk. It reads back as the `sipUsername`, or the `id` for a trunk with none, such as an IP-authenticated trunk. A SIP URI starts `sip:` or `sips:` and is not a private or reserved address. Null for `disconnected`, `time_of_day` and `geographic`. A phone number is never 000, 112 or 106, in any form (`+61000`, `0061112`, `1831000`). That is a `422`, "Calls can’t be diverted to an emergency number (000, 112 or 106)."

disconnectResponse.description: For `disconnected`, what the caller hears. It is `hangup` when you send none. Null for every other route type.

redirectCallerId.description: For `redirect`, the caller ID the forwarded call shows. It is the original caller's (the default) or this number. Null for every other route type.

label.description: Your name for this step; null for none.

failover.description: When the call moves on to the next step. Null on the last step, and on a step that never fails over.

trigger.description: `afterSeconds`: after `seconds` of ringing unanswered. `whenUnreachable`: when the destination cannot be reached.

seconds.description: For `afterSeconds`, one of 5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120 or 180, or a value we already set on this chain. Null for `whenUnreachable`.

timezone.description: The time zone its windows are in. Required for `time_of_day`, and only there.

windows.description: Required for `time_of_day`, and only there. We check them in order, and the first match takes the call.

days.description: The days of the week, 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday).

start.description: HH:MM, 24-hour. A window may cross midnight (22:00 to 06:00).

rules.description: Required for `geographic`, and only there. We check them in order, and the first match takes the call.

mode.description: `state`: callers in `states`. `area`: callers from mobile originating location (MOLI) codes in `molis`, or fixed numbers in the standard zone units in `szus`.

fallback.description: Where the call goes when no window or rule matches. Required for `time_of_day` and `geographic`.

SmsDelivery.description:
Where a mobile number's inbound SMS are delivered. A number with no method still receives and stores its messages (`GET /sms/{number}`). We just do not forward them.

We sign every webhook request. The `X-Signature-256` header is `sha256=` followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, keyed with the number's secret. Compare it in constant time and reject a request that does not match.

method.description: How messages are forwarded. Null when they are not.

vendor.description: The payload shape of a webhook. It is `generic`, which is our own, or `3cx` or `yeastar`. Null unless `method` is `webhook`.

destination.description: The webhook URL, which is a public HTTPS address, or the email address. Null when `method` is null.

secretSet.description: Whether a signing secret is stored. We never return the secret itself on a read.

secret.description: The new signing secret. It appears only in the answer to the `PATCH` or `PUT` that generated it. Store it now. We do not return it again.

DidNumber.description: A phone number on your account.

description.description: A label or description for this number. Null when you have not set one.

routeType.description: How incoming calls to this number are routed first. It is the first step of `routing`. Null for unrouted numbers. `route_to_server` is not yet generally available.

routeTarget.description: The target for the first route. It is a trunk's `sipUsername`, a redirect number, a SIP URI or a fax email. Null for disconnected, unrouted and composite routes.

trunkType.description: On a `trunk` route, where to find `routeTarget`. `trunk` is at `GET /trunks/{username}`. `residentialLine` is at `GET /residential-lines/{username}`. Null on every other route.

routingSteps.description: How many routes the number's chain has. That counts the first route and its failovers. 0 for an unrouted number.

hasAdvancedRouting.description: True when the chain has a failover, or its first route is time of day or geographic. A `PATCH` with `routeType` on such a number answers `409` unless it sends `replaceRouting: true`.

routing.description: The whole routing chain, first route first, as the portal shows it. Send it back, changed, as `routing` on `PATCH /numbers/{number}`.

faxEnabled.description: Whether this number takes faxes. It is true while the number is on one of your fax plans (`faxPlanId`). Only such a number can be routed to `fax2email`.

faxPlanId.description: The `id` of the fax plan this number is on, from `GET /fax/plans`. Null when it is on none.

smsEnabled.description: Whether this number can send and receive SMS. That applies to a mobile number you hold.

smsDelivery.description: Where this mobile number's inbound SMS are delivered. Null for any number that is not a mobile number.

status.description: `releasing` while we carry out a release. Once it is done the number is gone.

emergencyAddressId.description: The `id` of the emergency address this number is listed at (`GET /emergency-addresses`). Null until one is linked. A change to a number in use shows here once the register has been updated, a moment after the call.

ipnd.description: The last IPND record we sent for this number and what the IPND said about it. Null when we have sent none. The IPND record is the number's address. We upload it to the national database after the fact. It never changes how a call is routed or connected, and a call to 000 goes through whatever it says. A rejected record needs the emergency address fixed, so emergency services get the right one.

status.description: `waiting` until the IPND answers. `accepted` means the IPND took the record. `rejected` means it refused the record, and `errors` has the reasons. `fileRejected` means it refused the whole upload the record was in, so the record itself is not at fault.

lastSubmittedAt.description: When we uploaded the record. Null while it waits to go.

directoryListing.description: Whether the record lists the number in the public directory, as the emergency address's list code sets it. `unlisted` means it is not listed. `serviceAddress` means it is listed at the service address. `separateAddress` means it is listed at a separate directory address. Null when the address is no longer on the account.

errors.description: Each code the IPND returned, explained. Empty when there were none.

code.description: The IPND's code, as its manager writes it.

meaning.description: What it means, in plain words.

fixInAddress.description: True when a field of the emergency address needs correcting.

portOutCode.description: A mobile number's port-out code from the carrier. Your end user gives it to their new provider to move the number away. It is an identifier, not a password. Null on a fixed number, or when the carrier has not given one.

endUser.description: The end user who holds this number, by its public number. It is the end user the number is tagged to, or else the end user of the trunk it is on. Null when the number is your own.

monthlyCost.description: Monthly recurring cost for this number as a decimal dollar amount, without GST. Null when no hosting product prices this number's category. That is not the same as free. Deprecated. Read `monthlyCostExGst`, `monthlyCostGst` and `monthlyCostIncGst` instead.

monthlyCostExGst.description: The monthly cost without GST, as a decimal dollar amount. Null, with the other two, when nothing prices this number.

monthlyCostGst.description: The GST on the monthly cost. `0.00` on a GST-free account.

createdAt.description: When the number was added to the account's stock, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the number last changed, in UTC.

NumberOrder.description: A number order. We accept an order before it is done. It starts `pending`. We allocate and route the numbers in the background, usually within a minute. The order then ends `completed` with its numbers, or `failed` with `error`. An order inside a bundle is a `draft`, holding nothing, until the bundle is released.

id.description: The order's id, for `GET /numbers/orders/{id}`.

status.description: `draft` is in a bundle, waiting for the bundle to be released. `pending` is being set up. `completed` means the numbers are yours, listed in `numbers`. `failed` means nothing was allocated, and `error` says why. `cancelled` means the order was taken out of its bundle, or the bundle was abandoned.

type.description: The number type ordered.

szu.description: The numbering area of a geographic order; null for other types.

blockSize.description: How many consecutive numbers the order is for.

spare.description: True when you ordered the numbers spare. They are on no trunk and route to Disconnected until you set their route.

trunk.description: The `sipUsername` of the trunk the numbers go on. Null for a spare order.

emergencyAddressId.description: The emergency address the numbers are listed at; null for a spare order.

routeType.description: Where the order said calls go. `trunk` rings the trunk. `redirect` forwards to `routeTarget`. `sip_address` sends to a SIP URI. A spare order is `disconnected`.

routeTarget.description: The trunk's `sipUsername`, the forward number or the SIP URI; null when spare.

bundle.description: The bundle the order is in, when it was placed in one.

error.description: Why a `failed` order failed, or why a `cancelled` one was cancelled. Null otherwise.
error.example: No complete block of 10 numbers (e.g. X0–X9) is available.

numbers.description: The numbers allocated, once `completed`, each with the route it has now. Empty until then.

routeType.description: How the number's calls are routed, as `GET /numbers/{number}` shows it.

routeTarget.description: The route's destination, as `GET /numbers/{number}` shows it.

ResLineResolution.description: What happens to a Res Line that a change would leave with no number. A request refused with `409` `res_line_needs_number` names each line in `error.resLines`. Send the request again with one of these for each line. The change and the choice are then made together.

residentialLine.description: The line's SIP username, as `/residential-lines/{username}` names it.

action.description: `allocate_number` orders a new number like the one leaving. It uses the same emergency address unless `emergencyAddressId` names another. We bill it like any number. `move_number` puts `number`, another of your active numbers, on the line and routes it there. `suspend` stops the line making and taking calls until you resume it. It keeps billing. `cancel` cancels the line for good. A line in contract has an early termination charge. You see and accept it on the line's page in the portal, so `cancel` answers `422` for that line. Choose another resolution here.

number.description: For `move_number`, the number to move to the line, E.164 digits.

emergencyAddressId.description: For `allocate_number`, the new number's emergency address. Defaults to the leaving number's.

SmsDeliveryInput.description: Where a mobile number's inbound SMS are delivered. A field you leave out keeps what is stored. `method: null` turns forwarding off. Messages are still received and stored.

method.description: How messages are forwarded. Null turns forwarding off.

vendor.description: The webhook payload shape. It is `generic` when you leave it out.

destination.description: The webhook URL, which must be a public HTTPS address, or the email address.

secret.description: The signing secret. Required for `yeastar` while none is stored. For `generic` and `3cx`, we generate one when you leave it out. A blank `secret` keeps the stored one.

EmergencyAddress.description: The address emergency services get for a number, with the customer it is listed under. In Australia this is the number's IPND (Integrated Public Number Database) listing. Every Australian number needs one linked before it can be routed. Link a number to an address with `emergencyAddressId` on `PATCH /numbers/{number}`. The fields and their lengths are the IPND's own.

id.description: The address's identifier, as `emergencyAddressId` on a number names it.

country.description: The country whose emergency register lists the address. `AU` is the only value today. You can leave it out when you create an address.

label.description: Your name for the address. Unique on your account.

listCode.description: How the listing appears in directories. `LE` is a listed entry. `UL` is unlisted. `SA` is listed with the address suppressed.

usageCode.description: Who uses the service. `R` is residential. `B` is business. `G` is government. `C` is charity. `N` is not available.

findingNameSameAsCustomer.description: Whether the directory finding name is the customer's name. When false on an `LE` or `SA` listing, `findingName1` is required.

name1.description: The customer's surname or business name.

serviceAddress.description: Where the service is used. This is the address emergency services are sent to. Give a `streetName` or a `buildingProperty`.

gnafPid.description: The G-NAF address detail PID. It is the `gnafId` of a `GET /addresses/search` result. Send it on a create or an update and it fills every other service address field from that address, in the shape the IPND record needs. That covers building, unit, level, street number and suffix, street name and type, locality, state and postcode. The portal's address search does the same. A field you send beside it wins over the filled one. An unknown PID answers `422` on this field. The answer shows the filled address.

directoryAddress.description: The address printed in directories. On an `LE` or `SA` listing that does not use the service address, `locality`, `state`, `postcode` and a `streetName` or `buildingProperty` are required.

gnafPid.description: The `gnafId` of a `GET /addresses/search` result. Send it and it fills the directory address's street number, street name and type, locality, state and postcode from that address. It also sets `sameAsService` to false. It does neither if you send those fields beside it. An unknown PID answers `422` on this field.

liveNumbers.description: How many of your numbers are listed at this address. It cannot be deleted while any are.

FaxPlan.description: A fax plan. A number sends and receives faxes only while it is on an open plan.

id.description: The plan's ID.

kind.description: `bundle` is the Fax Bundle. It has one number, with pages included in the monthly fee. `service` is the fax service. It has any number of numbers, a monthly fee for each, and a charge for each page sent.

endUser.description: The number of the end user the plan is for, or null when it is your own.

numbers.description: The numbers on the plan now, as E.164 digits.

createdAt.description: When the plan was opened, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the plan last changed, in UTC.

CallingPermission.description: A calling-permission class you can apply to a trunk. `AUEmergency` and `AUFreecall` are always enabled and cannot be removed. You opt each trunk in to the other classes, up to the ceiling the wholesaler has set.

TrunkNumberFormat.description: How an Australian number is written on calls delivered to a trunk. `national` is `0` plus the national number (`0755501234`). `international` is the international number with a plus (`+61755501234`). `internationalDigits` is the international digits only, with no plus (`61755501234`).

TrunkIpEntry.description: One entry on a trunk's IP ACL.

id.description: The entry's id, as `DELETE /trunks/{username}/ips/{ipId}` takes it.

ipAddress.description: The allowed address in CIDR form, or the host name when `type` is `host`. A single host is `/32`, or `/128` for IPv6.

type.description: `cidr` is an address or range. `host` is a host name. We resolve it on its DNS TTL and allow the addresses it resolves to.

description.description: A label for this IP entry.

createdAt.description: When the entry was added, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the entry last changed, in UTC.

id.description: The trunk's public id. Every trunk has one, including a trunk set up without a SIP credential, so every `/trunks/{username}` endpoint accepts it in place of the SIP username. Trunk events carry it as `trunkId`. The internal database id is never exposed.

name.description: A friendly name for this trunk.

description.description: An optional description for this trunk.

authMethod.description: The SIP authentication method. A trunk is always `both`. It accepts either registration with its credential or a source IP on its IP ACL. The other values remain for compatibility. We never return them for a trunk.

sipUsername.description: The trunk's platform-generated SIP digest username. Every `/trunks/{username}` endpoint accepts it, as it accepts `id`. Null on a trunk set up without a SIP credential. That trunk authenticates only by IP, so address it by its `id`.

sipDomain.description: The SIP domain for this trunk.

type.description: The trunk's plan. It decides the price. On `ultimate` each channel is a recurring billed assignment. On `payg` the channels are a ceiling and outbound calls are metered per use.

channels.description: Maximum concurrent calls allowed on this trunk. On `ultimate` this is also the number of channels billed.

maxInternational.description: Maximum concurrent international calls. **Null means no trunk-level limit.** The trunk inherits your account's cap. It is not capped at zero. Setting it to `0` is different, and blocks international calling on this trunk. A limit applies only while `International` is among `callingPermissions`. Without it this is null.

activeCalls.description: Calls up on the trunk now, as the portal's Concurrency card counts them. `GET /voice/calls/active?trunk=` lists them.

recordingEnabled.description: Whether call recording is on. When it is, every call on the trunk is recorded.

callingPermissions.description: The calling-permission classes applied to this trunk, which is its call barring. `AUEmergency` and `AUFreecall` are always listed. We never bar 000 or freecall numbers.

defaultCallerId.description: The default outbound caller ID presented for calls from this trunk.

forcePrivateCli.description: Whether all outbound calls present as Private/Anonymous regardless of the caller ID set.

forceOutboundCli.description: Whether every outbound call presents `defaultCallerId`, whatever caller ID the PBX sends.

defaultState.description: The default registration state for this trunk. Null when none is set.

status.description: A `suspended` trunk makes and receives no calls. We refuse new outbound calls. We refuse calls to its numbers before they reach your PBX. It still places 000 (and 112 and 106) calls. For an hour after one, we deliver calls to its numbers so the emergency service can call back. See `suspendedBy`.

suspendedBy.description: Who suspended the trunk, while `status` is `suspended`. `account` means you did, in the portal or with `POST /trunks/{username}/suspend`. You can resume it. `checkNetworks` means we placed a hold, for example for non-payment or fraud. Only we lift it, and `POST /trunks/{username}/resume` answers 409. Null when the trunk is not suspended.

calledNumberFormat.description: How the dialled number is written in the Request-URI and To of calls delivered to this trunk. `national` is an Australian number as `0` plus the national number (`0755501234`). A number that is not Australian is delivered as digits only.

callerNumberFormat.description: How an Australian caller's number is written in From on calls delivered to this trunk. A number's own inbound format, where set, overrides this for calls to that number. An overseas or withheld caller is delivered as received.

provisioningState.description: Whether the trunk's latest change (to the trunk, its SIP credential or its IP ACL) has reached every customer SBC. It is `pending` until the next network reload, which runs every minute. It is `active` once every SBC has the change. A new trunk reads `pending` at first. Wait for `active` before a test call.

provisionedAt.description: When the voice network was first confirmed to hold the trunk's latest change. Null while `provisioningState` is `pending`.

internationalHold.description: An international-cap hold on the trunk, or null. While it is in force we refuse the trunk's international calls. Calls within Australia, and 000, still go. Raise a support ticket to have it released.

capMinutes.description: The trunk's international minutes cap for the period.

trippedMinutes.description: The international minutes the trunk had made when the hold was placed.

pendingPlanChange.description: A plan or channel change booked for the next billing cycle, or null. A downgrade made with `PATCH /trunks/{username}` is booked this way. `DELETE /trunks/{username}/plan-change` cancels it.

direction.description: Which way the change moves the trunk from its current plan and channels.

type.description: The plan the trunk moves to.

channels.description: The channels billed after the change; 0 on `payg`.

effectiveOn.description: The date the change takes effect, the start of the next billing cycle.

connection.description: What a PBX needs to connect to the trunk, as the portal's Trunk Configuration panel shows it.

registrar.description: The host name the PBX registers to and sends calls to.

udpTcpPort.description: The SIP port for UDP and TCP.

srtpRequired.description: Whether the trunk requires SRTP. When it does, the PBX must use TLS on `tlsPort`.

codecs.description: The codecs offered, in preference order.

dtmfMode.description: How DTMF digits travel between the network and the PBX.

dtmfWarning.description: A warning when `dtmfMode` is `inband`, which loses digits on some calls. Null otherwise.

numberFormat.description: The form the called number arrives in, as `calledNumberFormat`.

allowList.description: The addresses to allow through your firewall for this trunk, read from DNS. Returned by `GET /trunks/{username}` only, not on the list. Empty when DNS could not be read.

endUser.description: The end user this trunk belongs to, by its public number. Its calls are billed to that end user. Null when the trunk is your own.

allowedCountries.description: This trunk's own list of countries it may call (ISO 3166 alpha-2), or null when it follows your account's list.

effectiveAllowedCountries.description: The countries this trunk's international calls may reach. It is the trunk's own list, else your account's. We refuse a call to any other country. Calls to Australia and New Zealand follow `callingPermissions`. New Zealand is `NZMobile` and `NZNational`, and is never in a list. High-risk destinations stay blocked whatever the list says. 000 always connects.

followsAccountList.description: True when the trunk has no list of its own and follows your account's.

dailySpendCapExGst.description: The trunk's daily spend cap, ex GST, as a dollar string. Null is no cap. We measure the cap on our rated cost to you for the trunk's outbound calls since midnight Brisbane time.

spendTodayExGst.description: The trunk's outbound calls today, ex GST, since midnight Brisbane time. A call counts when it ends, so calls still up are not in it yet.

spendCapHeld.description: True while the trunk is held for reaching its daily spend cap. We refuse its outbound calls, all but 000 and 1800. Inbound calls are not affected.

spendCapReleasesAt.description: When the hold lifts by itself, the next midnight Brisbane time. Null when the trunk is not held. Release Spend Cap Hold lifts it sooner.

ips.description: IP ACL entries for this trunk. Empty when the trunk authenticates only by registration.

createdAt.description: When the trunk was created, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the trunk last changed, in UTC.

TransitBlackhole.description: A blackhole on one address of an IP transit service. All traffic to the address is dropped at our border until the blackhole expires or is released.

id.description: The blackhole's ID. Use it to release the blackhole.

serviceNumber.description: The IP transit service the address belongs to.

address.description: The blackholed address, IPv4 or IPv6.

route.description: The address as the host route that is dropped, a `/32` or a `/128`.

reason.description: The reason you gave when you placed it. Always `null` on one we placed.

placedBy.description: `customer` means your portal user or API key placed it. `staff` means we did.

expiresAt.description: When the blackhole lifts by itself. One you place always has an expiry. One we place may have none.

releasedAt.description: When it was released or expired. `null` while it is in force.

Cdr.description: One call detail record, as `GET /voice/cdrs` lists it and `GET /voice/cdrs/{cgrid}` reads it.

cgrid.description: A unique id for this call. Use it to de-duplicate, and to read one call with `GET /voice/cdrs/{cgrid}`. A re-rated call keeps its id.

source.description: The originating number or SIP URI.

callerId.description: The caller ID that was presented, digits only, as the portal shows it. Null when the caller withheld it or none was presented.

cost.description: Call cost as a decimal dollar amount, without GST. Deprecated. Read `costExGst`, `costGst` and `costIncGst` instead.

costExGst.description: The call's cost without GST, as rated.

costGst.description: The GST on the call. `0.00` on a GST-free account.

rerated.description: Whether the call was re-rated after it was first priced. A re-rated call is listed once, at its new price in `costExGst`, `costGst` and `costIncGst`, and counted once in the summary.

previousCostExGst.description: The price before the most recent re-rate, without GST. That is the price the call had just before its current one. A call re-rated more than once shows only that one here. Null when it was not re-rated.

previousCostGst.description: The GST on `previousCostExGst`. Null when the call was not re-rated.

previousCostIncGst.description: The price before the most recent re-rate, with GST. Null when the call was not re-rated.

answerTime.description: When the call was answered. Null if unanswered.

disposition.description: The call's final state. `blocked` means the call never reached a carrier. A barred call class, a high-risk prefix, an account hold or insufficient credit blocks a call. It is not the same as `failed`.

sipCauseCode.description: The SIP response code that ended the call, when the call reached SIP signalling.

callClass.description: The permission class the dialled destination fell into, such as `AUMobile` or `International`.

trunk.description: The `sipUsername` of the trunk this call belongs to, as `GET /trunks` returns it. Null for a call with no trunk.

trunkType.description: Where to find `trunk`. `trunk` is at `GET /trunks/{username}`. `residentialLine` is at `GET /residential-lines/{username}`. Null with no trunk.

endUser.description: The end user of the call's trunk, by its public number. We bill the call to that end user. Null for your own trunk or a call with no trunk.

createdAt.description: When the call record was written, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the call record last changed, such as by a re-rate, in UTC.

NetworkOutages.description: Check Networks outages affecting your account's services, in the list envelope every list uses.

queryDateTime.description: When this query was received, in UTC

total.description: Number of outages matching the query

perPage.description: The number of outages per page

TicketCategory.description:
The ticket's category. It says what kind of work the ticket is. We use it
for routing, and you can filter the list by it.

The same values apply everywhere a category appears, which is the filter,
create and the ticket body. The values you may send are exactly the values
you can be returned.

`security_incident` is its own category. It is not a technical ticket with a
note.

`remote_hands` is on-site hands-and-eyes work at a facility.
`scam_traceback` is a scam-call traceback handed to a wholesale client to
continue tracing their own end customer. We raise both of these, and they
appear on your tickets. An integration that filters the list must expect
them. `scam_report` is yours to raise. Use it for a scam call or SMS, or a
spoofed number, reported by you or your customer.

TicketComplaint.description: The complaint and its clocks. Null when the ticket is not a complaint. A complaint about one of your end users is yours to handle under the Telecommunications Consumer Complaints Handling Standard. Acknowledge it by `acknowledgeDueAt`. Answer an urgent one by `urgentResponseDueAt`. Resolve it by `resolutionDueAt`. Answer a TIO case by `tioDueAt`. The due times count in working days from when the complaint was received.

urgent.description: An urgent complaint has a shorter resolution deadline.

receivedAt.description: When the complaint arrived, which the deadlines count from.

acknowledgedAt.description: When the complaint was acknowledged to the consumer. Null while it has not been.

urgentResponseDueAt.description: Set when the consumer asked for urgent handling. Null otherwise.

resolutionDueAt.description: When the complaint must be resolved. Not the support target of the same name on the ticket.

outcome.description: How the complaint ended, once recorded. Record it with the resolve on `PATCH /tickets/{ticketRef}`.

tioReference.description: The TIO's case reference, once a TIO case is logged.

tioDueAt.description: When the response to the TIO is due, once a TIO case is logged.

reference.description: The public ticket reference, e.g. `INC-7K3F9Q`. Use this to address the ticket in all other endpoints.

status.description: `open` and `pending` are active states. `resolved` and `closed` are closed out. `pending` means we are waiting for your reply, and the response time clock is stopped until you reply. Replying to a resolved or closed ticket re-opens it.

endUser.description: The end user the ticket is about, by its public number. Null when the ticket is your own.

relatedService.description: What the ticket is linked to, by the same public reference `POST /tickets` takes. That is a data service's PRI (its AVC when it has none), a trunk's SIP username (its id when it has none), a number in E.164 without the `+`, or an invoice number. Null when the ticket is linked to none of these.

isComplaint.description: Whether the ticket is a complaint. `complaint` carries its deadlines.

updatedAt.description: When the ticket last changed, in UTC.

lastActivityAt.description: Updated on every message and state change. The list sorts by this, newest first.

awaitingCustomerReply.description: True while the ticket is `pending`, waiting on your reply.

resolveBlockedReason.description: Why the ticket cannot be resolved now. Null when it can. A refused resolve answers 422 with the same `code`.

canReopen.description: Whether `PATCH` with `status=open` would re-open the ticket. It can only when the ticket is resolved or closed.

TicketFaultChecklist.description: The checklist answers given. A question left unanswered is absent.

newService.description: The service was connected recently and has never worked.

devicesPowered.description: The end user's devices are powered on, and have been restarted.

cabledDirectly.description: The router (or phone) is cabled straight to our equipment, with nothing between.

siteAvailability.description: When someone is at the site to let a technician in.

inductionNeeded.description: A technician needs a site induction before they can enter.

endUser.description: The end user the ticket is about, by its public number. It must be one of your end users that is not archived. Any other number is a 422. Omitted or null raises the ticket as your own.

relatedService.description: Optionally link the ticket to one of your services, or to one of your invoices for a billing question. We check the reference against your account.

ref.description: The record's public identifier. For `data` it is an NBN service reference (AVC/PRI). For `trunk` it is the trunk digest username. For `number` it is the phone number. For `invoice` it is the invoice number. An invoice must be one of yours that has been issued, which means issued, paid or void. A draft is a 422.

isComplaint.description: Raise the ticket as a complaint. Its deadlines start from now, as `POST /tickets/{ticketRef}/complaint` would start them.

complaintUrgent.description: With `isComplaint`, raise it as an urgent complaint. Ignored without it.

fault.description: The fault, on a `technical` ticket about a data service, trunk or number. It is required there, and refused on any other ticket. There is no limit on open fault tickets for one service unless we set one. A service at the limit is refused with `fault_ticket_limit`. Add to the open ticket instead.

type.description: For a data service, one of `speed`, `dropouts`, `noConnection`, `noService` or `other`. For a trunk or a number, one of `noDialTone`, `noCalls`, `callQuality`, `noInternational`, `nuisanceCalls`, `hardware` or `other`. Any other value is a 422 on `fault.type`.

testRefs.description: Tests and health checks you have run on this data service. Send a test's `id` from `POST /nbn/diagnostics`, or a health check's `hrId`. One that belongs to another service, or is unknown, is a 422 on `fault.testRefs.{n}`. A trunk or a number has none to link.

siteContact.description: Who our technician calls about access to the site.

preferredAppointment.description: When suits the site for a technician, in your words.

additionalContacts.description: Email addresses to copy on our emails about the ticket.

TicketFaultTestRef.description: A test or health check linked to a fault ticket.

ref.description: The test's id (`GET /nbn/diagnostics/{id}`) or the health check's `hrId`.

TicketFaultSiteContact.description: Who to contact at the site, when one was given.

TicketFault.description: A fault ticket's fields, as raised with `POST /tickets`. Null on a ticket that is not a fault ticket.

serviceKind.description: `data` for a data service, `voice` for a trunk or a number. It says which list `type` comes from.

testRefs.description: The tests and health checks of the service you linked.

additionalContacts.description: Email addresses copied on our emails about the ticket.

TicketMessage.description: One public entry in a ticket's conversation thread.

id.description: The message's id, as the `ticket.replied` webhook names it in `messageId`. Opaque.

kind.description: `reply` is a human message. `event` is a system timeline entry, such as a status change.

author.description: The label shown for the author. It is `Support` for our staff, the user's name for portal users, `API` for messages posted through this API, and `System` for event entries.

updatedAt.description: The same as `createdAt`. A message is never edited.

attachments.description: Attachment metadata. Download the content from `GET /tickets/{ticketRef}/attachments/{attachmentId}`.

isInline.description: True when the file is embedded in the message body, referenced as `cid:<id>`. False when it is listed alongside the message.

Ticket.description: A support ticket with its public conversation thread.

escalation.description: Your latest escalation with `POST /tickets/{ticketRef}/escalate`; null until you escalate. Each one is also on the thread.

firstResponseDueAt.description: When our first response is due, under your support targets. The clock counts business hours (around the clock for an `urgent` ticket) and stops while the ticket is `pending`.

resolutionDueAt.description: When we aim to resolve the ticket, on the same clock. A complaint's own resolution deadline is `complaint.resolutionDueAt`.

messages.description: The public conversation thread, oldest first. Internal Check Networks notes are never included.

TicketsSummary.description: The ticket report's figures over a range, as the portal's Support Reports page shows them.

total.description: Tickets raised in the range.

open.description: Of those, the ones still `open` or `pending`.

byStatus.description: Tickets by status, every status listed, zeros included.

byPriority.description: Tickets by priority, every priority listed, zeros included.

byCategory.description: Tickets by category, every category listed, zeros included.

volumeByMonth.description: Tickets raised each month of the range, oldest first, months with none included.

firstResponseMetPercent.description: The percentage of tickets with a first response that had it by the target. Null when none in range had both.

resolutionMetPercent.description: The percentage of resolved tickets resolved by the target. Null when none in range had both.

averageFirstResponseMinutes.description: The average minutes from raising a ticket to our first response, over the tickets that had one.

averageResolutionMinutes.description: The average minutes from raising a ticket to its resolution, over the resolved ones.

count.description: Tickets in range with a satisfaction rating.

average.description: Their average rating, 1 to 5, to two decimal places. Null when none were rated.

OutageSubscription.description: An email address or Australian mobile subscribed to our outage notices for your account. It is `pending` until the person follows the link they are sent, and only then are notices sent to it.

id.description: The subscription's id, for `DELETE /outages/subscriptions/{id}`.

address.description: The email address in lower case, or the mobile in E.164.

scope.description: Which outages it is told of.

status.description: `pending` until the person confirms by the link; `active` after.

Watch.description: A subscription that emails one or more people when something we track changes. The human-facing counterpart to a webhook.

id.description: The watch's identifier. Use it to fetch or remove the watch.

reference.description: What is being watched. It is an order reference, a technician appointment reference, a service identifier or an outage reference. An order reference is either the carrier's, such as `OPO000000230683`, or ours, `PND…`. Both address the same order. A service identifier is a carrier service id or a trunk's SIP username.

referenceType.description: The kind of thing `reference` names. We work it out from the reference, so you never send it. It tells you which group in `GET /watch/event-types` applies to this watch. Treat it as an open set. Do not switch on it exhaustively, because we add more kinds over time.

supplier.description: The carrier the watched reference belongs to, filled in from the order. Null on a watch that is not carrier-specific.

eventTypes.description: Which events this watch notifies on. Null means every event. Null is the default.

emails.description: Where we send notifications. We lowercase and de-duplicate them on save.

status.description: Removing a watch sets it to `disabled`. We keep the record, and watching the same reference again re-enables it.

lastNotifiedAt.description: When this watch last caused an email to be sent.

updatedAt.description: When the watch last changed, in UTC.

EventTypeItem.description: One event you can subscribe to. `GET /webhooks/event-types` and `GET /watch/event-types` both list items of this shape.

value.description: The value to send in a webhook's `events` or a watch's `eventTypes`.

label.description: How this event is described to a reader, as the notification emails name it.

referenceType.description: The kind of watched thing this event applies to. It matches a watch's own `referenceType`. Null on the webhook list, because a webhook is not about one kind of reference.

WebhookEventType.description:
A subscribable webhook event type, or `*` for every event.

The subscription request and the subscription you get back share this
list. Anything you can be told about is something you can subscribe to.

The three `transit.blackhole.*` types are not available yet. IP transit is
not offered by API yet, so subscribing to one answers `422` and we send
none until it is. They are listed so a client built now knows them.

`ping` is not in the list. Only `POST /webhooks/{webhookId}/test` sends
it, whatever the subscription covers. It is not something to subscribe
to.

WebhookFilters.description: Limits an endpoint to some services or end users. We send an event about a service when its service is in `serviceIds` or its end user is in `endUserIds`. We send an event about no service or end user, such as an invoice or a ticket, only when the endpoint names its type in `events`. `*` does not cover it. Empty lists, or no filters, mean every event the endpoint takes.

serviceIds.description: Services by the id their events carry in `data.serviceId`. That is a data service's id, a trunk's `sipUsername`, or a transit or colocation uuid.

WebhookSubscription.description: A registered webhook endpoint. We return the signing secret once, at registration or rotation. You cannot read it afterwards. An endpoint a key limited to one end user registers belongs to that end user. It gets only that end user's SMS and fax events. Under `/webhooks` only keys for that end user see it. You can list and remove it with `/end-users/{endUser}/webhooks`.

id.description: The endpoint's id, as `/webhooks/{webhookId}` takes it. Opaque.

url.description: Your HTTPS endpoint. It must resolve to a public address, on port 443 or 8443.

events.description: Subscribed event types, or `["*"]` for all events.

isActive.description: We disable an endpoint automatically after 20 consecutive dead deliveries. Each delivery is 6 attempts over about 8.6 hours. While the endpoint is disabled, we still record events as `dead` deliveries with zero attempts. We do not drop them. Re-enable with a PATCH once your endpoint is healthy, then replay dead deliveries to catch up.

consecutiveFailures.description: Dead deliveries in a row. We disable the endpoint automatically at 20. The count resets to zero on a successful delivery or a re-enable. The dead deliveries themselves stay in the delivery history.

disabledReason.description: Why the endpoint is off. `auto` means 20 dead deliveries in a row. `manual` means you turned it off. Null while it is on.

lastDeliveredAt.description: When a delivery last succeeded, or null if none has.

lastError.description: Why the latest dead delivery failed. Cleared by the next successful delivery.

previousSecretExpiresAt.description: After a secret rotation, when the previous secret stops signing deliveries. Null when no rotation window is open.

updatedAt.description: When the endpoint last changed, in UTC.

sequence.description: A counter for the deliveries to this endpoint. Each delivery queued for it takes the next number. A redelivery or a replay is a new delivery, so it takes a new, higher number, and an old event sent again sorts after newer ones. Do not order events by it. Order them by `occurredAt`, which a redelivery keeps, and use `eventId` to drop repeats.

WebhookDelivery.description:
One attempted delivery of one event to one endpoint. We record each delivery
before we attempt it, and we never remove it. The history survives a failed
endpoint, and it survives the endpoint being deleted.

id.description: The delivery id. Use it to redeliver. Opaque.

webhookId.description: The endpoint it went to, as `GET /webhooks` names it.

eventId.description:
The event's id, as sent in the `eventId` field of the delivered payload.
A redelivery carries the SAME `eventId` as the attempt it replays, so
handlers that de-duplicate on it treat the replay as the same event.

status.description:
`queued` is in flight, `delivered` was acknowledged with a 2xx, and
`dead` exhausted its retries.

attempts.description: Delivery attempts made so far for this record.

responseCode.description: HTTP status your endpoint returned on the last attempt, if it answered.

lastError.description: Why the last attempt failed. It is the transport or HTTP error we saw.

payload.description: The event body that was POSTed to your endpoint.

updatedAt.description: When the delivery record last changed, which is an attempt, in UTC.

EndUserAddress.description: An Australian street address, as the End User form in the portal takes it.

EndUser.description:
One of your end users. This is a customer of yours who uses your services.
Its number (`endUser`) names it, and every other end-user call takes that
number.

**Family violence safety.** While an active safety record suppresses the
end user's contact details, `contactsMasked` is true and the contacts and
both addresses are null, exactly as the portal masks them. Only
`POST /end-users/{endUser}/contacts/reveal` returns them. It needs the
`safety:read` scope, and we audit every reveal.

endUser.description: The end user's number. Every end-user call names the end user by it.

name.description: The person's name, or the contact name for a business.

businessName.description: The legal business name. Set for a business end user only.

externalRef.description: Your own reference for the end user, such as its id in your CRM. Find an end user by it with `GET /end-users?externalRef=`.

status.description:
`suspended` means its voice services are cut off. A 000 call still goes
through. `archived` means a former end user, put away. You can restore
it.

suspendReason.description: The reason given when it was suspended. Null unless `status` is `suspended`.

lastVerifiedAt.description: When a one-time code we sent to the end user last proved who was on the call. You send the code with `POST /end-users/{endUser}/verification-codes`. Nothing requires it.

contactsMasked.description: True while a family violence safety record withholds the contacts and addresses below.

billingEmail.description: Where bills go, when not to `email`.

billingSameAsService.description: True when bills go to the service address. Null while the contacts are masked.

billingAddress.description: The billing address. Null when it is the service address.

usageNotificationMethod.description: How the end user is told about their data usage.

paymentTermsDays.description: Days to pay their bills. Null uses your default.

invoiceFormat.description: Summary or detailed bills. Null uses your default.

timezone.description:
The end user's own time zone. Their bills are cut on it, and their
portal shows times in it. Null is your zone. Change it with
`PATCH /end-users/{endUser}`. A change applies from their next billing
period.

creditLimit.description:
A credit limit for your own records, in dollars including GST. Nothing
reads it. It stops no call and no service. Null is none.

spendLimit.description:
A monthly spend limit, in dollars including GST. The end user is
emailed when the month's bill reaches 50, 85 and 100 per cent of it.
Nothing is stopped. Null is none.

notes.description: The free-text notes on the end user's details. Your notes history is `/end-users/{endUser}/notes`.

EndUserDetails.description:
The details of an end user that create and update share, as the End User
form in the portal takes them. Send `null` to clear a field.

businessName.description: The legal business name. Required for a business end user. Ignored for a residential one.

tradingName.description: Kept for a business end user only.

abn.description: An ABN, checked with the ATO check digit. Spaces are allowed. Kept for a business end user only.

acn.description: Kept for a business end user only.

externalRef.description: Your own reference for the end user, such as its id in your CRM.

invoiceDelivery.description: How their bills are sent. On a create, left out or null takes your default.

usageNotificationMethod.description: How they are told about their data usage. On a create, left out or null is email.

paymentTermsDays.description: Days to pay their bills. Null uses your default.

creditLimit.description: Dollars including GST, for your own records. Nothing reads it. Null is none.

spendLimit.description:
A monthly spend limit, in dollars including GST. The end user is
emailed at 50, 85 and 100 per cent of it. Nothing is stopped. Null is
none.

EndUserSettings.description: An end user's own defaults for the calls to their lines, whether they get billing texts, and whether you bill them through the platform.

blockInternationalInbound.description: Block calls from overseas numbers to their lines, by default.

allowNzInbound.description: While international calls are blocked, still let New Zealand (+64) callers through.

billingSms.description:
Whether they get the billing texts you have switched on. These are
payment reminders, final notices, receipts and failed automatic
payments. False when they asked you to stop them. Their billing emails
still go.

isBilled.description:
Whether you bill them through the platform. False for an end user you
bill some other way. They get no bill from it, and their services need
no retail price. What we bill you does not change. Every end user
starts billed.

allowApiKeys.description:
Whether API keys limited to this end user work. You make those keys
under API Keys in the portal. False refuses every call they make. Every
end user starts with it off.

EndUserNote.description: One of your own notes on an end user. The end user never sees it.

id.description: The note's public id.

author.description: Who wrote it. A note added through the API names the key, as `<key name> (API key)`.

EndUserSafetyRecord.description:
A family violence safety record on an end user (F2025L00664). Legal
obligations attach to this data. See the End users safety help page. While
a record is active with `suppressContactDisclosure`, the end user's
contacts are masked on every other read. The record's own safe contacts
are the safe number, email and postal address. They are masked on every
read of the record, this one included. `safeContactNumber`,
`safeContactEmail` and `safePostalAddress` are always null here.
`safeContactsMasked` says whether any is recorded. Only
`POST /end-users/{endUser}/safety-records/{recordId}/safe-contacts/reveal`
returns them.

id.description: The record's public id.

safeContactsMasked.description: Whether the record holds a safe number, safe email or safe postal address. They are masked on this read. The safe-contacts reveal returns them, and we audit it.

safeContactNumber.description: Always null here, because it is masked. Read it with the safe-contacts reveal. Write it on the record's create or update. Left out of an update, it is kept.

safeContactEmail.description: Always null here, because it is masked. Read it with the safe-contacts reveal. Write it on the record's create or update. Left out of an update, it is kept.

safePostalAddress.description: Where their bills are posted under `safe_post`, never the end user's own address. Always null here, because it is masked, as the safe number and email are. Read it with the safe-contacts reveal.

billDelivery.description: How the end user wants their bills while the record is active. `safe_email` emails bills and billing notices to `safeContactEmail` only. `safe_post` sends none and alerts you to post them to `safePostalAddress`. `portal_only` sends none, and they read their bills in the portal. `none` sends no bills or billing notices. When it is null, bills follow `agreedCommunicationMethod`.

billDeliveryNote.description: Anything more about how they want their bills.

billDeliveryRequest.description: The same as `billDeliveryNote`. Deprecated. Read `billDelivery` and `billDeliveryNote`.

identifiedBy.description: The portal user who raised it. Null when raised by API. The audit log names the key.

retentionExpiresAt.description: Set when the record closes. It is the earliest the record may be disposed of.

EndUserSafetyRecordInput.description: A safety record's own fields, with the portal's rules. On a change, a field you leave out stays as it is.

safeContactNumber.description: We store it encrypted and mask it on every read. On a change, leaving it out keeps it and null clears it.

safeContactEmail.description: We store it encrypted and mask it on every read. On a change, leaving it out keeps it and null clears it.

safePostalAddress.description: Where their bills are posted under `safe_post`. A PO Box is fine. Null clears it. We refuse `safe_post` with no safe postal address on the record. That is a 422 on `safePostalAddress`.

billDelivery.description: How the end user wants their bills. See the record's `billDelivery`. `safe_post` needs a `safePostalAddress`.

billDeliveryRequest.description: Sets `billDeliveryNote`. Deprecated. Send `billDelivery` and `billDeliveryNote`. We ignore this field when you send `billDeliveryNote`.

EndUserLogin.description: A login to the end user's own portal.

id.description: The login's public id.

EndUserLoginInvite.description: An invite to the end user's portal that has not been accepted or revoked. An invite that ran out is listed with `expired` true. You can resend it.

id.description: The invite's public id.

EndUserRepresentative.description: Someone the end user has authorised to act for them (IGN017). Only an active one confers authority.

id.description: The representative's public id.

authorities.description: The areas they may act on. `full` covers every area. When it is present, it is the only one listed.

EndUserService.description: A service an end user owns, or a number they hold.

reference.description:
The reference the service's own calls take. For a data service it is
the service reference. For a trunk it is the SIP username. For a number
it is the number. For an IP transit service it is the service number.
For a fax plan or a hosted PBX it is the id. A closed hosted PBX is not
listed.

label.description: A name that helps tell it apart, such as a data service's username or a number's label.

status.description: The service's own status, as its own calls show it.

suspensionTakesEffect.description: For a suspended data service, how soon the suspension takes effect, as on `GET /data/services/{ref}`. Null for any other service.

assignmentId.description:
The billed assignment the service carries, when it has one. End it with
`DELETE /end-users/{endUser}/services/{assignmentId}`. Always null for a
number.

endsOn.description: The last day the assignment is billed, once it has been ended.

EndUserImport.description:
One end-user import, as the portal's Import page lists it. The counts are
null while it is `processing`. A `failed` import stopped part-way. Its
counts are of the rows it wrote, and the rest of the `total` were not run.

id.description: The import's id.

status.description:
`processing` while it is on the queue, then `finished`. It is `failed`
when its run stopped part-way, or had not started an hour after we
queued it, in which case we wrote nothing. Import the rows not run
again. We skip those already made as duplicates.

source.description: Where it was sent from. It is `api`, or `wholesale` for the portal.

filename.description: The file's name, or null for rows sent as JSON.

total.description: The rows read from the file.

skipped.description: Rows passed over as duplicates of an end user already there, or of a row earlier in the file.

failed.description: Rows we did not make because a check failed or an unexpected error occurred. A check fails for a missing name, a business with no business name, a bad email, or an invite with no email.

EndUserImportDetail.description: One end-user import with each row's outcome, as the portal's import page shows it.

rows.description: Each row read, in file order. Empty while the import is `processing`.

rowNumber.description: The line in the file, or the row's place in `rows` counting from 1.

endUser.description: The end user made from this row, by number.

email.description: The row's email. Null while a family violence safety record withholds the contacts of the end user made from it.

reason.description: Why it was skipped or failed, or what went wrong after we made it, such as an invite we could not send.

NotificationSettings.description: Where automated mail goes, and the usage notices sent to your residential end users.

notificationEmail.description: The address automated mail goes to, such as a NOC alias. Null sends it to your primary or billing contact (`fallbackEmail`).

fallbackEmail.description: Where mail goes while `notificationEmail` is null.

enabled.description: Whether your residential end users are told at 50%, 85% and 100% of their data allowance. It is off by default. The notices go out under your name, and we bill the SMS to you.

smsSender.description: The approved sender the SMS go from. Null sends email only.

availableSenders.description: The approved senders you may send as.

PortalBranding.description:
The end-user portal's branding, as Portal Branding shows it in the
portal. The same values theme the end-user portal and the emails your end
users are sent.

displayName.description: The brand name end users see. Empty until first set.

brandColor.description:
Filled under white text, so it must reach 4.5:1 contrast against
white. Null uses the platform's colour.

supportHours.description: Free text, such as "Mon to Fri, 8am to 6pm", in the portal footer.

afterHoursPhone.description: A fault number for outside those hours, in the portal footer.

ticketsEnabled.description: Whether end users may raise tickets in the end-user portal.

emailLogoPosition.description: Where the logo sits in emails to end users.

logos.description:
Where to download each logo (with your token), or null when none is
set.

light.description: The main logo, also the logo on your end users' invoices.

dark.description: The logo shown in dark mode.
