PortalDomain.description:
The end-user portal's custom domain: the hostname claimed, the DNS records
to publish for it, and where its verification stands.

status.description:
`pending` until both records check out. `verified` once they have and
the portal answers on the domain. `failed` when the claim expired
unverified. Claim the domain again for a new TXT record.

live.description: Whether the end-user portal is served on this domain now.

records.description: The records to publish at your DNS host.

lastCheck.description: The record's result at the last verify.

checkedAt.description: When the records were last checked.

checkError.description: What the last check found missing.

expiresAt.description:
When an unverified claim stops holding the domain (seven days after
it was made). Null once verified.

DfvSupportChannel.description:
A way for an affected person to reach you (s18). The statement needs at
least two different types. At least one must reach a person.

id.description: The channel's public id.

connectsToIndividual.description: Reaches a person. Always false for a web form.

DfvStatement.description:
Your own domestic and family violence statement, under F2025L00664
(ss16-18). Your end-user portal shows yours once it is published, and ours
until then. Approval by your most senior executive and publishing both
happen in the portal, at `portalUrl`.

safetyCommitment.description: s17(2)(a), your safety policies and procedures.

continuityCommitment.description: s17(2)(b), staying connected and reversing restrictions.

nonPaymentCommitment.description: s17(2)(c), non-payment and financial hardship assistance.

contactInstructions.description: s17(2)(d), how to contact you for assistance.

supportOrganisations.description: Your own wording, shown beside the six statutory support services.

interimNotice.description: Shown until `supportAvailableFrom`. Changing it keeps approval.

approval.description: Null until approved, and again after a wording change.

outstanding.description: What stands between the statement and publishing.

portalUrl.description: The portal page where the statement is approved and published.

ComplaintsProcess.description:
Your own complaints-handling process and network outage
complaints-handling process, under the Consumer Complaints Handling
Industry Standard 2018 (s8(1)(f), s10A, s10B). Your end-user portal shows
yours once it is published, and ours until then. Approval by a named person
and publishing both happen in the portal, at `portalUrl`.

outageProcessSummary.description: s10B, how you handle complaints about a network outage.

approval.description: Null until approved, and again after a summary change.

outstanding.description: What stands between the process and publishing.

portalUrl.description: The portal page where the process is approved and published.

CreditAlertRecipient.description: One person who receives credit warnings, by email or by SMS.

id.description: The recipient's public id, for `DELETE /account/credit-alerts/recipients/{recipientId}`.

CreditAlertSettings.description: Your credit warning settings, as the portal's Credit Alerts page holds them.

thresholds.description: The percentages of your credit limit a warning is sent at.

fallbackEmail.description: Where warnings go while there are no recipients, your billing contact.

InvoiceDispute.description: A dispute you raised on one of our invoices, and where it is up to.

id.description: The dispute's public id.

invoiceId.description: The invoice's `id`, which is a ULID, as `GET /account/invoices` gives it.

lineId.description: The line disputed, by its public id, which is the invoice's `lineItems[].id`. Null for the invoice as a whole.

status.description: Where the dispute is up to, as the portal shows it.

ticketRef.description: The support ticket the dispute opened.

creditNoteId.description: The credit note it was resolved with, if any.

InvoiceGroup.description: A named section of an invoice, such as a site, a department or a cost centre. The account's own groups section our invoice to you. An end user's groups section the invoices you send that end user. Changes apply from the next invoice. An issued invoice keeps the groups as they were.

id.description: The group's public id.

name.description: The group's name. It is unique among the owner's groups, ignoring case. It can be at most 100 characters.

description.description: The billing description printed under the group's heading.

poNumber.description: The purchase order number printed with the group, unless a service sets its own.

costCentre.description: The cost centre printed with the group, unless a service sets its own.

serviceCount.description: How many services are in the group.

InvoiceGroupInput.description: A group's fields. On create, `name` is required. On update, only the fields you send change. A blank or null description, PO or cost centre clears it.

InvoiceService.description: A service's place on one owner's invoice. It has an invoice group, at most one, and its own billing label, PO number and cost centre. These override the group's. The service is named as invoice lines name it.

endUser.description: The number of the end user the service is set on, if any.

invoiceGroupId.description: The group the service is in, by its public id. Null for none. That service prints under Other.

invoiceLabel.description: The service's own billing label, printed with its lines.

poNumber.description: The service's own PO number. Null uses its group's.

costCentre.description: The service's own cost centre. Null uses its group's.

PartnerCommissionRun.description: One month's commission for one of your partners. We store figures without GST. Each one comes with its GST and the figure with GST. `gstShown`, beside the results, says which the portal shows.

id.description: The run's public id, for `GET /partners/commission-runs/{runId}`.

partnerId.description: The partner's user id, as on GET /account/users.

basis.description: What the rate was applied to.

payableExGst.description: Commission less clawbacks, what the partner is paid.

PartnerCommissionClawback.description: Commission taken back because revenue it was paid on was reversed. That is a credit note, a write-off or a dishonoured payment. It comes off the partner's next runs until `remaining` is zero.

id.description: The clawback's public id.

sourceRunId.description: The run that paid the commission now taken back, by its public id.

remainingExGst.description: What is still to come off.

RetailInvoice.description: An invoice you issued to one of your end users. It is never one of the invoices we issue to you. Those are on `/account/invoices`. Money is a decimal dollar string, each amount as ex-GST, GST and inc-GST.

endUser.description: The end user's number.

status.description: `held` only on a final invoice that answered held for approval. The lists never carry a held invoice. See `/end-users/invoice-approvals`.

final.description: True on an end user's final invoice.

amountPaid.description: What has been paid against this invoice, inc. GST.

amountDue.description: What is still owed on it, inc. GST.

remindersPausedUntil.description: While payment reminders on this invoice are paused, the day they start again.

remindersPauseReason.description: The reason given for the pause. On the single invoice only.

RetailPayment.description: A payment applied to an end-user invoice. Money is a decimal dollar string.

method.description: `recorded` for one you recorded; otherwise the gateway that took it.

appliedToInvoice.description: The part of it applied to this invoice. A payment can cover several invoices, oldest first.

paidOn.description: The day it was paid, on your account's time zone.

RetailCreditNote.description: A credit note you issued to one of your end users, the only correction to one of their invoices. Money is a decimal dollar string.

lines.description: On the single credit note only.

EndUserLedgerEntry.description: One transaction on an end user's account. Money is a decimal dollar string, including GST unless the field name says otherwise.

id.description: The entry's public id.

reference.description: The document number, where there is one.

direction.description: `debit` adds to what they owe. `credit` takes off it.

balance.description: The running balance after this transaction.

paidOn.description: For an invoice, the day it was paid in full.

HardshipCase.description: An end user's financial hardship case. It is an arrangement in force, or an application under assessment. Money is a decimal dollar string.

id.description: The case's public id, as `/end-users/{endUser}/hardship/{caseId}` takes it.

status.description: `proposed` is an application under assessment. `active` is an arrangement in force.

options.description: The assistance agreed, from the options you offer at `/retail/hardship-options`.

pauseAutopay.description: Whether automatic payments are paused while the case is open.

assessmentDueAt.description: The deadline to assess an application. It counts business days on your calendar.

instalmentAmount.description: On a payment plan, each instalment.

EndUserDispute.description: An end user's dispute of a charge on an invoice you issued them. While it is open the disputed amount is not collected.

id.description: The dispute's public id, as `/end-users/disputes/{id}` takes it.

invoiceLineId.description: The line disputed, by its public id, or null for the bill as a whole.

raisedBy.description: Who raised it, by kind. An example is the end user's own portal login.

inProgress.description: True when a decision is queued and has neither landed nor failed.

error.description: Why the last decision could not be completed. Retry sends it again.

creditNoteId.description: On a credited dispute, the credit note, at `/end-users/credit-notes/{id}`.

RetailPriceBookItem.description:
One product in your retail price book: what your end users are charged for
it. We hold prices ex-GST. We work out the GST and the price with GST
from your own tax settings and the product's GST treatment.

id.description: The price's public id, used to change or remove it.

priceExGst.description: The price each period (a month, or a year for an annual product), ex-GST.

setupFeeExGst.description:
The setup fee, ex-GST. Null when none is set. The setup fee then falls
back to your default markup on ours. "0.00" is a free connection.

effectiveFrom.description: The day the price applies from. Every end user on the product moves to it then.

planId.description:
The product's default call plan, one of your own published plans. It
prices calls for end users whose service has no plan of its own. Null
for none.

RetailPlan.description: One of your own call plans for your end users. A plan is versioned. Published versions never change. Every edit goes to the plan's one draft, which opens from the latest version on the first edit. A published version prices calls from its `effectiveFrom` date.

id.description: The plan's public ID.

code.description: The plan's code, unique across all plans.

archived.description: You cannot give an archived plan to another service. Services already on it keep being rated by it.

workingVersion.description: The version an edit starts from. It is the draft, else the version in effect, else the latest. Null for a plan with no version yet.

effectiveVersion.description: The published version that prices calls today, or null.

draftVersion.description: The open draft, or null when there is none.

assignedServices.description: How many of your end users' services the plan is pinned to.

status.description: `superseded` is a published version a later one has replaced from its effective date. It still prices calls made before then.

effectiveFrom.description: The date the version prices calls from. Null on a draft.

notes.description: Where the version came from, such as the card it was copied from.

RetailPlanDestination.description: One destination on a call plan version. It covers calls to numbers starting with `prefix`. The longest matching prefix wins. Each rate is shown ex-GST, with its GST, and with GST. Your end user's invoice bills it the same way under your own tax settings. Rates are dollar amounts to up to 5 decimal places.

prefix.description: The number prefix, in E.164 digits without the `+`. It names the destination on every version.

connectionFeeExGst.description: The charge for each answered call, ex-GST.

minimumChargeExGst.description: The least an answered call costs, ex-GST.

firstIncrementSeconds.description: The first billing increment, in seconds.

subsequentIncrementSeconds.description: Each billing increment after the first, in seconds.

RetailPriceSourced.description:
The price that will bill today, ex-GST with its GST, and where it comes
from. `service_price` is this service's own price. `retail_book` is your
price book. `default_markup` is your markup on what we charge you.
`unpriced` means nothing prices it. It bills nothing and holds the end
user's invoice for you to approve.

EndUserServiceBilling.description:
How one service you have given an end user bills. Its own price and setup
fee, when set, win over your price book. Null means the book applies.
Prices are ex-GST. We work out the GST under your tax settings.

planId.description: The call plan pinned to this service, by its public id. It is one of your own. Null uses the product's default plan.

priceExGst.description: This service's own price each period, ex-GST. Null when the price book applies.

setupFeeExGst.description: This service's own setup fee, ex-GST. Null when the price book applies. "0.00" is free.

notBilled.description:
True when the whole service, with its fees and its usage, is left off
the end user's invoices. Our invoice to you does not change.

endsOn.description: The last day the service is billed to the end user, once ended.

EndUserCharge.description:
One of your own charges on an end user's bill. The amount is ex-GST. We
add GST on the invoice.

id.description: The charge's public id, for `/end-users/{endUser}/charges/{chargeId}`.

kind.description: A recurring charge bills each month in advance. A once-off charge bills once, on the next invoice.

priceExGst.description: The amount, ex-GST. It is charged each month for a recurring charge, and once for a once-off charge.

startsOn.description: The start date for a recurring charge, or the date of the charge for a once-off charge.

endsOn.description: The last day a recurring charge bills. Null for no end, and for a once-off charge.

billFrom.description: The first day a recurring charge bills from. Null for a once-off charge.

invoiced.description:
True once a held or issued invoice carries the charge. A once-off
charge can then no longer change or be removed. A recurring charge can
change only its description, its amount for months not yet charged, and
its end date. You end it rather than remove it.

RetailInvoiceSettings.description: The settings printed on every invoice to your end users, as Retail Settings sets them in the portal. The logo is set under the portal's branding and domain settings, not here.

displayName.description: The business name your end-user invoices are issued by. Null for your account's name.

abn.description: Your ABN, printed on each tax invoice. It is 11 digits and must pass the ATO check digit. You may send spaces when you write it. We store bare digits.

defaultTermsDays.description: Days to pay for an end user with no terms of its own. Null for 14 days.

defaultInvoiceDelivery.description: The invoice delivery a new end user starts with.

invoiceCopyEmail.description: Blind-copied on each end-user invoice email. Null sends no copy.

defaultInvoiceFormat.description: Summary or detailed invoices, for an end user with no choice of its own. Detailed lists each call under its usage line.

invoiceNumberPrefix.description: Leads every end-user invoice and credit note number. Null for none.

invoiceNextNumber.description: The next number of one running sequence across all your end users. It is shared by invoices and credit notes. Null numbers each invoice by end user and month. Each bill run moves it on.

remittanceText.description: The bank transfer details printed on each invoice.
remittanceText.example: BSB 062-000, account 1234 5678, reference your invoice number.

bpayBillerCode.description: Your own BPAY biller code, 3 to 10 digits.

RetailReminderSchedule.description: When your end users are reminded of an overdue invoice. These are reminders only. We never suspend an end user automatically.

enabled.description: Whether overdue end users are reminded at all. Off until you turn it on.

reminderDays.description: Days after the due date the first reminder is sent.

finalNoticeDays.description: Days after the due date the final notice is sent. Must be after the first reminder.

sendNotices.description: Whether we email the reminders to the end user. Turn it off if you chase your end users through your own system. We still record the reminder stages.

RetailNotice.description: A notice your end users receive that you may reword.

key.description: The notice's key, used in its path.

group.description: The notices are grouped as in the portal.

description.example: Sent to an end user with each invoice from your bill run, the invoice PDF attached.

reworded.description: Whether you have saved your own wording. False sends our default.

requiredContent.description: The placeholders that must stay in the subject or the body.

tokens.description: Every placeholder the notice offers. Any other placeholder is refused.

body.description: The body in effect, in Markdown. A notice with a statutory footer gets it added on every send. The footer is not part of the body.
body.example:
Hi {{ customer_name }},

Your invoice **{{ invoice_number }}** from {{ brand }} is attached.

default.description: Our default wording, which a reset goes back to.

body.example:
Hi {{ customer_name }},

Your invoice **{{ invoice_number }}** from {{ brand }} is attached.

RetailPaymentGateway.description: One payment gateway you take your end users' card or direct debit payments through. No key, webhook secret or callback address is ever returned.

connected.description: Whether keys for this gateway are saved.

status.description: `verified` means the keys passed our check when they were last saved or the gateway was switched back on. `unverified` means they did not, so end users are not offered the gateway. `disabled` means you switched it off, and we keep its keys. Null when not connected.

working.description: Whether end users are offered this gateway now (its status is verified).

supportedMethods.description: The payment methods this gateway can take.

enabledMethods.description: The payment methods you have turned it on for. Empty when not connected.

verifiedAt.description: When the keys last passed our check. Null when they never have, or after a failed check.

lastCheckedAt.description: When we last checked the keys, whether or not they passed. The keys are checked when they are saved or the gateway is switched back on. Null when no check has been recorded.

lastError.description: Why the last check failed, as the portal shows it. It is the gateway's own reason and its HTTP status, or why it could not be reached. Null when the check passed or none has run. It never contains key material.

EndUserSpend.description: An end user's spend this month against the monthly spend limit you set on them. Spent is their Next Bill Estimate so far, with GST. Their spend alerts and your portal show the same figure. The limit is an alert only. Nothing is stopped when it is reached.

endUser.description: The end user's number.

month.description: The calendar month, in the billing time zone (Australia/Brisbane).

limit.description: The monthly spend limit, in dollars, GST-inclusive.

spentExGst.description: Spent so far this month without GST, in dollars.

spentIncGst.description: Spent so far with GST. We compare this figure with `limit`.

percent.description: Whole per cent of the limit spent, rounded down.

tiersReached.description: The alert tiers (50, 85 and 100 per cent) reached this month.

usageExcluded.description: Call usage is not in `spent` yet, as on the end user's Next Bill Estimate. The figure is their services and charges only.

EndUserUsageRecord.description: A record of usage you rated yourself, billed on your end user's next invoice. Money is a dollar string. The unit price can have up to five decimal places of a dollar. The amount is the quantity times the unit price, rounded up to the cent, as the invoice bills it. We work out GST under your own tax settings and the record's `gst` treatment.

id.description: The record's public id, for `DELETE /usage/{usageId}`.

endUser.description: The end user's number.

description.description: What the usage was, as it is printed on the invoice.

quantity.description: How much, to up to four decimal places.

unitPriceExGst.description: The price of one unit, ex GST.

unitPriceIncGst.description: The price of one unit with GST.

amountExGst.description: Quantity times unit price, ex GST, rounded up to the cent.

gst.description: The GST treatment. `gst` adds GST. `free` and `exempt` add none.

reference.description: Your own reference for the record, unique on your account.

service.description: The end user's service the usage relates to, if you named one. It is the `assignmentId` from List an End User's Services.

billed.description: Whether a held or issued invoice carries it. A billed record can no longer be removed.

EndUserUsageInput.description: One record of usage you rated yourself. The unit price is in dollars, ex GST, as the portal takes it. A record can come to at most $999,999.99.

usageDate.description: The day of the usage. It cannot be in the future. It cannot be in a bill period the end user already has a held or issued invoice for.

description.description: What the usage was. On a summary invoice, records with the same description, unit, unit price and GST treatment make one line. On a detailed invoice each record is its own line.

quantity.description: How much, above 0, to up to four decimal places.

unitPrice.description: The price of one unit in dollars, **ex GST**. It starts from 0 and can have up to five decimal places.

gst.description: The GST treatment. `gst` when left out.

reference.description: Your own reference for the record. It is unique on your account. We refuse a record whose reference you already added, so you can resend safely.

service.description: One of the end user's services the usage relates to, by its `assignmentId` from List an End User's Services.

XeroStatus.description: Your own Xero connection, as Integrations → Xero in the portal shows it: whether it works, what still stops a push, and how much is waiting.

configured.description: Xero can be connected here. `false` means connecting is not available at the moment.

connected.description: An organisation is connected and Xero still accepts the connection.

needsReconnect.description: Xero no longer accepts the connection. It expired, or you removed it in Xero. We send nothing until you connect again in the portal.

pushFrom.description: We send only documents from this date on. It is the day you connected. We take earlier ones to be in your books already.

pushPayments.description: Whether payments you record are sent too, as well as invoices and credit notes.

problems.description: What still stops a push, in words. It may be a mapping not chosen yet, or an account or tax rate archived in Xero since. Empty when ready. Fix these with Set Xero Mapping.

chartError.description: Why your chart of accounts could not be read from Xero just now, when it could not. `problems` is then empty.

counts.description: How many end-user ledger entries are in each state.

waiting.description: Not tried yet. The nightly push, or Send Now, sends them.

unmatched.description: Waiting on a Xero contact for the end user. Link one with Link Xero Contact.

partial.description: Sent in part. The next push finishes them.

failed.description: Xero refused them. `reason` on each says why. The next push tries again.

lastPushAt.description: When an entry was last sent or tried, by any push. That includes the nightly push, the portal's Send Now and this API.

lastError.description: The newest reason Xero gave for refusing an entry still failed or sent in part.

message.example: The document date cannot be before the period lock date.

XeroQueueEntry.description: One end-user ledger entry that has not reached Xero: the end user, the document it is for, and why.

entryId.description: The ledger entry's public id, as the end-user ledger names it.

endUser.description: The end user's number.

kind.description: What the entry is. It is `invoice_charge` for an invoice, `credit_note`, `payment`, `payment_reversal` for a dishonour or chargeback, or `adjustment`.

direction.description: A debit adds to what the end user owes you. A credit takes from it.

invoiceNumber.description: The end-user invoice the entry is for, when it is one.

creditNoteNumber.description: The end-user credit note the entry is for, when it is one.

amountExGst.description: The entry's amount without GST, in dollars. It is unsigned. `direction` carries the sign.

reason.description: Xero's reason, or ours, for the entry not being in Xero. `null` while waiting.
reason.example: The document date cannot be before the period lock date.

attempts.description: How many times a push has tried it.

XeroChoice.description: One account or tax rate your Xero chart of accounts offers.

code.description: The account code or tax type to send in Set Xero Mapping.

XeroMapping.description: Which of your Xero organisation's accounts and tax rates your end-user documents use. Every value is an account code or tax type from your own chart of accounts (`choices`). We assume nothing, so we send nothing until the mapping is complete.

revenueDefault.description: The sales account every invoice line goes to unless its product or charge has its own.

products.description: A sales account for a product's lines, by product ID, in place of `revenueDefault`.

charges.description: A sales account for one of your own charges, by charge ID, in place of `revenueDefault`.

paymentDefault.description: The account payments are received into, unless their gateway has its own. Needed only when `pushPayments` is on.

payments.description: A clearing account for each way an end user pays, which is `manual`, `stripe`, `square` or `gocardless`. It replaces `paymentDefault`.

tax.description: The Xero tax rate for GST lines (`taxed`), GST-free lines (`free`) and lines with no GST (`none`).

pushPayments.description: Whether payments you record are sent to Xero too.

choices.description: What your chart of accounts offers for each kind of mapping today.

problems.description: What still stops a push. Empty when ready.

EndUserXeroContact.description: The Xero contact an end user's documents go to.

endUser.description: The end user's number.

contactId.description: The Xero contact's ID, or `null` when none is linked.

TrunkCredential.description: A trunk's SIP digest credential, with its password in plain text. Store the password securely. The answers that carry it are not cached.

username.description: The SIP digest username, which also addresses the trunk on `/trunks/{username}`.

TrunkSourceRestrictions.description: Where a trunk's SIP credentials may be used from. We refuse a call that authenticates with the credentials from anywhere else. A stolen password is no use elsewhere. Both lists empty means no restriction. The trunk's IP list (`/trunks/{username}/ips`) is separate. It lets calls in without registering.

cidrs.description: Public source addresses or CIDR ranges. IPv4 ranges are no wider than `/24`. IPv6 entries are single hosts (`/128`). We store a bare address as `/32` or `/128`.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, upper case. The United Kingdom is `GB`, not `UK`.

NumberBulkJob.description: One bulk number change and what happened to each number.

status.description: `done` once every number has its result. A release is then queued, and the number reads `releasing` until it is gone. `running` means the call is still working through the numbers. A job left `running` stopped part way because the call timed out, and `results` are the numbers it reached.

done.description: How many numbers were changed, or for a release, asked for release.

skipped.description: How many were left alone, each with its reason.

failed.description: How many could not be changed just now. Try those again.

results.description: One per number, in the order sent.

reason.description: Why it was skipped or failed; null when done.
reason.example: This Number Is Suspended By Check Networks; Contact Support To Lift It

NumberOffer.description: A number, or the start of a block, you can order now, with its price per number. The price is the monthly price at the tier your holding of this type reaches with these numbers. Your invoice charges it the same way.

number.description: The number, or the first number of the block, as E.164 digits with no `+`.

lastNumber.description: The last number of the block. It is the same as `number` for a single number.

source.description: `stock` is a number we hold. Hold a single one with `POST /numbers/holds` and order it with the `holdId`. Order a block by its type, area and size, which takes this block. `offer` is offered where we hold none. Order it with `offerId`. Nothing is reserved until you order.

offerId.description: For an `offer` number, the reference to order it by. Null for `stock`.

monthlyPriceExGst.description: The monthly price per number without GST, in dollars. Null when no price applies.

setupPriceExGst.description: The one-off setup fee per number without GST, in dollars. Null when none applies.

NumberLookupResult.description: What the number register says about one Australian number, as the portal's Number Lookup shows it.

number.description: The number as it is dialled in Australia.

assignedCarrier.description: The carrier the number's block was assigned to.

currentCarrier.description: The carrier that serves the number now. It differs from `assignedCarrier` when the number has ported.

portedActionIndicator.description: The register's ported action indicator. A blank is a real state; null means the register has no entry.

alreadyPorting.description: Whether a port of the number is in progress. Null when the register could not say. `reason` says why. For a mobile, it is not an Australian fixed line.

heldByUs.description: True when the number is already on our books.

portable.description: A hint only, worked out from `alreadyPorting` and `heldByUs`. It is false when we hold the number or a port is already in progress. It is true when neither applies. It is null when the register could not say. It does not check that a port will be accepted.

reason.description: The register's own explanation, when it gave one.

source.description: Where the answer came from: `register` is our copy of the carrier register, `carrier` a live lookup at the carrier.

asAt.description: How current the answer is, the register file's date or the time it was asked.

PortState.description:
A number port's real state: the step it is at, not a summary. The same id
is a port's `state` on `GET /ports` and its `step.id` on the port webhooks.
Each state waits on one party (`waitingOn`):

| State | Track | `waitingOn` |
|---|---|---|
| `awaiting_authority` | fixed line, 13/1300/1800, sent to the holder | `wholesaler`: the number's holder confirms the Porting Authority by the emailed link; resend it if they need a new one. Cancelled after 14 days without |
| `requested` | every port-in | `us`: we check the request and send it to the losing carrier |
| `submitted` | fixed line, 13/1300/1800 | `losingCarrier`: with the losing carrier for approval |
| `confirmed` | fixed line, 13/1300/1800 | `us`: approved; we book the cutover |
| `scheduled` | fixed line, 13/1300/1800 | `losingCarrier`: the cutover is booked; the number moves on the day |
| `ppv_sent` | mobile | `wholesaler`: enter the verification code the number's holder was sent |
| `ppv_validated` | mobile | `us`: we lodge it with the carrier |
| `submitted_upstream` | mobile | `losingCarrier`: lodged; waiting for the number to move |
| `port_out_requested` | port-out | `us`: our team reviews the gaining carrier's request |
| `port_out_approved` | port-out | `gainingCarrier`: approved; waiting for the gaining carrier to take the number |
| `activated` | port-in, finished | null: the number is live on our network |
| `ported_away` | port-out, finished | null: the number has left |
| `rejected` | finished | null: refused; `statusReason` says why |
| `cancelled` | finished | null: withdrawn or cancelled; `statusReason` says why |

PortWaitingOn.description: Who the port is waiting on now, so you can tell whether to act or wait. `wholesaler` is you, for example with a verification code to enter. `us` means we work the next step. `losingCarrier` is the carrier the numbers are leaving, on a port-in. `gainingCarrier` is the carrier taking the number, on a port-out. Null once the port has finished. See `PortState` for the party each state waits on.

PortOrder.description: A number port, in or out, as the portal's port page shows it: its state, who it is waiting on, its history step by step, the cutover and why it stopped. Named by `reference`. Times are ISO 8601 with an offset; dates are on your account's calendar.

reference.description: The port's reference, as `GET /ports/{reference}` takes it.

direction.description: `in` brings the numbers onto your account. `out` is a number leaving you for another carrier. Our team works that with the gaining carrier.

portType.description: The kind of port-in. `CatA` is one fixed-line number. `CatC` is a list or range of fixed-line numbers. `Mob` is a mobile number. `Inbound` is a 13, 1300 or 1800 number. Null on a port-out.

numbers.description: The numbers on the port, as E.164 digits. A CAT C range keeps its wildcard tail. `#` is 10 numbers and `##` is 100.

stateName.description: The state's name, as the portal shows it.

group.description: The portal's tab for the port. `active` is in flight. `completed` is `activated` or `ported_away`. `rejected` is `rejected` or `cancelled`.

nextStep.description: The next step in plain words. Null once the port has finished.
nextStep.example: Enter the verification code the number's holder was sent.

attention.description: Why the port needs a person to look at it, or null. The reasons are a cutover date that passed without the number moving, a verification code that lapsed, or a step that has taken longer than it should.

stateEnteredAt.description: When the port entered its current state; null once finished.

preferredCutoverOn.description: The cutover date you asked for, if any. The carriers set the real one.

scheduledFor.description: The booked cutover, once the carriers have set it. On a port-out, it is the agreed date.

completedAt.description: When the number went live on our network, or left it on a port-out.

statusReason.description: Why the port was rejected, withdrawn or cancelled. Null otherwise.
statusReason.example: The account number does not match the losing carrier's records.

portOutResponseCode.description: On a port-out, the industry response code we gave the gaining carrier. `000` means approved. Any other code is the reason it was refused. Null on a port-in.

losingProvider.description: The provider the numbers are leaving, on a port-in.

carrierReference.description: The losing carrier's reference for the port, once it has one.

endUserName.description: The legal holder of the numbers, as given on the request.

endUser.description: The end user of the trunk the numbers land on, by its number; null for your own trunk.

trunk.description: The `sipUsername` of the trunk the numbers land on.

emergencyAddressId.description: The emergency address the numbers are listed at once live.

contact.description: Who we email about a port-in. Null on a port-out.

type.description: `sp` the service provider, `cr` the customer's representative.

verificationCode.description: A mobile port's verification code. Null on every other port. A code lasts 30 minutes. Send a fresh one with `POST /ports/{reference}/verification-code`. Five wrong codes per port reject the port. We count them across every code sent.

sentAt.description: When the latest code was sent; null if none has gone yet.

expiresAt.description: When the latest code lapses, while the port waits for it.

expired.description: True when the code lapsed before it was entered.

attemptsRemaining.description: Wrong codes the port can still take.

history.description: What has happened to the port, oldest first, as the portal's port page lists it.

PortInRequest.description: A port-in request, as the portal's port request form takes it.

numbers.description: The numbers to port, in E.164 or national form. One, except on `CatC`.

trunk.description: The `sipUsername` of the trunk the numbers land on.

emergencyAddressId.description: The emergency address the numbers are listed at.

endUserName.description: The legal holder of the numbers with the losing provider.

contactName.description: Who we email about the port.

contactType.description: `sp` the service provider, `cr` the customer's representative.

preferredCutoverOn.description: The cutover date you would like. It must be after today, in your account's time zone or the one you sent in `CN-Time-Zone`. The carriers set the real date.

accountNumber.description: Mobile postpaid only, and required there.

dateOfBirth.description: Mobile prepaid only, and required there.

authorityHolder.description: Send the port to the number's holder to give the Porting Authority, instead of giving it in `consents`. It works for any port but `Mob`. We save the port in `awaiting_authority` and email the holder a link on your end-user portal.

CdrExport.description: One scheduled call record export to our SFTP server.

description.description: When the export runs and what it covers.

id.description: The recording's public id. Fetch it with `GET /voice/recordings/{id}`.

trunk.description: The sipUsername of the trunk the call was on.

trigger.description: What started the recording, such as the trunk's always-on setting or an on-demand request.

retentionExpiresAt.description: When the recording is deleted under the retention period.

SmsMessage.description: One SMS sent from or received on your account.

id.description: The message's id, as `POST /sms` returned it in `messageId`.

from.description: The sender, a number in E.164 format or a sender ID.

to.description: The recipient number in E.164 format.

message.description: The message body. Blank once the text is no longer held (90 days, or 7 days after delivery).

status.description: `delivered` and `failed` are final. `pending` means the message may still move: queued, awaiting a delivery receipt, or held for review; `statusReason` says which.

statusReason.description: Present only where the status alone is ambiguous.

SmsSender.description: A sender your account has asked for or holds. It is a number you control, or a sender ID of 3 to 11 letters and digits. We approve numbers you hold with us automatically. Our team checks anything else first.

id.description: The request's public id, for `DELETE /sms/senders/{id}`.

status.description: `pending` until our team decides it. Only an `approved` sender can be used with `POST /sms`. `revoked` is a sender that left your account. `withdrawn` is a request you took back.

endUser.description: The end user the sender belongs to, by its public number. Null when it is your own.

FaxDocument.description: One fax sent or received on your numbers, as Fax History in the portal shows it. It holds metadata only, never the document or a link to it.

id.description: The fax's id, as the `fax.*` webhook events carry it in `faxId`.

number.description: Your number the fax was received on or sent from.

remoteNumber.description: The other party's number. Null when it was withheld.

pages.description: Pages received or sent. 0 until a sent fax has gone through.

status.description: A received fax is `received`, then `emailed` (sent on by email), `delivered` (kept for the portal) or `failed`. A sent fax is `pending` (queued), `rendering`, `dialing` and `sending`, then `sent` or `failed`. We retry a busy line or no answer, so a fax can go back to `pending` before it fails for good.

failureReason.description: Why it failed. Null unless `status` is `failed`.
failureReason.example: The destination fax number is busy.

endUser.description: The end user's account number when the fax is theirs. Null when it is yours.

createdAt.description: When the fax was received, or queued to send.

completedAt.description: When it finished arriving or finished sending. Null until then.

FaxSettings.description: Your fax domain and cover page, as Fax Settings in the portal.

domain.description: Your own fax domain. End users email faxes to `<number>@` the domain. We email received faxes and send results from it. Null for the platform's domain.

enabled.description: Whether a cover page goes ahead of each fax sent. It counts as a page sent, and we bill it as one.

company.description: The company name on the cover page.

footer.description: The line at the foot of the cover page.

FaxDomainCheck.description: A fax domain checked both ways. Nothing is stored.

inbound.description: Whether mail to `<number>@` the domain reaches us, from its public MX records. `ok` means it is delivered to us directly. `forwarding` means it points elsewhere. That works if the mail is forwarded to us. Send a test fax by email to be sure. `fail` means there is no MX record. `error` means the lookup failed.

outbound.description: Whether mail from the domain is accepted. We cannot read that from here, so it is always `unknown`. Ask us to confirm it.

AllowedCountries.description: Your account's list of countries its trunks may call.

allowedCountries.description: ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes, sorted. Every country until you set a list.

availableCountries.description: Every country a list can name, by name. Australia and New Zealand are not among them. Calls to either are never international. Calls to New Zealand follow each trunk's `NZMobile` and `NZNational` permissions.

name.description: A friendly name for the line.

username.description: The line's SIP username, which its phone registers with. It is the line's identifier. Every `/residential-lines/{username}` endpoint addresses the line by this value. Call records and numbers name it in their `trunk` field with `trunkType: residentialLine`.

sipDomain.description: The SIP domain the line's phone registers to.

plan.description: The line's plan. `payg` meters calls. `ultimate` includes Australian calls to landlines and mobiles, for a higher monthly price.

status.description: The line's status. A suspended line makes and receives no calls, except 000 and an emergency callback within the hour.

endUser.description: The end user this line is for, by its public number. Null for a line that is your own.

numbers.description: The line's live numbers, E.164 digits without the `+`.

numbersRoutedHere.description: The numbers in `numbers` whose route sends calls to this line. A number can be on the line, and billed there, while it is routed somewhere else. If this is empty while `numbers` is not, no call reaches the line.

awaitingNumber.description: True while the line has no live number. It bills from the day it is ordered, but it cannot make or receive calls until its number is ordered. The portal's Residential Lines list shows this as Awaiting Number.

defaultCallerId.description: The number the line presents on outbound calls. We set it to the line's own number when that number lands on the line. Null until then.

ResidentialLineSettings.description: A residential line's call settings. Its end user can change the same settings from the phone with star codes. They are *72 and *73 for forwarding, and *78 and *79 for Do Not Disturb.

forwarding.description: Forward every call to another number.

destination.description: The number calls are forwarded to, 6 to 15 digits. Required to turn forwarding on. Null while forwarding is off. It is never 000, 112 or 106, in any form (`0061000`, `1831112`). That is a `422`, "Calls can’t be diverted to an emergency number (000, 112 or 106)."

doNotDisturb.description: Send every incoming call straight to voicemail.

anonymousReject.description: Refuse incoming calls that withhold their number.

callWaiting.description: Let a second call through while the line is on a call.

callingPermissions.description: The kinds of number the line may call. It is shown for reference. We set it, and you cannot change it here.

ResidentialLineVoicemail.description: A residential line's mailbox. The PIN is the end user's own, set in the end-user portal or by phone, and is never read or set here.

enabled.description: Whether unanswered calls go to the mailbox.

email.description: Where each new message is emailed; null for none.

attachAudio.description: Attach the recording to the email. A line with no mailbox yet reads true. A new mailbox gets that value when it is turned on.

deleteAfterEmail.description: Delete the message once it is emailed. It takes effect only with an `email` set. Without one it reads false.

id.description: The request's public id.

number.description: The number asked for, E.164 digits without the `+`.

reason.description: Why you want to present the number, as you sent it.

status.description: `pending` until we decide it. `approved` means you can set the number as a trunk's default caller ID. `rejected` means you cannot, and `decisionNote` says why. `cancelled` means you withdrew the request.

decidedAt.description: When it was approved, rejected or cancelled. Null while pending.

decisionNote.description: Why a rejected request was refused. Null otherwise.

evidence.description: The proof sent with the request. The file itself is never returned. Both fields are null on a request made before 21 November 2026.

name.description: The file's name as it was sent.

DataSqBatch.description: A batch of premises qualified as one job. It is the API's form of the portal's Batch Qualification page, which lists the same batches.

id.description: The batch's id.

href.description: URL of this batch.

reference.description: Your name for the batch, as you sent it. A batch uploaded in the portal carries its file name.

status.description: `completed` once every row has its result. We qualify rows one by one, usually within minutes. Poll this batch to follow it.

total.description: Rows in the batch.

done.description: Rows with a result, whatever it is.

unresolved.description: Rows whose address did not resolve to one location.

failed.description: Rows the carrier could not qualify after retries. This is not a verdict on the premises. Qualify the row on its own with `GET /data/sq/{locId}`.

DataSqBatchRow.description: One row of a qualification batch and its result.

rowNumber.description: The row's place in the list you sent, from 1. For a batch uploaded in the portal, its line in the file.

reference.description: Your reference for the row, as you sent it.

input.description: The location id or address you sent.

status.description: `unresolved` is an address that did not resolve to one location. `failed` is a qualification the carrier could not answer after retries. It is not a verdict on the premises.

resolvedAddress.description: The address the row resolved to.

detail.description: The result in words, as the portal shows it, such as `FTTP · class 3 · port available`.

qualification.description: The row's qualification summary, once it resolves to a location. It uses the field names of `GET /data/sq/{locId}`. Follow `href` for the full qualification. Null until then, and for an unresolved row.

id.description: The location id (LOC… or OPC…).

href.description: URL of this location's full qualification.

id.description: The site's code, as `GET /colocation/sites` lists it.

ColocationSellUnit.description: The tier: a full rack, a half rack, or 1, 2, 4 or 10 rack units. Full and half racks are priced by quote.

ColocationService.description: One of your colocation services, rack space at one of our sites.

serviceNumber.description: The service's number, as the portal and your invoices show it.

position.description: The rack units the service holds, bottom up, as the portal shows them.

powerAmps.description: The power included with the service, in amps.

ColocationOrder.description: A colocation order. We assign the rack and rack units, and the service then appears on `GET /colocation/services`.

OccupancyDocument.description: A proof of occupancy you uploaded: what was sent, and the order that used it. The file itself is kept privately with us and never served back.

id.description: What an order takes as `occupancyDocumentId`.

name.description: The file's name, as it was sent.

used.description: Whether an order has used it. Each document is used once.

orderId.description: The order that used it, or null.

Bundle.description: A bundle of data orders, numbers and a voice trunk, ordered together in sequence. It matches the portal's Bundles page.

reference.description: The bundle's reference, as the portal shows it.

status.description: `draft` until something in it has been sent, `inProgress` while its items run, then `completed` or `cancelled`.

submitted.description: Whether it has been submitted. A submitted bundle takes nothing more and is not rearranged. The items that wait are released as the items before them complete.

sendAt.description: The time the bundle's submit holds it for. Its draft data orders, number orders and trunk are all sent then. Null when it holds nothing.

blockedReason.description: Why the bundle could not move on at its last attempt, or null.

endUser.description: The end user the bundle is for, by its public number, or null.

total.description: The running total of the bundle's draft data orders at today's prices, as the portal's bundle page shows it. It adds up each draft's `price`. A draft with no plan yet, or one your prices do not cover, is counted in `unpricedDrafts` and left out of the sum. Number orders and the trunk are not in it. Null for a key without `billing:read`.

pricedDrafts.description: How many draft data orders are in the sum.

unpricedDrafts.description: How many draft data orders have no price yet, and are left out of the sum.

draftRemoval.description: The first date one of the bundle's drafts is removed if you do not check it out. It also says whether Keep (`POST /bundles/{id}/keep`) can still keep any of them. Each item's `draftRemoval` has its own date. Null when none of its drafts is removed.

drafts.description: How many of its drafts are removed if not checked out.

VpnGroup.description: A VPN access group. Its users may reach what it allows.

id.description: The group's id.

accessMode.description: With `split`, only `destinations` go through the tunnel. With `full`, all the user's internet traffic does.

destinations.description: For a `split` group, the networks its users reach through the tunnel, as CIDRs. A bare address is a /32. Empty for a `full` group.

dedicatedEgressIp.description: The group's own public address on the internet, when we have given it one (billed monthly). Ask support for one.

userCount.description: The group's users, not counting removed ones.

VpnUser.description: A VPN user, with its own certificate and profile, billed monthly.

id.description: The user's id.

cn.description: The certificate's name. It never changes, through a rename or a move.

state.description: `provisioning` until its profile is ready, then `active`. `suspended` while we hold it for an unpaid account. We do not release its profile.

endUser.description: The number of the end user the seat is for, when you resell VPN. Null when none.

endUserName.description: That end user's name. Null when none.

vpnIp.description: The user's address inside the tunnel, once issued.

profileReady.description: Whether GET /vpn/users/{id}/profile will give a link now.

UsageAlertMetric.description: What a usage alert watches. `callSpendToday` is call charges today, without GST. `callSpendMonth` is call charges this month, without GST. `minutesMonth` is minutes of answered calls this month. `smsMonth` is messages sent this month. Days and months run on the Brisbane calendar our bill runs on. Only the call metrics can be limited to one trunk.

UsageAlertRecipient.description: One person a usage alert goes to, by email or by SMS. Each alert has its own list.

id.description: The recipient's public id.

mobile.description: An Australian mobile, as stored (E.164 digits without the `+`).

UsageAlert.description: A usage alert: when the metric reaches the threshold, we email and text the alert's own recipients once for that day or month, and send a `usageAlert.triggered` webhook event.

id.description: The alert's public id.

trunk.description: The SIP trunk the alert watches, by its `sipUsername`. `null` watches the whole account. Only the call metrics take a trunk.

threshold.description: Dollars without GST for a spend metric (`"50.00"`), otherwise a whole number of minutes or messages (`"1000"`).

currency.description: The threshold's currency for a spend metric. `null` otherwise.

channels.description: How the alert's recipients are told. Empty sends only the webhook event.

recipients.description: Who this alert goes to, oldest first. It takes up to 10 addresses and 10 mobiles. We tell only these people. There is no fallback to your billing contact or your credit alert recipients. An alert with none sends only the webhook event.

lastFiredAt.description: When the alert last went off. `null` if it never has.

lastFiredPeriod.description: The day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) or month (`YYYY-MM`) it last went off for.

UsageAlertRecipientInput.description: One recipient. Send `email` or `mobile`, not both. A mobile may be written in any usual form, such as `0491 570 006` or `+61491570006`. One that is not an Australian mobile answers `422`.

AuditLogEntry.description:
One entry in your account's audit trail: something one of your portal
users, one of your API keys or our support staff did on your account. The
same entries your portal's Audit Log page shows. Entries are never changed
or removed.

id.description: The entry's id. Opaque.

action.description: What was done, as a key. New keys are added as the platform grows.

actionLabel.description: The action in words, as the portal shows it. The wording can change.

type.description: `user` is one of your portal users. `apiKey` is one of your API keys. `support` is our support staff acting on your behalf, signed in as one of your users. We never name the staff member.

id.description: For a `user`, their id as `GET /account/users` names it. For an `apiKey`, the key's id, which is its `client_id`. `null` for `support`.

name.description: The user's name, the key's name as it is now, or `Support`.

email.description: A user's email address. `null` for any other actor.

target.description: What it was done to, when the entry names one. `ref` is its public id where it has one. That is an end user's number, a trunk's or user's id, an invoice's id or a ticket's reference. Otherwise `ref` is `null`.

ip.description: The address the action came from. `null` when our support staff did it or when none was recorded.

changes.description: What changed, by field. Each value has a `from` and a `to`, as text. Either is `—` where a value was not set. Empty when the entry records no change.

context.description: Further detail, by label, as text. Internal identifiers are never included. Empty when there is none.

ApiCall.description:
A summary of one call one of your API keys made, kept for 30 days. It never
holds the request or response body, the query string or any header.

id.description: The call's `CN-Message-Id`. Quote it to Support to find the call.

keyId.description: The key that made it, its `client_id`.

keyName.description: The key's name as it is now. `null` once the key is gone.

route.description: The endpoint as a pattern, such as `/v2/tickets/{ticketRef}`. Calls to the same endpoint share it. `null` for a path no endpoint matched.

path.description: The path called, without the query string.

status.description: The HTTP status we answered.

durationMs.description: How long we took to answer, in milliseconds.

ip.description: The address the call came from.

createdAt.description: When the call was made, in UTC.

apiVersion.description: The API version the event's `data` follows. It is `2`, as in the `/v2` paths. Within a version we only ever add fields to an event. Ignore fields you do not know.

livemode.description: `false` when the event comes from the sandbox. You can send both to one endpoint and tell them apart.

test.description: `true` for a delivery you asked for with `POST /webhooks/{webhookId}/test`. It is a ping, or a sample event whose `data` describes nothing real. Do not act on it.

accountId.description: The account the event belongs to, as `clientNumber` on `GET /account`. A delivery to an endpoint that a key limited to one end user registered leaves it out, tests, redeliveries and replays included.

resourceUrl.description: Where to read the current state of what the event is about. Events can arrive late or out of order. Re-read it rather than trusting the event alone. Null when there is no single resource to read, and on a test.

WebhookFeedEvent.description:
One event from the feed (`GET /events`). It has the body a delivery of it
carries, with the same `eventId`. A handler that de-duplicates on
`eventId` treats a feed event and a delivery of it as one. `sequence` is
`null`, because each endpoint numbers its own deliveries. We keep it for
30 days, and only when one of your endpoints subscribed to it.

eventId.description: The event's id, as every delivery of it carries.

eventType.description: The event type, as `GET /webhooks/event-types` lists them.

occurredAt.description: When the event happened, in UTC.

sequence.description: Always `null` in the feed. A delivery carries its endpoint's sequence.

data.description: The event's `data`, as the event's own schema under `webhooks` describes it.

StepDelegation.description: One step of a port or a data order handed to a named person by a one-use emailed link. We never return the link or the email code. Only the person they were sent to can use them.

action.description: The one step the link allows. With `confirmPort`, the mobile number's holder enters the verification code texted to it, on a mobile port-in waiting for it (`ppv_sent`). With `pickAppointment`, someone at the site picks the install time, on a data order with no appointment yet. With `confirmAuthority`, the fixed-line number's holder confirms the Porting Authority with their name and position, on a port waiting for it (`awaiting_authority`).

portReference.description: The port, for `confirmPort` and `confirmAuthority`. Null otherwise.

orderId.description: The data order, for `pickAppointment`. Null otherwise.

name.description: The person's name, as you gave it.

email.description: Where the link and the code went.

status.description: `sent` means the link works. `used` means the person did the step, and the link no longer works. `cancelled` means you cancelled it. `expired` means 7 days passed unused. Resend it for a new link.

type.description: A portal user or an API key handed it over.

name.description: The user's or the key's name.

sentAt.description: When the current link was sent, which is the last resend.

expiresAt.description: When the current link stops working, 7 days after it was sent.

resendCount.description: How many times the link was sent again.

codePassedAt.description: When the person last passed the email code on the current link.

ApiKey.description: The API key you called with. It shows the key's own details, never a secret and never another key. A key belongs to your account, not to the user who made it.

clientId.description: The key's client id, the one you send to `POST /oauth/token`.

scopes.description: The scopes the key may ask for.

ipAllowlist.description: The addresses and CIDR blocks the key may be used from. Empty is anywhere.

expiresAt.description: When the key stops working, in UTC. `null` for a key with no end date. An Owner or Admin sets it in the portal. We email the account's Owners 14 days and 1 day before.

previousSecretExpiresAt.description: While a rotation's overlap runs, when the old secret and its tokens stop working, in UTC. Otherwise `null`.

NotificationPreferences.description: A staff user's notice choices, as on their Notifications page: for each notice they can receive, the channels it can use and the one they chose. Read only: each user sets their own in the portal.

channels.description: The channels this notice can use.

channel.description: The channel chosen, or `none` for a notice turned off.

AccountInvite.description: An open invitation to a staff login on your account. Accepting it makes the login. Partner invitations are under `/partners/invites`.

id.description: The invitation's id.

role.description: The role the login gets on accepting.

status.description: `expired` once its link no longer works. Resend it for a fresh link.

AccountSecurity.description: Your account's security settings, as on Company Settings > Security. You can only read them here. An Owner or Admin changes them in the portal.

requireTwoFactor.description: Whether every staff login must use two-factor to sign in.

signInIpAllowlist.description: The addresses staff may sign in to the portal from. Empty means anywhere. This is the portal's list. Each API key has its own.

createdBy.description: The name of the user who added it.

BookedChangeSide.description: One side of a booked change. A disconnect moves `status` from the service's status now to `Cancelled`. A plan change moves `plan` and `channels`.

status.description: The data service's status, as `GET /data/services` names it. Null on a plan change.

plan.description: The trunk's plan. Null on a disconnect.

channels.description: The channels billed on the trunk, 0 on `payg`. Null on a disconnect.

BookedChange.description: A change booked on your account for a later date. It is either a data service disconnect booked for a later day, or a trunk plan change waiting for the start of the next billing cycle. `from` and `to` say what changes. Each has all three fields, null where the kind does not change it.

id.description: The booked change's id, for `DELETE /account/booked-changes/{id}`.

kind.description: `disconnect` is a data service disconnect booked for a later day. `planChange` is a trunk plan or channel change booked for the next billing cycle.

serviceId.description: For a data service, its `id`, as `GET /data/services/{ref}` takes it. For a trunk, its `sipUsername`, or else its `id`.

trunkId.description: The trunk's `id` for a plan change. Null for a data service.

effectiveOn.description: The day it takes effect. A disconnect goes to the carrier at the start of that day, Sydney time. A plan change applies on that day, which is the 1st of a month.

type.description: `user` is one of your portal users. `apiKey` is one of your API keys. `checkNetworks` is our staff, at your request. `system` is the platform itself.

name.description: The user's or the key's name. Null for Check Networks and the platform.

held.description: True when we are holding a booked disconnect for a person to decide, because the carrier could not take it. It does not go on `effectiveOn` until we send, move or cancel it. A `bookedChange.*` event tells you which. `effectiveOn` stays the day it was booked for. Always false for a plan change.

ApiExport.description: A background export, started with `POST /exports`. It shows the export's state. Once it is `ready`, it also shows the file's size, its row count and a signed link to download it. The webhook events carry the same fields without the link.

id.description: The export's id.

type.description: What it holds.

state.description: `queued` until a worker picks it up, `running` while the file is written, then `ready` or `failed`.

filters.description: The list filters it was started with.

rowCount.description: The rows in the file, once it is ready.

sizeBytes.description: The file's size in bytes, once it is ready.

failureReason.description: Why it failed, in words to act on. Null unless `failed`.

expiresAt.description: When the file is removed, 7 days after it was ready.

downloadUrl.description: While the export is ready and kept, a signed link to the file. It is good for one hour and needs no token. Each read gives a new link. An expired link answers `403`. It is on the API's reads only, not in webhook events.

PartnerProductRef.description: A product on your retail price book.

Partner.description: A partner: a login that sees only the end users, products and permissions you give it.

id.description: The partner's id, as in the commission routes.

endUsers.description: The end users the partner may reach, by end-user number.

products.description: The products the partner may sell.

permissions.description: What else the partner may do for its end users.

PartnerInvite.description: An open invitation to a partner login.

endUsers.description: The end users the partner will reach, by end-user number.

WebhookTicketEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `ticket.*` events. `data` carries the ticket's header (its reference, subject, status, priority, category, times and your own reference) plus the fields of the event. To get the whole ticket, as you may act on it now, read `resourceUrl` (`GET /tickets/{ticketRef}`).

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

data.description: What every ticket event sends, and the event's own fields. Anything that depends on who reads the ticket, such as `canResolve` and `actions`, is on the ticket read only.

reference.description: The public ticket reference, as `GET /tickets/{ticketRef}` takes it.

status.description: The ticket's status after the event.

lastActivityAt.description: The ticket's last message or change.

messageId.description: The new message's `id`, as `GET /tickets/{ticketRef}` lists it. On `ticket.replied` only.

author.description: Who wrote the reply. On `ticket.replied` only.

from.description: The previous status. On `ticket.statusChanged` and `ticket.informationRequired` only.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

cgrid.description: The call record's id, as `cgrid` on `GET /voice/cdrs`.

serviceId.description: The trunk's sipUsername, as `GET /trunks` and the trunk events name it. Null for a line with no SIP credential.

tenantHandle.description: Deprecated. Use `serviceId`. The trunk or line's internal handle. We remove it in the next release.

direction.description: `outbound` is a call your PBX placed to a carrier. `inbound` is a call a carrier delivered to your PBX.

costExGst.description: The rated charge without GST, as a dollar string. The same figure as `costExGst` on the CDR endpoints.

totalCents.description: Deprecated. Use `costExGst`. The rated charge in cents without GST. We send it for one more release and then remove it.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

serviceId.description: The trunk's sipUsername, as `GET /trunks` and the trunk events name it. Null for a line with no SIP credential.

tenantHandle.description: Deprecated. Use `serviceId`. The voice tenancy's internal handle. We remove it in the next release.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

cgrid.description: The call the recording belongs to, as `GET /voice/cdrs/{cgrid}` names it.

serviceId.description: The trunk the call was on, by its SIP username. It is the `sipUsername` `GET /trunks` returns and the `serviceId` the trunk events carry.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

serviceId.description: The trunk's `sipUsername`, or its `id` when it has no SIP credential.

trunkId.description: The trunk's `id`, which every trunk has.

lastSeenAt.description: When the trunk was last registered or sending OPTIONS. On `trunk.down` that is when it went quiet.

WebhookCallerIdEvent.description: A caller ID authorisation request approved or rejected.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. Use it to deduplicate.

id.description: The request's public id, as `GET /caller-id-authorisations/{id}` takes it.

callerId.description: The number asked for, E.164 digits without the `+`.

status.description: `approved` means the number can now be set as a trunk's default caller ID. `rejected` means it cannot, and `reason` says why.

reason.description: Why the request was refused. On `rejected` only.

WebhookVoiceHoldEvent.description: The delivery for `voice.hold.placed` and `voice.hold.released`. A hold never stops a 000 call.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

holdType.description: `spendVelocity` and `callingPattern` pause the account's new outbound calls until we release the hold. `internationalCap` refuses one trunk's international calls until we release it. `dailySpendCap` refuses one trunk's outbound calls, all but 000 and 1800, until midnight Brisbane time or until you release it or raise the cap.

serviceType.description: `voice` for a trunk's hold. Null for an account hold.

serviceId.description: The trunk's `sipUsername`. Null for an account hold.

unit.description: What `threshold` and `measured` count. It is international minutes, or dollars ex GST. Null for an account hold, and both figures are null too.

threshold.description: The cap the hold tripped at, as a string in `unit`.

measured.description: What the trunk had used when the hold tripped, in `unit`.

windowSeconds.description: The rolling window the figure was measured over. Null for a daily cap, which is measured since midnight Brisbane time.

releasesAt.description: When a `dailySpendCap` hold lifts by itself. Null for the others, which we release.

releaseReason.description: On `voice.hold.released`. `released` means we or you released it. `cap_raised` means you raised the daily cap above today's spend. `midnight` means a daily cap hold lifted by itself.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

number.description: The number, E.164 without `+`, as `GET /numbers/{number}` takes it.

serviceId.description: The trunk's `sipUsername`. On `number.assigned` it is the trunk the number was assigned to. On the other events it is the trunk the number was on. Null when the number was on no trunk.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

emergencyAddressId.description: The emergency address the refused record was built from.

status.description: `rejected` means the IPND refused this number's record. `fileRejected` means it refused the whole file the record was in. The record is not at fault, and we send it again. The values match those on the number's `ipnd`.

errors.description: The IPND's codes, each explained, as on the number's `ipnd.errors`.

fixInAddress.description: True when fixing the emergency address clears it.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

serviceId.description: The trunk's `sipUsername`, or its `id` when it has no SIP credential.

previousType.description: The plan the trunk was on when the change was booked.

previousChannels.description: The channels billed before the change; 0 on `payg`.

type.description: The plan the change moves the trunk to.

channels.description: The channels billed after the change; 0 on `payg`.

effectiveOn.description: When the change takes effect. For a booked change it is the start of the next billing cycle. For an upgrade that applied at once it is today.

WebhookBookedChangeEvent.description: The delivery for `bookedChange.applied` and `bookedChange.cancelled`. A change booked on your account for a later date either took effect on its date, or will no longer happen. `data` is the entry `GET /account/booked-changes` listed. `resourceUrl` is the data service or trunk it changes.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. Use it to deduplicate.

WebhookBookedChangeFailedEvent.description: The delivery for `bookedChange.failed`. A change booked on your account for a later date reached its date but could not be made. `data` is the entry `GET /account/booked-changes` listed, plus the `reason`. `resourceUrl` is the data service or trunk it was to change.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. Use it to deduplicate.

reason.description: Why the change was not made. For a disconnect, it is the carrier's reason for refusing it, as the order shows it. For a plan change, it is a plain reason. Contact us with the change's `id` for the detail.
reason.example: The plan change could not be applied to the trunk. Contact us with the change's id.

WebhookBookedChangeRescheduledEvent.description: The delivery for `bookedChange.rescheduled`. We moved a data disconnect booked on your account for a later day to another day. It is the same booking, with the same `id`. `data` is the entry `GET /account/booked-changes` now lists, with its new `effectiveOn`, plus the day it was moved from. `resourceUrl` is the data service it changes.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. Use it to deduplicate.

previousEffectiveOn.description: The day the change was due on before it was moved, in Sydney time. Null when it had no day, because we held it to check after its day came.

WebhookExportEvent.description: The delivery for `export.ready` and `export.failed`. A background export (`POST /exports`) either has its file, or could not be written. `data` is the export as `GET /exports/{exportId}` shows it, without the download link. `resourceUrl` is that read, which hands out a fresh link.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. Use it to deduplicate.

WebhookInvoiceEvent.description:
The delivery envelope for the `invoice.*` events. The event type, not a field, says which one it is. `occurredAt` is when it happened.

`invoice.issued` is sent when an invoice is finalised. `invoice.paid` is sent when it is settled in full. `invoice.voided` is sent when it is cancelled and its charges unwound. A voided invoice is no longer owed. Clear it from your receivables rather than carrying it as an open debt. Voiding is idempotent, so we send the event once however many times a void is attempted.

These events cover platform (wholesale) invoices only. Your own retail billing is your ledger and never sends an event here.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

totalExGst.description: The invoice's own charges without GST, as a dollar string. The same figure as `totalExGst` on `GET /account/invoices`.

totalGst.description: The GST on those charges, as the invoice states it.

totalCents.description: Deprecated. Use `totalIncGst`. The invoice total in cents, including GST. We send it for one more release and then remove it.

voidedAt.description: When the invoice was cancelled. Present on `invoice.voided` only.

WebhookPaymentEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `payment.succeeded`, `payment.failed` and `payment.reversed`. Every one carries the same keys. The money came either from a charge against an invoice (`source: charge`) or from a credit top-up (`source: topup`). On a top-up, `paymentId`, `invoiceId` and `invoiceNumber` are null. `failureCode` and `failureMessage` are set on `payment.failed` and `payment.reversed` only.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

paymentId.description: The payment's `id`, as `GET /account/payments` lists it. Null until the money is in. That means null on `payment.failed` and on a top-up.

invoiceId.description: The `id` of the invoice this payment was applied to, as `GET /account/invoices` gives it. Null for a payment not made against an invoice. That means null on a top-up.

amount.description: The amount charged, GST-inclusive, as a dollar string. A payment has no GST split of its own. The GST is on the invoices it pays.

amountCents.description: Deprecated. Use `amount`. The charged amount in cents. We send it for one more release and then remove it.

gateway.description: The payment gateway that processed the charge.

source.description: `charge` is a stored method charged against an invoice. `topup` is credit bought for the account, with no invoice behind it.

failureCode.description: The gateway's decline, error or dishonour code. On `payment.failed` and `payment.reversed` only.

failureMessage.description: A reason a person can read. On `payment.failed` and `payment.reversed` only.

WebhookCreditNoteEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `creditNote.issued`. It covers a credit note we issued against one of your invoices, whether by our staff or as the outcome of a dispute. The credit is on your account balance from that moment. Credit notes you issue to your own end users never send this. They send `endUser.creditNote.issued`.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

invoiceId.description: The `id` (a ULID) of the invoice the credit note corrects, matching `GET /account/invoices`.

totalExGst.description: The credit without GST, as a dollar string.

reason.description: Why it was issued, as the credit note states it.

WebhookDisputeEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `dispute.raised` and `dispute.decided`. They cover a dispute on one of our invoices to you. You raise it in the portal or by API, or our staff raise it for you. While it is open, we do not collect or chase the disputed amount. Disputes your end users raise on your bills to them never send these. They send `endUser.dispute.raised` and `endUser.dispute.decided`.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

invoiceId.description: The disputed invoice's `id`, a ULID. It matches the /account/invoices endpoints.

invoiceLineId.description: The line disputed, when the dispute names one, by its public id as the invoice's `lineItems[].id`.

amountDisputed.description: The amount disputed, GST-inclusive as it appears on the invoice, as a dollar string. It has no GST split of its own until it is credited.

reason.description: The reason given. On `dispute.raised` only.
