outcome.description: On `dispute.decided` only. `resolved_credited` means we issued a credit note and sent `creditNote.issued`. `resolved_no_change` means it closed with nothing owed either way, such as a withdrawn or duplicate dispute. `rejected` means the charge stands and is collected as normal.

amountCreditedExGst.description: The credit without GST. Null when nothing was credited. On `dispute.decided` only.

amountCreditedIncGst.description: The credit with GST. On `dispute.decided` only.

creditNoteId.description: The `id` of the credit note issued, a ULID, when credited. On `dispute.decided` only.

WebhookInvoiceOverdueEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `invoice.overdue`. It covers one of your invoices past its due date, at the payment reminder we have just sent. We send one event per overdue invoice the reminder covers. There are two reminders, `reminder` and then `warning`, and each sends once per overdue spell. We send it whether or not you receive the overdue emails.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

invoiceId.description: The invoice's `id`, a ULID. It matches the /account/invoices endpoints.

amountDue.description: What the reminder asks you to pay on this invoice, GST-inclusive, as a dollar string. It is the amount due less anything held by an open dispute.

daysOverdue.description: Days past the due date, on the Brisbane calendar.

reminderStage.description: `reminder` is the first overdue notice. `warning` is the later notice that services may be suspended.

WebhookPaymentMethodEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `paymentMethod.expiring`. A card you pay us with expires soon. Add a new one before it does. We send it once for each expiry date, alongside the email. Your end users' cards never send this.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

paymentMethodId.description: The card's public id, as `GET /account/payment-methods` returns it.

label.description: The card as the portal shows it.

expiryMonth.description: The last month the card can be charged, as `YYYY-MM`.

isDefault.description: Whether it is the card we charge by default.

WebhookPriceRiseEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `priceRise.noticed`. It tells you that the price of a product you hold goes up. We send it with the email, once per notice. `changes` lists each rise, with the date it takes effect and the services it reaches. Use it to reprice your own end users or pass the notice on.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

items.description: One rise. A recurring price carries `oldPrice*` and `newPrice*`. A metered price carries `oldUnitPrice*` and `newUnitPrice*`. The side a product is not priced on is null. Unit prices go to 5 decimal places.

productId.description: The product's public id, as the retail price book returns it.

subscriptionId.description: The product subscription that is billed, by its public id.

serviceId.description: A data service's id or a trunk's `sipUsername`, as the service events name them. Null for a subscription not tied to one service.

WebhookCreditEvent.description:
The delivery envelope for `credit.thresholdReached`, `credit.callsBlocked` and `credit.callsRestored`. We check credit every minute. Credit used is what you owe us plus usage not yet invoiced. Available credit is your credit limit less that. All three figures are without GST.

A block stops new outbound calls on your trunks. It never stops a call to 000.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

threshold.description: The percentage of your credit limit now used. It is one of the warning levels you set, or 100 when calls are about to be blocked. On `credit.thresholdReached` only.

creditUsed.description: What you owe plus unbilled usage, without GST, as a dollar string.

availableCredit.description: `creditLimit` less `creditUsed`, without GST. Zero or less blocks new calls. It goes below zero when you are over.

WebhookUsageThresholdEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `usage.thresholdReached`. One of your end users' data services has used 50, 85 or 100% of its monthly allowance. We send it once for each of those levels in a month, while usage notices are on for your account. We send it whether or not the end user could be told. An end user with no contact details still sends it.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

serviceId.description: The data service's id, as the service events name it.

endUser.description: The end user's number.

usedBytes.description: Data used this month when it was crossed.

billingMonth.description: The allowance month, `YYYY-MM`, on your account's calendar.

WebhookUsageAlertEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `usageAlert.triggered`. One of the usage alerts you set passed its threshold. We send it once per period, with the email and SMS the alert chose. The period is the day for `callSpendToday` and the month otherwise, on the Brisbane calendar our bill runs on. An alert is a warning only. Nothing is blocked.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

alertId.description: The alert's id, as `GET /account/usage-alerts` lists it.

trunk.description: The trunk's `sipUsername` when the alert is on one trunk. Null for the whole account.

threshold.description: The alert's figure. For a spend metric it is dollars without GST ("50.00"). Otherwise it is a whole number of minutes or messages ("500").

value.description: The period's usage when the alert fired, in the same unit as `threshold`.

currency.description: `AUD` for a spend metric, null otherwise.

period.description: The day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) or month (`YYYY-MM`) it fired for.

WebhookRealmEvent.description: The outcome of a PPPoE realm request.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. Use it to deduplicate.

reason.description: Why the realm was not granted. On `data.realm.rejected` only.

WebhookRadiusSessionEvent.description: An Opticomm RADIUS user's session, retrieved from Opticomm.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. Use it to deduplicate.

id.description: The RADIUS user reference.

online.description: Whether Opticomm reported a session up.

session.description: The current session, as *Retrieve the Current Session* gives it. Null when nothing is connected.

PortStep.description: A port state as the port webhooks name it.

name.description: The state's name, as the portal shows it.

WebhookOrderEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `order.statusChanged`. `data.from` and `data.to` carry the transition, in the same status words `/data/orders` publishes. An order moving between internal steps that share one published status does not emit. You get one event per status change. A number port (`orderType: numberPort`) is the exception. It emits on every step and on a moved cutover, with the step in `step`.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

from.description: The previous published status. Null when the order had not been published before. A draft order is not visible on `/data/orders`, so its first event has no `from`.

statusReason.description: Why the order failed. Present only when `to` is `Failed`. On a `numberPort`, why it was rejected, withdrawn or cancelled.

portReference.description: On a `numberPort`, the port's own reference, as `GET /ports/{reference}` takes it. Absent on other order types.

step.description: On a `numberPort`, the step the port is now at. It is the port's real state, the same as `state` on the port read. Absent on other order types.

previousStep.description: On a `numberPort`, the step before this event. The same as `step` when the event is a moved cutover (`scheduledFor` changed).

scheduledFor.description: On a `numberPort`, the booked cutover, once there is one. On a port-out it is the agreed date.

portOutResponseCode.description: On a port `out`, the industry response code we gave the gaining carrier. `000` means approved. Any other code says why it was refused.

orderType.description: What kind of order this is. `data` is a carrier connect/disconnect order on `/data/orders`. `numberPort` is a number moving between carriers. See `numbers`. A port OUT reaching `Completed` means the numbers have left you.

direction.description:
Which way a `numberPort` is moving the numbers. `in` brings them onto your account; `out` takes them off it. Present on `numberPort` only.

**Read this together with `to`.** On an `out` port, `Completed` means the numbers have LEFT you. That is the opposite of what `Completed` means on every other order. Branch on `direction`, not on the fact that something finished.

network.description: The carrier delivering the order. Null on a `numberPort`. A port has a losing carrier and a gaining one, and naming either as "the network" would be wrong half the time. See `losingCarrier` and `gainingCarrier`.

losingCarrier.description: Who the numbers are moving FROM, on a `numberPort`. On a port `in` this is the customer's previous provider; on a port `out` it is us. Null when we hold no name for them.

gainingCarrier.description: Who the numbers are moving TO, on a `numberPort`. On a port `in` this is us. On a port `out` it is **null**. We buy wholesale rather than porting as a carrier, so the receiving carrier reaches us by email and is not recorded. Null means we do not know it. It does not mean there isn't one.

orderReference.description: Your own reference, as supplied when the order was placed.

salesReference.description: The same value as `orderReference`, under the name your own reference has on trunks, numbers and services (`externalRef`).

serviceId.description: The service the order produced, once one exists. Null until the carrier has allocated it. Expect it to be populated by the time the order reaches `Completed`. Always null on a `numberPort`, which moves an existing number rather than producing a service.

numbers.description: The numbers on a `numberPort`, in E.164. Absent on other order types.

WebhookOrderDelayedEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `order.delayed`. It covers an order held for a later submit time. We send it when the hold starts and when its time changes. We also send it when we hold the order for you at its time because it could not be sent (`heldForAction`). We have not sent the order to the carrier. Once it is sent, `order.statusChanged` follows as for any order. A cancelled held order is announced there under its PND. A booked disconnection never sends this event. Nor does an order you sent that the carrier asked us to try again. That order is in progress, and we resend it ourselves.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

delayedOrderId.description: The held order's PND, as /data/orders/delayed and /nbn/orders/delayed name it.

orderReference.description: Your own reference, as supplied when the order was placed.

submitDateTime.description: When the order will be sent. Null while it is held for you.

heldForAction.description: True when the order was not sent at its time and needs you. Fix the cause and submit it now, give it a new time, or cancel it.

heldReason.description: Why the order was not sent, while heldForAction is true.

WebhookOrderAwaitingEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `order.appointmentRequired` and `order.ntdFull`. An order you placed with POST /data/orders is waiting for something only you can give. We have not sent it to the carrier. Answer it with PATCH /data/orders/{orderId}. An order still waiting after 7 days is cancelled, and we send `order.statusChanged`.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

orderId.description: The order's id until the carrier has it. It is our PND. It keeps finding the order on /data/orders/{orderId} afterwards.

locationId.description: The premises the order is for (LOC # or OPC #).

orderReference.description: Your own reference, as supplied when the order was placed.

statusReason.description: What the order needs from you.

demandType.description: The appointment type a technician visit for this order needs, as the order's timeslots read uses it.

expiresAt.description: When the order is cancelled if it is still waiting.

WebhookPortActionRequiredEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `port.actionRequired`. A number port has arrived at a step only you can move. Today that is a mobile port-in waiting for the verification code its number's holder was sent. The same step also arrives as `order.statusChanged`.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

portReference.description: The port's reference, as `GET /ports/{reference}` takes it.

orderId.description: The id `order.statusChanged` names the same port by.

action.description: What is needed. For `enterVerificationCode`, confirm the code with `POST /ports/{reference}/confirm`. For `openPort`, read the port for what it needs.

actionDescription.example: Enter the verification code the number's holder was sent.

expiresAt.description: When the verification code lapses. That is 30 minutes after it was sent. Send a fresh one with `POST /ports/{reference}/verification-code`.

WebhookServiceEvent.description: The delivery envelope for the `service.*` lifecycle events. The event type, not a field, says which thing happened. `data.status` is where the service ended up. `data.serviceType` tells you which surface the service belongs to, and so how to read `data.serviceId`.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

serviceType.description: `data` for a data service (NBN, Opticomm), `voice` for a SIP trunk, `transit` for an IP transit circuit, `colocation` for a rack or part-rack with its power.

serviceId.description: How to address the service. For `data`, the service id used by the data endpoints. For `voice`, the trunk's `sipUsername`, or its `id` when it has no SIP credential. It is never a numeric id. For `transit` and `colocation`, the service's uuid, which is what the portal shows.

trunkId.description: On a `voice` event only: the trunk's `id`, which every trunk has. Absent for other service types.

externalRef.description: On a `data` or `voice` event only, your own reference on the service or trunk.

metadata.description: On a `data` or `voice` event only, your own metadata on the service or trunk.

status.description: Where the service ended up. `data` and `transit` services report `Live`. `voice` trunks and `colocation` services report `Active`. All four use `Suspended` and `Cancelled`.

previousStatus.description: Where it was before. Null when the service had no prior state, such as a newly provisioned service.

reason.description: Why it changed. `nonPayment` is a suspension or restore under the payment rules. `fraud` or `scam` is a suspension our staff recorded as fraud or a scam, on you or one of your end users. It is also used for the lift. `customerRequest` is a change you asked for, such as a disconnect you ordered, a trunk you paused or an agreed hardship pause. `carrier` is a change the carrier made, such as a cease we did not order. `staff` is an operator hold or other staff action. A fraud cap on a trunk holds its international calls without changing the service, so it sends no `service.*` event. We may add more values. Treat one you do not know as `staff`.

source.description: Who made the change. `staff` is our staff. `wholesaler` is you, in the portal or this API. `carrier` is the carrier. `system` is the platform itself, such as the payment reminder ladder.

WebhookServiceCeaseScheduledEvent.description: The carrier will cease one of your data services on a future date, and you did not ask for it.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. Use it to deduplicate.

serviceId.description: The service id used by the data endpoints.

ceaseAt.description: When the carrier will cease the service. It stays live, and billed, until then.

carrierReference.description: The carrier's own reference on its notice. It is an order id, or Opticomm's product instance id. Null when the carrier gave none.

WebhookDiagnosticCompletedEvent.description: A line test on one of your data services finished.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. Use it to deduplicate.

testId.description: The test's reference, as the diagnostics reads take it (`GET /nbn/diagnostics/{testRef}` or `GET /opticomm/diagnostics/{testRef}`).

serviceId.description: The service id used by the data endpoints.

network.description: Which network's diagnostics endpoints read the test.

testType.description: The test, by the name the diagnostics reads give it.

status.description: How the test ended.

result.description: Whether the test passed. Null when there is no pass or fail, which means a cancelled or rejected test, an inconclusive one, or a result the carrier has not yet given us. Read the test for its measurements.

reason.description: The carrier's note on the outcome, when it gave one.

WebhookServiceHealthReportReadyEvent.description: A service health report on one of your data services is ready.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. Use it to deduplicate.

reportId.description: The report's reference (HRI #), as the health reads take it (`GET /nbn/service_health/report/{hrId}` or `GET /opticomm/service_health/{hrId}`).

serviceId.description: The service id used by the data endpoints.

network.description: Which network's health endpoints read the report.

overall.description: The report's overall condition as the carrier gives it, such as `Green`, `Amber` or `Red`. Null when it gave none.

readyAt.description: When the report was stored and became readable.

WebhookOntUpgradeCompletedEvent.description: An ONT upgrade on one of your Opticomm data services ended.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. Use it to deduplicate.

serviceId.description: The service id used by the data endpoints.

succeeded.description: Whether the ONT was upgraded. False when the carrier closed the upgrade without doing it. The service is unchanged.

targetSku.description: The speed asked for with the upgrade, by its SKU. Null when none was recorded.

targetSpeed.description: The same speed, by its name.

speedChangeSubmitted.description: Whether the change to the target speed was submitted after the upgrade. Always false when `succeeded` is false. When the upgrade succeeded but this is false, we could not send the change yet. Most often the site does not offer the speed yet. We follow it up, and the service stays on its current speed.

WebhookAppointmentEvent.description:
The delivery envelope for the `appointment.*` events. The event type, not a field, says which one it is.

The shape is the same for every carrier. An NBN and an Opticomm appointment arrive alike, with `data.network` naming whose technician it is. You handle appointments once, not once per carrier.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

appointmentId.description: The carrier's appointment reference, matching the appointment endpoints.

status.description: The appointment's status, in the words the appointment endpoints publish. It is never the carrier's raw string.

previousStatus.description: What it was immediately before this change.

slotStart.description: The appointment window, as the carrier's own ISO-8601 string with its offset intact. It is the time your end user was told. It is not converted to UTC.

previousSlotStart.description: The window this appointment used to hold. Present on `appointment.rescheduled` only. Use it to find the booking in your own calendar.

orderId.description: The order the appointment belongs to, in the same reference `/data/orders` publishes. Null for an appointment not yet attached to an order.

locationId.description: The carrier's location identifier for the premises.

WebhookOutageData.description: An unplanned outage in an `outage.*` event: the outage as `GET /outages` publishes it, with `planned` false and `yourAffectedServiceCount` and `yourAffectedServiceTypes` added.

reference.description: The register reference for this outage.

timezone.description: The zone the timestamps above are rendered in.

cause.description: `withheld` where the cause is not disclosable. We say so explicitly rather than send null, so you do not mistake it for missing data.

yourAffectedServiceCount.description: How many of YOUR services fall in the outage's scope. It includes services attributed to your own retail end customers, which are yours to relay to. Use it to tell "one site" from "everything you have in that area" without cross-referencing your inventory.

yourAffectedServiceTypes.description: Which service families of yours are affected.

WebhookMaintenanceData.description: Planned maintenance in an `outage.*` event, as the public status page shows it.

impact.description: What customers will notice during the window.

url.description: The maintenance on the public status page.

WebhookOutageEvent.description:
The delivery envelope for the `outage.*` events. The event type, not a field, says which one it is.

`data` is the same outage body `GET /outages` returns, plus two fields telling you how much of it is yours. You only receive an outage that affects services on your account. We match them the same way the read endpoint does, so a push and a poll never disagree about whether you are affected.

We send only outages that we have reviewed and published. An outage we detected automatically but have not yet reviewed is not sent.

We send planned maintenance on the same three events, with `data.planned` true and the maintenance body instead. `outage.opened` is sent when we first send you its notice. `outage.updated` is sent when the window or what we tell customers changes, or the work starts. `outage.closed` is sent when it is completed or cancelled. You receive maintenance whose notice we sent to your account.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

eventType.description: `outage.opened` is sent when an entry reaches the register while still running. `outage.updated` is sent when something a customer would be told changes, such as the estimated restoration time, the affected area, the cause or the notes. `outage.closed` is sent when services are restored. Sending an email about an outage does not send an event, so you will not get an `outage.updated` every time we email about it.

data.description: An outage when `planned` is false, planned maintenance when it is true.

WebhookDegradationData.description: A potential service degradation, as the public status page shows it, plus how many of your data services are at its POIs.

area.description: The affected points of interconnect, e.g. `Sandbox (0SND)`.

impact.description: What customers may notice until the capacity is added.

expectedResolutionAt.description: When we expect the extra capacity to be in place. Null until we have a date.

url.description: The degradation on the public status page.

yourAffectedServiceCount.description: Your live data services at the affected POIs.

WebhookDegradationEvent.description:
The delivery envelope for the `degradation.*` events. The event type, not a field, says which one it is.

A potential service degradation is not an outage. Our interconnect at a POI is busy and the extra capacity is delayed. Data services there may be slower at peak times, but they are not down. You receive one when you have a live data service at one of its POIs.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

eventType.description: `degradation.opened` when we first tell you of it, `degradation.updated` when the expected date or what we tell customers changes, and `degradation.closed` when the capacity has been added.

WebhookQuoteEvent.description:
The delivery envelope for the `quote.*` events. The event type, not a field, says which one it is.

We send each account linked to the quote its own event. It carries that account's own `externalId`, the reference it gave when it requested the quote. It never carries another account's.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.
Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.
Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

tier.description: The tier this event is for. Each is sent once a month.

WebhookEndUserCreditNoteEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `endUser.creditNote.issued`. It covers a credit note you issued on one of your bills to an end user. You may have issued it by hand, as a service credit, or as the outcome of the end user's dispute. It is on the end user's account from that moment. Credit notes we issue to you send `creditNote.issued` instead. Only for an account that bills its end users.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

endUser.description: The end user the credit note is for, by its number.

invoiceId.description: The `id` (a ULID) of the bill the credit note corrects, matching `GET /end-users/invoices/{id}`.

totalExGst.description: The credit without GST, as a dollar string.

reason.description: Why it was issued, as the credit note states it.

WebhookEndUserDisputeEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `endUser.dispute.raised` and `endUser.dispute.decided`. They cover a dispute an end user raised on one of your bills to them, from their portal, and your decision on it, made in the portal or by API. While it is open, we do not chase the disputed amount. Disputes on our invoices to you send `dispute.raised` and `dispute.decided` instead. Only for an account that bills its end users.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

endUser.description: The end user who raised it, by its number.

invoiceId.description: The disputed bill's `id`, a ULID. It matches `GET /end-users/invoices/{id}`.

invoiceLineId.description: The line disputed, when the dispute names one, by its public id.

amountDisputed.description: The amount disputed, GST-inclusive as it appears on the bill, as a dollar string. It has no GST split of its own until it is credited.

reason.description: The reason the end user gave. On `endUser.dispute.raised` only.

outcome.description: On `endUser.dispute.decided` only. `resolved_credited` means we issued a credit note to the end user and sent `endUser.creditNote.issued`. `resolved_no_change` means it closed with nothing owed either way. `rejected` means the charge stands and is chased as normal.

amountCreditedExGst.description: The credit without GST. Null when nothing was credited. On `endUser.dispute.decided` only.

amountCreditedIncGst.description: The credit with GST. On `endUser.dispute.decided` only.

creditNoteId.description: The credit note issued, when credited. On `endUser.dispute.decided` only.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

messageId.description: The message's id. It is the `messageId` from `POST /sms`, and the id `GET /sms/messages/{messageId}` reads.

from.description: The sender, a number in E.164 format or a sender ID.

to.description: The recipient number in E.164 format.

status.description: As `GET /sms/messages/{messageId}` reports it.

statusReason.description: Present where the status alone is ambiguous. Null otherwise.

sentAt.description: When the message was sent or received.

at.description: When it arrived, or when the delivery receipt settled it.

failureReason.description: Why it was not delivered. In `sms.failed` only.

WebhookFaxEvent.description: The delivery for `fax.received`, `fax.sent` and `fax.failed`. It carries metadata only. It never carries the document or a link to it.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. One emit shares one id across all your endpoints. Use it to deduplicate.

faxId.description: The fax's id, as `GET /fax/documents/{id}` reads it.

number.description: Your number the fax was received on or sent from.

remoteNumber.description: The other party's number, when known.

faxPlanId.description: The fax plan a sent fax went out under, or the plan the receiving number is on. Null when there is none.

status.description: `sent` or `failed` for a sent fax. For a received fax it is `delivered`, `emailed` or `failed`. `delivered` means we kept it for the portal. `failed` means we could not pass it on, and `failureReason` says why.

at.description: When the fax was received or sent.

WebhookAccountEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `account.suspended` and `account.reinstated`. They are about your own account. While it is suspended, writes through this API answer `403`. Webhooks keep coming.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. Use it to deduplicate.

status.description: Where the account ended up.

reason.description: On `account.suspended`, the reason we gave you by email.

WebhookEndUserEvent.description: The delivery envelope for the `endUser.*` events. It is light by design. It names the end user and what changed, not the new values. Read the end user to sync it. `data.full` is always `false`. For an end user under a safety flag, we withhold the reference and the names of changed contact fields, as the portal does, and `data.detailsWithheld` is `true`.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. Use it to deduplicate.

reference.description: Your own reference for the end user, or null when it has none or it is withheld.

changedFields.description: On `endUser.updated`, the names of the fields that changed, such as `name` or `billingEmail`. The values are not sent.

full.description: Always `false`. The event is a pointer; read the end user for its details.

detailsWithheld.description: `true` when the end user is under a safety flag and contact details are withheld.

WebhookEndpointDisabledEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `webhook.endpointDisabled`. We turned off another of your endpoints after 20 dead deliveries in a row. We send it to your other endpoints that take it, never to the one we turned off.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. Use it to deduplicate.

webhookId.description: The endpoint turned off: its public id, as `GET /webhooks` names it and `GET /webhooks/{webhookId}` takes it.

WebhookDelegationEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `delegation.used`. You handed a person one step by a one-use link (`POST /ports/{reference}/delegations` or `POST /data/orders/{orderId}/delegations`). They passed the email code and did the step. We send it once per link. Read the port or the order for its new state.

eventId.description: Unique for each event we emit. Use it to deduplicate.

delegationId.description: The delegation's id, as the delegation calls give it.

portReference.description: The port's reference, for `confirmPort` and `confirmAuthority`. Null otherwise.

orderId.description: The data order's id, for `pickAppointment`. Null otherwise.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path exists, but doesn't accept this HTTP method.

TooManyRequests.description: You are over a rate limit (see Rate Limits). It may be the call's own, your API Client's or your account's. Wait for `Retry-After` seconds.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. On every `429`.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The calls the limit that refused this one allows in its minute.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: The calls left under that limit; `0` here.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: When that limit starts again, as a Unix time.

InternalServerError.description: Something failed on our side. If it persists, contact Support with the `CN-Message-Id`.

ServiceUnavailable.description: We, or the carrier's system, are briefly unavailable. Retry shortly.

Unauthorized.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

Forbidden.description: Your token doesn't carry the scope this endpoint needs.

UnprocessableEntity.description: The request failed validation. `fields` names each input that was wrong.

error.reason: The location id field is required.

fields.reason: The location id field is required.

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed or had invalid parameters, or the carrier refused it. For a carrier refusal, `code` says so and `carrierCode` holds the carrier's own code.

invalid.summary: Our own check refused the request

error.reason: The provided AVC does not exist

NotFound.description: Nothing by that identifier exists on your account.

Conflict.description: The resource isn't in a state that allows this right now.

error.reason: Satisfaction has already been submitted for this ticket.

BadGateway.description: We couldn't reach the carrier, and the request was not processed. Retry shortly.

DataRadiusRetrieving.description:
Retrieving. The service is on Opticomm's RADIUS. Opticomm gives its sessions only as a diagnostic result, which arrives a minute or two after we ask. A session check is on its way.

Ask again after `Retry-After` seconds. Reading never asks Opticomm again. Or subscribe to `data.radius.sessionRetrieved`, which carries the answer when it arrives. If Opticomm never answers, send a new `POST /data/radius/{ref}/session-check` after five minutes to ask again.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before asking again.

testId.description: On `POST /data/radius/{ref}/session-check` only: the Session History test's reference. Absent when the test was started elsewhere and is not yet known here.

message.example: We are retrieving this session from Opticomm. Check again in a minute or two, or subscribe to the data.radius.sessionRetrieved webhook to be told when it arrives.

NotImplemented.description: This endpoint is Coming Soon and not yet available.

NotInSandbox.description: Only the API sandbox (`api.checknetworks.dev`) answers this. The call acts on our live network, which the sandbox never reaches. Production never answers it.

TicketResult.description: The ticket as it now stands.

EndUserResult.description: The end user, as it now stands.

Page.name: page
Page.description: The page to return, from `1`. A value that is not a whole number of at least 1 is refused with `422 - validation_failed` naming `page`. We never change it for you.

PerPage.name: perPage
PerPage.description: Rows per page. Send a whole number from `1` to `200`. The default is `50`. A value outside that range, or not a whole number, is refused with `422 - validation_failed` naming `perPage`. We never reduce or round it.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Send the `nextCursor` from the previous page. The list continues newest first from where that page ended. A row added meanwhile is neither repeated nor skipped. A cursor page carries only `perPage`, `nextCursor` and `results`. `page` is ignored. A cursor this list did not issue is refused with `422 - validation_failed`. So is a cursor sent with `sort`.

Q.name: q
Q.description: Only rows whose searchable fields contain this text, ignoring case. Each list's description names the fields it searches. Send at most 100 characters. A longer value is refused with `422 - validation_failed`.

UpdatedSince.name: updatedSince
UpdatedSince.description: Only rows changed at or after this time. Send an ISO 8601 date or date-time, such as `2026-11-01` or `2026-11-01T09:00:00Z`. A date alone means the start of that day (UTC). Any other value is refused with `422 - validation_failed`.

CreatedFrom.name: createdFrom
CreatedFrom.description: Only rows created at or after this time. Send an ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone means the start of that day (UTC). Any other value is refused with `422 - validation_failed`.

CreatedTo.name: createdTo
CreatedTo.description: Only rows created at or before this time. Send an ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone includes the whole of that day (UTC). Any other value is refused with `422 - validation_failed`.

IdempotencyKeyRequired.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyRequired.description: **Required.** Send a unique value for this operation, such as a UUID. A retry then never does the work twice. Without it the request answers `400`. Send the same key and the same request again and you get the stored response, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. See Idempotency, above.

IdempotencyKeyOptional.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyOptional.description: Optional. Send a unique value for this operation, such as a UUID. A retry then never does the work twice. Send the same key and the same request again and you get the stored response, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. See Idempotency, above.

Tag.name: tag
Tag.description: Only rows carrying this tag, matched whole, ignoring case. Repeat it, as `tag=Site%2012&tag=Brisbane` or `tag[]=`, and a row must carry every one. A tag may hold a comma, so we never split values. A blank tag, or one over 255 characters, is `422`.

ExternalRef.name: externalRef
ExternalRef.description: Only the object holding this `externalRef`, matched exactly (case counts). Send up to 64 letters, digits, `_`, `.` or `-`. Any other value is refused with `422 - validation_failed`. A reference no object holds gives an empty list.

NbnProductType.name: productType
NbnProductType.description: Optional. Only the products of this traffic class, as each product's own `productType` shows it. `EE` is Enterprise Ethernet. `TC4` is every other product. Any other value is `400`. That includes `TC1` and `TC2`, which no product reports, and a product family, which you filter with `techType`.

NbnTechType.name: techType
NbnTechType.description: Optional. Only the products of this product family, as each product's `technology` shows it. The values are `NFAS` (fibre), `NCAS` (copper), `NWAS` (fixed wireless), `NHAS` (HFC), `NSAS` (satellite) and `EEAS` (Enterprise Ethernet). Any other value is `400`.

SmsFrom.name: from
SmsFrom.description: Optional. Only messages sent on or after this time (ISO 8601). A date alone means the start of that day. An invalid value returns `422`.

SmsTo.name: to
SmsTo.description: Optional. Only messages sent on or before this time (ISO 8601). A date alone means the end of that day, so the day is included. An invalid value returns `422`.

SmsSearch.name: q
SmsSearch.description: Optional. Only messages whose sender, recipient or text contains this. It matches as the portal's search does.

SmsStatus.name: status
SmsStatus.description: Optional. Only messages with this `status`. Any other value returns `422`.

SmsExportFormat.name: format
SmsExportFormat.description: The bulk export format. Leave it out for paged JSON. Send `csv` or `ndjson` and every message the other filters match streams as one download, newest first. `page` and `perPage` are then ignored. Each row has `id`, `sentAt`, `direction`, `from`, `to`, `message`, `parts`, `status` and `statusReason`. An unrecognised value returns `422`.

IdempotencyKeyDerived.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyDerived.description: Recommended. Send a unique value for this send, such as a UUID. A retry then never sends twice. Send the same key and the same request again and you get the stored response, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Without a key, we make one from the request and the current minute. The same message from the same sender to the same number with the same API key within that minute is sent once. The repeat returns the first send's response. See Idempotency, above.

EndUserPath.name: endUser
EndUserPath.description: The end user's number. An end user on another account answers 404, as an unknown number does.

PortReferencePath.name: reference
PortReferencePath.description: The port's reference. A port on another account answers 404, as an unknown reference does.

UsageMonth.name: month
UsageMonth.description: The month, as `YYYY-MM`. The default is this month. You can ask for any of the eleven months before it. Months follow your bill's calendar, which is your account's time zone. Any other month returns `400`.

DelegationIdPath.name: delegationId
DelegationIdPath.description: The delegation's id, from its create or list. One on another object answers 404.

DataOrderIdPath.name: orderId
DataOrderIdPath.description: The order's id, as `GET /data/orders` gives it. That is the carrier's id, or the PND while the order waits for you. An order on another account answers 404.

ApiVersion.description: The API version that answered. It is `2` on every response, from `/v2` and the unprefixed paths alike (see Versioning).
